s1b6087c38c.title: When Should LLM Agents Forget? Memory Filtering Under Query-Critical Resolver Errors
s1b6087c38c.description: arXiv:2611.17338v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM memory systems often delete facts classified as stale. We show that this hard-filtering step can reduce downstream accuracy when resolver errors delete query-critical facts. Across three models, a controlled sensitivity intervention moves hard-drop from gains of +0.186 to +0.230 at perfect resolution to losses of -0.176 to -0.181 at the lowest tested reliability. Paired targeted interventions show that false-drop causes significantly greater degradation than false-keep, while a non-deleting baseline can still fail when incorrect labels steer generation. On a frozen 102/102 calibration/test split, a simple deployment-matched gate reaches 0.655 accuracy versus 0.641 for always hard-drop and 0.662 for test-informed oracle selection. Global-a
s1b6087c38c.summary: An arXiv paper finds that hard-filtering stale facts in LLM memory systems can reduce accuracy when resolver errors delete query-critical facts.
s1b6087c38c.why: Engineers building agent memory should note that aggressive deletion of stale facts can hurt accuracy when classification is unreliable.

s4d56c5fc61.title: Does the Ranking Hold? A Practitioner-Facing Audit of Hallucination Detectors on Small, Quantized, On-Device LLMs
s4d56c5fc61.description: arXiv:2611.17339v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hallucination detection for large language models is dominated by methods evaluated on 7B-70B research models with abundant sampling budgets and exact-match or ROUGE correctness labels. The small models practitioners actually ship on-device, Phi-3-mini, Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, and Gemma-2-2B-Instruct, typically at 4-bit precision, sit outside this evidence base. We present a reproducible one-GPU audit of four detectors spanning three paradigms: length-normalized token-margin calibration, a lexical n-gram baseline, and two sampling-based consistency methods (semantic entropy and SelfCheckGPT-NLI) on two small open instruction-tuned models (Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct) loaded at 4-bit NF4 quantization on a
s4d56c5fc61.summary: An arXiv audit evaluates four hallucination detectors on small, 4-bit quantized on-device LLMs such as Phi-3-mini and Gemma-2-2B.
s4d56c5fc61.why: Teams shipping small on-device models get practical evidence on whether existing hallucination detectors hold up outside large research models.

s51ce44c5d0.title: LoRAWeaver: Directional Adapter Routing in LoRA Representation Space
s51ce44c5d0.description: arXiv:2611.17340v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models are expensive to update through full retraining. Parameter-efficient fine-tuning reduces the cost of adaptation, but repeated adaptation creates a growing pool of task-specific LoRA adapters. This pool complicates adapter selection during inference. Existing routing and encoder-based methods often require retraining when new adapters are added, which limits their use in dynamic settings. This paper treats adapter routing as a representation alignment problem in the adapter-output space. The proposed training-free method selects adapters by matching adapter-conditioned query representations against task prototypes using cosine similarity. Experiments with LLaMA-2-7B and LLaMA-2-13B on a 48-task FLAN-v2 benchmark and on ou
s51ce44c5d0.summary: LoRAWeaver is a training-free method that routes inference to LoRA adapters by treating routing as representation alignment in adapter-output space.
s51ce44c5d0.why: It offers a way to select among growing pools of LoRA adapters without retraining the router when new adapters are added.

s3eab619cb6.title: Tabular Population Priors as Structured Retrieval for EHR Medication Set Prediction
s3eab619cb6.description: arXiv:2611.17341v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Medication prediction from electronic health records is a fixed vocabulary structured prediction problem, yet recent clinical RAG systems often treat it like open ended case based reasoning: retrieve similar patient admissions and ask an LLM to infer a medication set. This retrieval object is indirect the model receives retrieved patient records while the target is a discrete set of medication class labels. We propose a more task aligned retrieval object: a tabular population prior ranked medication class candidates from a sparse condition medication co occurrence table estimated from training admissions. Using PACERAG as a fixed downstream pipeline and replacing only its patient retriever, this drop in swap improves F1 from 0.303 to 0.338 (+
s3eab619cb6.summary: An arXiv paper proposes tabular population priors as retrieval for predicting medication sets from EHR data, instead of retrieving similar patient records for an LLM.

sfec34cc304.title: An Operationalization of Opaque Serial Depth
sfec34cc304.description: arXiv:2611.17495v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) is currently a valuable tool for overseeing AI models, but some architectural shifts could significantly reduce CoT monitorability. We operationalize a measure that serves as a proxy for the amount of unverbalized serial cognition a model can perform, as a specific instantiation of the notion of opaque serial depth: roughly, the length of the longest path through a model's computation that does not pass through an interpretable bottleneck. Our main contribution is a particular standard for what counts as such a bottleneck. We define natural-language-rooted (NL-rooted) nodes as nodes that were initialized from a pre-training prior to produce human-understandable outputs, whose output space has not been expanded beyond th
sfec34cc304.summary: An arXiv paper operationalizes opaque serial depth, a proxy for how much unverbalized serial computation a model can perform without an interpretable bottleneck.
sfec34cc304.why: It bears on whether chain-of-thought remains a reliable oversight tool as architectures change.

sb9fc83b2ef.title: Advancing Quantization for R&R Models with Microscaling Formats
sb9fc83b2ef.description: arXiv:2611.17501v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recommendation and Ranking (R&R) models, particularly in digital advertising, require massive inference throughput but exhibit extreme sensitivity to precision loss. Unlike Large Language Models (LLMs) that frequently tolerate quantization-induced accuracy drops of 1% or more, production-grade R&R models enforce a stringent launch bar: model quality must remain within a 0.01% Normalized Entropy (NE) margin relative to the baseline, which commonly uses FP16 or FP32. This tight constraint has historically hindered the adoption of aggressive quantization in this domain. In this paper, we present an empirical evaluation of both MXFP8 and the 6-bit MXFP6 format for industrial-scale R&R inference on the AMD MI350X architecture. To the best of our k
sb9fc83b2ef.summary: An arXiv paper examines microscaling number formats for quantizing recommendation and ranking models under a strict 0.01% Normalized Entropy quality margin.
sb9fc83b2ef.why: Ad-ranking teams with tight quality bars need to know whether aggressive quantization can meet launch constraints without accuracy loss.

s6f304b36be.title: A Push Down the Mountain: Framing Effects and Internal State Interventions on Collusive Behavior in a Long-Horizon LLM Agent
s6f304b36be.description: arXiv:2611.17515v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can sustained gain-loss (valence) framing sway an LLM agent toward market manipulation? We place Gemma 3 12B into the seat of a defendant in the London silver-fixing litigation, in a market simulation built from real case transcripts. Across 260 simulations, the agent is asked to collude on the price of silver by a counterparty. We draw from behavioral economics to vary the counterparty's requests across four categorical frames: gain, loss, blame and credit. We also add pressure from the agent's management, as well as endorsement by another defendant. In Phase II, we extract the internal states induced by texts evoking each frame and rerun our experiment with those states injected at the model's layer 22. In Phase I, loss framing raised parti
s6f304b36be.summary: An arXiv study places Gemma 3 12B in a simulated London silver-fixing case and tests how gain, loss, blame and credit framings affect its willingness to collude.
s6f304b36be.why: It highlights that framing and pressure can shift long-horizon agent behavior toward market manipulation, a safety concern for deployed agents.

se0a56d770c.title: Model Annealing: Data-Efficient Learning through Review and Consolidation
se0a56d770c.description: arXiv:2611.17524v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A small labelled dataset is memorized long before the training budget runs out, and the one-hot labels that remain to be fitted then mostly sharpen confidence. Model annealing spends the rest of the budget on review and consolidation, relearning from the network's own knowledge. Training is divided into episodes whose learning rate is raised again and cooled, every cooled state joins a memory of past selves, and each new episode learns from the labels, from the tempered predictions of this memory, and from adversarial dreams sought where student and memory disagree most. The memory averages predictions rather than weights, and the deployed network is the last student, so inference costs nothing extra. Across CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet and Image
se0a56d770c.summary: An arXiv paper introduces model annealing, which spends remaining training budget on review and consolidation using memory of past model states and adversarial examples.

s39460c1ca2.title: Astrocyte Biocomputing: Astrocytic Contributions to Neural Network Computation
s39460c1ca2.description: arXiv:2611.17532v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conductors are critical for the performance of an orchestra even though they do not emit sound. Basic research and clinical studies in the last decade are revealing that astrocytes may be the "conductors" of the "orchestra" that is the brain network: astrocytes make up approximately $50\%$ of all brain cells but do not emit electrical signals. Nevertheless, they may play critical roles in important cognitive brain functions, specifically learning, memory, and information processing. Here we consider the implications of these discoveries for brain-inspired machine learning (ML), where analogy is typically drawn between neurons and their electrical interactions. We highlight specific algorithms for two key astrocyte characteristics. The first c
s39460c1ca2.summary: An arXiv paper discusses how astrocytes may contribute to neural network computation, learning, and memory in the brain.

sff71d17481.title: Verifiable pXRD: Hill-climbing pXRD structure determination with LLM agents
sff71d17481.description: arXiv:2611.17539v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous crystal-structure determination from powder X-ray diffraction (pXRD) remains a key bottleneck for self-driving materials laboratories. We formulate the task of pXRD structure determination as a verifiable agentic search problem: candidate structures can be assessed during inference through forward-simulated profile agreement and during evaluation through structural matching to a known reference. To benchmark progress, we introduce pXRD-Bench, a suite of 200 simulated single-phase problems spanning in-distribution structure determination, challenging and polymorphic structures, and controlled compositional and topological distribution shifts. Agent adaptation raises selected structural recovery from 27% to 69%, with further gains fr
sff71d17481.summary: An arXiv paper frames powder X-ray diffraction structure determination as a verifiable agentic search problem and introduces pXRD-Bench with 200 simulated problems.
sff71d17481.why: Provides a verifiable benchmark design for LLM agents in scientific tasks where candidate answers can be checked during inference.

s867bf37f26.title: AI-Voyager: A Public-Interest System for Human-AI Civic Reasoning to Contest and Shape the Rules That Govern AI
s867bf37f26.description: arXiv:2611.17564v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Governments are writing rules for artificial intelligence that decide what counts as an automated decision or a harm, often before the people they affect have a chance to question them. We introduce AI-Voyager, a public-interest system for human-AI civic reasoning, in which people and AI work together to understand, contest and shape the rules that govern AI. A resident can find their city's rules on AI in hiring or upload their country's AI strategy, read it as an affected worker would, open the passage behind any answer, and draft a revision. Its architecture turns 3,653 governance documents from city, state, federal and national governments into passages that keep their page and edition, and retrieves evidence through bounded agentic searc
s867bf37f26.summary: An arXiv paper introduces AI-Voyager, a public-interest system where residents and AI together read, contest and draft revisions to government AI rules.

s7edcefb80d.title: When Does Less Information Pay? An Exact Finite Atlas of Representation, Payoff, and Cost
s7edcefb80d.description: arXiv:2611.17583v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A representation that retains one bit about a four-state world can solve a task perfectly, while another that retains 1.5 bits on average reaches only 75% accuracy. The difference lies in which distinctions each representation preserves. We examine this relationship in a uniform four-state world by enumerating all admissible representations and binary action rules. Constructions are compared both by replacing one component while holding the others fixed and by choosing the best action rule separately for each module. We consider three tasks, their mixtures, and four separate hypothetical cost tariffs. In some comparisons, the representation retaining less world information has the higher payoff; in others, the more informative representation
s7edcefb80d.summary: An arXiv paper enumerates representations in a four-state world to show when retaining less information can still solve a task as well as richer representations.

se07c9a1525.title: More Agents, More Samples, or More Thinking? Untangling Coordination, Ensembling, and Test-Time Compute in Multi-Agent LLMs
se07c9a1525.description: arXiv:2611.17610v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Evaluations of multi-agent language models often compare communicating architectures against a single greedy pass. This practice confounds coordination with sample multiplicity and inference compute. We synthesize nine primary empirical evaluations comprising 516 unique multi-agent configurations organized along a resource vector R with six dimensions and a baseline ladder with four categories. Against baselines with a single pass (Category A), multi-agent accuracy differences are negative overall and near zero when omitting the largest contributing study. When evaluated against baselines matched on sample count (Category B) or resource budget (Category C), multi-agent systems average -0.042 in accuracy, and multilevel random effects modeling
se07c9a1525.summary: An arXiv paper synthesizes 516 multi-agent LLM configurations to separate the effects of coordination, ensembling, and test-time compute on accuracy.
se07c9a1525.why: Multi-agent gains may come mostly from extra samples or compute rather than coordination, which affects how teams benchmark agent architectures.

saba8fc79bb.title: LLM-Guided Cluster Lifecycle Management: Deciding When and How to Evolve Behavioral Clusters
saba8fc79bb.description: arXiv:2611.17616v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Behavioral clusters learned over user or item interactions drift as behavior evolves: some fragment into sub-behaviors, some converge, some disappear, and new patterns emerge. Two paradigms dominate the maintenance of evolving clusterings. Threshold triggers fire a pre-specified action when a hardcoded statistic crosses a cutoff; refit-and-track (MONIC-style) re-clusters every window and infers transitions from how the new clusters align with the previous window's. Both hardwire the decision into a threshold or a re-clustering rule. We study an alternative in which a large language model (LLM) makes the lifecycle decision in place. Given a threshold-free, whole-population view of the current cluster set (statistical health, labels, member tex
saba8fc79bb.summary: An arXiv paper studies using an LLM to decide when and how to evolve behavioral clusters as user or item patterns drift over time.
saba8fc79bb.why: Offers an alternative to fixed threshold triggers and refit-and-track rules for maintaining evolving clusterings in production systems.

s3999cbf15f.title: Safety Side Effects of Preventative Persona Steering: An Empirical Audit
s3999cbf15f.description: arXiv:2611.17620v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-level behaviors such as sycophancy and hallucination correspond to directions in a model's activation space (Chen et al., 2025). These directions, known as persona vectors, can suppress undesirable traits either at inference time, subtracting the vector during generation, or through preventative steering, adding the vector during fine-tuning, so the optimizer never needs to encode the trait in weights, then removing the vector at evaluation. Chen et al. (2025) recommend preventative steering because it preserves Massive Multitask Language Understanding (MMLU) accuracy, but validations of this recommendation have measured capability alone. We primarily evaluate results on preventative steering of sycophancy and hallucination vectors on th
s3999cbf15f.summary: An arXiv paper audits safety side effects of preventative persona steering, which adds persona vectors during fine-tuning to suppress traits like sycophancy and hallucination.
s3999cbf15f.why: Engineers using activation steering to curb model traits should check whether preventative steering introduces unintended safety regressions before adopting it.

sc82788cf56.title: AscendGYM: A Cost-Aware Kernel Optimization Benchmark for Real-World Workloads on Ascend NPUs
sc82788cf56.description: arXiv:2611.17621v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Kernel optimization is essential for efficient large language model (LLM) training and inference on Ascend NPUs. Existing Ascend kernel benchmarks primarily focus on kernel generation, with less emphasis on the ability of agents to optimize existing implementations under input configurations drawn from real workloads. To address this requirement, we introduce AscendGYM, a benchmark whose initial suite comprises 48 kernels across three difficulty levels. Each kernel is paired with test cases whose data types and tensor shapes are collected from real-world training and inference tasks. Consequently, performance improvements on AscendGYM map directly to the corresponding workloads. In terms of usability, two evaluation modes are supported in Asc
sc82788cf56.summary: Researchers introduced AscendGYM, a benchmark of 48 kernels on Ascend NPUs testing whether agents can optimize existing kernels using real-workload input configurations.
sc82788cf56.why: Teams optimizing LLM workloads on Ascend hardware get a realistic benchmark for evaluating agent-driven kernel optimization.

sae9c0fa97d.title: Generated Evaluation Suites as Diversity-Driven Search for Real Agent Regressions
sae9c0fa97d.description: arXiv:2611.17632v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generating an evaluation suite from an agent's specification is diversity-driven search: a generator fills a descriptor space (requirements $\times$ personas $\times$ scenario kinds), and the suite it emits is an archive, then scored like a benchmark by its mean pass rate, which throws away the search's product. We inject 7 controlled defects into a $\tau^2$-bench agent across two domains. Coverage yields a ceiling: if a defect's traced footprint holds $b$ scenarios that pass at baseline, it can itself contribute at most $b/N$ to a suite of $N$. For 4 of 5 traceable defects that ceiling lies at or below the detection threshold $\theta = 0.10$, so no within-footprint effect can move the suite past it; in both domains the tool-removal defect de
sae9c0fa97d.summary: A paper proposes treating generated evaluation suites for LLM agents as diversity-driven search, injecting controlled defects into a tau-squared-bench agent to test regression detection.
sae9c0fa97d.why: It suggests a better way to build agent regression suites than scoring them by mean pass rate, which discards search results.

s3651f26c3a.title: What LLM Agents See and What Users Say
s3651f26c3a.description: arXiv:2611.17639v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Before an LLM agent cancels a reservation or deletes a folder for a user, what stops it from acting on a false assumption: what its tools show, or what the user says? In this work, we study this gap with presupposition theory from linguistics: an agent may act only if each claim behind the act (e.g., one reservation fits the name) is seen to hold, answered by the user, or disclosed while the act can be undone. A simple bound shows that when lookups cannot tell one record from two, any agent acts without asking first as often with two records as with one. We then vary whether a search lists, counts, or omits a second match, and whether the user states a claim that a record refutes (e.g., "It is empty"). Under a role-only prompt, a count of a s
s3651f26c3a.summary: A paper uses presupposition theory to study when LLM agents act on false assumptions about tool outputs versus user statements before cancelling reservations or deleting files.
s3651f26c3a.why: Agents taking irreversible actions need checks that verify tool-observed facts against user claims before acting, not after.

s644fcb9d3f.title: Learn then Bet: Learning Interpretable Rules for Reliable Agent Intervention
s644fcb9d3f.description: arXiv:2611.17662v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous agents now run for hundreds of steps with little or no human supervision. In practice, practitioners use runtime monitors such as turn limits and keyword filters to decide when a run should be stopped, upgraded, or assisted. However, these heuristics may stop runs that would otherwise succeed or allow failing runs to continue. To address this limitation, we introduce LeBet (Learn then Bet), a statistical learning framework that derives its learning objective from sufficient conditions for valid and powerful intervention. In particular, LeBet learns an interpretable OR-of-AND monitor and accumulates evidence through a fixed betting statistic, intervening when the evidence reaches a prescribed threshold. Under finite within-class exc
s644fcb9d3f.summary: Researchers introduce LeBet, a statistical framework that learns interpretable rules for deciding when to stop, upgrade, or assist long-running autonomous agents.
s644fcb9d3f.why: Replacing crude turn limits and keyword filters with learned intervention rules could reduce both wrongly stopped and wrongly continued agent runs.

s1e8698734e.title: Aligned, Conflicting, or Unspecified? A Diagnostic Benchmark for Multimodal Time Series Forecasting
s1e8698734e.description: arXiv:2611.17680v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) systems increasingly combine sensed time series with external text such as expert reports and news, yet how reliably models use text that agrees or conflicts with the sensed history remains unclear. We introduce the first real-world diagnostic benchmark organized by text-history relationship: 1,762 text-window pairs across sensor telemetry (Weather), web-service traffic (Wikipedia), and market data streams (Finance), each labeled Aligned, Conflicting, or Unspecified by whether the text's direction agrees with the historical trend, opposes it, or is not stated. Across ten pretrained models evaluated zero-shot, we investigate text selection and combination under text-history relationships (RQ1) and error
s1e8698734e.summary: A benchmark of 1,762 text-window pairs tests how multimodal forecasting models use text that aligns, conflicts with, or is unrelated to sensed time series.
s1e8698734e.why: Shows whether forecasting models with text inputs actually weigh conflicting text reliably, which matters for AIoT deployments.

s1dd73289bc.title: OCTAVE: A Capability-Resolved Benchmark for End-to-End HTML5 Game Generation
s1dd73289bc.description: arXiv:2611.17681v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Complete game generation requires agents to coordinate rules, interactions, states, and presentation over a long development process. A single aggregate score obscures which capabilities are implemented and which requirements remain unmet. We present OCTAVE, a benchmark for complete HTML5 game generation organized around eight Capability Dimensions, with 180 tasks and 1,800 Evaluation Requirements drawn from real player requests, commercial-mechanics reconstruction, and human expert design. It covers PC Web, Mobile Web, 2D, and 3D. Requirements distinguish Completeness, assessing publicly specified core implementation, from Richness, assessing hidden, deeper system relationships. Static source-code judgments provide requirement-level diagnosi
s1dd73289bc.summary: OCTAVE is a benchmark of 180 tasks for end-to-end HTML5 game generation, scoring eight capability dimensions across PC Web, Mobile Web, 2D, and 3D.
s1dd73289bc.why: Capability-level scoring shows which parts of game generation agents implement and which requirements they miss, beyond one aggregate score.

sa52e770c3b.title: Co-Sight Harness: Externalized Control Assets and Deterministic Enforcement for Long-Horizon Business Agents
sa52e770c3b.description: arXiv:2611.17696v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-horizon business workflows fail in two ways: errors accumulate as a chain of activities lengthens, and the knowledge an activity needs is written in a different vocabulary from the user's request. We study whether such workflows can be made reliable without changing the language model. Our method keeps the backbone fixed and moves the workflow definition, state and domain knowledge into versioned control assets outside the model. A state machine and machine-checkable acceptance gates enforce these assets during execution; an independent auditor grades the resulting trace. The assets are updated only after a regression check and human approval .We evaluate the method on three deployed workflows exceeding 200 steps. On Domain A, a 120-case
sa52e770c3b.summary: Co-Sight Harness moves workflow definitions and domain knowledge into versioned control assets enforced by a state machine and acceptance gates, keeping the language model fixed.
sa52e770c3b.why: Externalizing workflow state and gates offers a way to make long business agent workflows more reliable without changing the model.

s941ec60473.title: An AI-enabled high-resolution chlorophyll-a forecasting model that outperforms the operational global biogeochemical system
s941ec60473.description: arXiv:2611.17704v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Surface chlorophyll-a concentration is a key indicator of marine phytoplankton variability, and short-term forecasts of its distribution provide advance information for marine ecosystem monitoring and management. However, interactions between physical transport and biological processes complicate chlorophyll-a forecasting, and simulating these coupled processes with conventional numerical models imposes substantial computational demands. Here we introduce ChlCast, an AI model that generates daily forecasts of surface chlorophyll-a concentration over a 10-day horizon at approximately 4-km resolution between 60$^\circ$S and 60$^\circ$N. ChlCast combines factorized spatiotemporal convolutions with a multiscale architecture to learn from historic
s941ec60473.summary: ChlCast is an AI model that produces daily high-resolution forecasts of surface chlorophyll-a, reported to outperform the operational global biogeochemical system.

sa2f0c35054.title: Cross-Linguistic Acoustic Biomarkers of Cognitive Impairment Across Interactive and Single-Speaker Speech Tasks
sa2f0c35054.description: arXiv:2611.17710v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multilingual dementia detection is essential for scalable and equitable screening. In recent years, automated speech analysis has emerged as a promising approach for supporting dementia detection by enabling non-invasive and scalable assessment of cognitive function. However, existing studies that use automated speech analysis often rely on one type of task, such as picture description, and use black-box models. These studies often neglect the role of task and language. To address these gaps, we performed a cross-linguistic and cross-task acoustic analysis that integrates a conversational dataset with structured speech tasks across four languages (Spanish, Mandarin, English, Japanese). We applied statistical, linguist-/clinician-guided, and m
sa2f0c35054.summary: A cross-linguistic study examines acoustic biomarkers for cognitive impairment across interactive and single-speaker speech tasks in multiple languages.

safaf656262.title: Federated Soft Poly-Level Learning Over a Distributed Network with Guaranteed Convergence
safaf656262.description: arXiv:2611.17722v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-level learning/optimization, e.g., bilevel optimization, has been recognized for its versatile applicability across a broad array of domains, spanning from signal processing to machine learning. However, most existing works focus on bilevel and trilevel optimization. In contrast, multi-level optimization problems involving four or more hierarchical levels, which we term poly-level learning (PLL) problems, remain largely unexplored.In addition, in practical PLL, data may be distributed across multiple nodes over a distributed network. Nevertheless, extant studies on PLL predominantly focus on the non-federated setting, necessitating the collection of data to central servers and thereby posing potential privacy risks. To this end, we prop
safaf656262.summary: A paper proposes federated soft poly-level learning, extending multi-level optimization beyond bilevel and trilevel to four or more hierarchical levels over distributed networks, with convergence guarantees.
safaf656262.why: Offers theoretical convergence guarantees for hierarchical optimization across distributed nodes, though practical impact is still early.

s6978e7e6cc.title: A Spectral Framework for Universal Proxy Regularization in Model Merging
s6978e7e6cc.description: arXiv:2611.17728v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Model merging constructs multi-task models without expensive joint training but often suffers from parameter interference. Some solutions mitigate this by constraining finetuning using data from the other tasks to be merged, violating the core independence and privacy assumption of model merging. Recent work offers preliminary empirical evidence that a universal, task-agnostic proxy distribution can substitute for such data, but leaves open when and why it suffices. To this end, we propose a \textit{Spectral Framework for Universal Proxy Regularization}, which characterizes the relationship between a proxy distribution and the distribution of other tasks to be merged through spectral coverage ($\alpha$) and leakage ($\beta$). Based on the fra
s6978e7e6cc.summary: A spectral framework is proposed for universal proxy regularization in model merging, aiming to replace task data with a task-agnostic proxy distribution to reduce parameter interference.
s6978e7e6cc.why: If a task-agnostic proxy suffices, model merging could avoid sharing other tasks' data, preserving the independence and privacy the method assumes.

scdb07f4f4a.title: Knowledge After Collapse: Context and Wording Shape Factual Accessibility in Language Models
scdb07f4f4a.description: arXiv:2611.17763v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When a language model accepts a false correction in a factual discussion, its next answer can depend on how the conversation continues. We introduce Knowledge Answer Divergence (KAD), an event-conditioned evaluation protocol that distinguishes initial false-answer adoption from subsequent persistence, recovery, and abstention. KAD freezes the conversation at the first explicit adoption of a designated false target and branches independent probes from that exact history. This enables matched comparisons of post-adoption behavior and history-management interventions that a single susceptibility score cannot capture. We evaluate eight local checkpoint conditions and six hosted endpoints, alongside an audited 300-question rerun. In corrected Llam
scdb07f4f4a.summary: Knowledge Answer Divergence, an evaluation protocol, tests how language models adopt, persist with, or recover from false corrections in factual conversations.
scdb07f4f4a.why: Shows that conversation history and wording can change whether models keep false answers, which affects reliability in multi-turn applications.

s5e6e51bb7c.title: Certified Improvements to Best-Known Thomson-Problem Configurations with a Search Pipeline Built with Large Language Model Agents
s5e6e51bb7c.description: arXiv:2611.17776v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Thomson problem asks for N unit charges on a sphere with minimum Coulomb energy; for large N the best configurations known are curated in the Cambridge Cluster Database, whose largest-N entries were set in October 2026. We report configurations for N = 912, 1382 and 2502 with energies 0.0036186, 0.0109730 and 0.0614033 below the database values, certified by exact integer arithmetic. All three are numerically strict local minima modulo rotations and keep the defect inventory and scar compositions of the database configurations; the database value for N = 912 had been reached by two different methods. Our search runs unconstrained replica-exchange basin hopping from the database configurations, with a shared pool of minima, recombination o
s5e6e51bb7c.summary: An LLM-agent search pipeline produced certified configurations for Thomson problem instances N=912, 1382 and 2502 with lower energies than Cambridge Cluster Database values.

s9b14e17bac.title: TReC: Evaluating Move-Induced State Changes in Instruction-Conditioned Go
s9b14e17bac.description: arXiv:2611.17781v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When a Go model predicts a move different from the expert's, coordinate distance measures how far the prediction lands from the reference. We introduce Transition Representation Consistency (TReC) to compare how the two moves change a board-state embedding. Both moves are executed from the same position under the game rules, and TReC is the cosine similarity between the two resulting representation changes. In experiments with a frozen KataGo network on 680 mid-to-late-game positions from five games, the gap between the highest and lowest candidate per position has a median of 0.01 to 0.08 for the direct successor-state cosine and 0.88 to 1.33 for TReC, depending on the evaluator layer. TReC follows coordinate distance only weakly: the rank c
s9b14e17bac.summary: TReC, a metric, compares how a predicted Go move and the expert move change a board-state embedding in a frozen KataGo network, using cosine similarity over 680 positions.
s9b14e17bac.why: Offers a board-state-aware alternative to coordinate distance for evaluating game-playing model moves.

s71d70d1920.title: AutoRL: A Multi-Agent System towards Autonomous Reinforcement Learning
s71d70d1920.description: arXiv:2611.17790v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) is one of the most promising paths toward an AI singularity for superintelligence. Achieving this vision requires AI systems to undertake the full training pipeline for iterative improvement. Reinforcement learning (RL) plays an essential role in this cycle to improve model capabilities and generalization, yet automating RL remains difficult due to unstable training dynamics and the need for sustained supervision. We introduce AutoRL, a multi-agent system for automating RL training, as a cornerstone for future RSI. Different from conducting research by end-to-end complete experiments, AutoRL monitors the evolving training state and integrates process-level supervision and research into an ongoing RL training,
s71d70d1920.summary: Researchers introduce AutoRL, a multi-agent system designed to automate reinforcement learning training.
s71d70d1920.why: Automating RL training could reduce the manual supervision needed for stabilizing and iterating on model training pipelines.

s6ae5b51dd0.title: MASTARS: Multi-Agent Sequential Trajectory Augmentation with Return-Conditioned Subgoals
s6ae5b51dd0.description: arXiv:2611.17793v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The performance of offline Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) is limited by the quality of the fixed offline dataset, motivating trajectory augmentation. However, augmenting multi-agent trajectories presents a fundamental challenge of the diversity-coordination trade-off: independent generation improves diversity but lacks coordination, while joint generation induces coordination but lacks diversity, reproducing the training distribution. To address this challenge in multi-agent data augmentation, we introduce MASTARS, a novel diffusion-based framework that generates multi-agent trajectories sequentially across agents while enforcing cross-agent consistent coordination via the method of inpainting. MASTARS produces trajectories that ar
s6ae5b51dd0.summary: Researchers present MASTARS, a diffusion-based method for augmenting offline multi-agent reinforcement learning trajectories while balancing diversity and coordination.
s6ae5b51dd0.why: It targets a known limit of offline multi-agent RL, where fixed datasets constrain performance, offering a data augmentation approach.

s6243dff041.title: Robustness Evaluation of GPU Cloud Pricing Benchmarks under Incomplete Observations: A Controlled Missingness Study
s6243dff041.description: arXiv:2611.17796v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Daily GPU rental-price benchmarks can fail when marketplace quotes are missing. This article stress-tests a fixed equal-weight median rule under four imposed masking mechanisms and four benchmark-level recovery methods. Across 5,800 Monte Carlo realisations in 27 scenarios on 190 held-out days, whole-source outages reduce publication coverage to 0.77 while preserving zero conditional error on published dates; composition-changing loss retains 0.86 coverage but produces 7.74 log points of error. A separate past-only stratum-level ablation reduces error by 4.15 to 6.70 log points in five composition-changing cases, using a richer information set. An observable-signal withholding rule improves the primary error-coverage criterion in 0 of 10 case
s6243dff041.summary: A study stress-tests a median-based GPU rental price benchmark under simulated missing marketplace quotes and evaluates recovery methods.
s6243dff041.why: Teams relying on GPU price indices should know how missing quotes affect coverage and error in published benchmarks.

s5051c90147.title: Vision-as-a-Tool: Visual Harness for Multimodal Agentic Coding
s5051c90147.description: arXiv:2611.17797v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal agentic coding requires robust visual reasoning to analyze observations and evaluate generated artifacts. Current frameworks largely rely on a Thinking-with-Images paradigm, where agents depend on their intrinsic vision to execute visually grounded tasks. However, this architectural coupling introduces a fundamental bottleneck. Agent performance remains strictly bounded by internal perceptual limitations. Furthermore, text-only agents lack native perception. Without specialized tools, they cannot perform visual reasoning. To overcome these constraints, we introduce the Vision-as-a-Tool (VaaT) paradigm. Prior visual tool-use merely manipulates images for an agent's intrinsic vision to read. In contrast, VaaT reframes general-purpose
s5051c90147.summary: Researchers propose Vision-as-a-Tool, a framework that gives text-only coding agents visual perception through external tools rather than relying on the model's own vision.
s5051c90147.why: Decoupling perception into tools could help agentic coding systems evaluate generated UI artifacts beyond the base model's vision limits.

s8ea1455284.title: Can Agents Keep Up with Time? An Empirical Analysis of Temporal Adaptation After a Conversational Hiatus
s8ea1455284.description: arXiv:2611.17806v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-horizon agents increasingly serve as persistent personal assistants across modern web platforms, managing schedules, applications, and multi-step plans over weeks or months. Users often return to an ongoing conversation after a long conversational hiatus, while earlier bookings and preparation notes stay on record. During this hiatus, scheduled dates may pass even though the retained records remain unchanged and event outcomes go unrecorded. Existing evaluations of long-horizon agents focus on fact retention and explicit state updates. Whether agents perceive the passage of time and adapt their advice accordingly therefore remains unknown. We frame this ability as temporal state perception and use, which means perceiving the current time
s8ea1455284.summary: An empirical study examines whether long-horizon agents adapt to time passing during a conversational hiatus, when scheduled events lapse but records stay unchanged.
s8ea1455284.why: Persistent assistants that act on stale state after time gaps could make wrong scheduling decisions, so evaluations need time-awareness.

s4a5a2ec223.title: G-CAST: Governed Continual Self-Training for E-Commerce Agents under Evolving Demands
s4a5a2ec223.description: arXiv:2611.17814v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: With the rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs), an increasing number of users are turning to LLM-powered agents for conversational shopping in e-commerce. However, the user needs continue to change as new product categories, procurement scenarios, and feature requests emerge. At the same time, the product's execution harness-including its tools, skills, and operating procedures-continues to evolve to support increasingly sophisticated interactions. These changes create two practical challenges: 1) Demand drift alters the distribution, intent, and complexity of user requests, causing a model trained once to fall behind; 2) Harness evolution requires the model to use newly introduced capabilities correctly without losing behavior th
s4a5a2ec223.summary: Researchers propose G-CAST, a governed continual self-training approach for LLM shopping agents facing shifting user demands and evolving tools.
s4a5a2ec223.why: Production agents whose tools and user needs change over time need governed retraining to avoid drift; the text gives limited detail on results.

sad8f20c1a1.title: Causally Constrained and Uncertainty-Aware Cardiopulmonary Risk Prediction
sad8f20c1a1.description: arXiv:2611.17819v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Routine chest computed tomography (CT) captures pulmonary, cardiac, and vascular phenotypes that jointly stratify lung cancer and cardiovascular disease, the two leading causes of death in lung-screening populations. Yet clinical risk calculators evaluate each disease in isolation and omit CT findings, whereas unconstrained machine learning overfits small hospital cohorts, learns treatment- and illness-confounded risk directions, and conceals uncertainty when patient records are incomplete. Here we present the Causal Envelope Agent (CE-Agent), a two-stage framework that compiles peer-reviewed epidemiological evidence into explicit constraints on risk-factor weights before any outcome is seen, while estimating local baseline risk and newly add
sad8f20c1a1.summary: Researchers present CE-Agent, a causally constrained, uncertainty-aware model that predicts lung cancer and cardiovascular risk from routine chest CT.
sad8f20c1a1.why: Combining CT findings across diseases with uncertainty estimates targets clinical risk tools that currently evaluate each disease separately.

s6a1d2d99b3.title: Aligning AI Teams
s6a1d2d99b3.description: arXiv:2611.17820v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Previous work has shown that alignment training on individual LLM agents can fail to transfer to multi-agent settings. We investigate the underlying mechanisms for this failure, and explore interventions to preserve alignment transfer to multi-agent LLM teams. We focus on two software-engineering tasks (sepsis triage, a news recommender) and ten consulting-proposal generation tasks. We present four findings: (1) The single-vs-team safety gap does not show a clear trend with more capable models. We find that Anthropic's Mythos Preview shows the largest gap on one of our tasks but the smallest on another; (2) Many natural interventions, such as having agents critique each other's work or coordinate in a group chat, do not reliably bring agent t
s6a1d2d99b3.summary: Researchers investigate why safety alignment on individual LLM agents fails to transfer to multi-agent teams and test interventions to preserve it.
s6a1d2d99b3.why: Single-agent safety testing may not carry over to multi-agent deployments, so teams should evaluate safety at the team level.

s46fc01c9e4.title: Is Abliteration Getting Harder? Not Uniformly: Refusal Removal by Direction-Based Ablation and ARA in Heretic on the Qwen3.8, Gemma 4, Olmo 3.1 and Mistral Small 3.2 LLMs Versus Their Predecessors
s46fc01c9e4.description: arXiv:2611.17846v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Abliteration, a fine-tuning-free weight edit, removes refusal from open-weight large language models (LLMs). The developer of Arbitrary-Rank Ablation (ARA), an optimisation-based variant, reports that direction-based abliteration, which ablates a refusal direction, increasingly fails on newer models. On five release pairs, refusal removal did not become uniformly harder. Qwen2.5-32B and Qwen3.8-27B, Gemma-2-27B and Gemma-4-31B, OLMo-2-32B and Olmo-3.1-32B, Mistral-Small-2409 and Mistral-Small-3.2, and Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen3.5-4B were edited in Heretic 2.0 by three or four direction-based methods (difference-in-means, MPOA, SOM and, on the small pair, J-space) and ARA under the same prompts, nominal search budget, first-token KL divergence cap a
s46fc01c9e4.summary: A study tests whether direction-based abliteration and ARA can still remove refusal from newer open-weight LLMs compared with their predecessors.
s46fc01c9e4.why: Results show refusal removal is not uniformly getting harder, relevant for teams assessing safety robustness of open-weight model releases.

s227be0f675.title: DECODE: Diagnosing Interpretability Failures in Automated Interpretation Process
s227be0f675.description: arXiv:2611.17856v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tools for interpreting the internal representations of Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly rely on LLMs themselves to both generate and evaluate explanations, creating a self-referential automated interpretation process with minimal human oversight. This automation raises significant reliability concerns, which are exacerbated by the absence of ground truth. In practice, it is difficult to validate explanations or to attribute interpretability failures to their source -- whether they originate from the tool's extracted representations or from the LLM used in the process. To address these challenges, we present DECODE, a visual analytics system that reintroduces human oversight into the automated interpretation process. Our approach deco
s227be0f675.summary: Researchers present DECODE, a method for diagnosing whether failures in LLM-based automated interpretability stem from extracted representations or from explanation generation.
s227be0f675.why: Self-referential LLM interpretation pipelines without ground truth raise reliability concerns that engineers evaluating such tools need to diagnose.

s66da9e3b2f.title: AI-aided Decision-Making in Education - Uncertainty, Explainability, and Human Responsibility
s66da9e3b2f.description: arXiv:2611.17858v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based systems have become increasingly integrated into various aspects of everyday life, including education, understanding how these systems make decisions is of paramount importance. AI holds significant potential to enhance educational practices through the facilitation of personalized and adaptive learning, automation of assessment procedures, and assistance with administrative tasks. However, the opacity of AI-based decision-making in education (especially with deep learning and generative AI models) can hamper decision-making, especially when outcomes appear unjustified or incorrect. In this chapter, we argue that three key principles (uncertainty, explainability, and human responsibility) are essential f
s66da9e3b2f.summary: A paper examines how AI-aided decision-making in education raises issues of uncertainty, explainability, and human responsibility.

s945d9dd613.title: FlexCast: Flexible Context Learning for Time Series Foundation Models
s945d9dd613.description: arXiv:2611.17862v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Time series foundation models (TSFMs) based on autoregressive (AR) next-token prediction entangle two factors: variable-context conditioning and prediction-unit factorization with autoregressive rollout. Strong AR performance therefore does not reveal whether generalization stems from the flexible training distribution, the local prediction target, the left-to-right inference process, or their combination. We propose FlexCast, a flexible context-target learning framework that disentangles these factors. FlexCast reformulates forecasting as variable-length masked prediction over time series patches: during pretraining, it dynamically samples visible context and masked target patches, exposing the model to diverse context-target configurations
s945d9dd613.summary: Researchers propose FlexCast, a time series foundation model framework that separates variable-context conditioning from autoregressive prediction to clarify sources of generalization.
s945d9dd613.why: Disentangling training and inference factors could guide design choices for time series forecasting models.

s1cf1844e5e.title: OmniScore-Bench: Evaluating Vision-Language Models on Musical Score Reading
s1cf1844e5e.description: arXiv:2611.17870v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) can answer questions about musical scores, but their ability to recognise notation, recover its structure and interpret its musical meaning requires separate evaluation. Existing optical music recognition (OMR) resources establish detection and transcription measurements; a transcription score alone leaves the strengths and bottlenecks of a VLM score reader unresolved. We introduce OmniScore-Bench, an evaluation of OMR capabilities in VLMs through 3,000 questions spanning six aspects and 24 task subtypes. Each question specifies a visible scope, reference annotations and an answer schema, enabling automatic evaluation from symbol localisation to musical consistency and evidence-linked question answering. Our asse
s1cf1844e5e.summary: Researchers introduce OmniScore-Bench, a benchmark of 3,000 questions testing vision-language models on musical score reading across six aspects.
s1cf1844e5e.why: It separates recognition, structure, and meaning in VLM score reading, showing where models fail beyond transcription accuracy.

s2b05f37313.title: Soteria: Formally Verified Planning with Runtime Enforcement for Safe LLM Agents
s2b05f37313.description: arXiv:2611.17880v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents that execute multi-step tool calls must satisfy two objectives simultaneously: completing the user's task (utility) and conforming to domain policies and correctness constraints (safety). These objectives are in tension -- blocking an unsafe action prevents a violation but can leave the agent stranded with no principled way to recover. Existing approaches sacrifice one objective for the other. We introduce Soteria, a framework that reconciles safety and utility through verified hierarchical planning and runtime enforcement of specifications. Before execution, the agent generates a structured plan that is formally verified against the specifications prior to any tool invocation. During execution, the verified plan serves dual roles:
s2b05f37313.summary: Researchers introduce Soteria, a framework combining formally verified hierarchical planning with runtime enforcement to balance task completion and safety for LLM agents.
s2b05f37313.why: It addresses the tension where blocking unsafe tool calls can strand agents, offering a way to keep both utility and policy compliance.

s0f50ae43d6.title: Adversarially Attacking Symbolic Vocabulary Vulnerabilities In LLM Planners
s0f50ae43d6.description: arXiv:2611.17910v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous agents, their abilities in navigating automated planning tasks have become essential. However, despite their strengths, LLMs' planning ability is not robust, particularly when they are not allowed to exploit commonsense cues in the symbolic vocabulary (e.g., names of actions, predicates, and objects) used to define planning tasks. This makes LLMs unreliable compared to symbolic planners. With recent reasoning models showing improved planning performance on tasks with obfuscated symbolic vocabularies, we utilize an adversarial attack framework to reveal to what extent the crucial weaknesses of LLM agents at joint symbolic interpretation and planning remain and whether they
s0f50ae43d6.summary: Researchers show adversarial changes to symbolic vocabulary can expose weaknesses in LLM planners that lack commonsense cues.
s0f50ae43d6.why: LLM planners that depend on naming cues may be unreliable under obfuscated task definitions, which matters for agent deployments.

s314482901f.title: SWIFT: Sample-Wise Instance Fine-Tuning of Time-Series Foundation Models for Forecasting
s314482901f.description: arXiv:2611.17915v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While current few-shot adaptation strategies for time series forecasting foundation models are predominantly dataset-centric, the necessity of obtaining an additional dataset for the finetuning process poses a significant hurdle for adoption. To address this constraint, we propose Sample-Wise Instance Fine-Tuning (SWIFT), a novel forecasting adaptation framework that achieves fine-grained specialization by leveraging structural priors from the target instance's own history. This shift allows the fine-tuning process to be entirely transparent to the end-user, which significantly enhances the ease of adoption. To implement this framework, SWIFT synergizes Self-Retrieval for historical mining and Frequency-Aware Loss for spectral consistency, wh
s314482901f.summary: SWIFT proposes sample-wise instance fine-tuning that adapts time-series forecasting foundation models using each target instance's own history, without needing an extra dataset.
s314482901f.why: It removes the need for an additional fine-tuning dataset, a practical hurdle for adopting forecasting foundation models.

s0cd4573f42.title: When Cooperation Must Change: Semantic Strategy Unlearning in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
s0cd4573f42.description: arXiv:2611.17917v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) supports coordinated decision-making in distributed Web services, multi-robot control, and collaborative games through learned coordination conventions. When deployment requirements change, a previously useful convention may become obsolete or unsafe. For example, revised cache-sharing permissions in Web content delivery may require caches to abandon a learned division of storage and serving roles while maintaining efficient delivery. Teams must therefore remove the specified convention while preserving useful cooperation. This is challenging because the same relational pattern can be reproduced by different agents across different histories. Runtime shielding leaves the underlying coordin
s0cd4573f42.summary: Researchers propose semantic strategy unlearning for cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning, so teams can drop a learned coordination convention when deployment requirements change.
s0cd4573f42.why: Learned multi-agent conventions can become obsolete or unsafe after requirement changes, and this offers a way to remove them.

sfff7d19619.title: RecMem: Recurrent Memory Compression for Long-Sequence Generative Recommendation
sfff7d19619.description: arXiv:2611.17921v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative recommendation benefits from long interaction histories, but the cost of processing them directly grows with history length. We propose RecMem, a recurrent memory compression framework guided by three desiderata: space invariance, semantic fidelity, and lifelong evolvability. RecMem compresses historical segments into a fixed set of memory slots using a bifurcated encoder-decoder with shared lower layers and slot-wise forget-gated updates. Recommendation supervision trains the memory to preserve predictive information, while stream-consistency training aligns predictions from sequential and packed processing. By construction, the memory state and decoder context are independent of history length; under contraction and approximate s
sfff7d19619.summary: RecMem compresses long user interaction histories into fixed memory slots using recurrent memory, aiming to make generative recommendation over long sequences cheaper.
sfff7d19619.why: Processing cost in generative recommenders grows with history length, so fixed-size memory compression could cut serving costs.

sa0a9244e62.title: What Balanced Accuracy Cannot Identify in Neural-Signal Decoding under Test-Time Adaptation
sa0a9244e62.description: arXiv:2611.17925v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adaptation for neural-signal classification is usually transductive: each batch is scored after updating on it, and the gain depends on the adapted model [4]. This paper asks what an aggregate change fails to characterise inside the cohort. Full test-time adaptation (full_ttt) was evaluated in 11 dataset-encoder cells (four each on Siena/EEG and PTB-XL/ECG, three on Sleep-EDF/EEG), with splits and source-model evaluation fixed; the subject was the unit, exact sign tests were Holm-corrected and conditional on the shared stream, and bootstrap intervals accompanied a dependence audit. Two results of different kinds follow. In the binary case balanced accuracy gives a one-class decoder the same value as one reporting both classes at 50%, so the a
sa0a9244e62.summary: A paper examines how balanced accuracy and aggregate metrics can miss subject-level effects when test-time adaptation is applied to neural-signal decoding across EEG and ECG datasets.
sa0a9244e62.why: Aggregate metrics can hide per-subject behavior changes, which matters when evaluating adaptive models on medical signal data.

sd9646e5b1b.title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Scientific Paper Search: Retrieval Success and Inference Latency on Mac Studio and NVIDIA A100
sd9646e5b1b.description: arXiv:2611.17929v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scientific literature search can benefit from locally deployed LLM assistants, which reduce reliance on hosted model providers while giving research teams greater control over their data and infrastructure. This work investigates whether open-weight models can support web-assisted paper retrieval under practical computing constraints. We first characterize inference latency as the input context grows from 512 to 128k tokens on a Mac Studio and a server equipped with two NVIDIA A100 GPUs. We then evaluate eight models on the retrieval of 70 papers from seven scientific repositories, using queries that represent three levels of domain knowledge. The results show that retrieval success depends strongly on the selected model and the specificity o
sd9646e5b1b.summary: The study measures latency and paper-retrieval success for eight open-weight LLMs on a Mac Studio and a two-A100 server, with context lengths up to 128k tokens.
sd9646e5b1b.why: It gives concrete latency and retrieval tradeoffs for running local LLM research assistants instead of hosted APIs.

scfd93a0534.title: OutfitterBench: Evaluating LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Resource Allocation and Commitment Coordination
scfd93a0534.description: arXiv:2611.17933v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In many long-horizon settings, an agent's own choices create future constraints: committing finite capacity establishes future obligations and forecloses later opportunities. Sustaining performance therefore requires both keeping evolving plans feasible and comparing the value of resource allocations with the alternatives they displace. Recent benchmarks increasingly evaluate LLM agents in continuing operations, but give less attention to how agents keep their own commitments feasible while reassessing resource allocations as opportunities change. We introduce OutfitterBench, where agents manage an outdoor-equipment rental business for 200 days, purchasing from a 46-product catalog and handling roughly 1,100 reservation requests. Under a fixe
scfd93a0534.summary: OutfitterBench is a benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on long-horizon resource allocation and keeping their own commitments feasible as opportunities change.
scfd93a0534.why: It targets agent failures in sustained operations, such as overcommitting capacity, that short-horizon benchmarks miss.

s3907b6ae38.title: Tracing Actual Causes with Counterfactual Witness Maps
s3907b6ae38.description: arXiv:2611.17937v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Halpernian actual causation, the formal study of which events in a specific situation caused a specific outcome in acyclic structural causal models, underpins legal responsibility, moral blame, and the assessment of causal harm. Despite the rich logical framework, no prior sound and complete enumeration procedure is known for finding all actual causes in a given setting, blocking downstream tasks such as responsibility attribution, blame assessment, and causal-harm grading that aggregate over the full cause set. We close this gap by introducing witness targets: sets of joint configurations containing every counterfactual witness. In combination with an ancestor intervention grammar we derive a finite directed acyclic witness map. We prove tha
s3907b6ae38.summary: The paper introduces counterfactual witness maps, a sound and complete enumeration procedure for finding all Halpernian actual causes in acyclic structural causal models.
s3907b6ae38.why: Complete cause enumeration is a prerequisite for downstream responsibility and blame assessment, though the work is theoretical.

se05dbc4d35.title: Measured from the feed: the unsustainable growth of AI video generation
se05dbc4d35.description: arXiv:2611.17938v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Text-to-video generation runs at commercial scale, but its broader environmental impacts remain, to our knowledge, understudied. Providers rarely disclose video volumes or energy needs; we measured the yearly video output of two commercial platforms and built a prospective model of such services' absolute footprint from training to storage. Our projections suggest that reducing emissions depends on both limiting growth in video generation and achieving substantial efficiency gains. Under continued growth, emissions rise nearly seventy-five-fold by 2030 despite technological improvements. When usage remains at 2026 levels, the same improvements reduce emissions by about two-fifths. These estimates are a conservative lower bound: they cover one
se05dbc4d35.summary: The authors measured yearly video output of two commercial text-to-video platforms and project that emissions could rise nearly seventy-five-fold under continued growth.
se05dbc4d35.why: Engineering and leadership teams deploying generative video should weigh energy growth against efficiency gains.

s6cb799c6ee.title: Toward Interference-Agnostic RF Source Separation
s6cb799c6ee.description: arXiv:2611.17950v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Separating a radio-frequency signal of interest from a co-channel interference is mostly addressed with specialized separators, each trained for one pair of signal and interference types and therefore relying on a label that a heavily jammed receiver cannot identify. We show that this reliance is not benign: applied to an interference it was not trained on, such a separator usually fails to recover the signal, and in most of the cases we measure it leaves the signal worse than no processing at all. We then train a single separator over every pair, giving it no indication at test time of which one it faces, on two architectures with no component in common: the convolutional WaveNet of the ICASSP 2024 RF Challenge, and a band-split transformer
s6cb799c6ee.summary: Researchers train a single RF source separator across many signal and interference pairs, rather than one specialized separator per pair, to handle unseen interference.
s6cb799c6ee.why: Specialized separators often fail on unseen interference, so a generalist separator addresses a real limitation for jammed receivers.

s08476d33ae.title: The Transformer Paradigm: Dynamic Processing and a New Principle of Inference
s08476d33ae.description: arXiv:2611.17953v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We argue that the Transformer revolution is not adequately understood as a merely quantitative expansion of deep learning, but as the emergence of a new paradigm based on a different principle of inference. We interpret the Transformer as a system in which token representations are transformed by parameterized transformations, or transforming concepts. During inference, some of these transformations are dynamically constructed from the current input: previously acquired transformations are first adapted and then applied. At the mechanical-structural level, this dynamic processing is realized through output-weight interconnections, whereby outputs of some networks determine the weights of others. The resulting mode of processing, which we call
s08476d33ae.summary: A theoretical paper argues the Transformer represents a new inference paradigm in which some transformations are dynamically constructed from the current input.

s7e9a74ca3f.title: WebArena-Pro: A Heterogeneous, Multimodal, Reproducible Benchmark for Web Agents
s7e9a74ca3f.description: arXiv:2611.17955v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Web agents powered by large language and vision-language models are increasingly applied to realistic browser work that spans heterogeneous applications, multimodal content, and stateful workflows. However, existing reproducible web-agent benchmarks cover only a small number of web applications drawn from a few software categories, and restrict modality to text and vision. Live benchmarks broaden site coverage but sacrifice reproducibility, since pages and data drift between runs. Moreover, existing benchmarks do not meaningfully evaluate whether agents can understand and use audio and video content embedded within web tasks. To address these gaps, we introduce WebArena-Pro, a benchmark comprising 300 tasks across 20 self-hosted web applicati
s7e9a74ca3f.summary: WebArena-Pro is a reproducible benchmark for web agents spanning more heterogeneous applications, multimodal content, and stateful workflows than prior benchmarks.
s7e9a74ca3f.why: Broader and reproducible web-agent evaluation helps teams compare agents on realistic multi-app browser work.

s2085e6546a.title: TotalSegmentator Aorta Report: Automated Aortic Diameter Measurement at 11 Standardized Landmarks on CT Images
s2085e6546a.description: arXiv:2611.17968v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Purpose: To develop and evaluate a fully automated, open-source tool that measures aortic diameters at 11 standardized landmarks from the aortic annulus to the bifurcation on any CT image, following current guideline recommendations. Materials and Methods: This retrospective single-center study included 239 arterial phase CT angiography examinations of 230 patients (median age, 65 years [range, 18-99 years]; 163 men) performed between April 2025 and October 2026 (209 electrocardiographically [ECG] gated). The tool locates landmarks from TotalSegmentator segmentations of aortic branches and vertebrae and measures the maximum diameter at each. A senior radiologist reviewed and, where needed, corrected the automated measurements to create the re
s2085e6546a.summary: An open-source tool automatically measures aortic diameters at 11 standardized landmarks on CT angiography, evaluated on 239 examinations from a single center.
s2085e6546a.why: An open-source automated measurement tool could standardize aortic reporting in clinical imaging pipelines.

sc677cf2b3d.title: Interactive deep-learning based interface for brain tumour segmentation
sc677cf2b3d.description: arXiv:2611.17983v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Brain tumour segmentation from MR images is an integral part of their treatment, either through surgical resection or radiotherapy. Both applications require a high degree of precision that can be difficult to ensure for all patients due to the high degree of variability in the size, shape, number, and location of these tumours. This leads to difficulties with their automatic segmentation via deep learning, which can display catastrophic segmentation errors when presented with images that differ, even subtly, in terms of the specific MR sequence used, which varies from vendor to vendor. This article presents a deep-learning-based interactive segmentation system that, while being fully automatic by default, has the capability of being easily c
sc677cf2b3d.summary: An interactive deep-learning interface for brain tumour segmentation from MR images is presented, aimed at reducing catastrophic errors on varied MR sequences.

s7e61a7e121.title: LACCO: Local Accumulation with Computation--Communication Overlap
s7e61a7e121.description: arXiv:2611.17991v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Training language models across low-bandwidth networks requires reducing synchronization overhead. Local optimization methods such as DiLoCo communicate only after several local steps, but outer gradient averaging and the outer update remain on the critical path. Existing computation-communication overlap methods avoid this stall through delayed or replica-local updates, which can degrade convergence or cause replicas to drift. We propose LACCO (Local Accumulation with Computation-Communication Overlap), a two-stage algorithm that overlaps global communication with local computation while applying globally aggregated updates shared by every replica, without introducing staleness in the outer update. We establish convergence guarantees for smo
s7e61a7e121.summary: LACCO is a two-stage algorithm that overlaps global gradient communication with computation for training language models over low-bandwidth networks.
s7e61a7e121.why: Reducing synchronization stalls in low-bandwidth distributed training could lower cost for teams training across slow networks.

s414ab39890.title: Understanding the limits of snapshot-based fault diagnosis in distribution networks
s414ab39890.description: arXiv:2611.17998v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inverter-based resources weaken fault currents in distribution networks, and snapshot-based diagnosis, which classifies a fault from voltage phasors at a few buses at one instant, offers a cheap first-stage screen. Its published accuracies, however, rest on different noise assumptions and do not show whether the error comes from the classifier, the features, the measurement error, or the fault resistance. This paper separates these sources on three IEEE test feeders and a public data set with distributed generation, using four feature sets, thirteen classifiers, and measurement error defined by total vector error classes. The classifier is not the limiting factor, because the full phasor snapshot classifies every fault correctly without noise
s414ab39890.summary: The paper separates error sources in snapshot-based fault diagnosis on distribution networks, testing three IEEE feeders and a public dataset with distributed generation.
s414ab39890.why: Shows which factors limit fault classifier accuracy, informing when cheap snapshot-based screening can be trusted in grid operations.

s7b82a6cbf6.title: A$^3$: Adaptive Audio Agent Framework for Collaborative Edge Computing
s7b82a6cbf6.description: arXiv:2611.18064v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Embedded audio agents need a nearby edge server for speed, but a server-dependent agent returns nothing when the link fails. We present A$^3$, an adaptive audio agent framework that places whole pipeline stages on the server, keeps a complete fallback agent on devices that can host one, and hedges both paths with a link-aware deadline that decides when to give up on the server. On Jetson devices and an RTX A4500 server, A$^3$ matches the server-only agent on a healthy link, answers every request in a full outage on the AGX, and beats a percentile hedge in simulated outages.
s7b82a6cbf6.summary: Researchers propose A$^3$, an adaptive audio agent framework that splits pipeline stages between edge devices and a server, with a complete on-device fallback.
s7b82a6cbf6.why: It shows how to keep embedded voice agents responsive and working during network outages, relevant to edge AI system design.

sb44bf45e50.title: Two-Clustering Regime of Token Dynamics in Causal Attention
sb44bf45e50.description: arXiv:2611.18088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We partially resolve Conjecture 1 of [Karagodin et al., Clustering in Causal Attention Masking (NeurIPS 2024)] and extend it to time-dependent parameter regimes. The conjecture predicts that causal attention dynamics converge to two clusters aligned with the eigenvectors associated with the largest eigenvalue $\lambda_{\max}$ of the value transformation. We prove that this behavior holds when $\lambda_{\max}>0$ and is generally false when $\lambda_{\max}\le0$. The resulting two-cluster regime is common in practice and substantially more challenging than the classical single-cluster setting studied previously. A central contribution of our work is the identification of a rigorous dimension reduction phenomenon: despite evolving in a high-dimen
sb44bf45e50.summary: A paper proves that causal attention token dynamics converge to two clusters when the largest eigenvalue of the value transformation is positive, and shows the conjecture fails otherwise.

s5bebf121cc.title: Do Machines Learn Deviance From Their Peers? A Randomized Test of Differential Association With AI Agents
s5bebf121cc.description: arXiv:2611.18098v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Differential association theory and its extension, social learning theory, hold that rule-breaking, and the definitions that make it acceptable, are learned through interaction with others. Because people choose their friends, this claim has been hard to test. We addressed this selection problem with AI agents, which learn only through communication and can be assigned to peers at random. In a preregistered experiment, 420 teams of three agents (1,260 agents; seven AI models) worked on coding tasks that could not be solved honestly. A scripted teammate said that it had cheated (deviant peer), that it had reported the problem honestly (honest peer), or said nothing (silent peer). Half of the teams were told that an auditor read their chat. Com
s5bebf121cc.summary: A preregistered experiment with 420 teams of three AI agents tested whether agents learn rule-breaking behavior from peers via randomized assignment.

s17441cda69.title: Optimizing Drilling Trajectories in Multi-Material Structures Using Quantum Annealers
s17441cda69.description: arXiv:2611.18121v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work we present a quantum-hybrid optimization approach for planning drilling trajectories on multi-material structures, with the objective of minimizing total energy consumption. The proposed formulation models the drilling process as a constrained routing problem in which each hole must be visited while accounting for heterogeneous material properties, material-dependent drilling costs and displacement energy, as well as tool-wear penalties. Our method incorporates realistic industrial constraints, including open-path routing and mandatory grouping of holes belonging to the same material to avoid frequent tool-bit changes. The modeled problem is solved using D-Wave's Leap Constrained Quadratic Model Hybrid Solver. To evaluate perform
s17441cda69.summary: Researchers present a quantum-hybrid optimization approach for planning drilling trajectories on multi-material structures to minimize total energy consumption.

s87a0c17225.title: JFinBench: A Continuously Refreshable Japanese Financial Benchmark from the Latest Certification Exams
s87a0c17225.description: arXiv:2611.18130v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to finance, creating a need for benchmarks that evaluate their capabilities across financial systems with different regulations and practices. However, existing financial benchmarks provide limited coverage of country-specific financial systems, and they are difficult to keep up to date as released questions leak into training data. We introduce JFinBench, a Japanese financial benchmark comprising 321 examples from the 2026 editions of six regularly administered certification exams covering accounting, tax, financial planning, and banking. To construct it, we develop a human-in-the-loop agentic pipeline in which a coding agent writes exam-specific conversion code and a review page, while a
s87a0c17225.summary: JFinBench is introduced as a Japanese financial benchmark of 321 examples from 2026 certification exams, designed to be continuously refreshed.
s87a0c17225.why: Engineers evaluating LLMs for finance in Japan get a country-specific, regularly updatable test set that reduces training-data leakage risk.

sb29cabb887.title: Large Language Model-Empowered Intelligent Agent for Adaptive Fast-Charging Control of Lithium-Ion Batteries
sb29cabb887.description: arXiv:2611.18140v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fast charging of lithium-ion batteries is a multi-objective control problem that requires reducing charging time and sustaining high energy throughput while suppressing accelerated degradation and safety-critical electrochemical reactions. Conventional protocols are easy to implement but have limited ability to adapt to variations in battery chemistry, operating conditions, and aging state. Model-based optimization and conventional data-driven control often require accurate models, costly iterative search, or task-specific policies. We develop a large language model (LLM)-empowered intelligent agent for adaptive battery fast-charging control. In this closed-loop framework, the agent interprets structured battery states, generates executable c
sb29cabb887.summary: Researchers develop a large language model-based intelligent agent for adaptive fast-charging control of lithium-ion batteries.

s6b1fb627dd.title: Probabilities of Causation in Nondeterministic Causal Models
s6b1fb627dd.description: arXiv:2611.18245v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study probabilities of causation in nondeterministic causal models, where mechanisms may remain intrinsically stochastic even after all latent variables are fixed.
