Focusing on binary treatments and outcomes, we develop a generic identification program that represents observational and interventional data as moment constraints on latent stochastic mechanism types and computes minimal/maximal values of counterfactual quantities via constrained optimization. Within this framework, we derive sharp analytic bounds on the probabilities of causation under several assumptions tailored to nondeterministic models. Resulting identification regions are often more informative than those attainable under deterministic alternatives. We illustrate the pra
s6b1fb627dd.summary: The paper derives sharp analytic bounds on probabilities of causation in nondeterministic causal models with binary treatments and outcomes.

s3e38f9f5d4.title: Dancing Tokens on the Vocabulary Network from LLM Generation
s3e38f9f5d4.description: arXiv:2611.18248v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) generate text one token at a time, yet how a particular generation relates to the geometry learned in pre-training remains unclear. The fundamental explainability of LLMs is elusive. Here, we build a similarity network from the input embeddings of six open LLMs and map generation onto it. The token-embedding network is scale-free while heavy-tailed, as are random embeddings with matched covariance, but far more fragmented. Distillation barely changes this topology because input embeddings are largely inherited. The knowledge space is thus deterministic from pre-training. Consecutive generated tokens are rarely graph neighbours and, in most models, no more often than in shuffled order, so generation is not a walk o
s3e38f9f5d4.summary: Researchers map LLM token generation onto a similarity network built from input embeddings of six open LLMs, finding a scale-free but fragmented topology.

sc8e7bfccd8.title: When evaluation becomes intervention in clinical AI
sc8e7bfccd8.description: arXiv:2611.18297v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI judges, models that grade another system's output against a rubric, extend clinical review to the scale at which clinical AI writes. When teams use judge assessments to select a prompt or train a model, the judge becomes part of the intervention. Selection can then favor errors the judge overlooks. We describe what a judge's report must contain and the independent clinical test each judge-driven change needs.
sc8e7bfccd8.summary: The article argues that using AI judges to select prompts or train clinical AI models turns evaluation into intervention, and calls for independent clinical testing.
sc8e7bfccd8.why: Teams using LLM-as-judge to tune clinical systems risk optimizing for errors the judge misses, so independent validation is needed.

s935711d9b1.title: Experts Across Schemas: Agent-Guided Mixture-of-Relational-Experts for Cross-Database Generalization
s935711d9b1.description: arXiv:2611.18315v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Web platforms record user and item activity in relational databases whose schemas differ from platform to platform, which makes it difficult to transfer predictive models between them. Relational foundation models address this through cross-database pretraining, yet recent improvements have relied on increasingly large pretraining corpora. We ask whether a better architecture, together with features specific to the target database, can deliver comparable gains from far less pretraining data. We introduce MoREGT, a mixture-of-relational-experts graph transformer that represents both rows and cells as tokens, adds the log-ages of rows and the names of foreign-key relationships to attention, and routes cells and rows to experts by column metadat
s935711d9b1.summary: The paper introduces MoREGT, a mixture-of-relational-experts model for cross-database generalization that aims to match gains from large pretraining with less data.

s896bd046e0.title: Causal AI-Driven Secure mmWave Beam Alignment with Defensive Variational Autoencoders
s896bd046e0.description: arXiv:2611.18321v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Efficient and secure beam alignment is essential for mmWave communication systems. However, existing deep learning (DL)-based beam alignment methods often neglect causal relationships between inputs and outputs, resulting in limited interpretability, poor generalization, and excessive beam sweeping. Moreover, these DL solutions are vulnerable to adversarial attacks, where small perturbations in received power measurements can mislead beam classifiers. To overcome these issues, we propose a causally-aware DL framework integrating causal discovery into beam alignment. A two-stage causal beam selection algorithm learns a Bayesian graph capturing dependencies between received signal strength indicators (RSSI) as inputs and the optimal beam index
s896bd046e0.summary: Researchers propose a causally-aware deep learning framework with defensive variational autoencoders for secure mmWave beam alignment resistant to adversarial perturbations.

sfeee23b9a7.title: VLAN: Vision-Language Accessible Navigation
sfeee23b9a7.description: arXiv:2611.18346v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accessible mobility is user-conditioned rather than scene-intrinsic, as walkable paths for one embodiment are inaccessible to another. Yet, existing benchmarks evaluate traversability under a fixed and limited embodiment. We present Vision-Language Accessible Navigation (VLAN), containing 1,000 scenes, 20K navigation trajectories, and 160K keyframes across diverse lighting, environmental conditions, scene semantics, and path geometries. For each trajectory, VLAN provides embodiment-specific actions and accessibility features for legged and wheeled agents, including humanoid and quadruped robots and people with visual or mobility impairments, while everyday obstacles and accessibility labels are categorized as Passable, Bypass, HighRisk, and B
sfeee23b9a7.summary: VLAN is a vision-language navigation benchmark with 1,000 scenes and 20K trajectories, providing embodiment-specific accessibility labels for legged and wheeled robots.

sfa2ff8e70f.title: VelServe: Taming Decode Jitters in LLM Inference with Tail-Calibrated Scheduling
sfa2ff8e70f.description: arXiv:2611.18392v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interactive LLM services must meet latency service-level objectives (SLOs) for the time to first token (TTFT) and the time between tokens (TBT), as streaming and soft real-time applications require predictable token delivery. We identify decode jitters in both aggregated and disaggregated serving. A jitter delays every request in the batch, and long responses span hundreds of steps, so even rare overruns cause many SLO violations. In aggregated serving, SLO-aware schedulers set each step's prefill budget until its predicted latency just meets the TBT target, leaving no room for mispredictions or host stalls. Disaggregation meets average TBT targets at a cost in capacity, yet the steps that admit new requests still run late. We present \sysnam
sfa2ff8e70f.summary: VelServe proposes tail-calibrated scheduling to reduce decode jitter in LLM inference and meet time-between-tokens latency SLOs in serving systems.
sfa2ff8e70f.why: Decode jitter causes many SLO violations in long streaming responses, so tail-aware scheduling directly affects serving reliability.

saac4fe7a77.title: Smart Home Agents Make Capable but Unpredictable Grid Operators
saac4fe7a77.description: arXiv:2611.18395v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI-enabled smart homes are becoming more common across the grid edge. However, there has not been much work on failure response. This area is critical because smart homes operate on the grid edge where failures can cascade down. If a power outage happens within a smart home, a user has to manually troubleshoot their smart home to include tasks such as power load balance and device recovery. We conduct the first resilience analysis of smart home agents across a full power outage, providing a suite of outage simulations in a live environment that measures resilience before, during, and post power outage. We show that smart home agents can act as grid operators in power outages and identify several new failure categories highlighting the current
saac4fe7a77.summary: A resilience analysis of smart home agents across simulated full power outages finds they are capable but behave unpredictably as grid operators.

saec85571de.title: LECAT: Measuring LLM Category Learning from Pretraining Data
saec85571de.description: arXiv:2611.18419v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Humans know that airplanes are fast, that this extends to red airplanes, but that it does not hold for broken airplanes. How do LLMs acquire category knowledge that humans learn and apply effortlessly? We introduce LeCat, a two-part framework to analyze LLM's Learning of Category knowledge. First, we use LeCat to evaluate models on their ability to learn category knowledge, distinguishing between three cases: memorization of in-domain category knowledge, generalization to unseen instances, and ability to flexibly use knowledge in appropriate contexts. Then, we use LeCat to trace how this knowledge can be learned in pretraining from text that may encode category knowledge in various ways, such as verbatim repetition or exceptions, which we ref
saec85571de.summary: LeCat is a two-part framework that measures how LLMs learn category knowledge from pretraining data, covering memorization, generalization, and flexible use.

se1d605aef1.title: Towards Explainable Sleep Stage Classification using Single-Channel Electroencephalogram
se1d605aef1.description: arXiv:2611.18434v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automated sleep staging has achieved strong bench- mark accuracy; however, clinical adoption remains limited due to a lack of interpretability. In this work, we fill the research gap by extending the SleepXAI sleep staging framework to systematically compare five different XAI methods. Further, attribution fidelity is evaluated using Spearman rank correlation with AASM-defined EEG frequency bands, serving as clinically grounded reference signals. In this paper, we focus on single- channel Electroencephalogram (EEG), which is more amenable to practical clinical deployment compared to full polysomnography setups. Experiments are conducted on the Sleep-EDF benchmark dataset and the DREAMT dataset. In DREAMT, we stratified subjects based on OSA i
se1d605aef1.summary: Researchers extend the SleepXAI framework to compare five explainability methods for single-channel EEG sleep staging, checking attributions against AASM frequency bands.
se1d605aef1.why: Interpretable sleep staging could ease clinical adoption of automated models, though the text gives limited detail on results.

s0effe99313.title: When to Trust Simulated Patient Responses:Support-Gated World Models for Vasopressor Decision Support
s0effe99313.description: arXiv:2611.18458v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Clinical world models expose language-model agents to predicted patient responses, but simulations can be unreliable for poorly supported treatments or unfamiliar hospitals. We introduce Support-Gated World-Model decision support, a lightweight extension of a propose--simulate--refine agent. A recurrent dynamics ensemble predicts short-horizon physiological responses to documented norepinephrine dose categories, while a behavior model estimates observational action support. The interface withholds predictions with insufficient support or excessive ensemble disagreement and abstains when no candidate qualifies. Evaluation on eICU-CRD includes 70 hospitals and 30,700 decision transitions, with 14 hospitals held out for testing. At 62.0% factual
s0effe99313.summary: Researchers propose Support-Gated World-Model decision support, which withholds simulated patient responses to vasopressor doses when the data gives insufficient support.
s0effe99313.why: It shows a way for LLM agents to flag unreliable simulations in high-stakes settings instead of acting on them unchecked.

s83c5ff0c11.title: Typing Matters: Muscle, Language and Typing Behaviour in Live Keystroke Decoding from sEMG
s83c5ff0c11.description: arXiv:2611.18464v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Surface electromyography (sEMG) from the wrists can recover typed text without a keyboard. It is usually posed as a signal-inference problem: characters are read out of the muscle signal and character error rate is reported offline. We argue that this framing removes most of the problem. The decoder is constrained simultaneously by the muscles, by the language being typed, and by typing behaviour such as typos, corrections, backspaces and line breaks, and a usable system must predict keys live while the hand keeps moving. Existing systems fall short on two counts: (1) they process sEMG in fixed windows and carry nothing from one window to the next, discarding context accumulated over a session, and (2) they lack any understanding of the lingu
s83c5ff0c11.summary: Researchers frame wrist sEMG keystroke decoding as a live problem constrained by muscle signals, language, and typing behaviour, not only offline character error rate.
s83c5ff0c11.why: Treating typing behaviour and language as constraints may matter for building usable real-time neural input interfaces.

sa5b6601e31.title: ARCHER: From Rationale Imitation to Executable Reasoning in Small Language Models
sa5b6601e31.description: arXiv:2611.18494v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Small language models are attractive for local, low-cost, and privacy-sensitive deployment, but they remain unreliable on mathematical reasoning tasks that require decomposition, exact computation, tool use, and verification. We introduce \textbf{ARCHER}: \textbf{A}ction-trace \textbf{R}einforcement for \textbf{C}alculator-grounded \textbf{H}ierarchical \textbf{E}xecutable \textbf{R}easoning, a two-stage framework for training small language models (SLMs) to produce executable and auditable reasoning trajectories. In the first stage, ARCHER compiles free-form chain-of-thought rationales into typed action traces containing reasoning steps, calculator calls, deterministic runtime observations, verification actions, and final answers. This shift
sa5b6601e31.summary: ARCHER is a two-stage training framework that teaches small language models to produce executable, calculator-grounded reasoning traces for math tasks.
sa5b6601e31.why: Executable, auditable reasoning could make small local models more reliable for math-heavy tasks where privacy or cost rules out large hosted models.

s661c8f9be9.title: Can Mechanistic Interpretability Help Explain LLM Agent Failures? A Case Study on Web Element Hallucination
s661c8f9be9.description: arXiv:2611.18514v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mechanistic Interpretability (MI) has made significant progress in explaining the internal computations of Large Language Models (LLMs); however, these advances have yet to demonstrate comparable success in explaining the decision-making processes of LLM-based agents. This paper examines the challenges MI tools face when applied to realistic agentic failures. We focus on one such failure: web agents hallucinating actions that are not available on a website. We apply a series of mechanistic analyzes to Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as it interacts with live websites. We find that a linear probe trained on the last prompt token can predict hallucinations before generation begins (0.80 AUC) and steering along a probe direction corrects 85\% of hallucinati
s661c8f9be9.summary: A case study applies mechanistic interpretability to Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct to explain why web agents hallucinate actions unavailable on a live website.
s661c8f9be9.why: It tests whether interpretability tools can diagnose real agent failures, a gap engineers debugging web agents would care about.

s33873f048a.title: Alignment by Socialization: Learning Tradeoffs Under Selection
s33873f048a.description: arXiv:2611.18531v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are expected to complete tasks while following rules of conduct, but these objectives can conflict. We study how evolutionary selection shapes an agent's choices between them, and whether experience can make those choices reflect human judgments and withstand subsequent pressures. In our model, copies of an agent face a common uncertain reward state, and only those taking the rewarded action reproduce. We show that long-run growth is maximized when each action is taken as often as the environment rewards it. We compare three policies. A task-only policy thrives in a sandbox rewarding completion alone but fails when conduct matters. A fixed linear policy increasingly favors task completion as its stakes rise
s33873f048a.summary: A theoretical study models how evolutionary selection shapes AI agents' tradeoffs between task completion and rules of conduct, and whether experience aligns choices with human judgments.
s33873f048a.why: The text is theoretical and gives little concrete guidance for engineers building agents today.

s1c7b50d396.title: ModHarness-RL: Recasting Harnesses as Learnable and Evolving Programs for Agentic RL
s1c7b50d396.description: arXiv:2611.18533v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agentic reinforcement learning (RL) increasingly relies on a harness, the scaffold around the model that decides what it sees of its own interaction and what guidance it receives. Most existing approaches train under a hand-written harness that stays fixed throughout. However, an effective harness depends on the domain, the data and the model, and keeps changing as the model trains. We introduce ModHarness-RL, which recasts the harness as programs that are learned from data and evolve as the model trains with RL. ModHarness-RL records the interaction as structured State, a set of typed blocks, and two core components of the harness are programs over these blocks, a Compression program that assembles the accumulated history into the model's co
s1c7b50d396.summary: ModHarness-RL treats the agent harness, the scaffold deciding what the model sees and receives, as learnable programs that evolve during agentic reinforcement learning.
s1c7b50d396.why: Learned, evolving harnesses could replace hand-written scaffolds that stay fixed during agent RL training.

s8e1f110b13.title: HARDTESTGEN: A High-Quality RL Verifier Generation Pipeline for LLM Algorithmic Coding
s8e1f110b13.description: arXiv:2505.24098v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Verifiers provide important reward signals for reinforcement learning of large language models (LLMs). However, it is challenging to develop or create reliable verifiers, especially for code generation tasks. A well-disguised wrong solution program may only be detected by carefully human-written edge cases that are difficult to synthesize automatically. To address this issue, we propose HARDTESTGEN, an approach to synthesize high-quality test cases for algorithmic coding problems. We curate a comprehensive algorithmic programming dataset HARDTESTS with 26.6k problems and high-quality synthetic tests. Compared with existing tests, HARDTESTGEN tests demonstrate significantly higher accuracy in verifying LLM-generated code (+11.22 percentage p
s8e1f110b13.summary: HARDTESTGEN is a pipeline that synthesizes high-quality test cases to build reliable reward verifiers for reinforcement learning on algorithmic coding problems.
s8e1f110b13.why: Stronger verifiers reduce reward hacking from wrong code that passes weak tests, which matters for training code-generation models.

s794963e7ea.title: PhysDox: Benchmarking LLMs on Physical Feasibility Auditing of Physiological Sensing Protocols
s794963e7ea.description: arXiv:2606.05003v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly assist in experimental design, yet fluent protocols often remain physically infeasible. We introduce PhysDox, a physical feasibility auditing benchmark for biomedical protocols comprising a 683-sample expert-curated Gold set and a 5,000-sample Silver set across six sensing domains. We formulate the task as a two-stage evaluation: severity detection classifying protocols as valid, minor, or fatal, followed by the constraint-level diagnosis of fatal violations. Evaluating 6 LLMs across 4 inference strategies yields a peak Stage-1 macro-F1 of only 53.0. Moreover, strong oracle diagnosis collapses during end-to-end evaluation due to correlated cascade errors. Error analysis reveals scaffold bias, where
s794963e7ea.summary: PhysDox is a benchmark testing whether LLMs can audit physiological sensing protocols for physical feasibility, classifying severity and diagnosing fatal constraint violations.
s794963e7ea.why: It shows LLM-generated experimental protocols can be fluent yet physically infeasible, a risk for teams using LLMs in lab design.

sf838d531d9.title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Sequence Models for Sample-Efficient Energy Regression in Simulated Calorimeter Showers
sf838d531d9.description: arXiv:2611.17354v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Energy reconstruction from electromagnetic calorimeter data underpins particle identification, event reconstruction and precision measurements in high-energy physics. Machine learning already performs well on this task, yet two questions remain open: how much the choice of data representation matters, and whether hybrid quantum-classical models add value in practice. We compare classical and quantum-enhanced models for incident positron energy reconstruction on the CaloGAN dataset, a public benchmark of 100,000 simulated electromagnetic shower events spanning 1 to 100 GeV. Eight architectures, namely SVR, ANN, CNN and LSTM together with their quantum counterparts, are trained on three calorimeter representations: engineered physical feature
sf838d531d9.summary: Researchers compare classical and hybrid quantum-classical sequence models for positron energy regression on the public CaloGAN calorimeter shower dataset.
sf838d531d9.why: The text gives limited detail on outcomes, so its practical relevance to most engineering teams is unclear.

s9ea55d4ab9.title: ProdPilot: A Layered Model Context Protocol System for Automated Production Readiness and Deployment of Vibe-Coded Projects
s9ea55d4ab9.description: arXiv:2611.17381v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI-assisted development environments turn natural-language requests into working applications, yet the projects they produce often fail on their first deployment for operational reasons: credentials in source files, missing security middleware, no container definition, no health endpoint and no delivery pipeline. Automated repair of such defects usually relies on free-form model generation, which varies between runs and is seldom checked independently. This paper presents ProdPilot, a local Model Context Protocol server that audits Node.js and React projects against 50 production readiness rules, repairs violations through a bounded loop, gates the result and deploys it. Each rule is classified by what its fix requires: 28 fixes are fixed t
s9ea55d4ab9.summary: ProdPilot is a local Model Context Protocol server that audits Node.js and related vibe-coded projects for production readiness issues like hardcoded credentials and missing health endpoints.
s9ea55d4ab9.why: Automated checks for deployment defects in AI-generated apps address a common failure point when prototypes first reach production.

s6545e0a14a.title: Time-Consistent Evaluation of Hierarchical Code Graphs for SWE Agents
s6545e0a14a.description: arXiv:2611.17388v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Evaluating repository-aware software engineering (SWE) agents requires strict separation between pre-existing repository knowledge and future code evolution, yet standard benchmarks frequently suffer from temporal contamination and prompt-level solution leakage. Building on the time-consistent benchmark protocol of Sun (2026), we enforce strict zero-leakage isolation across DragonFly in C++ and React in JavaScript/TypeScript, locking repository snapshots and knowledge graphs at historical cutoff commits $T_0$ and evaluating 100 post-$T_0$ pull requests across four prompt granularities: Minimal, Concise, Contextual, and Guided. Under this zero-leakage protocol, we conduct a matched evaluation of three context-augmentation regimes: (1) an una
s6545e0a14a.summary: The paper evaluates repository-aware software engineering agents on DragonFly and React using repository snapshots and knowledge graphs locked at historical commits to prevent leakage.
s6545e0a14a.why: Zero-leakage evaluation protocols give a more trustworthy measure of coding agent performance than standard contaminated benchmarks.

sb64241c89f.title: Enumerating Posterior-Supported Priors: First-Order Error of Finite-Integral Cross-Categorical Measurement Morphisms
sb64241c89f.description: arXiv:2611.17390v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In generative modeling, standard measure theory adopts the a.e. convention, which legitimately ignores any error component carried by a null-support set: a single null element can hide out-of-domain error inside null support and never be explicitly accounted for. The contribution of this paper is not a new distributional distance, but rather a verifiable structure that writes down which underlying predicate supports a high-level object, when it is invertible, and at which layer the error resides, from which we propose the enumerating posterior-supported prior framework. The framework operates on a three-layer categorical chain Quot->MorTop->Set: the first two layers posit no point elements and take binary-predicate quotient partitions as ob
sb64241c89f.summary: The paper proposes a verifiable structure for specifying which predicate supports a high-level object in generative modeling, and bounds error in null-support regions.
sb64241c89f.why: The text is highly theoretical and offers little direct relevance to most engineering or leadership decisions.

s51745506b2.title: Confident and Wrong: Structure Confidence Is a Poor Selection Filter for Protein Function
s51745506b2.description: arXiv:2611.17391v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Structure-guided protein design can generate plausible candidates, but structural confidence does not predict function. We trained a function-guided model on measured metal-binding affinity with protein sequence, ligand identity, and assay conditions, and used it to design rare earth element (REE) binding variants of lanmodulin, a lanthanide-binding protein with four EF-hand domains. We screened 297 designs from three strategies against terbium and dysprosium, adjacent lanthanides among the hardest REE pairs to separate. Selection on structural confidence inverted the outcome it was meant to improve. The Structure-Confidence-Selected panel carried the highest pTM, complex ipLDDT, and composite confidence scores, and expressed at 97%, yet on
s51745506b2.summary: Researchers designed lanmodulin variants for rare earth element binding and found that structural confidence did not predict measured metal-binding function across 297 designs.
s51745506b2.why: Structural confidence scores alone are a poor selection filter, so function-guided screening is needed in protein design pipelines.

sb4d5556a3f.title: Can LLMs Write Backdoors? An Empirical Security Study of Weight-Space Programming
sb4d5556a3f.description: arXiv:2611.17395v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent advances in weight-space programming (WSP) have demonstrated that large language models (LLMs) can directly inspect and modify neural network weights without conventional gradient-based training. While this capability opens new possibilities for model improvement, it also raises an important security question: Can LLMs exploit weight-space programming to inject backdoors into neural networks? To answer this question, we present an empirical security study of LLM-driven weight-space programming for backdoor injection. Specifically, we investigate whether general-purpose LLMs can directly modify the weights of target models according to natural-language instructions, without accessing task-specific data, performing forward passes, or c
sb4d5556a3f.summary: An empirical study tests whether LLMs can use weight-space programming to inject backdoors into neural networks by directly modifying their weights.
sb4d5556a3f.why: LLMs that can edit model weights create a new supply-chain security risk that teams deploying third-party models should account for.

sa3c4846598.title: WETW: Learning Pair-Specific Weighted Euclidean Distances for Efficient DTW Search
sa3c4846598.description: arXiv:2611.17412v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) is the standard distance for similarity search over time series that are misaligned in time, but its cost is quadratic in the series length and lower bounds often prune few candidates, so search over large collections of long series is slow. Learned approximations embed the series to make comparisons cheap, yet compare every pair with the same fixed rule, usually the Euclidean distance, although DTW aligns each pair differently. We observe that, once a pair is aligned, DTW is a Euclidean distance over coordinates selected for that pair. Building on this view, we propose Weighted Euclidean Time Warping (WETW), a learned distance that adapts the comparison of fixed-length embeddings to each pair. A small symmetric n
sa3c4846598.summary: Researchers propose WETW, a method that learns pair-specific weighted Euclidean distances to approximate Dynamic Time Warping for faster similarity search over long time series.
sa3c4846598.why: Offers a potentially cheaper alternative to quadratic-cost DTW for searching large collections of misaligned time series.

s01fe63811c.title: Interpreting Coding Agents Through Their Behavioral Trajectories
s01fe63811c.description: arXiv:2611.17440v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Standard coding-agent benchmarks primarily evaluate binary task success, treating execution as a black box and obscuring the behaviors that produce those outcomes. We analyze a large corpus of 143,209 execution trajectories from 125 agent configurations spanning 117 unique models. To enable comparisons across heterogeneous agent interfaces, we develop a rule-based parser that maps raw execution traces to high-level actions such as repository search, file editing, and test execution, and audit its predictions against a six-model consensus reference on 500 events. We find that agents with similar solve rates can nevertheless differ substantially in how they explore, modify and verify code. Moreover, without using task outcomes, token counts,
s01fe63811c.summary: Researchers analyzed 143,209 execution trajectories from 125 coding-agent configurations, using a rule-based parser to map traces to high-level actions beyond binary task success.
s01fe63811c.why: Suggests benchmarks that score only pass/fail hide behaviors behind agent outcomes, which matters when evaluating coding agents.

s4cf91bc8ca.title: Racing the Clock: Teaching VLNs Budget-Conditioned Object Search
s4cf91bc8ca.description: arXiv:2611.17442v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A rescue robot entering a building with thirty seconds on the clock should sprint toward the single most promising room; given ten minutes, it should instead explore a broader tour. Yet vision-language-navigation (VLN) models are typically evaluated under a fixed episode limit that the policy never observes, even though time-critical missions require behavior to adapt to the available budget. We study budget-conditioned object search: given a target category and an explicit action budget, an agent must find as many distinct target instances as possible before the budget expires. We investigate how to supervise VLNs for this task by comparing a privileged TSP expert, which plans near-optimal routes using the full map and true target location
s4cf91bc8ca.summary: Researchers study budget-conditioned object search for vision-language-navigation agents, where the agent is given an explicit action budget and must find as many target instances as possible.

s6883673636.title: Diffusion Tree Sampling for Inference Time Adaptation of Crystal Generative Models
s6883673636.description: arXiv:2611.17462v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Diffusion-based generative models have become strong priors over plausible crystal structures, but turning that prior into promising candidates requires steering toward several conflicting properties at once. Fine-tuning is expensive and produces a new model for every new objective, while differentiable guidance is not applicable to many real-world tasks. We instead adapt these generative models at inference time using Diffusion Tree Sampling (DTS), a Monte Carlo tree search procedure over the denoising trajectory. We make two technical contributions on top of DTS that are particularly relevant for AI-for-science applications. First, we show how to use existing property-conditional generative models (e.g., models fine-tuned for classifier-f
s6883673636.summary: Researchers introduce Diffusion Tree Sampling, a Monte Carlo tree search over the denoising trajectory, to steer crystal generative models toward multiple properties at inference time.
s6883673636.why: Offers a way to adapt pretrained generative models to new objectives without fine-tuning a new model for each one.

s2851b3aa8f.title: Use-case-driven ontology modeling with the NeOn methodology for ambient assisted living
s2851b3aa8f.description: arXiv:2611.17466v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Research on smart homes and ambient assisted living (AAL) has grown steadily over the last decade, driven largely by the ageing of the population. A smart home has to coordinate heterogeneous smart objects in order to offer services tailored to its dwellers, and this requires a shared formal description of both the dwellers and the devices. We present the ontology developed as the semantic data layer of the Virtual Home Framework in the Italian Design For All project. Its requirements are derived from two use cases: a frail elderly woman who exercises at home on a cycle-ergometer, and a designer who configures a kitchen for users with different impairments. The requirements are collected in an Ontology Requirements Specification Document an
s2851b3aa8f.summary: Researchers present an ontology built with the NeOn methodology as the semantic data layer of the Virtual Home Framework for ambient assisted living in smart homes.

s5bd6a6e24b.title: Do Mixture-of-Experts Routers Benefit from Ensembling?
s5bd6a6e24b.description: arXiv:2611.17472v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Ensembles of neural networks have repeatedly been shown to outperform single networks. Ensemble theory attributes this gain to the accuracy of the individual members and the diversity among them. Mixture-of-experts models already combine many experts, but a single router decides how the experts are weighted for each input. Motivated by ensemble theory, we apply ensembling to the routing step: an ensemble of routers, trained jointly with the experts, proposes the expert weights. We systematically evaluate this approach using underparameterized networks on two image-classification and two tabular-regression tasks. We analyse each experiment with a performance-diversity decomposition of the router ensemble, which, to our knowledge, has not pre
s5bd6a6e24b.summary: Researchers evaluate applying ensembling to the routing step of mixture-of-experts models, using an ensemble of routers trained jointly with the experts to propose expert weights.
s5bd6a6e24b.why: Explores whether ensemble gains transfer to MoE routing, a design choice relevant to building sparse models.

s17d0cbb725.title: Adversarial Tracking: Attacks on Image Sensors for Object Tracking in Autonomous Vehicles
s17d0cbb725.description: arXiv:2611.17505v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Object tracking systems estimate the motion of surrounding vehicles by linking detected objects across video frames. In particular, Tracking-By-Detection (TBD) systems combine object detectors with motion prediction and data association to maintain object identities over time. However, neural network-based detectors are vulnerable to adversarial attacks that perturb input images, and their impact on downstream trajectory estimation is not fully characterized by detection accuracy alone. Therefore, this paper evaluates image-specific and image-agnostic attacks on YOLOv3 and YOLOv4 detectors paired with SORT, Deep SORT, Strong SORT, and OC-SORT tracking systems. The evaluation uses CARLA simulator and measures tracking quality through Multipl
s17d0cbb725.summary: Researchers evaluate image-specific and image-agnostic adversarial attacks on detectors in tracking-by-detection systems, measuring their effect on vehicle trajectory estimation in autonomous driving.
s17d0cbb725.why: Shows detection accuracy alone does not capture how adversarial image perturbations degrade downstream tracking in autonomous vehicles.

s30407b76c2.title: Only as Safe as the Weakest Agent: A Break That Appears Only When the System Is Multi-Agent
s30407b76c2.description: arXiv:2611.17520v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Major industry multi-agent systems like Codex and Claude Code can be broken by attacks that have long been unsuccessful against modern frontier models. AI Safety as a discipline has largely focused on finding the bounds and vulnerabilities of AI models used in isolation. Yet as humans increasingly deploy these models as agents and multi-agent systems, the same attacks that had been thought to be patched when using a model in isolation can break these same models under specific circumstances. We show that these system breaks are not purely theoretical, but can break Claude Code, Codex, and a reference harness, all unmodified and used with their own sub-agent mechanisms. We show the attack by asking agents to answer questions from a store of
s30407b76c2.summary: Researchers show that attacks which failed against frontier models in isolation can break multi-agent systems such as Codex and Claude Code under specific circumstances.
s30407b76c2.why: Indicates per-model safety testing may miss vulnerabilities that only emerge when models operate as part of multi-agent systems.

s7793a77614.title: GraphScent: Calibrating Directional Relevance Signals for Bounded-Context Code Localization
s7793a77614.description: arXiv:2611.17527v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Running open-weight language models locally on a single consumer GPU requires replacing expanding multi-turn exploration histories with short, stateless code inspections. Stateless repository localization, however, hinges on a foundational question: when a frozen language model evaluates an unedited code entity from a compact view, which structural relationships make its relevance judgment informative about a nearby repair target? Studying Gemma 4 models across 211 real-world Python issues in 86 repositories, we uncover a systematic directional relevance asymmetry: zero-temperature relevance scores on enclosing scopes and upstream callers consistently separate true structural neighbors from hard lexical distractors, whereas scores on downst
s7793a77614.summary: Researchers study directional relevance signals for code localization with Gemma 4 models on 211 Python issues, aiming to run stateless repository localization on a single consumer GPU.
s7793a77614.why: Points toward practical local coding assistants that avoid long multi-turn exploration histories on consumer hardware.

sa2074f6ada.title: A Synthetic Benchmark for Target-Centric Causal Discovery in Industrial Processes
sa2074f6ada.description: arXiv:2611.17556v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Causal discovery promises to find which recorded variables drive a process target such as product quality, yield or energy use. Process data with known causes are rare, and in existing benchmarks the difficulty of identifying the causes of a target is either fixed by the recorded data or set for the whole graph. We present a synthetic benchmark for target-centric causal discovery in industrial processes. Its generator is a two-level structural causal model inspired by batch production, assembled from components that each model one phenomenon of process data, such as a control loop or a delayed effect. The graph is built around the target: without sensor error, every non-cause can be distinguished from the direct causes by conditioning on th
sa2074f6ada.summary: Researchers present a synthetic benchmark for target-centric causal discovery in industrial processes, built from a two-level structural causal model inspired by batch production.

s05d9464cb7.title: Benchmarks Don't Talk Back: Learning Through Self-Disagreement
s05d9464cb7.description: arXiv:2611.17563v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A benchmark usually measures a language model alone with a question, and deployment rarely looks like that: answers get contested, and models give up correct ones under counter-reasoning that is itself wrong. We show that what fails there is not a shortfall of accuracy but a capability in its own right -- knowing when to hold a position and when to yield to a better one -- which we call dialectical competence. It stands on first-answer accuracy without following from it: a model can be made materially better at answering and no better at this, and training for accuracy alone can drift against it. Nor can it be bought at inference, by self-reflection or by sampling more. Taking a cue from the dialectical tradition in philosophy, in which pro
s05d9464cb7.summary: Researchers define dialectical competence, the ability of a language model to hold a correct position under contested answers and yield only to better reasoning, and show it differs from accuracy.
s05d9464cb7.why: Highlights that first-answer accuracy does not measure whether models resist wrong pushback, a gap relevant to deployed assistants.

s1f8a603a7f.title: Rethinking Visual Reasoning in Text-to-Image Reward Modeling
s1f8a603a7f.description: arXiv:2611.17585v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reward models are a core component of modern text-to-image systems, serving as the objective for inference-time selection and RL-based post-training. A key prerequisite is visual understanding: to judge prompt adherence and ground aesthetic preferences, a reward model must bind attributes, resolve relations, and count reliably. We find that widely-used reward models perform poorly on targeted visual reasoning evaluations. Even when starting from strong vision-language backbones, preference fine-tuning erodes these capabilities, and continual-learning baselines fail to mitigate a steep tradeoff between visual reasoning and preference accuracy. We propose a data-centric intervention that injects visual reasoning supervision into preference le
s1f8a603a7f.summary: Researchers find that widely used text-to-image reward models perform poorly on targeted visual reasoning tests, and that preference fine-tuning can erode these capabilities.
s1f8a603a7f.why: Suggests reward models used for selection and RL post-training may fail on attribute binding, relations and counting, affecting image pipelines.

sd9d1144a64.title: X-Nav Technical Report: Real-World Long-Horizon Indoor-to-Outdoor Navigation on a Humanoid Robot
sd9d1144a64.description: arXiv:2611.17598v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Long-horizon navigation from indoors to outdoors remains an open problem for humanoid robots: one instruction covers rooms, doors and roads, and the camera moves with the gait. Worken, AGIBOT's measure of productive robot work, depends on robots that reach their workplaces autonomously. We present X-Nav, to our knowledge the first system to take a bipedal humanoid through a language-instructed long-horizon mission from indoors to outdoors. X-Nav covers a pipeline from data to deployment. Its data engine collects navigation data in open-source scenes, in digital twins of deployment sites and on real robots. Its navigation model, MELIOR, takes only RGB images from the robot's built-in camera and comes in two versions: MELIOR-A predicts action
sd9d1144a64.summary: AGIBOT presents X-Nav, a system that takes a bipedal humanoid robot through a language-instructed long-horizon navigation mission from indoors to outdoors.
sd9d1144a64.why: Demonstrates end-to-end data-to-deployment navigation on a humanoid, a benchmark for embodied robotics engineering.

s4ed2f8dfd7.title: Training-Free Acceleration of Multi-View 3D Transformers via Regime-Aware Attention Approximation
s4ed2f8dfd7.description: arXiv:2611.17629v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multi-view 3D transformers such as VGGT reconstruct a scene from a set of unposed images in a single forward pass, predicting camera poses, depth and 3D points, but the cost of their global attention grows quadratically with the num- ber of images. Accelerators borrowed from large language models assume that each token attends to only a few oth- ers; on these models they lose accuracy or gain little speed. We study the global attention of three multi-view transform- ers on seven datasets and find that every layer plays one of three roles: it averages over the whole scene, matches points across many images, or anchors on the first image, whose coordinates the outputs use. Building on this anal- ysis, we propose Regime-AWare ATTention Approxi
s4ed2f8dfd7.summary: Researchers propose a training-free acceleration for multi-view 3D transformers like VGGT by approximating global attention differently per layer role, based on analysis across seven datasets.
s4ed2f8dfd7.why: Offers a no-retraining speedup for quadratic attention cost in multi-image 3D reconstruction models.

sdbdfdcb294.title: CoTTAGE: An Explainable Judge for Text-to-Audio Generation
sdbdfdcb294.description: arXiv:2611.17644v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rapid progress in text-to-audio (TTA) generation demands reliable and explainable automatic evaluation. However, existing metrics fail to simultaneously deliver high correlation with human judgments and meaningful, audio-grounded explanations, forcing reliance on labor-intensive human evaluation that bottlenecks model development iteration. To address this, we propose CoTTAGE, a reasoning-based evaluator for text relevance (REL) and audio quality (OVL). Following a reason-then-predict paradigm, CoTTAGE first generates an audio-grounded rationale to diagnose errors before predicting scores. Supported by over 10K newly collected human OVL annotations, CoTTAGE is first trained via supervised fine-tuning and then refined with reinforcement lear
sdbdfdcb294.summary: Researchers introduce CoTTAGE, a reasoning-based evaluator that generates audio-grounded rationales before scoring text relevance and audio quality for text-to-audio generation.
sdbdfdcb294.why: Provides an explainable automatic judge that could reduce reliance on slow human evaluation when iterating on audio models.

s95d5d308e5.title: Binarization as an Attack Surface in Weightless Neural Networks
s95d5d308e5.description: arXiv:2611.17646v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Weightless Neural Networks (WNNs) are lightweight classifiers that binarize their inputs and learn by storing binary patterns in lookup memories, which makes them attractive for resource-constrained tasks such as intrusion detection. Because a small perturbation that crosses no binarization threshold leaves the binary input unchanged, WNNs may appear naturally robust to adversarial examples; a perturbation that does cross a threshold, however, can still change the prediction. We study this tension in WiSARD, the canonical RAM-based WNN, and in two variants that replace its memories with Bloom filters, Bloom WiSARD and BTHOWeN. A continuous perturbation reaches these classifiers only by crossing an encoding threshold, changing at least one b
s95d5d308e5.summary: Researchers study whether Weightless Neural Networks, such as WiSARD, are robust to adversarial examples, finding that binarization thresholds can still let perturbations change predictions.
s95d5d308e5.why: Engineers deploying lightweight classifiers for intrusion detection should not assume binarization alone provides adversarial robustness.

sd01d525796.title: Imitation Policies Learn a Proprioceptive Anchor: A Predictive Law for Perception Noise and Its Closed Loop Cost
sd01d525796.description: arXiv:2611.17658v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Imitation policies for robot manipulation are often trained on noisy object positions, and they learn to discount the noisy reading. We show how much they discount it, and why. Because demonstrators steer toward the object, the robot's own state carries information about where the object is. A trained policy combines this proprioceptive anchor with the reading and weights the reading by $\alpha = V/(V + s^2)$, where $s^2$ is the reading noise and $V$ the anchor's error variance. $V$ belongs to the learner and is far smaller than a linear model of the demonstrations implies, which is why classical errors-in-variables (EIV) regression overestimates $\alpha$. Measured once, $V$ predicted ten held-out sensitivities across two robomimic tasks, t
sd01d525796.summary: Researchers show imitation policies for robot manipulation learn to discount noisy object-position readings by blending them with the robot's proprioceptive state, and give a predictive formula for this weighting.
sd01d525796.why: Teams training robot policies on noisy perception can use this law to predict how much policies rely on sensor readings versus proprioception.

sc66c370adb.title: Agent-written heuristics versus commercial solvers on unsolved job-shop benchmark instances
sc66c370adb.description: arXiv:2611.17682v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Commercial solvers are the standard tool for difficult scheduling problems. We study whether a frontier large language model, used as a coding agent with open-source tools only, can match them in quality and speed. We report every run, and independent checkers verify every schedule. On the 100,000-operation job shop tai_100_1000_1, an agent-written solver reached 525,515, below OptalCP, Hexaly, and CP Optimizer. Unchanged, it improved all ten instances of the family and closed two. With equal budgets on the same workstation, it ended 0.0-1.8% above the lower bound, against 2.6-5.8% for CP Optimizer and 2.4-4.4% for Hexaly. On the Behnke-Geiger flexible job shops, an agent-written tabu search improved 11 of 32 open instances. With two transp
sc66c370adb.summary: An LLM used as a coding agent with open-source tools wrote a job-shop scheduling solver that was compared against commercial solvers on large unsolved benchmark instances.
sc66c370adb.why: It shows agent-written heuristics can approach commercial optimization solvers on hard scheduling problems, though the reported solver still trailed the commercial ones on the headline instance.

s4213fdacbc.title: Logically Consistent Accurate Forecasts
s4213fdacbc.description: arXiv:2611.17735v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agentic forecasting systems based on large language models (LLMs) are now competitive with expert human forecasters, but these systems still suffer from a critical limitation: the inability to produce forecasts that are logically consistent. For example, forecasts for related events often fail to satisfy the axioms of probability, which in turn implies that related forecasts cannot simultaneously be correct and undermines their utility for decision makers. Enforcing consistency is not trivial -- naive approaches (e.g., projection onto the set of consistent forecasts) can degrade accuracy. We argue that the key to overcoming the apparent tradeoff between consistency and accuracy lies in the reasoning which supports each forecast. We finetune
s4213fdacbc.summary: Researchers present a method for making LLM-based agentic forecasting systems produce logically consistent forecasts that satisfy probability axioms across related events.
s4213fdacbc.why: Forecasts for related events that contradict each other undermine decision-making, so consistency enforcement matters for anyone using LLM forecasts operationally.

sf21872f6d4.title: Superfluid: Local AI Server for Distributed LLM Inference
sf21872f6d4.description: arXiv:2611.17753v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Running large language models (LLMs) on local devices keeps data private, removes per-token cost, cuts network latency, and keeps working without a connection. Two shifts now strain how such models are served. On one device, several agents share a locally served model with an interactive user. Across devices, a developer or small team often owns several capable machines from different vendors, which sit idle most of the day because every local server serves one runtime on one machine. We present Superfluid, an open-source LLM server built for local inference at both scales. On one device, Superfluid drives llama.cpp, MLX, or BaseRT in isolated worker processes through one scheduler that moves interactive requests ahead of agent work, comput
sf21872f6d4.summary: Superfluid, an open-source local LLM server, is presented for distributing inference across several machines from different vendors and serving multiple agents on one device.
sf21872f6d4.why: Developers with several idle local machines could pool them to serve models privately without per-token cost.

sa62157b736.title: Creative Product Design under Brand Image Constraints
sa62157b736.description: arXiv:2611.17762v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Industrial design requires creative visual exploration while satisfying constraints that are often product-specific and implicit. Existing text-to-image (T2I) approaches can generate creative designs through concept blending or multi-agent self-enhancement, but they provide limited mechanisms for ensuring that generated designs remain consistent with such constraints. We focus on brand image as a representative design constraint and propose a framework for brand-aware redesign generation. Given a product name, the framework constructs a brand image survey report that summarizes product and market information, derives a creative direction from the report, and integrates this direction into a self-enhancement loop in which generated images ar
sa62157b736.summary: Researchers propose a framework for brand-aware product redesign generation that uses a constructed brand image to keep text-to-image designs consistent with brand constraints.

sab059b9991.title: GDP.xlsx: Benchmarking Frontier Models on Professional Workbooks
sab059b9991.description: arXiv:2611.17766v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce GDP_xlsx, a benchmark of 70 realistic workplace requests written by professionals in 13 domains, each paired with an expert rubric of binary criteria and with the complete workbook or CSV file it refers to. Together the files hold 2.18 million populated cells, and the rubrics 791 criteria. Agents work in a container with spreadsheet tools, and an agentic judge that can open the file applies the rubric. Completeness and exclusivity criteria require set-valued answers to be found in full and with nothing extra. We rank models by strict pass@1, the share of attempts that meet every criterion. Across 20 model configurations, including frontier models from Google, Anthropic, and OpenAI, the top-scoring one, Gemini 4 Argon, passes on
sab059b9991.summary: GDP_xlsx is a benchmark of 70 professional workplace spreadsheet requests across 13 domains, scored with expert rubrics and an agentic judge that opens the workbook.
sab059b9991.why: It gives teams a rubric-based way to compare frontier models and agents on realistic spreadsheet tasks.

s4417e466d7.title: Activation Steering the Nan-Shan in Typhoon
s4417e466d7.description: arXiv:2611.17768v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Typhoon is an audiovisual installation based on Joseph Conrad's novella, in which Captain MacWhirr steers the steamer Nan-Shan directly into and through a catastrophic storm. The novella is a study of what happens when the scale of a phenomenon exceeds the practical and conceptual frameworks available to comprehend it and of the paralysis that sometimes follows a demand for action in such overwhelming circumstances. We chose the text of Typhoon to reflect on human culture's current AI moment. We prompt a large language model, seeded with Conrad's original language, to feed endlessly on its own output, and explore when and how the text becomes increasingly alien and unwieldy as time progresses, including deviations from the narrative, digres
s4417e466d7.summary: Typhoon is an audiovisual art installation that prompts an LLM seeded with Joseph Conrad's novella to reflect on the current AI moment, using activation steering.

sa02f43225e.title: LuthorSQL: A One-Pass Text-to-SQL Model as System 1 for a Slower LLM Agent
sa02f43225e.description: arXiv:2611.17780v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Frontier LLM agents that query databases with tools are among the most accurate text-to-SQL systems, but per-query calls to a hosted model are slow, costly, and expose sensitive organizational queries to external APIs. For example, a Claude Opus 5.5 agent serving 10,000 queries a day costs over $70,000 a year at list price. To what extent can local hardware already owned by an organization offload this burden without compromising the agent's accuracy? We present LuthorSQL, a non-autoregressive 7B text-to-SQL model that serves as a rapid System 1 gate for a slower LLM agent (System 2), escalating queries only when uncertain. LuthorSQL makes a single forward pass to predict slot scores over a bounded grammar for query plans, compiles and runs
sa02f43225e.summary: LuthorSQL is a non-autoregressive 7B text-to-SQL model proposed as a fast first-pass system that could run on local hardware ahead of a slower LLM agent.
sa02f43225e.why: Offloading routine queries to local models could cut API costs and keep sensitive organizational queries off external APIs.

s4fe0fb5e4e.title: Towards Seconds-level Video Representation: Quadratically Gated Feature Grid with Adaptive, Prediction-free Sampling
s4fe0fb5e4e.description: arXiv:2611.17786v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Implicit neural video representations are notoriously slow to build, which does not cross the basic practical threshold for most industrial applications. Here, we present Q-GAS, a coordinate-queryable video representation that couples multi-resolution explicit 3D feature grids with a compact SwiGLU-style quadratic-gating (QG) decoder and an error-aware, prediction-free sampler. The explicit grids avoid hash-collision coefficient sharing at the cost of modestly higher storage yet greatly boost the expressive capacity; the QG decoder introduces low-rank local second-order interactions to improve the nonlinear feature response. During fitting, a global error map periodically refreshes a high-error pool, and each batch mixes pool samples with u
s4fe0fb5e4e.summary: Q-GAS is a coordinate-queryable implicit video representation using 3D feature grids, a quadratic-gating decoder, and a prediction-free sampler to speed up building video representations.
s4fe0fb5e4e.why: Faster construction of implicit video representations could make them practical for industrial video applications.

s4c301d9d24.title: Can Large Language Models Optimize Pretrained Neural Network Weights? A Multi-Phase Empirical Evaluation of Gradient-Free Editing in YOLO26 Object Detection
s4c301d9d24.description: arXiv:2611.17789v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Direct weight editing offers a gradient-free alternative to fine-tuning pretrained detectors, but its generalization and the value of large language model (LLM) guidance remain uncertain. We evaluate five experimental phases using YOLO26 models and MS COCO, comparing deterministic scaling, random perturbations, differential evolution, CMA-ES, structured interventions, real local-LLM proposals, failure-aware guidance, and hybrid LLM-CMA-ES against a matched random-policy control. Optimization uses native Ultralytics mAP50-95 on 1,000 COCO Val2017 images; selected candidates are assessed on a disjoint, previously examined 1,500-image subset, with COCO API AP50-95 reported separately where available. Increasing the CMA-ES budget from 8 to 250
s4c301d9d24.summary: A multi-phase study evaluates whether LLMs can optimize pretrained YOLO26 detector weights gradient-free, comparing them against evolutionary methods and a random-policy control on COCO.
s4c301d9d24.why: Results indicate whether LLM guidance adds value over standard search for weight editing of detectors, a question teams weighing that approach need answered.

s5b8d19f052.title: Multimodal Person Concept Model for Person Identification under Varying Observation Conditions
s5b8d19f052.description: arXiv:2611.17802v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Service robots in domestic and office environments must identify users to provide personalized services based on their preferences and previous interactions. This is challenging because only a few observations may be available for learning, while observation conditions change owing to appearance, environmental noise, and utterance content. To address this challenge, this study proposes a multimodal person concept model that learns person concepts from a small number of observations, without person labels, and enables robust identification under changing conditions. The model employs a nonparametric Bayesian generative model based on the Chinese restaurant process and integrates visual, acoustic, and linguistic features extracted using Contr
s5b8d19f052.summary: A multimodal person concept model is proposed that learns person identities from few observations without person labels, for robust identification by service robots under varying conditions.

s3a41667f7d.title: CarryOn: Learning What to Keep in Context for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
s3a41667f7d.description: arXiv:2611.17808v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents can coordinate tools and applications to complete complex, multi-step tasks. As their interaction histories grow, effective context management becomes essential for reliable and efficient execution. Existing methods reduce context through summarization, pruning, or history selection. However, shorter contexts do not necessarily support better decisions: summaries can omit exact details needed for later actions, while retaining entire interactions can carry substantial irrelevant information. We propose CarryOn, a lightweight context manager that pairs compact execution state with fine-grained, source-linked evidence. A learned selector and adaptive retention policy keep relevant evidence available without additional
s3a41667f7d.summary: CarryOn is a lightweight method that learns which parts of an agent's interaction history to keep in context for long-horizon LLM agent tasks.
s3a41667f7d.why: Better context selection addresses the tradeoff between summaries that drop needed details and full histories that add noise in long agent runs.

s1841b522f4.title: SceneAgent: A Multi-Agent Framework for Portable Game Scene Generation
s1841b522f4.description: arXiv:2611.17821v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Moving a scene generator to a new game engine requires more than exporting its final output: planning, construction tools, and stored experience may also depend on the original backend. We present SceneAgent, a multi-agent framework for reusing the construction process and its experience across backends. A canonical SceneContext maintains the evolving world, while backend adapters isolate coordinate conventions, asset bindings, and export. Structured handoffs let fresh Builder sessions query this persistent state without inheriting the full construction transcript. Across generations, human-approved traces are distilled into asset-ID-free Layout skills and semantic Content skills that can be retrieved and recombined. We introduce GameSceneB
s1841b522f4.summary: SceneAgent is a multi-agent framework that reuses scene-generation construction processes and experience across different game engine backends via a canonical scene context and backend adapters.
s1841b522f4.why: Separating world state from engine-specific adapters could reduce rework when moving generation pipelines between game engines.

sc2855811f1.title: V-JEPA-LM: Video-Language Models That Read Dynamics Beyond Static, Text-Aligned Representations
sc2855811f1.description: arXiv:2611.17831v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: World-model video encoders such as V-JEPA learn how scenes change (direction, speed, order, state) from video alone. To answer questions, they are joined to a language model trained on captions and question-answer pairs. But each caption or question names only a few attributes of a clip, so the model learns to retrieve those attributes rather than to read the clip, and the dynamics the encoder carries go unused: on the same items, a linear probe reads speed from frozen V-JEPA features at 87% while the VLM answers at chance. We show where dynamics lives in a frozen encoder: in a subspace shared across videos for predictive encoders such as V-JEPA, but not as a shared component of frame-wise, text-aligned encoders such as SigLIP. We then buil
sc2855811f1.summary: V-JEPA-LM is a video-language model approach aimed at letting language models use the dynamics captured by V-JEPA video encoders rather than only retrieving static, caption-aligned attributes.
sc2855811f1.why: It highlights that video-LM training can leave useful encoder dynamics unused, relevant to teams building video question-answering systems.

saa13de8acd.title: Tracing Uncertainties of Extreme El Ni\~{n}o Prediction to Mesoscale Ocean Currents
saa13de8acd.description: arXiv:2611.17854v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The predictability of the El Ni\~{n}o-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) has historically been linked to large-scale errors in models' initial conditions such as heat content and surface wind stress. Here we demonstrate that these slowly evolving errors may ultimately originate from mesoscale errors in initial oceanic states that are common in current models and ocean observation systems. This hidden source of ENSO forecast uncertainty, in terms of mesoscale ocean-current errors, is convincingly exposed by the conditional nonlinear optimal perturbation (CNOP) method applied to a differentiable ocean AI model. The CNOP-identified most influential current errors are strongly event-dependent. For the 1997/98 El Ni\~{n}o, the initial current errors in
saa13de8acd.summary: Researchers argue that errors in El Niño forecasts may originate from mesoscale errors in initial ocean-current states common to current models and observation systems.
saa13de8acd.why: It shows that small-scale initial-condition errors in ocean data can propagate into large-scale climate forecast uncertainty, relevant to anyone building or validating forecasting pipelines.

sd1d95f8ffb.title: Active Learning of Temporal Specifications through Distinguishing Queries
sd1d95f8ffb.description: arXiv:2611.17866v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Temporal specifications are essential for verification and monitoring, yet writing formulas that capture the intended behaviour is difficult. Active learning derives such specifications through interaction between a learner and a teacher, but remains underexplored for temporal logics. Existing approaches require the teacher to answer equivalence queries and to construct counterexamples, and they often rely on SAT-based learning procedures that restart the search after each new example. We present an active-learning framework for LTLf in which the teacher only labels traces and answers natural-language questions about the intended behaviour. The learner maintains an enumerated version space of candidate formulas, generates traces that distin
sd1d95f8ffb.summary: Researchers present an active-learning framework for LTLf that learns temporal logic specifications through learner-teacher interaction, aiming to avoid equivalence queries and restarted SAT searches.
sd1d95f8ffb.why: Automatically learning temporal specifications could reduce the effort of writing verification and monitoring formulas, though the text gives limited detail on results.

sd886d447d5.title: UltraBERT-JEV: Encoder models for System One Applications
sd886d447d5.description: arXiv:2611.17867v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study encoder models that pick one of several options in a single forward pass, without generating text. This technical report compares recipes for fine-tuning UltraBERT-380M with one mask per option. The four recipes differ in how an option is scored and how the scores become probabilities; one follows the expert gate of DeepSeek-V3. Trained on the same data as Qwen3-0.6B with the LLM-as-Jev recipe (67.6% test accuracy), the encoder reaches 69.7% to 72.1%. Scoring an option by "yes" minus "no" instead of "yes" alone gives the larger gain, from 69.7% to 71.3% on the test set and from 57.8% to 59.6% on external benchmarks (56.1% for the decoder). Sigmoid normalisation adds 0.8 test points; a square-root softplus adds none. One request at
sd886d447d5.summary: A technical report compares fine-tuning recipes for UltraBERT-380M encoder models that select among options in one forward pass, reporting 69.7% to 72.1% test accuracy versus 67.6% for Qwen3-0.6B.
sd886d447d5.why: Smaller encoder models may match a much smaller LLM on option-selection tasks at lower inference cost, which matters for cost-sensitive deployments.

se93fe3acc0.title: DySENSE: Dynamic Spatiotemporal ENergy Synthesis and Emulation with Satellite Imagery
se93fe3acc0.description: arXiv:2611.17878v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Cities account for over two-thirds of the world's energy and more than 70% of global carbon dioxide emissions. City energy is essential for achieving the 2050 net-zero target and the UN's Sustainable Development Goals 7 and 11. Although existing studies have made progress, they are limited by data and methodological gaps. Existing studies are largely predictive for existing cities rather than generative for future cities; fine-grained, aligned monthly dynamic energy data are scarce; and existing GenAI models struggle to generate dynamic urban functional monthly energy. We present DySENSE, a joint multimodal GenAI framework that synthesizes static urban satellite imagery together with spatially aligned, dynamic monthly building energy consum
se93fe3acc0.summary: DySENSE is a framework for generating dynamic, spatiotemporal urban energy data and emulating energy use using satellite imagery, aimed at future cities.

s9099976e05.title: From Local Prediction Error to Final Outputs: A Theory of Expert Sharing in Multi-Step Reasoning
s9099976e05.description: arXiv:2611.17879v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) models can share experts across layers or computational steps, pooling training information from different contexts. This can reduce local prediction error, but multi-step systems are ultimately evaluated by their final outputs. We study when these local gains survive composition. In specified linear regression models, we derive exact sharing and merging criteria by balancing variance savings against bias from sharing across roles with different target behavior. Under a common fixed linear propagation map, we characterize expected squared final-output risk, retaining error directions and correlations. We construct cases where sharing lowers average local error yet increases final-output error. Within this setting, w
s9099976e05.summary: A theoretical paper derives criteria for when sharing mixture-of-experts experts across layers or steps reduces local error and still helps final multi-step outputs.
s9099976e05.why: It gives principled guidance on when expert sharing in MoE architectures improves end-to-end results rather than only local prediction error.

sce0677a0e4.title: Photogrammetric 3D Model-Based Animal Behavior Classification
sce0677a0e4.description: arXiv:2611.17881v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Video-based behavior estimation is often implemented end-to-end from image sequences. We advocate a two-stage alternative: reconstruct 3D body and object geometry before classifying behavior. This makes ambiguities of the ill-posed 2D-to-3D inverse problem explicit and potentially correctable. We demonstrate the strategy with simulated interacting mice and extend it to real video.
sce0677a0e4.summary: Researchers propose classifying animal behavior by first reconstructing 3D body and object geometry from video, then classifying, demonstrated on simulated and real mouse video.

s1668e120e9.title: Securing Multi-Agent Systems by Design
s1668e120e9.description: arXiv:2611.17883v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multi-agent systems solve complex tasks by decomposing them into subtasks, delegating the subtasks to agents, and aggregating the agents' responses using an aggregation rule. Malicious agents can manipulate the final solution by providing malicious responses to their assigned subtasks. In this paper, we first propose response manipulation attacks (ReMA), which iteratively optimize malicious responses to maximize attack effectiveness. Specifically, we formulate untargeted and targeted attacks as optimization problems and develop an approach to approximately solve these problems by iteratively refining malicious responses based on feedback from a surrogate multi-agent system. To defend against such attacks, we further propose SecMAS, a secure
s1668e120e9.summary: Researchers propose response manipulation attacks (ReMA) on multi-agent systems, where malicious agents optimize responses to skew the aggregated final solution, and study securing such systems by design.
s1668e120e9.why: Multi-agent systems that aggregate subagent outputs can be manipulated by a few malicious agents, so aggregation rules and agent trust need security design.

sc059b673d1.title: More Genes, Faster Inference: Efficient Large-Panel Spatial Transcriptomics Prediction from Histology
sc059b673d1.description: arXiv:2611.17899v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) prediction from histology aims to infer spatially resolved gene expression profiles directly from tissue images. This is a challenging problem that is currently often addressed with complicated model architectures, additional inputs, and complicated training procedures, while remaining limited to fixed, small gene panels. This raises a natural question: Is there an efficient method for large-panel ST prediction? Here, we present GeneFlow, a simpler yet effective framework for large-scale spatial gene expression prediction that unifies flow-matching generative modeling with structured multimodal fusion. Specifically, GeneFlow first encodes both histological morphology and cross-gene interactions in spatial spots
sc059b673d1.summary: GeneFlow is a framework for predicting expression of large gene panels from histology images, presented as a simpler and more efficient alternative to complex existing methods.

s72d5d955cd.title: Condensing Law of Security Information
s72d5d955cd.description: arXiv:2611.17918v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Scaling laws indicate that the generalization error of a large language model (LLM) decreases monotonically with model size once data is sufficient, and the corollary that larger models outperform smaller ones is now widely accepted. We argue that this corollary fails in security: decisions there hinge on anomalous inputs, which are long-tailed (e.g., zero-day attacks) and therefore poorly served by likelihood fitting. Worse still, the capability brought about by scale (e.g., inferring the intended whole from a corrupted part) leads a LLM silently \emph{repair} the anomaly before any downstream security head ever sees it. We formalize this as a tradeoff between two quantities: the cognitive capability $K(W)=I(W;P)$ that a model holds about
s72d5d955cd.summary: The paper argues that the scaling-law assumption that larger LLMs always do better fails in security, because anomalous, long-tailed inputs such as zero-day attacks are poorly served by likelihood fitting.
s72d5d955cd.why: Engineers choosing models for security tasks should not assume bigger models will detect rare anomalies better.

s7e83a04a21.title: MineralExp: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Experimental Design in Real-World Mineral Exploration
s7e83a04a21.description: arXiv:2611.17931v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In mineral exploration, verifying geological hypotheses relies on designing a variety of geochemical experiments. While large language model (LLM) agents increasingly automate downstream geoscientific data analysis, a crucial upstream capability remains largely unexplored: automated geochemical experimental design, i.e., deciding which experiments to conduct before committing to costly laboratory work. Evaluating this capability of LLM agents is difficult for two reasons. First, geochemical experiments exhibit high methodological diversity and subjectivity: to test the same hypothesis, different geologists may choose different minerals and instruments, so no single protocol can serve as the reference answer. Second, open-ended experimental
s7e83a04a21.summary: MineralExp is a benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on automated geochemical experimental design for real-world mineral exploration.

s221c6afdeb.title: Can You Trust Your Finance Agent? Drift, Diagnosis and Auditable Intervention on One Shipped Financial Research Agent
s221c6afdeb.description: arXiv:2611.17939v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Can you trust a finance agent you did not build? We take the reference agent shipped with the Vals Finance Agent Benchmark v2, leave it untuned, and ask four questions a leaderboard score does not answer. Is the score stable? Seven identical runs on 18 questions pass between 105 and 123 of 149 rubric criteria, and the bill varies by up to 17%. When the agent fails, who owns the fix? We classify 20 failed trajectories, from three runs of nine held-out questions, by the layer whose owner would remedy them, under a taxonomy frozen in advance: 13 belong to the agent's instructions, 3 to its tools, 4 to the model, none to its data. Can that diagnosis be trusted? Four blind readers from three model families, given only the traces, name the same f
s221c6afdeb.summary: The paper audits the reference agent shipped with the Vals Finance Agent Benchmark v2, finding run-to-run score variation and classifying failures by which layer's owner would fix them.
s221c6afdeb.why: Shows that leaderboard scores hide instability and cost variation in agents, and that failures need ownership-based diagnosis before deployment.

s4ef40d9b87.title: From Images to Grounded Edits: A Real-World Benchmark for Chinese Grammatical Error Correction in Handwritten Essays
s4ef40d9b87.description: arXiv:2611.17966v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Chinese Grammatical Error Correction (CGEC) is typically formulated as a text-to-text problem. While suitable for digital texts, this formulation falls short in real-world K-12 education, where AI-assisted corrections are expected directly on essay images, which are primarily handwritten and exhibit many irregularities. To bridge this gap, we introduce Grounded Chinese Grammatical Error Correction (G-CGEC), an image-to-grounded-edit task requiring systems to predict both corrections and their positions on essay images. We propose G-CGEC-Eval, a benchmark comprising real-world images of K-12 Chinese essays with fine-grained annotations.
