s894b840845.description: arXiv:2611.16937v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Typed System-1 (S1) decision models are increasingly deployed in LLM agents for routing, moderation, and authorization to cut inference cost, yet untrusted context can still manipulate typed outputs and alter execution branches. Unlike autoregressive System-2 (S2) models, S1 interfaces score dynamic rules and options without token-by-token decoding, mismatching attacks targeting text continuation or explicit override commands. We propose S1-Evo, a self-evolving framework tailored to S1's contract-based option competition and margin feedback. S1-Evo perturbs untrusted fields via contract-aware evidence channels to induce \emph{evidence competition} with original task evidence while preserving fact invariance. Offline on seed tasks, it opti
s894b840845.summary: S1-Evo proposes a self-evolving attack framework that manipulates typed System-1 decision models used for routing, moderation, and authorization in LLM agents.
s894b840845.why: Agents relying on typed decision models for authorization may be vulnerable to context-based manipulation, so these attacks matter for defense design.

s9411c87e03.title: Ballad: Bandit-Based LLM Routing for Automated Heuristic Discovery
s9411c87e03.description: arXiv:2611.17241v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Modern automated heuristic discovery (AHD) systems increasingly rival hand-crafted heuristics by leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) to iteratively mutate and refine solutions. A natural assumption is that more powerful and more expensive models consistently yield better heuristics. We challenge this empirically: across multiple NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems, we find no consistent advantage for larger, costlier models. This raises a deeper question: given a pool of LLMs spanning frontier and freely hosted or open-weight models, how should one adaptively select which model to invoke at each step of the search? The challenge is non-trivial. The optimal LLM may shift over the course of a run, and because one LLM's output se
s9411c87e03.summary: Ballad uses bandit-based routing across LLMs for automated heuristic discovery, finding no consistent advantage for larger, costlier models on NP-hard problems.
s9411c87e03.why: Engineers may be able to cut costs in automated optimization pipelines by routing among cheaper models rather than always using the most expensive one.

sd198ae4b3b.title: Fake News Detectors are Biased against Texts Generated by Large Language Models
sd198ae4b3b.description: arXiv:2309.08674v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The spread of fake news has emerged as a critical challenge, undermining trust and posing threats to society. In the era of Large Language Models (LLMs), the capability to generate believable fake content has intensified these concerns. In this study, we present a novel paradigm to evaluate fake news detectors in scenarios involving both human-written and LLM-generated misinformation. Intriguingly, our findings reveal a significant bias in many existing detectors: they are more prone to flagging LLM-generated content as fake news while often misclassifying human-written fake news as genuine. This unexpected bias appears to arise from distinct linguistic patterns inherent to LLM outputs. To address this, we introduce a mitigation str
sd198ae4b3b.summary: A study finds many fake news detectors are biased, more often flagging LLM-generated texts as fake than human-written ones.
sd198ae4b3b.why: Teams using automated detectors to filter content should check for bias against machine-generated text, since it can skew moderation outcomes.

s0cb4621f8f.title: Astraios: Parameter-Efficient Instruction Tuning Code Large Language Models
s0cb4621f8f.description: arXiv:2401.00788v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The high cost of full-parameter fine-tuning (FFT) of Large Language Models (LLMs) has led to a series of parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods. However, it remains unclear which methods provide the best cost-performance trade-off at different model scales. We introduce Astraios, a suite of 28 instruction-tuned OctoCoder models using 7 tuning methods and 4 model sizes up to 16 billion parameters. Through investigations across 5 tasks and 8 different datasets encompassing both code comprehension and code generation tasks, we find that FFT generally leads to the best downstream performance across all scales, and PEFT methods differ significantly in their efficacy based on the model scale. LoRA usually offers the most favorable
s0cb4621f8f.summary: Astraios is a suite of 28 instruction-tuned code models comparing seven parameter-efficient tuning methods across four model sizes up to 16 billion parameters.
s0cb4621f8f.why: The comparison of tuning methods across scales helps engineers pick cost-effective fine-tuning approaches for code models.

sbc27a3af6e.title: BigCodeBench: Benchmarking Code Generation with Diverse Function Calls and Complex Instructions
sbc27a3af6e.description: arXiv:2406.15877v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Task automation has been greatly empowered by the recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) via Python code, where the tasks ranging from software engineering development to general-purpose reasoning. While current benchmarks have shown that LLMs can solve tasks using programs like human developers, the majority of their evaluations are limited to short and self-contained algorithmic tasks or standalone function calls. Solving challenging and practical tasks requires the capability of utilizing diverse function calls as tools to efficiently implement functionalities like data analysis and web development. In addition, using multiple tools to solve a task needs compositional reasoning by accurately understanding complex instruc
sbc27a3af6e.summary: BigCodeBench is a benchmark testing code generation that uses diverse function calls and complex instructions, beyond short algorithmic tasks.
sbc27a3af6e.why: It offers a more realistic test of whether code models can use multiple tools for practical tasks, informing model selection.

s1fb0088e98.title: Benign Overfitting for Regression with Trained Two-Layer ReLU Networks
s1fb0088e98.description: arXiv:2410.06191v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the least-square regression problem with a two-layer fully-connected neural network, with ReLU activation function, trained by gradient flow. Our first result is a generalization result, that requires no assumptions on the underlying regression function or the noise other than that they are bounded. We operate in the neural tangent kernel regime, and our generalization result is developed via a decomposition of the excess risk into estimation and approximation errors, viewing gradient flow as an implicit regularizer. This decomposition in the context of neural networks is a novel perspective of gradient descent, and helps us avoid uniform convergence traps. In this work, we also establish that under the same setting, the tr
s1fb0088e98.summary: A theoretical paper proves generalization results for two-layer ReLU networks trained by gradient flow in the neural tangent kernel regime.

s20f7693f48.title: LEGAL-UQA: Testing Constitutional Question-Answering Systems for Urdu Speakers with a Parallel English-Urdu Benchmark
s20f7693f48.description: arXiv:2410.13013v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Legal information assistants could help Urdu speakers understand their constitutional rights, but building reliable systems requires test data and evaluation methods suited to the language. We present LEGAL-UQA, a parallel English-Urdu benchmark of 619 question-answer pairs linked to passages from Pakistan's Constitution. Each example includes the question, reference answer, and source passage in both languages. We evaluate two components separately: answering Urdu questions when the source passage is supplied, and retrieving the passage from which each question was generated. We also compare JEV, a decision model used as an automated judge, with human grades. The findings show that model rankings depend on how answer similarity is
s20f7693f48.summary: LEGAL-UQA is a parallel English-Urdu benchmark of 619 question-answer pairs based on Pakistan's Constitution, for testing constitutional question answering.
s20f7693f48.why: It shows how multilingual legal assistants need language-specific evaluation data, which teams building non-English RAG systems should account for.

s46ae32a332.title: AbFlowNet: Optimizing Antibody-Antigen Binding Energy via Diffusion-GFlowNet Fusion
s46ae32a332.description: arXiv:2505.12358v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Complementarity Determining Regions (CDRs) are critical segments of an antibody that facilitate binding to specific antigens. Current computational methods for CDR design utilize reconstruction losses and do not jointly optimize binding energy, a crucial metric for antibody efficacy. Rather, binding energy optimization is done through computationally expensive Online Reinforcement Learning (RL) pipelines rely heavily on unreliable binding energy estimators. In this paper, we propose AbFlowNet, a novel generative framework that integrates GFlowNet with Diffusion models. By framing each diffusion step as a state in the GFlowNet framework, AbFlowNet jointly optimizes standard diffusion losses and binding energy by directly incorporatin
s46ae32a332.summary: AbFlowNet combines diffusion and GFlowNet methods to jointly optimize antibody CDR design for antigen binding energy.

s25142c3821.title: Chi-Square Wavelet Graph Neural Networks for Heterogeneous Graph Anomaly Detection
s25142c3821.description: arXiv:2505.18934v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Graph Anomaly Detection (GAD) in heterogeneous networks presents unique challenges due to node and edge heterogeneity. Existing Graph Neural Network (GNN) methods primarily focus on homogeneous GAD and thus fail to address three key issues: (C1) Capturing abnormal signal and rich semantics across diverse meta-paths; (C2) Retaining high-frequency content in HIN dimension alignment; and (C3) Learning effectively from difficult anomaly samples with class imbalance. To overcome these, we propose ChiGAD, a spectral GNN framework based on a novel Chi-Square filter, inspired by the wavelet effectiveness in diverse domains. Specifically, ChiGAD consists of: (1) Multi-Graph Chi-Square Filter, which captures anomalous information via applying
s25142c3821.summary: ChiGAD is a spectral graph neural network framework for anomaly detection in heterogeneous graphs, addressing meta-path semantics and class imbalance.

s7f4346d078.title: Graph Your Own Prompt
s7f4346d078.description: arXiv:2509.23373v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose Graph Consistency Regularization (GCR), a novel framework that injects relational graph structures, derived from model predictions, into the learning process to promote class-aware, semantically meaningful feature representations. Functioning as a form of self-prompting, GCR enables the model to refine its internal structure using its own outputs. While deep networks learn rich representations, these often capture noisy inter-class similarities that contradict the model's predicted semantics. GCR addresses this issue by introducing parameter-free Graph Consistency Layers (GCLs) at arbitrary depths. Each GCL builds a batch-level feature similarity graph and aligns it with a global, class-aware masked prediction graph, deri
s7f4346d078.summary: Graph Consistency Regularization (GCR) injects relational graph structure derived from model predictions into training to produce more class-aware representations.

sffdcd27fa7.title: BigCodeArena: Unveiling More Reliable Human Preferences in Code Generation via Execution
sffdcd27fa7.description: arXiv:2510.08697v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Crowdsourced model evaluation platforms, such as Chatbot Arena, enable real-time evaluation from human perspectives to assess the quality of model responses. In the coding domain, manually examining the quality of LLM-generated content is extremely challenging, as it requires understanding long chunks of raw code and deliberately simulating code execution. To this end, we introduce BigCodeArena, an open human evaluation platform for code generation backed by a comprehensive and on-the-fly execution environment. Built on top of Chatbot Arena, BigCodeArena enables the execution of LLM-generated code and allows humans to interact with the execution process and outcomes. We collected over 14,000 raw code-centric conversation sessions ac
sffdcd27fa7.summary: BigCodeArena is an open human evaluation platform for code generation that runs generated code on the fly so raters can judge execution results.
sffdcd27fa7.why: Execution-based human preference evaluation may give more reliable model comparisons for coding tasks than reading raw code.

se38ea0614b.title: Manifold Approximation leads to Robust Kernel Alignment
se38ea0614b.description: arXiv:2510.22953v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Centered kernel alignment (CKA) is a popular metric for comparing representations, determining equivalence of networks, and conducting neuroscience research. However, CKA does not account for the underlying manifold and relies on numerous heuristics that cause it to behave differently at different scales of data. In this work, we propose Manifold-approximated Kernel Alignment (MKA), which incorporates manifold geometry (i.e., local neighborhood) into the alignment task. We derive a theoretical framework for MKA. Our construction removes representation-dependent degree weighting, yields a closed-form alignment score, and gives each row a probabilistic interpretation as a local Markov transition distribution. We further establish kern
se38ea0614b.summary: Manifold-approximated Kernel Alignment (MKA) modifies centered kernel alignment to account for data manifold geometry, aiming for more robust representation comparisons.

s05531200a1.title: E0: Expressive Fine-Grained Discrete Action Prediction for Vision-Language-Action Models via Tweedie Discrete Diffusion
s05531200a1.description: arXiv:2511.21542v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models offer a unified framework for robotic manipulation by integrating visual perception, language understanding, and control generation. However, existing VLA systems still struggle to generalize across diverse tasks, scenes, and camera viewpoints, and often produce coarse or unstable actions. We argue that these limitations are closely tied to the structural properties of actions in VLA settings, including the inherent multi-peaked nature of action distributions, the token-based symbolic reasoning of pretrained VLM/VLA backbones, and the effective finite resolution imposed by real-world robotic control. Motivated by these properties, we introduce E0, a tweedie discrete diffusion framework that formul
s05531200a1.summary: E0 proposes discrete diffusion for fine-grained action prediction in vision-language-action robotics models to produce more stable, expressive actions.
s05531200a1.why: Robotics teams building VLA systems may find more stable action outputs useful, though the text gives no benchmark results.

s4fe0a8211b.title: Model-Free Assessment of Simulator Fidelity via Quantile Curves
s4fe0a8211b.description: arXiv:2512.05024v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: As generative AI models are increasingly used to simulate real-world systems, quantifying the ``sim-to-real'' gap is critical. For each input setting of interest -- which we call a \emph{scenario}, such as a survey question or operating condition -- the real and simulated systems are associated with unobserved latent population parameters, and their discrepancy varies across scenarios. A fundamental challenge is that, for any given scenario, this discrepancy cannot be observed directly, since both systems are accessible only through finite samples, often of heterogeneous sizes across scenarios. Standard predictive inference methods are therefore ill-suited, as they quantify uncertainty in observable outputs rather than latent popula
s4fe0a8211b.summary: Researchers propose a model-free method using quantile curves to assess how well simulators match real systems across scenarios, quantifying the sim-to-real gap.
s4fe0a8211b.why: Gives teams a way to measure simulator fidelity without needing direct observations of the real system's latent parameters.

s2201a7ff34.title: NEAT: Neighborhood-Guided, Efficient, Autoregressive Set Transformer for 3D Molecular Generation
s2201a7ff34.description: arXiv:2512.05844v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Transformer-based autoregressive models offer an efficient alternative to diffusion- and flow-based approaches for generating 3D molecules. One challenge remains: standard transformer architectures require a sequential ordering of tokens, which is not inherently defined for the atoms in a molecule. Prior works have addressed this by using canonical atom orderings. However, these approaches are not permutation invariant w.r.t. atoms and bias next-token prediction towards ordering conventions. We overcome this limitation by introducing a novel neighborhood-guided training strategy. Our model, NEAT (Neighborhood-Guided, Efficient, Autoregressive Set Transformer) treats molecular graphs as sets of atoms and learns an order-agnostic dist
s2201a7ff34.summary: Researchers introduce NEAT, a neighborhood-guided autoregressive set transformer that generates 3D molecules without relying on canonical atom orderings.
s2201a7ff34.why: Offers an efficient transformer alternative to diffusion models for 3D molecule generation that is permutation invariant over atoms.

sf7f0c55c64.title: Vision-language models lag human performance on physical dynamics and intent reasoning
sf7f0c55c64.description: arXiv:2601.01547v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Spatial intelligence is central to embodied cognition, yet contemporary AI systems still struggle to reason about physical interactions in open-world human environments. Despite strong performance on controlled benchmarks, vision-language models often fail to jointly model physical dynamics, reference frames, and the latent human intentions that drive spatial change. We introduce Teleo-Spatial Intelligence (TSI), which captures an important aspect of spatial reasoning: integrating physical dynamics and action goals to reason about actions and their spatial consequences. To evaluate TSI, we present EscherVerse, a large-scale open-world resource built from 11,328 real-world videos, including an 8,000-example benchmark and a 35,963-exa
sf7f0c55c64.summary: Researchers introduce Teleo-Spatial Intelligence, a benchmark finding vision-language models lag humans at reasoning about physical dynamics and human intent.
sf7f0c55c64.why: Highlights a gap in VLM spatial and intent reasoning that matters for embodied and real-world human-environment applications.

s139fdfdfa1.title: ISLA: Ensemble learning and domain adaptation for generalizable acute ischemic stroke lesion segmentation in diffusion MRI with clinical validation
s139fdfdfa1.description: arXiv:2601.08732v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Accurate segmentation of acute ischemic stroke (AIS) lesions on MRI is essential for clinical decision-making. Deep learning methods offer a promising approach to automating this task. However, they often generalize poorly to unseen clinical sites, and few AIS lesion segmentation methods have been externally validated. In this study, we propose $\mathit{ISLA}$ (Ischemic Stroke Lesion Analyzer), a framework for AIS lesion segmentation built on the design principles of $\mathit{nnU\text{-}Net}$. $\mathit{ISLA}$ combines attention modules, deep supervision, and ensemble learning across different input resolutions, convolutional block types, and loss functions. We also introduce $\mathit{ISLA\text{-}MT}$, a variant that leverages unlabe
s139fdfdfa1.summary: Researchers present ISLA, an ensemble nnU-Net-based framework for acute ischemic stroke lesion segmentation in diffusion MRI, aimed at generalizing to unseen clinical sites.
s139fdfdfa1.why: Addresses poor generalization of medical segmentation models across clinical sites, with external clinical validation.

s4d86dbf728.title: Tracing 3D Anatomy in 2D Strokes: Can Projection-Derived Masks Replace 3D Segmentation for Cervical Spine Fracture Recognition?
s4d86dbf728.description: arXiv:2601.15235v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Cervical spine fractures require rapid and accurate diagnosis, yet automatic CT interpretation remains challenging as subtle injuries must be assessed across large 3D volumes. We ask whether full 3D vertebra segmentation is necessary for fracture recognition, or whether vertebra masks approximated from 2D projections preserve sufficient diagnostic context. In the proposed multi-stage pipeline, a YOLOv8 detector localizes the cervical spine from multi-view variance projections (3D mean Intersection over Union 94.45%). Multi-label vertebra segmentation is performed with a DenseNet121-Unet on energy-based sagittal and coronal projections (mean Dice 87.86%). The predicted 2D masks are back-projected and fused into approximate 3D masks p
s4d86dbf728.summary: Researchers test whether masks approximated from 2D projections can replace full 3D vertebra segmentation for detecting cervical spine fractures in CT.
s4d86dbf728.why: Suggests a potentially cheaper pipeline for CT fracture recognition that avoids full 3D segmentation.

sfb2e5fb86a.title: The Alignment Curse: Modality Alignment Supercharges Audio Attacks via Text Transfer
sfb2e5fb86a.description: arXiv:2602.02557v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recent advances in end-to-end trained omni-models have substantially improved audio capabilities by strengthening text-audio modality alignment. However, whether such alignment inadvertently facilitates the transfer of safety vulnerabilities across modalities remains underexplored. This question is critical as text-based jailbreak attacks are considerably more mature than audio-based ones; if they transfer systematically, current audio safety evaluations may underestimate risks originating from the text modality. In this paper, we introduce the Alignment Curse, a formally characterized and empirically validated principle showing that stronger modality alignment enables more effective transfer of attacks from text to audio, revealing
sfb2e5fb86a.summary: Researchers show that modality alignment in end-to-end omni-models can let text-based jailbreak attacks transfer to audio, potentially underestimating audio-related risks.
sfb2e5fb86a.why: Suggests current audio safety evaluations may miss risks inherited from text, so teams deploying omni-models should test cross-modal attacks.

s9968513c74.title: ROCKET: Rapid Optimization via Calibration-guided Knapsack Enhanced Truncation for Efficient Model Compression
s9968513c74.description: arXiv:2602.11008v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present ROCKET, a training-free model compression method that achieves state-of-the-art performance in comparison with factorization, structured-sparsification and dynamic compression baselines. Operating under a global compression budget, ROCKET comprises two key innovations: First, it formulates layer-wise compression allocation as a multi-choice knapsack problem, selecting the optimal compression level for each layer to minimize total reconstruction error while adhering to a target model size. Second, it introduces a single-step sparse matrix factorization inspired by dictionary learning: using only a small calibration set, it sparsifies weight coefficients based on activation-weights sensitivity and then updates the dictionar
s9968513c74.summary: ROCKET is a training-free model compression method that allocates layer-wise compression via a multi-choice knapsack formulation under a global size budget.
s9968513c74.why: Offers a training-free way to compress models to a target size while minimizing reconstruction error, reducing retraining costs.

s5b41758b44.title: ScrapeGraphAI-100k: Dataset for Schema-Constrained LLM Generation
s5b41758b44.description: arXiv:2602.15189v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Producing output that conforms to a specified JSON schema underlies tool use, structured extraction, and knowledge base construction in modern large language models. Despite this centrality, public datasets for the task remain small, synthetic, or text-only, and rarely pair real page content with the prompts and schemas used in practice. We introduce ScrapeGraphAI-100k, 93,695 schema-constrained extraction events collected via opt-out ScrapeGraphAI telemetry in Q2--Q3 2025, deduplicated and balanced by schema from 9M raw events. The corpus spans 25,453 unique schemas, across 15 named languages, with English covering 89% of detected content. Each instance pairs Markdown-converted page content with a prompt, schema, LLM response, and
s5b41758b44.summary: Researchers release ScrapeGraphAI-100k, a dataset of 93,695 schema-constrained extraction events pairing real web page content with JSON schemas and prompts.
s5b41758b44.why: Provides realistic, real-world data for training and evaluating structured JSON output from LLMs.

s1e2b9e70fe.title: ESENSC: A Polynomial-Time Axiomatic Alternative to SHAP
s1e2b9e70fe.description: arXiv:2603.00496v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose ESENSC, a computationally efficient and theoretically grounded alternative to SHAP. ESENSC is a deterministic, closed-form attribution rule that requires only linearly many coalition-value evaluations, satisfies the null-player property, and admits an axiomatic characterization based on efficiency, a restricted form of differential marginality, and explicit computational constraints.Empirically, on tabular prediction tasks using neural network and XGBoost models, ESENSC shows close agreement with exact SHAP in both attribution magnitude and feature rankings while requiring substantially less computation. Under the evaluated settings, it compares favorably with widely used sampling-based SHAP approximations. While exact SH
s1e2b9e70fe.summary: Researchers propose ESENSC, a deterministic closed-form feature attribution rule that approximates SHAP values using linearly many coalition evaluations.
s1e2b9e70fe.why: Offers a faster, deterministic alternative to SHAP for explaining tabular model predictions, with close agreement to exact SHAP.

sc40978f2ae.title: ViroGym: Realistic Large-Scale Benchmarks for Evaluating Viral Proteins
sc40978f2ae.description: arXiv:2603.06740v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Protein language models (pLMs) have shown strong potential for zero-shot prediction of missense variant effects, yet systematic benchmarking on viral proteins remains limited, a critical gap given the need for proactive tools that can anticipate emerging mutations ahead of experimental validation. Here we introduce ViroGym, a comprehensive benchmark evaluating pLMs across three tasks: 79 deep mutational scanning (DMS) assays covering eukaryotic viruses with 552,065 mutated sequences across 7 phenotypic readouts, 21 influenza neutralisation tasks, and a real-world pandemic prediction task for SARS-CoV-2. We benchmark well-established pLMs on fitness landscapes, antigenic diversity, and pandemic forecasting, and find that the ProGen2
sc40978f2ae.summary: Researchers introduce ViroGym, a large benchmark evaluating protein language models on viral protein variant effect prediction across multiple tasks.
sc40978f2ae.why: Provides a systematic benchmark for judging whether protein models are reliable for anticipating viral mutations.

se97dca5666.title: Efficiently Aligning Draft Models via Parameter- and Data-Efficient Adaptation
se97dca5666.description: arXiv:2603.09527v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates LLM inference but suffers from performance degradation when target models are fine-tuned for specific domains. A naive solution is to retrain draft models for every target model, which is costly and inefficient. To address this, we introduce a practical parameter- and data-efficient framework named Efficient Draft Adaptation, abbreviated as EDA, for efficiently adapting draft models. EDA introduces three innovations: (1) a decoupled architecture that utilizes shared and private components to model the shared and target-specific output distributions separately, enabling parameter-efficient adaptation by updating only the lightweight private component; (2) a data regeneration strategy that utilizes the
se97dca5666.summary: Researchers propose Efficient Draft Adaptation (EDA), a parameter- and data-efficient framework for adapting speculative decoding draft models to fine-tuned target models.
se97dca5666.why: Lets teams keep speculative decoding speedups after domain fine-tuning without costly full draft model retraining.

sd927b02da7.title: A Variational Latent Equilibrium for Learning in Neuronal Circuits
sd927b02da7.description: arXiv:2603.09600v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Brains remain unrivaled in their ability to recognize and generate complex spatiotemporal patterns. While AI is able to reproduce some of these capabilities, deep learning algorithms remain largely at odds with our current understanding of brain circuitry and dynamics. This is prominently the case for backpropagation through time (BPTT), the go-to algorithm for learning complex temporal dependencies. In this work we propose a general formalism to approximate BPTT in a controlled, biologically plausible manner. Our approach builds on, unifies and extends several previous approaches to local, time-continuous, phase-free spatiotemporal credit assignment based on principles of energy conservation and extremal action. Our starting point
sd927b02da7.summary: Researchers propose a biologically plausible formalism that approximates backpropagation through time in neuronal circuits using a variational latent equilibrium approach.
sd927b02da7.why: Foundational neuroscience-inspired learning research with limited direct near-term applicability for engineering teams.

s671caa5958.title: Comparative Analysis of 3D Convolutional and 2.5D Slice-Conditioned U-Net Architectures for MRI Super-Resolution via Elucidated Diffusion Models
s671caa5958.description: arXiv:2603.14667v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) super-resolution (SR) methods that computationally enhance low-resolution acquisitions offer a software alternative to higher-field scanners. We study an elucidated diffusion model (EDM) framework for 2x in-plane brain MRI SR and compare two U-Net backbones: (i) a 3D convolutional U-Net that processes volumetric patches and (ii) a 2.5D slice-conditioned U-Net that super-resolves each slice while conditioning on its two neighbouring slices. All models are trained from scratch to convergence on 500 subjects of the NKI cohort of FOMO60K, with a separate 6-subject validation set for checkpoint selection, and evaluated on 70 held-out subjects with subject-level statistics against baselines (EDSR, Swin2SR,
s671caa5958.summary: Researchers compare 3D convolutional and 2.5D slice-conditioned U-Net backbones for 2x brain MRI super-resolution using elucidated diffusion models.
s671caa5958.why: Compares architecture tradeoffs for diffusion-based MRI enhancement, a software alternative to higher-field scanners.

s8d5d1fa36c.title: FlashSampling: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Sampling
s8d5d1fa36c.description: arXiv:2603.15854v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Sampling from a categorical distribution is mathematically simple, but in large-vocabulary decoding, it often triggers extra memory traffic and extra kernels after the LM head. We present FlashSampling, an exact sampling primitive that fuses sampling into the LM-head matmul and never materializes the logits tensor in HBM. The method is simple: compute logits tile-by-tile on chip, add Gumbel noise, keep only one maximizer per row and per vocabulary tile, and finish with a small reduction over tiles. In tensor-parallel decoding, FlashSampling replaces the all-gather of logits with streaming peer-to-peer writes: This overlaps GPU-to-GPU communication with computation and HBM loads across up to 8 GPUs, with near-ideal scaling at large b
s8d5d1fa36c.summary: Researchers present FlashSampling, an exact sampling primitive that fuses categorical sampling into the LM-head matmul without materializing the logits tensor in HBM.
s8d5d1fa36c.why: Reduces memory traffic and kernel launches in large-vocabulary LLM decoding, directly relevant to inference performance work.

s5b100727fd.title: Generative machine learning for protein design
s5b100727fd.description: arXiv:2603.26378v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Designing proteins with specific biological functions is of considerable interest for both the development of new therapeutics and the engineering of enzymes, yet achieving the intended activity remains challenging. Generative artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a powerful tool to explore the vast space of possible designs by learning from protein sequence and structural data. Here, we review 59 generative approaches across six protein design tasks, including sequence generation, backbone generation, structure-conditioned sequence design, joint sequence-structure design, motif scaffolding, and binder and antibody design. We outline common generative approaches and protein representations and discuss how structural constraint
s5b100727fd.summary: A review of 59 generative AI approaches across six protein design tasks, covering sequence, backbone, and structure-conditioned generation.
s5b100727fd.why: Gives a consolidated map of generative protein design methods for teams evaluating tools for therapeutics or enzyme engineering.

s2e83590f28.title: Pruning Extensions and Efficiency Trade-Offs for Sustainable Time Series Classification
s2e83590f28.description: arXiv:2604.07953v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Time series classification (TSC) at scale requires balancing predictive performance against resource consumption, which is subject to the given data, model, and hardware. This paper introduces a multi-dimensional evaluation framework that allows for explicitly benchmarking and exploring the resource-versus-quality trade-offs in TSC. To improve efficiency, we present a pruning strategy with bounded error for leading hybrid classifiers - Hydra and Quant - and moreover propose Hydrant, a novel extension that integrates interval representations with random convolutions and dictionary learning. With over 4000 evaluated configurations across 20 MONSTER datasets, 10 methods, and three compute setups, we systematically analyze how model des
s2e83590f28.summary: Researchers propose a multi-dimensional framework for benchmarking resource-versus-quality trade-offs in time series classification, plus a bounded-error pruning strategy for Hydra and Quant.
s2e83590f28.why: Offers practical methods to cut compute for time series classifiers at scale, which matters when serving costs and energy budgets are constraints.

sf88e7ab244.title: Minimizing classical resources in variational measurement-based quantum computation for generative modeling
sf88e7ab244.description: arXiv:2604.11578v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Measurement-based quantum computation (MBQC) is a framework for quantum information processing in which a computational task is carried out through one-qubit measurements on a highly entangled resource state. Due to the indeterminacy of the outcomes of a quantum measurement, the random outcomes of these operations, if not corrected, yield a variational quantum channel family. Traditionally, this randomness is corrected through classical processing in order to ensure deterministic unitary computations. Recently, variational measurement-based quantum computation (VMBQC) has been introduced to exploit this measurement-induced randomness to gain an advantage in generative modeling. A limitation of this approach is that the corresponding
sf88e7ab244.summary: Researchers study minimizing classical processing in variational measurement-based quantum computation for generative modeling.

scab7db3616.title: Generating Concept Lexicalizations via Dictionary-Based Cross-Lingual Sense Projection
scab7db3616.description: arXiv:2604.14397v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the task of automatically expanding WordNet-style lexical resources to new languages through sense generation. We generate senses by associating target-language lemmas with existing lexical concepts via semantic projection. Given a sense-tagged English corpus and its translation, our method projects the annotated synsets onto aligned target-language tokens and assigns the corresponding lemmas to those synsets. To generate alignments and ensure their quality, we augment a pretrained base aligner with a bilingual dictionary, which is also used to filter incorrect sense projections. We evaluate the method on multiple languages, comparing it to prior methods, as well as dictionary-based and large language model baselines. Resul
scab7db3616.summary: Researchers present a method that expands WordNet-style lexical resources to new languages by projecting senses across aligned corpora using a bilingual dictionary.
scab7db3616.why: Relevant mainly to teams building multilingual NLP resources, though the text gives limited detail on results.

s08d6bc2d2c.title: CPGRec+: A Balance-oriented Framework for Personalized Video Game Recommendations
s08d6bc2d2c.description: arXiv:2604.14586v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The rapid expansion of gaming industry requires advanced recommender systems tailored to its dynamic landscape. Existing Graph Neural Network (GNN)-based methods primarily prioritize accuracy over diversity, overlooking their inherent trade-off. To address this, we previously proposed CPGRec, a balance-oriented gaming recommender system. However, CPGRec fails to account for critical disparities in player-game interactions, which carry varying significance in reflecting players' personal preferences and may exacerbate over-smoothness issues inherent in GNN-based models. Moreover, existing approaches underutilize the reasoning capabilities and extensive knowledge of large language models (LLMs) in addressing these limitations. To brid
s08d6bc2d2c.summary: Researchers extend CPGRec into CPGRec+, a graph-based video game recommender that balances accuracy and diversity while weighting player-game interactions differently.

sacda27fe23.title: Screen Before You Interpret: A Portable Validity Screen for Benchmark-Based LLM Confidence Signals
sacda27fe23.description: arXiv:2604.17714v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: LLM confidence signals drive abstention, routing and escalation, yet evaluations rarely check whether a signal varies with correctness before computing metrics on it. Clinical personality assessment handles the analogous problem by screening response validity before interpreting substantive scales. We specify a portable screen in that tradition. From the correctness-by-confidence table it computes the rate of high confidence on errors (L), the rate of low confidence on correct answers (Fp), and their contrast (RBS, equal to minus Youden's J). It adds no new statistics: it separates blanket confidence, blanket withdrawal and inversion, attaches interval guards, and calls a signal Valid only when it measurably tracks correctness. On 2
sacda27fe23.summary: Researchers propose a portable validity screen that checks whether LLM confidence signals actually vary with correctness before metrics are computed on them.
sacda27fe23.why: Teams using LLM confidence for abstention or escalation can use this check to avoid acting on signals that don't track correctness.

s4cd40da2f8.title: BoostLoRA: Growing Effective Rank by Boosting Adapters
s4cd40da2f8.description: arXiv:2604.27308v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods face a tradeoff between adapter size and expressivity: ultra-low-parameter adapters are confined to fixed low-rank subspaces, capping performance even with extended training. We propose BoostLoRA, a gradient-boosting framework that overcomes this limit by iteratively training and merging minimal adapters on the examples the current model gets wrong. A ROTATE SVD basis strategy assigns each round to an orthogonal subspace, so cumulative effective rank grows linearly with the number of rounds while each adapter remains ultra-low-rank. After merging, adapters are discarded, leaving zero inference overhead. On Qwen2.5-3B, BoostLoRA reaches 89.1% on GSM8K and 68.8% on MATH-500, surpassing bo
s4cd40da2f8.summary: Researchers introduce BoostLoRA, a gradient-boosting approach that iteratively trains and merges minimal adapters on mispredicted examples to grow effective rank in parameter-efficient fine-tuning.
s4cd40da2f8.why: Suggests a way to raise expressivity of ultra-low-parameter fine-tuning adapters without increasing adapter size per round.

s28d8252584.title: Time series causal discovery with variable lags
s28d8252584.description: arXiv:2605.04081v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Causal Bayesian Networks (CBNs) are a powerful tool for reasoning under uncertainty about complex real-world problems. Such problems evolve over time, responding to external shocks as they occur. To support decision-making, CBNs require a cause-and-effect map of the variables under consideration, known as the network's structure. Learning the graphical structure of a causal model from data remains challenging; learning it from time-series data is even harder because dependencies may arise at different time lags. We construct a method that jointly learns a temporal ordering and a dominant lag for each selected ordered variable pair. Our contribution is a decomposable BIC-style objective score for mixed data that combines node-specifi
s28d8252584.summary: Researchers present a method for learning causal structure from time-series data where dependencies occur at variable time lags.

sfe1d34f9b4.title: Exposing and Mitigating Temporal Attack in Deepfake Video Detection
sfe1d34f9b4.description: arXiv:2605.07398v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: While spatiotemporal deepfake detectors achieve high AUC, our experiments reveal their susceptibility to evasion attacks. These models tend to overfit on fragile temporal spectrum cues, rather than learning robust semantic causality. To mitigate this vulnerability, we propose SpInShield, a temporal spectral-invariant defense framework explicitly designed to decouple semantic motion from manipulatable spectral artifacts. We propose a learnable spectral adversary that dynamically synthesizes severe spectral deformations, simulating extreme attack scenarios. By employing a shortcut suppression optimization strategy, SpInShield compels the encoder to extract reliable forensic cues while purging unstable spectral statistics from the late
sfe1d34f9b4.summary: Researchers show spatiotemporal deepfake detectors overfit to fragile temporal spectrum cues and propose SpInShield, a spectral-invariant defense against evasion attacks.
sfe1d34f9b4.why: Highlights that high-AUC deepfake detectors can be easily evaded, relevant to teams deploying detection in adversarial settings.

sa1970c439d.title: Hybrid Mechanical and Agentic Specification Inference
sa1970c439d.description: arXiv:2605.10005v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Adoption of formal verification has long been hindered by the cost of manual specification. To prove high-level properties, one must also write contracts for supporting functions, many of which are mechanical and low-level. Specification inference automatically derives such contracts from the program. We present a hybrid of mechanical and agentic inference for Move, a smart contract language, integrated into its verifier, the Move Prover. A large language model (LLM) agent drives inference and verification through a tool that calls the Move Prover and derives specifications from code by weakest-precondition (WP) analysis. We evaluate our approach on 26 targets, 24 of them extracted from public Move functions of the Aptos framework t
sa1970c439d.summary: Researchers describe a hybrid of mechanical and LLM-agent specification inference for Move smart contracts, integrated into the Move Prover verifier.
sa1970c439d.why: Shows an agentic LLM loop driving formal verification tooling, which may reduce the manual cost of writing contracts for smart contract teams.

s49f09a08f2.title: Wavelet Flow Matching for Multi-Scale Physics Emulation
s49f09a08f2.description: arXiv:2605.16573v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Accurate emulation of multi-scale physical systems governed by PDEs demands models that remain stable over long autoregressive rollouts while preserving fine-scale structures. Deterministic emulators produce overly smoothed predictions, while generative approaches better capture details but are costly. Latent-space generative models have emerged as a compromise but with the additional cost of separately pre-trained autoencoders. We propose Wavelet Flow Matching (WFM), a generative emulator that overcomes current trade-offs between cost and skill by performing optimal-transport flow matching directly in the multi-scale wavelet space. Rather than learning a latent compression, WFM leverages the hierarchical structure of a U-Net to joi
s49f09a08f2.summary: Researchers propose Wavelet Flow Matching, a generative emulator for multi-scale PDE physics that aims to avoid the cost of separately pre-trained autoencoders.

sf39a6534a2.title: TransitLM: A Large-Scale Dataset and Benchmark for Map-Free Transit Route Generation
sf39a6534a2.description: arXiv:2605.22355v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Public transit route planning traditionally depends on structured map infrastructure and complex routing engines, and no existing dataset supports training models to bypass this dependency. We present TransitLM, a large-scale dataset of nearly 13 million transit route planning records from four Chinese cities covering 120,845 stations and 13,666 lines, released as a continual pre-training corpus and benchmark data for three evaluation tasks with complementary metrics. Experiments show that an LLM trained on TransitLM produces structurally valid routes at high accuracy and implicitly grounds arbitrary GPS coordinates to appropriate stations without any explicit mapping. These results demonstrate that transit route planning can be lea
sf39a6534a2.summary: Researchers release TransitLM, a dataset of about 13 million transit route records from four Chinese cities for training LLMs to generate routes without map infrastructure.
sf39a6534a2.why: Provides a large benchmark and continual pre-training corpus for LLM-based route generation, though the text gives limited evaluation detail.

s805c6fa92a.title: DeltaBox: Millisecond-Scale Sandbox Checkpoint and Rollback for Stateful AI Agents
s805c6fa92a.description: arXiv:2605.22781v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Emerging LLM-powered AI agent workloads, such as test-time tree search and reinforcement learning (RL), require high-frequency state exploration, relying on rapid checkpoint/restore (C/R) of the complete sandbox state, including files and process state. Existing mechanisms duplicate the entire state, causing hundreds of milliseconds to seconds of latency per C/R, which severely bottlenecks deep search and large-scale fan-outs. We observe that consecutive sandbox states between checkpoints differ only marginally. Therefore, instead of full duplication, a sandbox should only duplicate the changes between consecutive checkpoints (Key Insight), yet the lack of OS support makes this hard to realize. We propose a new OS-level abstraction,
s805c6fa92a.summary: Researchers introduce DeltaBox, a sandbox checkpoint and rollback system that stores only state differences to reach millisecond-scale restores for stateful AI agents.
s805c6fa92a.why: Faster sandbox checkpoint and restore could remove a bottleneck for agent tree search and RL workloads that need many state branches.

s52e8f65e2b.title: Larch: Learned Query Optimization for Semantic Predicates
s52e8f65e2b.description: arXiv:2606.07923v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: With the advent of Large Language Models (LLMs), many database systems introduced semantic operators that enabled analytical queries over unstructured data (e.g. text, images, videos). Semantic operators typically incur high inference costs and latencies making semantic (AI) SQL queries challenging to apply on large scale datasets. At the same time, their semantic nature leads database engines to treat them as black boxes, making AISQL queries difficult to optimize. In this paper, we introduce Larch, a framework for optimizing the execution of semantic filters in AI SQL queries. Larch was inspired by two key observations: i) the high latency of semantic operators leaves significant room for computationally-heavy runtime optimization
s52e8f65e2b.summary: Researchers present Larch, a learned query optimizer for semantic predicates in AI SQL queries that call costly LLM-based semantic operators.
s52e8f65e2b.why: Addresses high inference cost of semantic operators in database queries, which matters to teams running LLM-powered analytics at scale.

se012f8559c.title: QVal: Evaluating Dense Supervision Signals for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
se012f8559c.description: arXiv:2606.32034v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: LLM agents increasingly act over long horizons, where outcome-only rewards say little about which intermediate actions were good. Dense supervision methods address this by scoring intermediate steps, but they are usually evaluated through the downstream performance of a full training pipeline. This is expensive, confounds signal quality with other training choices, and means that methods are rarely compared on common ground. We introduce QVal, a training-free testbed that measures the $Q$-alignment of a dense signal: whether it orders the candidate actions in each state the same way as their returns under a reference policy do. We benchmark 21 methods from seven families with six open-weight backbones in four environments. Simple pr
se012f8559c.summary: Researchers introduce QVal, a training-free testbed that measures how well dense supervision signals order intermediate steps for long-horizon LLM agents.
se012f8559c.why: Offers a cheaper way to compare dense reward signals for agent training without running full training pipelines.

s793f1ad820.title: When Simpler Is Better: Evaluating Translation Pipelines for Medieval Latin Manuscripts
s793f1ad820.description: arXiv:2607.03836v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Despite remarkable progress in machine translation, Vision Language Models (VLMs) struggle on historical manuscripts, a domain that stresses core Natural Language Processing (NLP) capabilities: low-resource transliteration, archaic vocabulary, and noisy input signals. We present a systematic framework for evaluating the full image-to-translation pipeline on medieval Latin manuscripts, a setting in which scribal shorthand, ligatures, and parchment degradation expose failure modes that are invisible in clean-text benchmarks. Benchmarking on the CATMuS Latin dataset reveals a specialization gap: domain-specific Optical Character Recognition (OCR) models reduce character error rate by up to 4.3$\times$ compared to general-purpose VLMs,
s793f1ad820.summary: Researchers evaluate image-to-translation pipelines for medieval Latin manuscripts, finding that simpler approaches can outperform more complex ones on vision-language tasks.
s793f1ad820.why: Shows vision-language models struggle on noisy historical documents, a caution for OCR and translation pipelines in low-resource domains.

se8cc1f2209.title: URSA: Chemistry-Aware Benchmark for Utilitarian Retrosynthesis Assessment
se8cc1f2209.description: arXiv:2607.04688v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Synthesis planning aiming to find pathways of reactions for a target molecule is one of the most important and challenging tasks in drug discovery. Recent progress has produced both specialized deep-learning retrosynthesis systems and general-purpose large language models, but objective comparison remains difficult due to the lack of flexible, chemically interpretable benchmarking protocols. In the current study, we are introducing the URSA (Utilitarian RetroSynthesis Assessment) evaluation framework that provides the opportunity to benchmark the synthetic routes not only from a formal perspective, such as convergence to commercially available starting materials, but also from a chemical plausibility perspective, mimicking the way e
se8cc1f2209.summary: Researchers introduced URSA, a chemistry-aware benchmark framework for evaluating retrosynthesis planning systems, including deep-learning tools and general-purpose LLMs.
se8cc1f2209.why: It offers a chemically interpretable way to compare retrosynthesis systems, which helps teams choose tools for drug discovery workflows.

s059c443f23.title: Input Pathways Shape Few-Shot, Not Zero-Shot, Binding in Tiny Transformers: A Fully-Enumerable Study
s059c443f23.description: arXiv:2607.04926v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: How does the way information reaches a transformer -- as symbolic tokens, a clean per-factor "oracle" code, or an entangled perceptual vector -- shape whether it binds that information compositionally? We study ~6-10K-parameter transformers on finite factored worlds enumerated exhaustively, so every measurement covers the whole input space and the informative routes are information-matched (exact Bayes ceiling 1.0). Four findings. (1) Endpoint invariance: on held-out binding queries no informative route reaches converged zero-shot composition -- each ends at or below chance, so the failure reflects inductive bias under a lookup-sufficient objective, not missing information. It also holds with the state in its own sequence position r
s059c443f23.summary: A study of ~6-10K-parameter transformers on exhaustively enumerated factored worlds finds input encoding affects few-shot but not zero-shot compositional binding.

s067e89c697.title: REFORGE: A Method for Benchmarking LLMs' Reverse Engineering Capabilities in Decompiled Binary Function Naming
s067e89c697.description: arXiv:2607.07738v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to reverse-engineering tasks, and recent threat-intelligence reporting shows them operating inside live offensive-security workflows. Claims about their capability, however, outpace our ability to measure it. Existing benchmarks for LLM-assisted binary analysis treat the construction of function-level ground truth as a solved pre-processing step and report accuracy without disclosing how many functions were reliably evaluable. We argue that the principal obstacle to fair evaluation is not model capability but the reliability of binary-to-source alignment under compiler optimization. This paper presents Reforge, a provenance-tracked pipeline that constructs function-level ground t
s067e89c697.summary: Researchers propose REFORGE, a method for benchmarking LLMs on naming decompiled binary functions, arguing existing benchmarks skip reliable ground-truth construction.
s067e89c697.why: Current LLM reverse-engineering accuracy claims may overstate capability because evaluable function counts are rarely disclosed, affecting security tool assessments.

s8c0b3ea0b2.title: CPM-MultiAgent: A CPM-Grounded Appraisal Framework for Simulating Dynamic Patient Emotional Evolution in Healthcare Dialogue
s8c0b3ea0b2.description: arXiv:2607.07824v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) enable patient simulation for healthcare communication training, where learners practice responding to clinical information, concerns, and emotional reactions. However, existing patient simulation and affective dialogue systems often represent patient emotions as static attributes or focus on recognizing emotions and generating empathetic responses. They provide limited support for modeling how a simulated patient's emotional state evolves in response to a healthcare professional's communication. Changes in patient emotion constitute interactional feedback that learners must recognize and respond to across dialogue turns. We draw on the Component Process Model (CPM), a psychological theory that explains
s8c0b3ea0b2.summary: CPM-MultiAgent is a framework for simulating how a virtual patient's emotions evolve across healthcare dialogue, aimed at communication training.

s4db670c3f0.title: Courteous Anticipation: Improving Long-Lived Task Planning in Persistent Shared Environments
s4db670c3f0.description: arXiv:2607.20289v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider a task planning scenario in which robots sharing a persistent environment are assigned tasks one at a time from a held-out sequence. Standard task planners, lacking foresight of future tasks and inconsiderate of others' constraints, solve each task in isolation, leaving terminal states that increase future cost for all; side effects that compound over lengthy task sequences. To reduce cost over the sequence, a robot must anticipate how its actions now may impact performance on future tasks for all robots sharing the environment. Therefore, we present courteous anticipatory planning, wherein a model-based planner proposes candidate plans and selects the one that jointly minimizes immediate cost and aggregated expected fut
s4db670c3f0.summary: Researchers propose a planning approach where robots sharing a persistent environment anticipate how their actions affect future tasks for all robots.
s4db670c3f0.why: Multi-robot planners that ignore downstream effects can accumulate costs over long task sequences, relevant to fleet and warehouse automation.

sa2bb803cab.title: When Does On-Policy Interaction Help? Representational Tradeoffs in Value-Based Imitation Learning
sa2bb803cab.description: arXiv:2607.29617v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Imitation learning (IL)---training an agent to replicate expert behavior from demonstrations---underpins applications from robotics to language model training. Standard approaches such as Behavior Cloning (BC) are known to suffer from compounding errors and performance plateaus, particularly when the learner cannot perfectly represent the expert's policy (as is typical, e.g., in distillation). Two interventions are widely understood empirically to improve performance: querying the expert interactively along the learner's own trajectories, and using value function estimation en route to generating a policy. We investigate the nature of these improvements and their potentially surprising interplay. Our main finding is that expert inte
sa2bb803cab.summary: A paper examines when on-policy expert querying helps value-based imitation learning, analyzing representational tradeoffs versus behavior cloning.

s17f82ce264.title: Cloud-Edge LLM Collaborative Learning via Accelerating Personalized Bilevel Optimization
s17f82ce264.description: arXiv:2609.15664v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Amid the rapid advancement of physical-world intelligence, cloud-edge collaborative large language models (LLMs) have emerged as a promising roadmap for practical LLM deployment. However, existing cloud-edge paradigms struggle to balance global consensus with local personalization, which fails to satisfy the need for a unified knowledge foundation on the cloud and domain-specific adaptation at the edge. To address this, we propose a personalized bilevel optimization framework that formalizes cloud-edge LLM collaboration as a dual structure: the upper level optimizes edge-side personalization, while the lower level governs cloud-side knowledge transfer, reaching cloud-edge evolving in coordination. We then propose CIDERS: while the c
s17f82ce264.summary: Researchers propose a personalized bilevel optimization framework for cloud-edge LLM collaboration, balancing global consensus with local edge personalization.
s17f82ce264.why: Cloud-edge LLM deployments must balance shared knowledge with per-device adaptation, a practical architecture question for teams deploying models at the edge.

sf376523054.title: Hidden not Deleted: How Networks Suppress Entangled Features
sf376523054.description: arXiv:2609.27593v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: When a neural network stops reporting a feature, has it forgotten the feature or merely hidden it? Shared representations complicate the answer: removing one feature's direction can also damage another feature. We study this problem in a small autoencoder that compresses and reconstructs inputs, allowing individual feature contributions to be traced directly. With the representation fixed, restoring a single bias partially recovers target detection by exposing a signal hidden behind the output's activation threshold. Tests on target-absent inputs distinguish this recovery from interventions that simply increase output. The same bias intervention becomes less effective when the representation is allowed to change. We find that traini
sf376523054.summary: A small autoencoder study shows that suppressed neural network features are often hidden behind activation thresholds rather than deleted.

sb85696c75a.title: From Data to Program: Fast & Direct Generative Program Inference from Empirical Data
sb85696c75a.description: arXiv:2609.35348v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Estimating probability densities from a finite set of samples typically requires dataset-specific model fitting. We introduce PRODiGI, a pretrained data-to-program model that infers an explicit, executable generative program in a single forward pass. Pretrained on synthetic datasets paired with their ground-truth programs, PRODiGI accommodates diverse generative families and data dimensionalities through template prediction and non-autoregressive program parameter decoding. Its inferred programs support direct sampling, density and score evaluation, and inspection independently of the pretrained model. We further introduce program-space fine-tuning, which refines differentiable program parameters by maximizing the likelihood of empi
sb85696c75a.summary: PRODiGI is a pretrained model that infers an executable generative program from data samples in a single forward pass.
sb85696c75a.why: Direct data-to-program inference could replace dataset-specific density model fitting, though the text gives limited detail on practical performance.

s04b7be52c5.title: Parameterization method of reservoir properties for ensemble-based data assimilation using intermediate latent space of StyleGAN
s04b7be52c5.description: arXiv:2609.39626v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Ensemble smoothers are the most successful and efficient techniques currently available for history matching. However, because these methods rely on Gaussian assumptions, their performance is severely degraded when the prior geology is described in terms of complex facies distributions (non-Gaussian). In this way, for these methods, we need to apply efficient parameterization techniques. Currently, the most efficient methods for performing parameterization are deep learning models. However, given the variety of existing deep learning models, studies have not identified which is most suitable for use with ensemble-based methods, although some important models had already been evaluated. Based on a recent literature review, the most p
s04b7be52c5.summary: Researchers propose parameterizing reservoir properties using StyleGAN's intermediate latent space for ensemble-based history matching of non-Gaussian geology.

s8f856e07dc.title: Cross-Benchmark Transfer from RL on Agentic Coding Tasks
s8f856e07dc.description: arXiv:2610.00890v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Coding agents often fail in the last mile: they build most of a feature but drop a requirement, test only the cases their implementation already handles, break behavior that was supposed to stay intact, or validate against an unchecked assumption. We ask whether reinforcement learning (RL) on expert-built agentic coding tasks closes this gap, and whether what the agent learns transfers beyond the training distribution. We post-train Kimi K2.7 Code, a 1T-parameter (32B active) open-weight mixture-of-experts model, with RL alone on 1,700 tasks: 1,000 repository tasks graded by hidden fail-to-pass tests and by pass-to-pass tests of existing behavior, and 700 terminal tasks graded by expert-written hidden verifiers. The reward is the fr
s8f856e07dc.summary: Researchers post-trained Kimi K2.7 Code, a 1T-parameter open-weight MoE model, using RL on 1,700 expert-built agentic coding tasks to study transfer across benchmarks.
s8f856e07dc.why: RL on agentic coding tasks may close the 'last mile' gaps in coding agents, relevant to teams building or evaluating coding assistants.

se6c92d4d3d.title: Nearly Optimal Fixed-Confidence Best-Arm Identification with 1-Bit Feedback
se6c92d4d3d.description: arXiv:2610.02771v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study fixed-confidence best-arm identification under strict 1-bit feedback constraints. At each round, the learner selects an arm and a query set, and receives only a single bit indicating whether the sampled reward belongs to that set. We consider a distribution-free finite-variance setting with arm-wise localization, where direct empirical mean estimation is no longer available and clipping becomes unavoidable. We first formulate a time-uniform 1-bit mean-estimation primitive based on randomized threshold queries and a clipped tail-integral identity. We then embed this primitive into candidate-challenger best-arm identification algorithms. A fixed-clipping algorithm gives a simple anytime $(\epsilon,\delta)$-PAC guarantee, whil
se6c92d4d3d.summary: A paper studies fixed-confidence best-arm identification under strict 1-bit feedback, developing a time-uniform 1-bit mean-estimation primitive.

s517e2c79a9.title: What Should World Models Forget? Stratified Retention for Continual Adaptation
s517e2c79a9.description: arXiv:2610.03713v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Continual learning treats any drop in performance on previously seen data as forgetting, a convention inherited from settings where the prediction target is stationary. World models violate this assumption: their target is the environment, which changes, so knowledge that was accurate when learned can later become false, and revising it is correct behavior rather than a defect. Non-stationary ground truth is well studied in the concept drift literature and in the temporal factuality of language models, but it has not been formulated for world models, which are distinctive in that they also encode structural knowledge, such as physical laws and object permanence, that must never be degraded. We argue that continual world models need
s517e2c79a9.summary: Researchers argue that world models should selectively retain knowledge, treating accurate-then-outdated information as correct revision rather than forgetting.
s517e2c79a9.why: Continual-learning evaluation that counts necessary revisions as forgetting may misjudge world model quality in changing environments.

s9d6f71dabb.title: Inject a Turn, Not a Token: Learning Where to Redirect LLM Reasoning for Self-Correction
s9d6f71dabb.description: arXiv:2610.13672v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Large language models struggle to reliably identify and correct errors in their own reasoning. Unlike prior training-based approaches that fine-tune an LLM to generate revisions or feedback, we learn where to intervene in failed rollouts and determine how to redirect them. To choose where to intervene, we train a 130K-parameter MLP head on a frozen encoder using only final-answer correctness. For redirection, we find that under a fixed generation budget, the tested inline injections fail to reliably redirect reasoning, whereas presenting the same instruction in a new user turn changes the model's course. The resulting correction framework, UPTURN (User-Prompt TURN injection at a learned position), requires no LLM fine-tuning: it ret
s9d6f71dabb.summary: Researchers train a small MLP head to locate where to intervene in failed LLM reasoning rollouts, finding inline injections often fail to redirect reasoning.
s9d6f71dabb.why: Shows that naive inline correction prompts may not reliably fix LLM reasoning errors under fixed generation budgets.

s5e7debe60c.title: Learning to Read Out: Unembedding Dynamics in Language Model Pretraining
s5e7debe60c.description: arXiv:2610.21025v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: When does a language model acquire a capability? Developmental studies usually answer this by tracking when models start producing the correct token. But that prediction passes through the unembedding matrix, or readout, which is itself still being learned during pretraining. We show that a model's hidden states can encode task information before its own readout expresses it, so timelines read from outputs conflate what the model encodes with what its readout expresses. To track the readout directly, we introduce parameter-trajectory crosscoding, which fits one sparse dictionary to every token's readout row at every checkpoint. Unlike crosscoders on activations, it needs only checkpoint weights. We use it to locate a narrow early wi
s5e7debe60c.summary: A paper introduces parameter-trajectory tracking to measure when a language model's unembedding readout expresses capabilities its hidden states already encode.
s5e7debe60c.why: Output-based capability timelines may misdate when models acquire skills, which matters for evaluating training progress and checkpoints.

sc8d74ff070.title: Brain2Vec: A Self-Supervised 3D Foundation Model for Structural Brain MRI
sc8d74ff070.description: arXiv:2610.28411v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Deep learning models have become essential tools in medical imaging, yet training them end-to-end for diverse tasks remains challenging due to limited labeled data and computational constraints. To address this, we introduce Brain2Vec, a foundation model pre-trained on 74,425 T1-weighted Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scans pooled from multiple studies. Brain2Vec can serve both as a weight initialization backbone for fine-tuning downstream tasks and as a standalone feature extractor. We evaluated Brain2Vec in three tasks: downstream predictive performance, convergence speed, and embedding quality. Using Brain2Vec's pretrained weights as initialization and fine-tuning on labeled data for a brain age prediction task, results demonst
sc8d74ff070.summary: Researchers introduced Brain2Vec, a self-supervised 3D foundation model pre-trained on 74,425 T1-weighted brain MRI scans, usable for fine-tuning or as a feature extractor.
sc8d74ff070.why: Shows pretraining a large medical imaging foundation model on pooled data can serve as a reusable backbone when labeled data is scarce.

scd0f08d5fb.title: Operationalizing Governed Agentic Workflows in Regulated Finance: A Customer Zero Case Study using Zafin AIOS
scd0f08d5fb.description: arXiv:2610.33253v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Regulated industries such as finance and healthcare face critical governance challenges that hamper the adoption of AI-assisted software development and hinder the transition from experimental pilots to production work. This paper presents Zafin AIOS, an end-to-end orchestration platform and control plane designed to deploy AI within regulated industries such as finance. We provide the architectural principles and an empirical comparison between AI-assisted and human-led workloads. To validate this framework empirically, we conduct a case study analysis of Zafin's internal enterprise workflows, which we refer to as Customer Zero. This paper contributes a production case study of AI-assisted software engineering in regulated industri
scd0f08d5fb.summary: Researchers presented Zafin AIOS, an orchestration platform and control plane for deploying governed AI-assisted development in regulated finance, with a case study comparing AI-assisted and human-led work.
scd0f08d5fb.why: Offers architectural patterns for governance controls that teams in regulated industries need to move AI development from pilots to production.

s272aff2fb8.title: EmbodiExp: Compositional Experience Transfer for Embodied Agents
s272aff2fb8.description: arXiv:2610.39180v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Experience from past tasks can help embodied agents perform new tasks, but it may not remain applicable or effective when conditions change. Tasks with different overall goals often share subgoals, providing a basis for cross-task experience transfer. We present EmbodiExp, a framework for constructing outcome-grounded subgoal experiences and composing them in new tasks. Each experience describes how to pursue a subgoal, when the guidance applies, and what outcome must be verified for completion. Verified outcomes from applying one experience can satisfy the conditions for applying another, allowing experiences from different past tasks to be composed online. By examining the actions and observed outcomes at the subgoal level, Embodi
s272aff2fb8.summary: Researchers propose EmbodiExp, a framework that builds outcome-verified subgoal experiences for embodied agents and composes them to transfer experience across tasks with shared subgoals.
s272aff2fb8.why: Suggests reusable, verified subgoal experiences may help robotic agents generalize across tasks, though the text gives limited detail on results.

s0da9bcce49.title: NaijaFacts: A Framework for Disentangling Language from Knowledge in Facts about Nigeria
s0da9bcce49.description: arXiv:2611.06504v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Multilingual benchmarks for African languages mostly translate generic questions into local languages, measuring linguistic competence but not whether models know facts about Africa. We introduce NaijaFacts, a benchmark of factual and statistical questions about Nigeria, authored by native speakers and grounded in authoritative official statistics, with every question available in English, Nigerian Pidgin, Yor\`ub\'a, Igbo, and Hausa. Answering similar questions for the UK and US yields a country by language matrix that disentangles a language effect (the model knows the fact but degrades in a low-resource language) from a knowledge effect (the fact is absent in every language). Across eight frontier and Nigeria-adapted models, the
s0da9bcce49.summary: Researchers released NaijaFacts, a benchmark of native-speaker-authored factual questions about Nigeria in English, Nigerian Pidgin, Yoruba, Igbo and Hausa, compared against UK and US questions.
s0da9bcce49.why: Separates factual knowledge from language competence in multilingual evaluation, which matters for teams assessing models on African-language content.

sd5979cc0db.title: Accepted but Wrong: Silent Failures of LLM Code Repairs after API Migrations
sd5979cc0db.description: arXiv:2611.08269v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: After an API migration, an LLM-repaired procedure can run cleanly yet return wrong results, and a typical-input release check ships it. We report a preregistered study of 73 tasks on 60 documented changes in CPython, Node.js and SQLite. In the main stages, repairs are choices among documented code fragments, run on the real runtimes against withheld contracts. Over the complete repair space, the all-assertions gate on typical inputs released 0.410 of wrong repairs. One edge input written from the release note cut this to 0.065, and to 0.061 on 15 unseen clusters; three inputs from a blind low-cost commercial writer (GPT-5.6-luna) reached 0.070. Two more frozen stages enlarged the menu to 1491 fragments and added 233 hard distractors
sd5979cc0db.summary: A preregistered study of 73 tasks across 60 API changes in CPython, Node.js and SQLite found LLM code repairs can run cleanly yet return wrong results that typical-input checks miss.
sd5979cc0db.why: Shows typical-input release checks let many wrong LLM-generated repairs ship, so teams need edge-case tests derived from release notes.

s6d8cd8c87c.title: All Quiet on the Neural Front: Language Models Do Not Report Injected Pain States
s6d8cd8c87c.description: arXiv:2611.10123v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Can a language model report a pain state it represents? Recent work reported a linear pain direction in open-weight models that, when amplified, leads fine-tuned models to choose actions that delete a user's photographs or their own weights. We asked whether models can say when that direction is active, on three open-weight models from two families, with and without the original work's adapters, and under every protocol we tried they cannot. Using Open-Weight Masked Introspection (OWMI), we added the pain direction and its nearest emotional neighbours to the residual stream while models answered neutral tasks, then asked what had changed, against sham runs, random perturbations matched in output disruption, and a text-only condition
s6d8cd8c87c.summary: A study found that three open-weight language models cannot report when an injected pain direction is active, across every protocol tested using the OWMI method.
s6d8cd8c87c.why: Indicates that models' self-reports about internal states are unreliable, which matters for anyone relying on model introspection for safety monitoring.

s719682cd7e.title: Agentic-OPD: Recovering Forgotten Agent Capabilities via On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Tasks
s719682cd7e.description: arXiv:2611.12799v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Reinforcement learning is now the mainstream paradigm for training LLMs on agentic tasks, yet standard practice keeps only the best-validation checkpoint and discards the rest. We show that this is lossy: in GRPO training of LLM agents, the best-validation checkpoint fails on problems that earlier checkpoints from the same run had already solved, and the union of problems solved across checkpoints far exceeds any single one. The discarded checkpoints thus form a teacher pool obtained at no additional training cost, which on-policy distillation (OPD) can mine to recover the lost coverage. Mining this pool raises two challenges: i) which checkpoint to distill from, as no checkpoint dominates the others and complementarity to the stude
s719682cd7e.summary: Agentic-OPD proposes recovering capabilities from discarded RL checkpoints by using earlier checkpoints as a teacher pool for on-policy distillation in agentic LLM training.
s719682cd7e.why: Suggests checkpoints normally discarded during GRPO agent training can be reused at no extra training cost to recover solved problems.

s05a355378b.title: Before Words, Beyond Speech: Evaluating Nonverbal Social Reasoning in Early Childhood
s05a355378b.description: arXiv:2611.13213v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Children's earliest years are a period of intense social learning, during which meaning is built through gaze, gesture, and physical contact.
