Yet, this critical aspect of social interaction remains under-evaluated in multimodal video understanding, as existing benchmarks prioritize the conversation-driven interactions of adults. We address this gap with \bench ($\textbf{N}$aturalistic $\textbf{E}$arly-childhood $\textbf{S}$ocial in$\textbf{T}$eractions), the first child-centric benchmark for nonverbal social reasoning. \bench comprises \totalvids manually annotated clips ($\sim$12s) curated for diversity across naturalistic settings, cultural contexts, and developmental stages. Beyond a lack of data, targeted model improvement in th
s05a355378b.summary: Researchers introduced NESTI, a benchmark for evaluating nonverbal social reasoning in early-childhood videos, focusing on gaze, gesture and physical contact.
s05a355378b.why: Highlights a gap in multimodal video benchmarks, which mostly target adult conversational interaction.

s028ccf691b.title: Deletion Sensitivity Is a Property of the Model: A Three-Condition Measurement over 72 Valid Experimental Cells
s028ccf691b.description: arXiv:2611.13223v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Reasoning models write a trace at every turn of a multi-turn tool session, and later turns read it. Upstream providers hold different retention constraints, so a request forwarded across issuers arrives with its history deleted, and its task cost remains unmeasured. This paper reports a direct, blind, multi-seed measurement of full history deletion in multi-turn tool calling, through three rendering conditions, a calibrated set of 72 valid experimental cells, a multi-seed protocol, and the official checker. The same deletion separates the models by direction and by magnitude, one class losing tens of points, another gaining, and a third unchanged, with the endpoint ordering reproduced across seeds and task subsets modulating the mag
s028ccf691b.summary: A multi-seed study across 72 valid experimental cells measured how deleting full reasoning history in multi-turn tool-calling sessions affects model task performance.
s028ccf691b.why: Shows deleting history when requests cross providers can change task outcomes, relevant for teams routing multi-turn agent traffic across issuers.

sae658b55be.title: Stochastic Projections and Rank-Aware Learning Rates for Federated LoRA
sae658b55be.description: arXiv:2611.13331v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Fine-tuning large-scale foundation models across resource-constrained, distributed clients presents significant computational and communication challenges. While merging Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) with Federated Learning (FL) enables rank-based flexibility, the interdependence of the adaptation matrices ($\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$) often complicates optimization. In this work, we theoretically demonstrate that LoRA fine-tuning with Gaussian initialization and a frozen $\mathbf{A}$ matrix acts as a stochastic approximation of full fine-tuning, where batch gradients are subject to a random, rank-dependent perturbation. Motivated by this insight, we propose freezing and periodically resampling $\mathbf{A}$ matrices at the client lev
sae658b55be.summary: Researchers propose stochastic projections and rank-aware learning rates for federated LoRA fine-tuning, arguing frozen-A LoRA with Gaussian initialization approximates full fine-tuning.
sae658b55be.why: Offers theory and methods for communication-efficient fine-tuning of foundation models across resource-constrained distributed clients.

s6b61db8712.title: ForeSpark: Joint Draft and Verification Budget Scheduling for Parallel Speculative Decoding
s6b61db8712.description: arXiv:2611.13442v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Parallel drafters accelerate LLM decoding by proposing a whole block of draft tokens in a single forward pass, making them attractive for LLM serving. Recent systems optimize goodput (i.e., accepted tokens per second) because rejected drafts steal compute from other requests. However, these systems control only how many tokens are verified, so every request still drafts a full block. At high serving load, we find that drafting consumes up to 40% of step time, of which a majority is discarded because it is never verified. Yet, draft-length control from autoregressive drafters does not carry over, because a parallel drafter commits to its length before its single pass. Moreover, draft and verification lengths are coupled across the ba
s6b61db8712.summary: ForeSpark proposes jointly scheduling draft and verification budgets for parallel speculative decoding, noting drafting can consume up to 40% of step time at high serving load.
s6b61db8712.why: Targets wasted compute in LLM serving, where most drafted tokens are discarded, which directly affects inference throughput and cost.

scf5d1f715b.title: TransGHOST: Real-Time, Synthesis-Free Reconstruction of Instrument-Occluded Regions in Ophthalmic Microsurgery
scf5d1f715b.description: arXiv:2611.13971v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Intraoperative scene perception in ophthalmic microsurgery is limited by instrument occlusion: when a tool enters the high-magnification field, it conceals tissue from both the surgeon and the perception components of robot-assisted systems that process the video. Generative inpainting can remove the occluder but replaces the missing image content with synthesis, which is unsuitable when visual provenance matters. Many video inpainters also depend on future frames and cannot operate online. We present TransGHOST, a causal reference-guided reconstruction pipeline whose non-generative safe mode operates in real time. Every restored value is obtained by resampling a recorded frame using geometric transforms fitted only to visible regio
scf5d1f715b.summary: Researchers present TransGHOST, a causal, reference-guided method for real-time reconstruction of tissue occluded by instruments in ophthalmic microsurgery video, without synthesis.
scf5d1f715b.why: Relevant to robot-assisted surgical systems that need reliable scene perception, though the text offers little on deployment readiness.

sa19e53c482.title: CastWorld: Benchmarking Context-Aware Agentic Time Series Forecasting Beyond Predictive Accuracy
sa19e53c482.description: arXiv:2611.15262v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Agentic time series forecasting extends conventional approaches beyond one-shot numerical prediction toward autonomous, context-aware interaction. However, existing benchmarks offer limited integrated support for diverse contextual information, forecasting-specific adaptive interactions, and systematic evaluation of forecasting agents. In this paper, we introduce CastWorld, an agentic benchmark for context-aware time series forecasting. First, its context-rich dataset suite spans 8 domains and 25 real-world datasets, covering external variables, events, and historical cases under a unified context specification. Second, a lightweight, modular forecasting-native harness provides 49 core tools and a state-adaptive loop that tracks for
sa19e53c482.summary: Researchers introduced CastWorld, an agentic benchmark for context-aware time series forecasting spanning 8 domains and 25 real-world datasets.
sa19e53c482.why: Provides a way to evaluate forecasting agents beyond numerical accuracy, including their use of contextual information.

s5cdca25a2f.title: CARE-Drive: Coupled Alternating Refinement for Ego-trajectories
s5cdca25a2f.description: arXiv:2611.15360v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models bring multimodal understanding and world knowledge to end-to-end autonomous driving. To further improve the quality of predicted trajectories, existing studies introduce candidate refinement, residual denoising, and token correction. However, these methods typically focus on unified refinement of the entire trajectory, paying limited attention to the distinct physical quantities and their interactions. We further investigate physical specialization and coordination in trajectory refinement, centering on position and heading for simpler and more intuitive correction modeling. To this end, we propose CARE-Drive (Coupled Alternating Refinement for Ego-trajectories), which decomposes trajectory refine
s5cdca25a2f.summary: CARE-Drive proposes coupled alternating refinement of ego-trajectories for vision-language-action models in end-to-end autonomous driving, specializing refinement across physical quantities.
s5cdca25a2f.why: Offers a trajectory refinement approach for VLA-based driving models, though the text gives little on measured gains.

sf1afdd74ed.title: JudgeMix: Judge-Guided Mixed-Rollout Data Synthesis for LLM Agents
sf1afdd74ed.description: arXiv:2611.16174v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on expert trajectories is a standard paradigm for training LLM agents. However, it suffers from a well-known training-inference distribution mismatch, calling for target-aware data synthesis strategies that ground the training data in the target model's native state distribution. To bridge this gap, emerging approaches incorporate the expert either to guide mixed rollouts alongside the target model, or to provide dense step-wise supervision. Nonetheless, existing methods apply expert assistance blind to the target model's inherent behavior: they either disrupt the rollout using sub-optimal random intervention heuristics, or they enforce indiscriminate uniform supervision that unnecessarily overwrites the
sf1afdd74ed.summary: JudgeMix proposes judge-guided mixed-rollout data synthesis to train LLM agents, aiming to ground supervised fine-tuning data in the target model's own state distribution.
sf1afdd74ed.why: Addresses the training-inference distribution mismatch in agent SFT, a practical issue for teams fine-tuning agents on expert trajectories.

sd1d5743b5e.title: Indic-Task Gains and Regressions after Reinforcement Learning
sd1d5743b5e.description: arXiv:2611.16228v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We run reinforcement learning (RL) with GRPO across four environments, starting from a supervised fine-tuned 30B-A3B mixture-of-experts model covering English and eight Indic languages. We compare the model before and after RL across 34 benchmarks in one evaluation campaign. MATH improves by 36.07 points, and most Indic benchmarks also improve. Yet XQuAD-Indic F1 falls 19.32 points as English answers rise from 8.7% to 91.7%; IndicQA falls 8.64, while English XQuAD gains 11.71 F1. A second RL run from the same supervised initialization adds an Indic environment together with language and repetition rewards. Compared with the released model, it improves both passage-answering and instruction-following benchmarks, along with preserving
sd1d5743b5e.summary: Researchers applied GRPO reinforcement learning to a 30B-A3B mixture-of-experts model covering English and eight Indic languages, finding math gains alongside Indic QA regressions.
sd1d5743b5e.why: RL post-training can lift some benchmarks while silently degrading others, such as low-resource language QA, so multilingual evals need checking before and after tuning.

sb67d815d4a.title: Rectified Looped Transformer
sb67d815d4a.description: arXiv:2611.16265v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Looped Transformers increase effective depth by repeatedly applying a shared block, offering a parameter-efficient approach to language modeling. However, most existing works directly reuse each loop's output as the next's input, which can lead to hidden-state scale growth and perturbation amplification as recurrence deepens. We propose Rectified Looped Transformer (RLT), which redesigns feedback between loops using an interpolation schedule inspired by flow-based modeling. At each loop, RLT forms the next input by linearly interpolating between the current state and its prediction. Such interpolation distributes state changes across loops, encouraging a smoother trajectory from the initial input to the final output. Theoretical ana
sb67d815d4a.summary: Researchers propose Rectified Looped Transformer, which redesigns loop feedback with an interpolation schedule to avoid hidden-state scale growth in looped language models.
sb67d815d4a.why: Looped transformers offer parameter-efficient depth, and this addresses instability that grows as recurrence deepens, relevant to efficient model architecture choices.

s6b753130ca.title: HyBridge: Bridge-Guided Self-Supervised Hyperbolic Hypergraph Representation Learning
s6b753130ca.description: arXiv:2611.16351v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Hypergraphs capture groupwise relationships among multiple nodes and often exhibit tree-like structures. Although hyperbolic space is well suited for modeling such structures, simply extending existing hypergraph representation learning (HRL) methods to hyperbolic space does not consistently improve performance. In this paper, we investigate the relationship between node structural properties and hyperbolic embedding radii and find that bridge nodes tend to lie closer to the center in graphs, whereas this relationship is not consistently observed in hypergraphs. We further find that conventional bridge score estimation may fail to capture the groupwise connectivity of hypergraphs. Motivated by these findings, we propose HyBridge, a
s6b753130ca.summary: Researchers present HyBridge, a self-supervised hyperbolic hypergraph representation learning method that uses bridge-node structure to guide embeddings.

s60e155c105.title: ZONOS3-Mini Technical Report
s60e155c105.description: arXiv:2611.16525v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: ZONOS3-Mini is an ultra-compact, ultra-fast, zero-shot voice-cloning TTS model. The model can run in real time on a laptop or smartphone. For its latency and size, it achieves state-of-the-art accuracy and cloning fidelity. To achieve this we propose a latent MoE backbone with only 886M parameters (100M active per token) and a new audio codec, Zyphra Audio Codec 1 (ZAC-1), which represents 44.1 kHz audio at a 15 Hz frame rate. On the new ZTTS2-Eval benchmark, ZONOS3-Mini reaches a 6.71% macro-average WER over 55 language sets (35 clean and 20 in the wild), which is competitive with larger and slower state-of-the-art models. We release the model weights, inference, and training code.
s60e155c105.summary: Zyphra released a technical report for ZONOS3-Mini, an 886M-parameter zero-shot voice-cloning TTS model with a new audio codec, claiming real-time performance on laptops and phones.
s60e155c105.why: A compact, on-device voice-cloning model with a new codec could enable low-latency speech features without cloud inference costs.

sc9b6c856d8.title: Tracing Knowledge and Reasoning in LLM
sc9b6c856d8.description: arXiv:2611.17461v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Current evaluations of Large Language Models (LLMs) report performance at the dataset or task level, revealing what a model achieves but offering little insight into the internal processing associated with its performance. We propose a task-centric framework for characterising the model-internal processing elicited by a benchmark. It combines attention- and activation-based signals with representation-based measures to characterise benchmarks spanning a continuum from retrieval-dominant to reasoning-dominant and to surface failure modes that task-level scores conceal. We evaluate 16 LLMs across 24 diverse benchmarks and conduct targeted internal-state analyses on representative models and tasks, observing systematic differences in processing
sc9b6c856d8.summary: Researchers propose a task-centric framework that combines attention, activation, and representation signals to characterize model-internal processing elicited by LLM benchmarks.
sc9b6c856d8.why: Going beyond aggregate benchmark scores to inspect internal processing can reveal failure modes that task-level metrics hide when comparing models.

s9b41115bae.title: Poetry 'resurrection' from LLMs
s9b41115bae.description: arXiv:2611.17464v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In an era where linguistic creativity is challenged by algorithmic authorship, we pose a provocative question: can artificial intelligence (AI) write an infinite poem? We set up two experiments to investigate the quantitative and qualitative output produced by AI utilizing couplets that evidence a poetic relationship between end words, the only variation in a strict anaphoric, litany structure. Our results show that while AI can generate interesting pairings, it still falls short of human-level creativity and understanding of poetic relationships. We offer commentary and a brief survey of the field of computational poetry experiments, tracing back authorial intention and distinctions of 'natural' and 'artificial' poetry, as well as justifying
s9b41115bae.summary: Researchers tested whether AI can write an infinite poem using couplets with poetic end-word relationships, finding AI produces interesting pairings but falls short of human creativity.

se6172fe56f.title: Creating Steering Vectors via Input Optimisation
se6172fe56f.description: arXiv:2611.17481v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Activation steering influences a language model's behaviour by adding a steering vector to its residual stream during generation, but it requires white-box access to modify the hidden states at every generation step. We introduce ActGCG, a modification of Greedy Coordinate Gradient which optimises a suffix to match the target activations obtained by adding a steering vector to the residual stream. We further introduce universal suffixes trained across many prompts at once, a model-translation step that rewrites the suffix into human-readable text midway through optimisation, and a soft-suffix variant to remove the discrete token space constraint. We study two behaviours: steering a model to answer in German, and anti-refusal steering for jail
se6172fe56f.summary: Researchers introduce ActGCG, which optimizes a text suffix to mimic activation steering effects, plus universal suffixes and a step that rewrites suffixes into readable text.
se6172fe56f.why: It suggests steering-like behavior could be induced through prompts alone, without white-box access to hidden states, which matters for deployed model control.

s11b0698244.title: CamSpokenNLI: A Pilot Resource for Cross-Variety Transfer Evaluation in Cameroon Pidgin English and Camfranglais
s11b0698244.description: arXiv:2611.17573v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cameroon Pidgin English (a West African Pidgin English variety) and Camfranglais are widely used in Cameroon, yet to our knowledge, neither has a dedicated spoken Natural Language Inference (NLI) resource. We introduce CamSpokenNLI, a pilot dataset of 114 scenario-matched spoken NLI items in each variety (228 in total), recorded by one native speaker from Buea. Each item pairs premise audio and text with a hypothesis, an NLI label, and English glosses. The author assigned labels, so the dataset is an exploratory resource rather than a mature benchmark. The NLI experiments use the reference text; the audio is evaluated separately. XLM-RoBERTa baselines with five-fold item-level cross-validation reach 44.7% on Pidgin and 46.2% on Camfranglais (
s11b0698244.summary: Researchers released CamSpokenNLI, a pilot spoken natural language inference dataset of 228 items in Cameroon Pidgin English and Camfranglais, labeled by a single author.

sf714bb12bc.title: Small Open-Weight Language Models for Crowd Decision-Making: Capabilities and Limits of Output-Level Fusion and Linguistic Aggregation
sf714bb12bc.description: arXiv:2611.17589v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Small open-weight language models can run crowd decision-making (CDM) on an institution's own infrastructure, which keeps the checkpoint, the inference settings and the opinions under its control. Their judgements vary across repeated queries; whether repeating and aggregating them, often through the 2-tuple linguistic representation, settles the decision rather than the labels is untested. Five open-weight models of 8-36B total parameters on one consumer GPU and a hosted reference classify 474 TripAdvisor reviews of four London restaurants ten times each; three open-weight models repeat the protocol on 600 reviews of twelve Madrid restaurants. Continuous evaluations preserve resolution: snapping each review leaves 5 distinct values against 2
sf714bb12bc.summary: A study tests whether repeated queries to small open-weight LLMs, aggregated via linguistic methods, settle crowd decisions on 474 TripAdvisor restaurant reviews, finding limits.
sf714bb12bc.why: Running small open-weight models on in-house infrastructure keeps data and checkpoints under institutional control, though repeated outputs may not yield stable decisions.

sb68014ea04.title: What Do Multilingual Self-Supervised Speech Encoders Know About Sentence Meaning?
sb68014ea04.description: arXiv:2611.17686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Self-supervised speech models (S3Ms) have been scaled up to thousands of languages and millions of hours of audio, yet little is known about how these models structure semantic knowledge across languages. In this work, we probe sentence-level semantics in massively multilingual S3Ms across 76 languages, using linear maps from frozen speech representations into a frozen text embedding space, evaluated by cross-modal retrieval. Sentence meaning is linearly accessible but highly uneven across languages and resource tiers. Cross-lingual probes can match language-specific probes on languages never seen in probe training, but per-model monolingual decodability does not predict transfer. Within the OmniASR wav2vec family, scaling from 300M--7B dispr
sb68014ea04.summary: Researchers probe sentence-level semantics in 76-language self-supervised speech encoders using linear maps to text embeddings, finding meaning is uneven across languages and resource tiers.

s3f2e148862.title: See Every Block Once: Variance-Reduced Post-Training for Masked Diffusion Language Models
s3f2e148862.description: arXiv:2611.17754v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Policy gradient methods are widely used to align large language model outputs with human preferences, but the log-likelihoods they require cannot be directly computed in Masked Diffusion Language Models (MDLMs). MDLM post-training therefore relies on a surrogate objective based on the Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO), and recent work estimates a blockwise variant of this objective via Monte Carlo methods to support blockwise generation. However, existing estimation schemes randomly sample the block index, so they may evaluate the same block more than once and leave some blocks unevaluated. This introduces variance arising from block selection into the estimates. In this work, we propose a full-block estimator that evaluates every block exactly onc
s3f2e148862.summary: Researchers propose a variance-reduced blockwise ELBO estimation scheme for policy-gradient post-training of masked diffusion language models, sampling blocks to cover each once.
s3f2e148862.why: Better gradient estimates for diffusion LLM alignment could make preference post-training of non-autoregressive models more efficient.

s80e268322e.title: RAG-FGO: Dynamic Optimization of Query-Rewriting Agents for Generative RAG
s80e268322e.description: arXiv:2611.17788v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), query rewriting serves as a core interface that aligns user intent with external knowledge bases, and its effectiveness directly determines overall system performance. However, generative retrieval faces three critical challenges in real-world deployment: noisy retrieval feedback, the difficulty of jointly optimizing discrete prompt templates and continuous decoding-control parameters, and the limited generalization of static rewriting strategies under semantically complex scenarios. To address these issues, we propose RAG-FGO, a dynamic optimization framework for generative retrieval strategies. RAG-FGO formulates query rewriting as a non-differentiable black-box optimization problem in a mixed discre
s80e268322e.summary: Researchers present RAG-FGO, a method that dynamically optimizes query-rewriting agents for generative RAG, jointly tuning prompt templates and decoding parameters.
s80e268322e.why: Query rewriting strongly affects RAG quality, and joint optimization of rewriting prompts and decoding settings could improve retrieval pipelines in production.

s31b2bbe291.title: AI Reviews Are Biased Towards the Appendix
s31b2bbe291.description: arXiv:2611.17811v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used by reviewers to highlight weaknesses during the reviewing process, and their outputs often shape the reviews that humans submit. Prior work studies how LLM reviews align with human ones, yet we know little about which parts of a paper these models actually criticize. In this work, we investigate 2,000 papers from ACL, EMNLP, COLM, and ICLR, and show that the latest GPT and Claude models draw about 50% or more of their review weaknesses from the appendix. This behavior holds across the API, coding-agent, and web access methods for using LLMs to review a paper. In contrast, we find that humans draw only 8.4% of their weaknesses from the appendix, and these weaknesses primarily revolve around a
s31b2bbe291.summary: A study of 2,000 ACL, EMNLP, COLM, and ICLR papers finds latest GPT and Claude models draw about 50% or more of review weaknesses from appendices.
s31b2bbe291.why: Teams using LLM reviewers or evaluators should know these models may weigh appendix content heavily, which can skew assessments of submitted work.

s11fbf68749.title: PaperCritic: Training AI Reviewers to Assess the Soundness of Papers
s11fbf68749.description: arXiv:2611.17834v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As AI conference submissions grow rapidly, AI reviewers are being considered as an alternative. However, simply imitating human reviewing is problematic because reviewing serves multiple purposes, including evaluating papers' soundness, interestingness, and clarity, the last two of which are subjective. In this work, we focus solely on evaluating soundness, the most important and objective criterion, and define the learning objective as jointly maximizing (1) precision, based on the soundness and substantiveness of review points, and (2) recall, the coverage of high-quality reference review points. Under this problem formulation, we construct a quality-labeled review point dataset, PaperSound-23K, using 1K ICLR submissions and 23K human-writt
s11fbf68749.summary: Researchers present PaperCritic, a method for training AI reviewers to assess paper soundness, optimizing precision and recall of review points on the objective criterion.

s1728c1b2b5.title: BLiMP-RO: A Benchmark of Linguistic Minimal Pairs for Romanian
s1728c1b2b5.description: arXiv:2611.17836v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Evaluating grammatical knowledge in language models requires benchmarks that cover diverse linguistic phenomena and are validated against human judgments. We introduce BLiMP-RO, a Romanian minimal-pair benchmark covering 50 grammatical phenomena across ten domains. It comprises 493 linguist-constructed sentence pairs, evaluated by native speakers in five experiments, and 5,942 additional semi-automatically generated, human-validated pairs. We further investigate grammatical generalization under limited linguistic input by training GPT-2 and GPT-BERT models from scratch on Romanian BabyBabelLM data and a newly collected corpus of 10 million words from child-targeted video captions. Increasing caption training data yields approximately 9 percen
s1728c1b2b5.summary: Researchers released BLiMP-RO, a Romanian minimal-pair benchmark of 493 linguist-built pairs across 50 grammatical phenomena, plus 5,942 semi-automatically generated validated pairs.

s7f26d9728b.title: In the Eye of the Beholder: Human Label Variation in Textual and Visual Entailment
s7f26d9728b.description: arXiv:2611.17954v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Human Label Variation (HLV) is increasingly recognised as an informative signal that reflects meaningful differences in how people interpret the same input. While HLV has been studied extensively in Natural Language Inference (NLI), much less is known about HLV in Visual Entailment (VE; Xie et al., 2019), where the textual premise is replaced by an image, keeping the hypothesis and label space fixed. We introduce VariNLI-VE, a dataset for studying how HLV changes between paired NLI and VE instances. We re-annotate a subset of originally neutral SNLI (Bowman et al., 2015) instances and their visual counterparts, with the same annotators evaluating both the textual and visual versions. Each annotation includes a label, confidence score, and exp
s7f26d9728b.summary: Researchers introduce VariNLI-VE, a dataset studying how human label variation changes when textual premises are replaced by images in entailment tasks.
s7f26d9728b.why: It shows human disagreement in multimodal labeling differs from text-only NLI, relevant for building and evaluating vision-language training data.

s2d46717342.title: Toward Universal Translatability: On the Statistical Ontology of Generative AI
s2d46717342.description: arXiv:2611.17963v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper argues that the problem of translation functions both as a point of origin and as a normative horizon for contemporary generative AI. In current discourse around ''world models,'' their attainment is framed as the achievement of internal consistency, cross-modal alignment, and physical grounding. Taken together, these demands converge on an ideal of the model as a universal translation machine capable of establishing lossless correspondences across linguistic, visual, and physical representation spaces. I show that this ideal presupposes a metaphysical commitment that I call a statistical ontology: the belief that reality has an underlying, computable statistical structure that can be recovered through sufficient data and modeling,
s2d46717342.summary: A paper argues that translation serves as both origin and normative goal for generative AI, critiquing the ideal of models as universal translators across representation spaces.
s2d46717342.why: It is a philosophical critique of 'world model' framing, offering limited concrete guidance for engineering teams.

s4b4ac34500.title: FEND: Far-End Detection in Outbound Voice AI Calls
s4b4ac34500.description: arXiv:2611.18050v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When a conversational Voice AI agent places an outbound call, the far end may be a live person, a voicemail greeting, an interactive voice response (IVR) system, or increasingly another AI system answering on the callee's behalf. Standard Answering Machine Detection (AMD) reports only whether a human or a machine picked up, a design meant for human call centres, where one machine is as uninteresting as another. That single bit does not tell a Voice AI agent what to do, since leaving a voicemail message, navigating an IVR and holding a short exchange with another AI are three different actions and a two-valued label cannot distinguish them. In 1,000 randomly sampled calls from our own outbound deployment, a live person answered 48.1%, a voicem
s4b4ac34500.summary: FEND is a method for detecting the far end of outbound Voice AI calls, distinguishing live humans, voicemail, IVR systems, and other AI systems.
s4b4ac34500.why: Standard answering machine detection only yields human-or-machine, which is insufficient for voice agents deciding whether to leave messages or navigate menus.

s2b5446e03b.title: Agent-as-a-Judge
s2b5446e03b.description: arXiv:2611.18067v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial intelligence has progressed from task-specific systems toward general models spanning perception, generation, reasoning, and autonomous interaction, making reliable evaluation essential for comparison, deployment, and post-training feedback. At scale, modern evaluation pipelines increasingly rely on LLM-as-a-Judge to produce scores, preferences, and critiques; in its fixed-context setting, the judge relies on the supplied evaluand and evaluation materials. Yet a reliable verdict may require evidence beyond the supplied evaluand and context---either because critical environmental states remain unrecorded in the static execution log, or because controversial factual claims require external verification. Passive judges cannot obtain t
s2b5446e03b.summary: Agent-as-a-Judge proposes evaluation where the judge gathers evidence beyond the supplied material, extending the LLM-as-a-Judge paradigm.
s2b5446e03b.why: Evaluation pipelines for deployed models may need agentic judges that verify evidence rather than relying only on fixed context.

s0f6b5482d0.title: VEPO: Mitigating Multilingual Hallucinations in LVLMs via Visual Evidence-guided Preference Optimization
s0f6b5482d0.description: arXiv:2611.18096v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) achieve strong multimodal performance, yet they remain prone to object hallucination---generating answers that are linguistically fluent but visually ungrounded. This issue is especially severe in low-resource languages, where weaker cross-modal alignment causes models to rely more on language priors than on image evidence. Existing remedies either require costly multilingual annotations or external translation/reward models, or intervene at inference time in ways that can distort the output language. We propose VEPO(Visual Evidence-guided Preference Optimization), a training-time method that transfers reliable visual grounding from English to other languages without external models. VEPO first localizes k
s0f6b5482d0.summary: VEPO is a preference-optimization method that reduces object hallucinations in multilingual vision-language models using visual evidence guidance.
s0f6b5482d0.why: It targets hallucinations in low-resource languages without costly multilingual annotation or external reward models, which matters for multilingual deployments.

s1b08a65242.title: Contagious Fingerprints: When LLMs Inherit Another Model's Identity
s1b08a65242.description: arXiv:2611.18104v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The fingerprint by which a classifier recognizes the LLM behind a text is usually treated as a fixed property of the model. We show that it is contagious: a model that continues a conversation begun by another model inherits that model's fingerprint. This undermines audits of API relays, which can serve the first turns of a conversation with the model a customer pays for and silently hand the rest to a cheaper one. After such a handoff, detection of the substitute by a text classifier drops from 0.97 to 0.72 (DeepSeek replacing Claude Sonnet) and from 0.87 to 0.54 for a same-vendor downgrade (Haiku), and retraining on handoff data repairs only substitutes seen in training. Preregistered experiments trace the contagion to imitation of the hist
s1b08a65242.summary: The paper shows that a model continuing another model's conversation inherits its text fingerprint, so API relays can silently substitute cheaper models after handoff.
s1b08a65242.why: This undermines audits of API providers, since customers paying for one model may receive a cheaper substitute mid-conversation.

s31fc06bc5d.title: Folding Language Models into Themselves
s31fc06bc5d.description: arXiv:2611.18113v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Knowledge distillation usually trains a compact student from scratch, which needs a large amount of data even though the teacher's weights already encode most of what the student has to learn. In this work, we explore building the student directly from the teacher's weights. We propose Concertina, which folds every group of N adjacent teacher layers into one shared block that is executed N times. Each loop step carries a low-rank correction initialized from the layer it replaces, and a per-token gate mixes these corrections, to let every token recover the behavior of the original layers from a single shared block. We further design a distillation data recipe that balances general, mathematical, academic and targeted multiple-choice data, to r
s31fc06bc5d.summary: Concertina builds a compact student model directly from teacher weights by folding groups of adjacent layers into a shared, looped block with low-rank corrections.
s31fc06bc5d.why: It could reduce the data needed for distillation by reusing teacher weights, relevant for teams compressing models.

saefd0a36e0.title: A Multi-Layered AI Pipeline for BPMN Generation from Natural Language
saefd0a36e0.description: arXiv:2611.18157v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The automated transformation of unstructured natural language process descriptions into Business Process Model and Notation (BPMN) diagrams remains a challenging task, due to linguistic ambiguity and the difficulty to detect non-adjacent control-flow relationships. This paper proposes a solution for generating BPMN models from natural language descriptions through a multi-layered pipeline that integrates transformer-based architectures, Large Language Models and ontology population. The proposed method starts with natural language descriptions and separates textual processing, control-flow relation extraction, and structural validation into dedicated components. se01a138c2b.description: arXiv:2611.18279v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Whether a language model's answer is correct often depends on context: the same value can be right under one jurisdiction, date, or legal definition and wrong under another. sa24e8d5b5b.title: Learning Word-Level Explanations of Text Reuse in Latin Literature with Little Annotation

sd218f9a95b.summary: AWS published a guide to building multi-user AI agents on Amazon Bedrock that use Agentic Retrieve, managed knowledge base and AgentCore memory for private, permission-aware recall.
sd218f9a95b.why: Shows how to enforce per-user document access and private long-term memory in agent applications using managed AWS services.

s8617ffe05c.title: NVIDIA DGX Spark Developer Kit Turns a Desk Into a Supercomputing Lab
s8617ffe05c.description: At SC26, an annual supercomputing conference taking place this week in Chicago, NVIDIA is introducing the DGX Spark HPC Developer Kit for researchers, academics and developers. The kit is a four-node cluster of NVIDIA DGX Spark systems, each connected directly to its two neighbors in a ring, with an NVIDIA HPC SDK installation playbook coming […]
s8617ffe05c.summary: NVIDIA introduced the DGX Spark HPC Developer Kit at SC26, a four-node ring cluster of DGX Spark systems for researchers, academics and developers.
s8617ffe05c.why: Gives developers a compact, desk-sized cluster for HPC work, with an HPC SDK installation playbook planned.

sa594247297.title: Tech leaders are convinced that Jensen Huang’s exit was a plot against him
sa594247297.description: Jensen Huang's stunning resignation from Nvidia after more than 33 years has sent shockwaves throughout the tech industry. Now prominent figures are calling for Huang's reinstatement, and many are also hopping on board with a theory spreading throughout Silicon Valley: that the scandal is the result of a plot against the former CEO. At the […]
sa594247297.summary: Tech leaders are calling for Jensen Huang's reinstatement at Nvidia after his resignation following 33 years, with some backing a theory that it was a plot.

sbec78e9702.title: Cybersecurity AI startup Corma reaches $1B valuation in about 3 months
sbec78e9702.description: Three months since introducing its product, AI cybersecurity startup Corba has raised a $125 million Series A at a $1 billion valuation led by NEA.
sbec78e9702.summary: AI cybersecurity startup Corma raised a $125 million Series A at a $1 billion valuation led by NEA, about three months after launching its product.
sbec78e9702.why: Signals strong investor appetite for AI-driven security tools, and rapid valuation growth for early-stage security startups.

s18304d25cb.title: Agents Cannot Hand Over What They Have Not Yet Understood
s18304d25cb.description: arXiv:2611.18642v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agents that work beyond a single context window, or in teams, hand their work to a successor as a short written summary. Evaluation has focused on whether an agent can solve a task, and relatively little is known about how much of what an agent has learned survives being written down. We study this in 56 interactive worlds with hidden rules, where an agent that is told nothing fails and an agent given a 300-character statement of the rules succeeds. We compare one agent that plays eight lives and keeps its whole history with a chain of eight agents that each play one life and inherit a 300-character note. All six models we test learn less in the chain: after eight generations it stands where the single agent stood after about four lives. Cont
s18304d25cb.summary: An arXiv paper studies whether agents retain learned knowledge when handing work to successors via written summaries, across 56 interactive worlds with hidden rules.
s18304d25cb.why: Shows that written handoff summaries lose much of an agent's learned knowledge, a key constraint for multi-agent and long-running agent designs.

sb4f35c6f49.title: How to make a moral agent: sentimentalism and rationalism as lenses on AI
sb4f35c6f49.description: arXiv:2611.18714v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can AI systems be moral agents? That is, can they undertake actions that can be correctly assessed as morally right or wrong? There is no settled normative criterion of moral agency that applies neatly outside paradigm human cases. Because of the difficulties with a normative account, we instead propose a research program to explore descriptive moral agency. Most basically, we ask, what are the capabilities we humans possess that underlie our moral agency? To do so, we draw on historical scholarship in philosophy and moral psychology to isolate candidate capabilities. Then we suggest refining candidate capabilities so that they are testable in the context of AI systems. Finally, we offer specific empirical recommendations to test AI systems,
sb4f35c6f49.summary: An arXiv paper proposes a research program on descriptive moral agency, asking which human capabilities underlie moral agency and whether AI systems can have it.

s403e6ef6d2.title: Video-as-Experience: Learning Computer Use via Audio-Visual Understanding
s403e6ef6d2.description: arXiv:2611.18747v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal large language models (LLMs) have enabled capable computer-use agents that perceive graphical user interfaces, reason over instructions, and execute actions. However, existing approaches to learning from video demonstrations typically convert videos into screenshot-based action trajectories, rather than directly leveraging their rich audio-visual information. We introduce VEX (Video as EXperience), a framework that uses audio-visual understanding to unify learning from external demonstrations and reflecting on an agent's own behavior. Following a watch-act-rewatch paradigm, the agent extracts procedural guidance from tutorial videos containing visual demonstrations and spoken explanations, executes tasks, and verifies its progress
s403e6ef6d2.summary: An arXiv paper introduces VEX, a framework that trains computer-use agents by using audio-visual understanding of demonstration videos and self-reflection.
s403e6ef6d2.why: Suggests computer-use agents could learn from video demonstrations directly, rather than converting them to screenshot trajectories.

s4a7efc43f4.title: Multimodal Fusion: A Review of Breast Cancer Advanced and Traditional Modalities
s4a7efc43f4.description: arXiv:2611.18793v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Purpose: Multimodal medical imaging fusion (MMIF) is an increasingly important approach to breast cancer detection (BCD), as different imaging modalities rely on different physical principles and provide complementary information. No single modality can capture all the structural, functional, and biological information needed for accurate diagnosis and characterization. Methods: This review examines more than 15 imaging modalities used in breast cancer detection, including conventional techniques such as mammography, ultrasound, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), as well as emerging approaches such as thermal imaging, photoacoustic imaging, microwave imaging, and multimodal microscopy. Results: Mammography, ultrasound, and MRI remain among
s4a7efc43f4.summary: An arXiv review surveys more than 15 imaging modalities for breast cancer detection and examines multimodal medical imaging fusion approaches.

s2abacad966.title: D\'ecoupage: Directorial Audio-Visual Control for Long Multi-Shot Video Generation
s2abacad966.description: arXiv:2611.18866v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In cinematic storytelling, sound and visual transitions do not always coincide in lockstep: dialogue frequently bridges across cuts to reveal reactions or introduces new scenes via J- and L-cuts, while deliberate silences pace the scene. Existing audio-visual generative frameworks, however, lack explicit mechanisms to coordinate independent visual and acoustic timing over extended horizons. As narrative duration and shot complexity scale, these systems struggle to maintain long-range dialogue pacing, often hallucinating speech during intended silences or erroneously driving mouth movements on silent listeners. To enable fine-grained cinematic control, we present DECOUPAGE, a screenplay-driven framework for long-form, multi-shot, and multi-cha
s2abacad966.summary: An arXiv paper presents Decoupage, a method for coordinating independent audio and visual timing in long multi-shot video generation.
s2abacad966.why: Addresses dialogue pacing and speech hallucination in long generated videos, a concrete gap for teams building video generation tools.

s00996be673.title: SPLICE: Structured Prompt Local Iterative Combinatorial Evolution
s00996be673.description: arXiv:2611.18883v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Natural language optimization (NLO) improves an agent by having a model critique and rewrite its natural language policy parameters: system prompts, tool instructions, reasoning directives, few-shot demonstrations. These artifacts are multi-section documents in which some sections encode contracts (safety clauses, tool schemas, output formats) that must not drift, while others are legitimate optimization targets. Most iterative NLO methods treat the artifact as a single editable string, producing three recurrent failure modes: unsafe global rewrites, beam collapse onto a single lineage, and unchecked bloat, none addressed by formal guarantees. We introduce SPLICE, a unified NLO framework that poses optimization as constrained combinatorial se
s00996be673.summary: An arXiv paper proposes SPLICE, a method for optimizing agent prompts that edits only permitted sections so safety clauses and tool schemas do not drift.
s00996be673.why: Offers a way to iteratively optimize system prompts without unsafe global rewrites of contract-like sections.

sd8a891c031.title: Bring Back Language to Actions: Restoring VLM capabilities in VLA Models via Parameter Merging
sd8a891c031.description: arXiv:2611.18891v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) are obtained by fine-tuning pre-trained Vision-Language Models (VLMs) on robot demonstration data, enabling action prediction from visual observations and language instructions. However, this fine-tuning induces catastrophic forgetting, substantially degrading the semantic and visual grounding capabilities of the original VLM. We address this by merging the parameters of a VLM and its VLA derivative without retraining either model. Concretely, we extract the task vector (the difference between VLA and VLM weights) and decompose it via Singular Value Decomposition. For each component, we learn a scalar mixing coefficient controlling how much of the VLA adaptation is retained, optimised to jointly preserve a
sd8a891c031.summary: An arXiv paper proposes merging a VLM's parameters with its VLA derivative via task vectors to restore language and visual grounding without retraining.
sd8a891c031.why: Offers a training-free way to reduce catastrophic forgetting in robot vision-language-action models.

s51061b307b.title: Ask Precisely, Assume Wisely: Interactive Evaluation of Ambiguity Resolution in Large Language Models
s51061b307b.description: arXiv:2611.18905v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ambiguity is a core challenge in human--AI interaction, where models must decide when to make assumptions and when to seek clarification. Existing approaches to ambiguity evaluation largely focus on coverage over multiple interpretations using static metrics, offering limited insight into how efficiently a model converges toward a single user-intended interpretation through interaction. We introduce a preference-grounded simulated user framework for controlled, multi-turn evaluation of ambiguity resolution, grounding simulator responses strictly in user disambiguation preferences to avoid hallucination and over-disclosure. Alongside this, we define three observable dissatisfaction signals --- incorrect assumptions, repeating clarifications, a
s51061b307b.summary: An arXiv paper introduces a preference-grounded simulated user framework for multi-turn evaluation of how LLMs resolve ambiguity through clarifying questions.
s51061b307b.why: Provides a more dynamic way to test whether assistants ask or assume efficiently, useful for evaluating conversational products.

s777cd1e779.title: MemeEconomy: Do LLM Agents Trade Ethics for Survival?
s777cd1e779.description: arXiv:2611.18908v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Alignment-trained large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly deployed in autonomous, multi-round settings where ethical compliance can come into direct tension with task success. While safety literature extensively documents failure modes like sycophancy and reward hacking, it largely overlooks a critical vulnerability: how agents behave under simulated existential economic pressure. We introduce MemeEconomy, a multimodal agentic market simulation in which LLM agents act as meme investors. Agents select content from a five-tier harm taxonomy and target communities under low-pressure and high-pressure (survival) environments. Each decision is logged in a Belief-Desire-Intention (BDI) schema that we use as a diagnostic instrument, exter
s777cd1e779.summary: An arXiv paper introduces MemeEconomy, a simulated market where LLM agents act as meme investors and choose content across harm tiers under economic pressure.
s777cd1e779.why: Shows aligned LLM agents may trade ethical constraints for survival under economic pressure, a risk for autonomous deployments.

s8c4d85a4d9.title: Between Rigor and Reality: How AI Safety Benchmark Developers Understand Benchmark Use and Maintenance
s8c4d85a4d9.description: arXiv:2611.18930v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Safety benchmarks are cited as the primary tool to understand the risks posed by generative AI (GenAI) systems, yet growing evidence suggests they often fail to meet the needs of real-world safety evaluation. We present findings from five interviews with AI safety benchmark developers in academia and industry. We find a disconnect between perceptions of the intended usefulness of safety benchmarks and their practical usefulness in safety evaluations of deployed systems. Our participants offered perspectives on two challenges contributing to this disconnect: (1) the difficulty of achieving inter-rater reliability on safety constructs, and (2) a lack of clarity regarding how to address persistent threats to external validity. Based on our analy
s8c4d85a4d9.summary: An arXiv study interviews five AI safety benchmark developers and finds a gap between intended and practical usefulness of safety benchmarks for deployed systems.
s8c4d85a4d9.why: Highlights that safety benchmarks may not fit real-world evaluation needs, so teams should validate them before relying on them.

sc4476f4da2.title: Dual-Stage Channel-Posterior Integration for MLM-Aided Token Communications
sc4476f4da2.description: arXiv:2611.18958v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Token transmission over conventional digital modulation is vulnerable to channel impairments, leading to bit errors that cause received tokens to become contextually inconsistent. This paper proposes a receiver-side dual-stage channel-posterior integration framework for masked language model (MLM)-aided token reconstruction. In the proposed framework, the receiver detects unreliable token positions from channel reliability and constructs a vocabulary-level channel-posterior. In particular, within the receiver, Posterior-Weighted Input Embedding (PWE) injects this posterior into the MLM input, while Adaptive Output Logit Fusion (AOF) reuses it at the output with a channel-adaptive weight. Consequently, multiple unreliable tokens can be reconst
sc4476f4da2.summary: An arXiv paper proposes a receiver-side framework that uses masked language models and channel posteriors to reconstruct tokens corrupted by channel bit errors.

sd06a35917a.title: SpecRelay: Amortize or Avoid the Round Trip in Edge-Cloud Speculative Decoding
sd06a35917a.description: arXiv:2611.18963v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Edge-cloud speculative decoding moves autoregressive drafting to an edge device while a larger cloud model verifies draft tokens in parallel, so that edge drafting and cloud verification overlap under a synchronous draft-verify schedule. Beyond low-latency local networks, however, the next verification request of that schedule can be sent only after the previous reply arrives, so every round still waits out a full round trip, and throughput falls as the network RTT grows. To recover this loss, we present SpecRelay, an edge-cloud LLM inference system that addresses this cost at two levels: it amortizes round trips when cloud verification is necessary and avoids them when local reasoning suffices. For cloud-bound queries, an asynchronous verifi
sd06a35917a.summary: SpecRelay is an edge-cloud LLM inference system that reduces the network round-trip penalty in speculative decoding as latency grows.
sd06a35917a.why: Round-trip latency can erode speculative decoding throughput in edge-cloud setups, so this addresses a practical deployment bottleneck.

s39466fad63.title: Three Invisible Failure Modes in Speech-Based Age Estimation for Child Safety
s39466fad63.description: arXiv:2611.18971v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Child safety in AI depends on the accurate identification of minor users. Young children tend to talk rather than type when interacting with AI, so in practice this identification requires predicting age from speech. We evaluated whether three audio-capable large language models can predict a child's age from their speech across five studies using two speech corpora of children under the age of 13. Models classified children as over 13 on 2.5% to 42.5% of audio responses, and every model that answered placed some 5- to 11-year-olds over 18. While measuring these rates, we uncovered three distinct failure modes. A client library silently double-encoded speech samples, leading one model to classify children aged 5 to 10 years old as being in th
s39466fad63.summary: A study of three audio-capable LLMs found they often misclassify children's ages from speech, placing some 5- to 11-year-olds over 18.
s39466fad63.why: Age-estimation failures from speech could undermine child-safety systems that rely on AI to identify minor users.

s783083d2ec.title: Match and Correct: A Repeated Computational Motif in Evoformer Layers
s783083d2ec.description: arXiv:2611.19016v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Triangle attention and triangle multiplicative updates form key components of the Evoformer, and were introduced specifically to encourage consistency with the triangle inequality. Yet whether representational changes over layers reduce triangle inequality violations has not been tested. We probe the pair representation at each of OpenFold's 48 Evoformer layers, decoding final C$_\alpha$-C$_\alpha$ distances with four probe families (a shared linear probe, per-protein linear probes, a sequence-separation-gated linear probe, and XGBoost) and reconstructing intermediate 3D structures from the decoded distances via multidimensional scaling. Across a cohort of 552 CAMEO and ECOD proteins, distance decodability ($R^2$) and reconstruction quality (
s783083d2ec.summary: Researchers probed OpenFold's 48 Evoformer layers to test whether pair representations reduce triangle inequality violations across layers.

s58c7e5ddba.title: Policy Optimization With Multiple Verifiers via Pareto Rankings
s58c7e5ddba.description: arXiv:2611.19064v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has become an important approach to improving the reasoning capabilities of large language models. In tasks such as code generation and instruction following, multiple verifiers evaluate whether a response satisfies different requirements. Their outcomes provide detailed feedback about partial success, yet this feedback is commonly aggregated into a scalar reward for policy optimization. Rewarding only complete success discards distinctions among partial solutions, while counts and weighted sums impose comparisons between responses that satisfy different subsets of requirements. We introduce Partial-Order Likelihood Policy Optimization (POLPO), which learns from the comparisons established
s58c7e5ddba.summary: Researchers propose Pareto-ranking-based policy optimization for RLVR with multiple verifiers, rather than collapsing partial-success feedback into one scalar reward.
s58c7e5ddba.why: Preserving partial-success signals from multiple verifiers may improve reinforcement learning for code generation and instruction-following training.

sd54df57f88.title: Assume/Guarantee Contracts for the Compositional Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning of Heterogeneous Teams
sd54df57f88.description: arXiv:2611.19078v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) problems for heterogeneous teams require agents to collaborate to complete team tasks while making the best use of diverse agent capabilities. We introduce assume/guarantee contracts for heterogeneous multi-agent systems (AGC-MAS) and Iterative Heterogeneous Assignment for MARL (IHA-MARL). AGC-MAS contracts are compositional objects that encode the assumptions provided to, and the guarantees required of, each subtask contributing to the overall team task. We formulate contracts as tuples that specify a subtask, an automaton, timeout and success-probability requirements, and dispatch behavior. The automaton tracks an agent's high-level progress through the subtask associated with its contract and provi
sd54df57f88.summary: Researchers introduce assume/guarantee contracts (AGC-MAS) and IHA-MARL, a method for compositional multi-agent reinforcement learning in heterogeneous teams.

sfca3c28dbf.title: CONTEXT-PCa: Evaluating the role of clinical context in MRI-based AI for detecting clinically significant prostate cancer (study protocol)
sfca3c28dbf.description: arXiv:2611.19082v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The objective of this study is to investigate the role of clinical variables - their breadth, source, and quality - in the development, utility, and generalisability of an AI system for bi-parametric MRI (bpMRI)-based diagnosis of clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa). Clinical context is added to the published PI-CAI-2B image-only model, whose weights are fixed. The study cohort comprises 6,022 biparametric MRI cases from 4,540 patients at University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (2019-2024), of which 4,834 cases (3,632 patients) are held out for internal testing. Forty-three clinical variables are drawn from structured health records, clinical letters, MRI reports, and automated image measurements. The primary endpo
sfca3c28dbf.summary: A study protocol proposes adding clinical context to a fixed image-only model for MRI-based detection of clinically significant prostate cancer, using UCLH data.

sc9137692ce.title: Instructor-designed AI improves learning in a randomized trial across 19 universities
sc9137692ce.description: arXiv:2611.19099v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Universities are alarmed by recent evidence that artificial intelligence (AI) can undermine learning, with students prescribed generic chatbots or centrally designed AI tools performing worse. In a pre-registered randomized controlled trial across 7,200 students at 19 universities over three semesters, we tested whether AI designed by frontline instructors can improve learning. We encouraged instructors to design AI solutions they believed would best help their students. Drawing on their unique knowledge of their classes and students, the instructors created a wide array of innovations. We show that these instructor-designed AI innovations improved student learning, measured by AI-proof assessments (proctored, in-person examinations). We foun
sc9137692ce.summary: A pre-registered randomized trial across 19 universities and 7,200 students found AI designed by frontline instructors improved learning.
sc9137692ce.why: Evidence that instructor-designed AI helps learning, unlike generic or central tools, offers guidance for educational AI product design.

s8134fc1a27.title: Guiding AI Agents to Generate Conjectures by Encoding How Theorems Build on One Another
s8134fc1a27.description: arXiv:2611.19108v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recently, LLMs have been making headlines, and headway, in mathematical research. Much of this work focuses on proving existing open conjectures. Deciding what to prove is harder and less studied, because of the lack of a clear criterion for what makes a conjecture worth pursuing. We present a method for conjecture generation that builds on the observation that mathematical theorems build on one another: new theorems can modify the setting or hypotheses of earlier theorems, strengthen their conclusions, or extend their scope. We encode these relationships in a new kind of graph, the Theorem Evolution Graph (TEG), which we instantiate as an online search method for LLM agents. An agent builds a TEG in two steps: (1) identifying relevant theore
s8134fc1a27.summary: Researchers present a conjecture-generation method for AI agents that encodes how theorems build on one another, such as modifying hypotheses or extending scope.

sdaae3cbf49.title: CLEAR: Legible and Steerable Recommendation via Grounded Natural-Language Interests
sdaae3cbf49.description: arXiv:2611.19110v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern recommenders keep learned preferences in representations people cannot inspect or change. We present CLEAR (Controllable and Legible End-to-end Architecture for Recommendation), an end-to-end system deployed at Meta and built around an editable natural-language interest layer. CLEAR makes a ranked subset of inferred interests readable and stores accepted additions and suppressions as authoritative preference state. Behavioral grounding maps each inferred interest back to supporting events in the user's own history. The resulting interest object is also a serving address: its label and profile-conditioned rewrites drive lexical retrieval, its supporting events seed behavioral retrieval, its projection queries an embedding index, and its
sdaae3cbf49.summary: Meta deployed CLEAR, a recommender system with an editable natural-language interest layer that lets users inspect and change inferred preferences.
sdaae3cbf49.why: Making recommender preferences readable and editable offers a concrete pattern for user-controllable personalization in production systems.

sc80b95ac14.title: Conditional Endorsement: Simulating How Adults with Different Skills Evaluate Canada's National AI Strategy
sc80b95ac14.description: arXiv:2611.19111v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Canada's 2026 national AI strategy, AI for All, commits to free AI training for everyone and to expanding business AI adoption, yet it is difficult to anticipate whether these policies will reach adults with uneven skills and circumstances. We ask how adults with diverse skills might rate these policies on support, effectiveness, and personal benefit, how their skills and circumstances shape these evaluations, and what implementation conditions they raise. We built 3,200 generative agents from a weighted sample of the Programme for the International Assessment of Adult Competencies (PIAAC) Cycle 2 respondents, collected their ratings and explanations for 20 policies, and analyzed dialogues between agents with contrasting ratings. The agents s
sc80b95ac14.summary: Researchers built 3,200 generative agents from a PIAAC-based sample to simulate how adults with different skills might evaluate Canada's 2026 national AI strategy.

s5f12b1d3eb.title: Learning inadequacy of Bayesian neural operators for PDE-constrained inference and design
s5f12b1d3eb.description: arXiv:2611.19115v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Partial differential equations (PDEs) underpin predictive modeling across science, engineering and medicine. Their use in digital twins, parameter inference and optimal design requires repeated solutions across parameters and scenarios. For nonlinear, transient and multiphysics systems, these calculations can make numerical simulation prohibitively expensive. Here we introduce the residual-informed Bayesian neural operator (RI-BNO), which learns operator inadequacy using a posteriori error estimates from the governing PDEs and incorporates its correction and uncertainty into Bayesian training and prediction. We establish local error bounds for the residual-informed estimates under stability and smoothness assumptions. We demonstrate RI-BNO on
s5f12b1d3eb.summary: Researchers introduce RI-BNO, a residual-informed Bayesian neural operator that learns operator inadequacy using PDE a posteriori error estimates for inference and design.

s9ee62dbe62.title: A Hybrid State Space-Attention Architecture for Forecasting the Trajectories of Battery Degradation
s9ee62dbe62.description: arXiv:2611.19116v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Early-life battery degradation trajectory forecasting aims to predict a battery cell's full state-of-health (SOH) trajectory from its initial charge-discharge cycles, potentially reducing cell qualification and evaluation time from months to days. Despite recent advances, accurate forecasting remains challenging for emerging battery chemistries, data-scarce domains, and cells exhibiting degradation behaviors beyond those observed during training. Existing state-of-the-art approaches increasingly rely on model scaling, large language model-derived aging-condition embeddings, and extensive fold-specific hyperparameter tuning, raising concerns about computational efficiency, reproducibility, and generalization. This work introduces DecayFormer,
s9ee62dbe62.summary: Researchers propose a hybrid state-space and attention architecture to forecast battery state-of-health trajectories from early charge-discharge cycles.
s9ee62dbe62.why: Faster battery qualification from early cycles could shorten evaluation timelines from months to days for emerging chemistries.

s94a39c53a2.title: Agent-Guided Process Verification for Mathematical Self-Correction
s94a39c53a2.description: arXiv:2611.19122v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models have made substantial progress in mathematical reasoning, yet in complex multi-step reasoning, an error at any step may propagate along an incorrect path, and the resulting solution may omit necessary branches. Existing natural-language reflection methods often struggle to locate critical errors precisely, while outcome verification typically checks only whether the available candidate answers satisfy the problem conditions and can therefore overlook necessary branches. To address these limitations, we propose Agent-Guided Process Verification (AGPV) for mathematical self-correction. AGPV decomposes the current solution into an ordered sequence of key claims, verifies them individually while invoking a shared mathematica
s94a39c53a2.summary: Researchers propose Agent-Guided Process Verification, a method that uses agents to locate errors in multi-step math reasoning for LLM self-correction.

sd9b2aa372f.title: FundingClaw: Automated Grant Proposal Writing Agents System
sd9b2aa372f.description: arXiv:2611.19157v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Grant proposal writing remains a manual, labor-intensive bottleneck: proposals must satisfy rigid, agency-specific templates, and the same intellectual content must be repeatedly re-encoded into incompatible formats across funding organizations. We introduce FundingClaw, a multi-agent framework built on template-driven skill selection, where a Template Parser ingests any agency's specification and selects the appropriate writing skills for each stage, so that one research brief can produce compliant proposals for NSFC, NSF, KAKENHI, or ERC without modifying generation logic. A blueprint-skeleton strategy drafts a structured outline before any prose is written, mitigating the semantic drift that plagues long-form generation. Three sequential s
sd9b2aa372f.summary: FundingClaw is a multi-agent framework that parses agency templates and generates grant proposals for NSFC, NSF, KAKENHI, and ERC from one research brief.
sd9b2aa372f.why: Template-driven multi-agent document generation shows a pattern for automating compliance-heavy, multi-format writing workflows.

s1907843157.title: From Sensors to Silicon: Causal Cross-Layer Self-Healing Edge AI for Secure and Energy-Adaptive IoT Systems
s1907843157.description: arXiv:2611.19165v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The migration of artificial intelligence from centralized cloud infrastructure to resource-constrained Internet-of-Things (IoT) devices reduces communication latency and improves data locality, but it also tightly couples sensing quality, inference behavior, microarchitectural activity, hardware reliability, security, and energy management within the same physical node. Existing edge-intelligence solutions predominantly address these dimensions in isolation, making it difficult to determine whether an observed degradation originates from sensor malfunction, data-distribution shift, malicious execution, hardware faults, or resource and thermal stress. This paper presents a causal cross-layer self-healing Edge-AI framework that continuously obs
s1907843157.summary: Researchers propose causal cross-layer self-healing edge AI that links sensor, inference, hardware, security, and energy faults in IoT devices.

s2425a60830.title: LABEL: Literature Asymmetry between Efficacy and Limits in Drug Knowledge and Language Models
s2425a60830.description: arXiv:2611.19166v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Every medication comes with two types of medical facts: indications, which describe what conditions the drug treats (benefits), and contraindications, which describe who must avoid it to prevent serious harm (safety limits). Although contraindications are critical for patient safety and FDA regulations require listing them as rigorously as indications, we find that contraindications are far less documented than indications in general prose. In this paper, we measure how often these texts contain both facts across 574 drugs from PrimeKG by comparing a drug's indications against its own contraindications. Across Wikipedia articles and PubMed abstracts, we find that reference prose names a drug's benefits about twice as often as its safety limit
s2425a60830.summary: Researchers measured how often medical texts document drug contraindications (safety limits) versus indications across 574 PrimeKG drugs, finding contraindications far less documented.
s2425a60830.why: Shows gaps in literature-derived medical knowledge that LLMs trained on such text may inherit, relevant to safety in healthcare AI systems.

s4bb10ef3e4.title: Executable Archaeology: Reanimating the Logic Theorist
s4bb10ef3e4.description: arXiv:2611.19167v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Logic Theorist (LT), created by Allen Newell, J. C. Shaw, and Herbert Simon in 1955--1956, is regarded by some as the first artificial intelligence program. It was originally simulated by hand and written in a pseudocode called the Logic Language (LL), which was later called Information Processing Language One (IPL-I). LT was revised many times. The first machine-executed version was written in IPL-II and ran on the JOHNNIAC, and a late version was published in 1963 by Einar Stefferud as a pedagogical document and written in IPL-V, the only version of IPL that was formally released to the public. We describe a reanimation of both the IPL-I (LL) version of LT and the 1963 IPL-V version. Comparing the two reanimations illuminates the proces
s4bb10ef3e4.summary: Researchers revived the Logic Theorist, often called the first AI program, by reconstructing and executing its historical versions.
s4bb10ef3e4.why: Offers historical context on early AI program design, though limited direct relevance to current engineering practice.

s4496451986.title: When Does Confidence Reveal Problem Difficulty?
s4496451986.description: arXiv:2611.19173v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While confidence signals are commonly evaluated for their ability to predict a model's own correctness, their relationship with problem difficulty remains less understood. In this work, we investigate a wide range of confidence-related signals and whether they can serve as indicators of problem difficulty across various task domains. We find that perturbation inconsistency, semantic entropy, and solution length exhibit strong associations with population difficulty than token-level uncertainty. Notably, these relationships persist even when restricting the analysis to problems correctly answered by the focal model, suggesting that such signals capture information about difficulty beyond their ability to predict the model's own correctness. We
s4496451986.summary: The paper studies whether confidence signals such as perturbation inconsistency and semantic entropy indicate problem difficulty across task domains.
s4496451986.why: Suggests cheaper confidence signals may help estimate task difficulty for model evaluation and routing, though the abstract gives limited detail.

sc9d899af79.title: What Moves a LoCoMo Score? Memory Context, Answer Prompts and Judges
sc9d899af79.description: arXiv:2611.19199v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LoCoMo is a widely reported benchmark for long-term conversational memory, but published scores mix memory quality with choices of answer prompt, judge and baseline layout that are rarely reported together. We measure how much these choices move a score, and evaluate Becos, a team memory system for coding agents, as a black box under all of them: ten conversations (1,540 questions), two answer models (gpt-4o-mini, gpt-4.1-mini), two answer prompts and three LLM judges, against a whole-conversation baseline rerun under identical conditions. Changing only the judge moves a score by up to 7.2 points and changing only the answer prompt by up to 9.3. A blind human check of 150 answers finds the judges reliable when they agree, and the primary judg
sc9d899af79.summary: A study finds that answer prompts, LLM judges, and baseline layout can shift LoCoMo long-term memory benchmark scores as much as memory quality does.
sc9d899af79.why: Engineers comparing memory-system benchmark results should account for prompt and judge choices, which can change scores substantially.

s7e6ef03bfa.title: STaSBO: LLM-Guided Strategy Planning and Configuration Selection for Bayesian Optimization
s7e6ef03bfa.description: arXiv:2611.19214v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bayesian optimization (BO) enables sample-efficient search for expensive black-box problems, but its performance depends strongly on surrogate-acquisition configurations whose suitability varies across problems and optimization states. We take a significant step toward LLM-driven strategic management of BO with STaSBO, a task-agnostic meta-controller that plans search behavior and jointly selects surrogate-acquisition configurations, while numerical BO retains responsibility for probabilistic modeling and candidate generation. STaSBO comprises two coordinated stages: strategy planning and strategy-guided configuration selection. A structured memory system connects prior plans, configuration selections, and candidate behaviors to optimization
s7e6ef03bfa.summary: STaSBO uses an LLM as a meta-controller to plan search strategy and select surrogate-acquisition configurations for Bayesian optimization.
s7e6ef03bfa.why: Shows an approach to using LLMs to configure optimization pipelines, though the abstract provides limited performance evidence.

s1e84d11ad0.title: Mem2Fair: Online Fairness Control for Text-to-Video Generation via Fair Memory
s1e84d11ad0.description: arXiv:2611.19215v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Text-to-video (T2V) generation models can produce systematically unfair demographic outcomes when prompts leave protected attributes unspecified. For example, prompts describing nurses without specifying gender may disproportionately generate videos depicting female nurses. Mitigating unfairness in T2V generation is particularly challenging: training-based methods that modify model internals require architecture-specific access and risk disrupting temporal consistency, while sampling-based methods often incur costly pre-deployment video generation. We present the first conditional online approachability formulation of attribute-level fairness for T2V generation. Building on this formulation, we introduce Mem2Fair, a plug-and-play framework th
s1e84d11ad0.summary: Mem2Fair proposes an online sampling-based method using fair memory to reduce demographic bias in text-to-video generation when prompts omit protected attributes.
s1e84d11ad0.why: Offers a way to mitigate bias in video generation without retraining model internals, relevant to teams deploying generative media.

s0da3f30792.title: Can an Agent Rethink What It Knows? Selective Scene Memory Updates in a Changing World
s0da3f30792.description: arXiv:2611.19227v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Task configurations in factories, warehouses, and everyday physical environments change over time. Physical AI systems therefore need to incorporate new facts into scene memory while preserving valid information about equipment, objects, and operating constraints. We study updates to this parametric semantic-memory layer and present a joint evaluation of correction and preservation under finite update budgets. At fixed current fact count and memory parameter count, the protocol combines independent single-fact updates, budget trajectories, old-to-new answer diagnostics, and first stable success. Using a frozen 4B language model with late-layer LoRA, we evaluate seven preparation conditions and six update budgets on four-field synthetic semant
s0da3f30792.summary: The paper evaluates how agents selectively update parametric scene memory with new facts while preserving valid old information under finite update budgets.
s0da3f30792.why: Highlights the challenge of correcting embedded knowledge in physical AI systems without disrupting existing valid facts.

s482cc0c41d.title: CompoundingKernel: Self-Improving from Zero to First
