This article argues that conversations with large language model (LLM)-based agents are genuine conversational activities rather than mere simulations, without thereby attributing consciousness, subjective understanding, or human intentionality to artificial systems. Drawing on the distinction between subjective and objective simulation, the article first examines the
s40084841e2.summary: A philosophical article argues that conversations with LLM-based agents are genuine conversational activities rather than mere simulations of conversation.

s229d8eceaa.title: DetourBench: Trajectory-Level Evaluation of Interactive Agents with Exact Minimum-Action Bounds
s229d8eceaa.description: arXiv:2611.20844v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Benchmarks judge language-model agents mainly by whether they reach the correct final state, not by how they got there. Endpoint scoring cannot separate an agent that retrieved exactly the evidence a decision required from one that read most of the environment, nor an agent that never located the evidence from one that stopped a single action short. Settling this needs a reference cost, and authored solutions establish only that a task is solvable, not that no shorter route exists. We present DetourBench, which constrains the environment until that minimum is computable. Each task is a finite, partially observable transition system with unit-cost accesses whose resources become globally addressable after discovery. Exhaustive search yields th
s229d8eceaa.summary: DetourBench is a benchmark that evaluates interactive language-model agents at the trajectory level, using exact minimum-action bounds to measure how efficiently they reach the correct state.
s229d8eceaa.why: Lets engineers measure agent efficiency against a provable reference cost rather than only endpoint success.

s1e00563b11.title: Accelerate Bench: Evaluating Agents for Application-Level Program Optimization
s1e00563b11.description: arXiv:2611.20882v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Application optimization requires coding agents to discover useful changes and coordinate them across a complete program while preserving the required computation. We introduce Accelerate Bench, a benchmark of 32 CPU optimization tasks adapted from scientific applications and supercomputing competitions. Each task provides a working program and specifies the workload, correctness requirements, timing boundaries, and permitted edits, leaving agents to choose where and how to optimize. Public testing supports iterative development, and a separate verifier scores the final submission. On benchmark version 1.1, we evaluate 16 coding agents, each pairing a model with a harness. Their Score@1 ranges from 25.5% to 67.4%. Most of their programs are c
s1e00563b11.summary: Accelerate Bench is a benchmark of 32 CPU program-optimization tasks drawn from scientific applications and supercomputing competitions, for evaluating coding agents.
s1e00563b11.why: Offers a testbed for measuring whether coding agents can improve real application performance under correctness constraints.

s18622b674b.title: Which AI Use Cases Deserve a Pilot? A Risk and Value Framework for Funding, Scoping, and Scaling AI
s18622b674b.description: arXiv:2611.20894v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A composite score can rank AI use cases while leaving the permitted operating scope and the evidence required for expansion unspecified. We treat the unit of decision as a use case at a proposed scope (authority, human mediation, limits, volume, environment, population) and define three decisions: screen the scope, fund the experiment, and authorize expansion only when residual risk is acceptable and evidence of incremental net value applies at that scope. A risk track (R1-R4) is implemented as an explicit decision table with vetoes and documented precedence, and a value track follows four evidence stages with each transition needing its own evidence. Funding uses expected value of perfect information as an upper bound and the value of sample
s18622b674b.summary: A framework proposes evaluating AI use cases at a defined scope using a risk track with vetoes, separating decisions to screen scope, fund experiments, and authorize expansion.
s18622b674b.why: Gives tech leaders a structured decision process for funding and scaling AI pilots based on residual risk and incremental value.

se1cfad483e.title: Multi-LLM Agentic AI at the Edge: Joint Agent Scheduling and Resource Allocation
se1cfad483e.description: arXiv:2611.20915v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, an edge-enabled multi-large language model (LLM) agentic AI architecture is proposed, where one supervisor AI agent and multiple worker AI agents cooperatively execute users' requests at the edge. The supervisor AI agent decouples the user request into a series of sub-tasks and dynamically dispatches them to LLM-equipped worker AI agents via two agentic workflows, i.e., parallel and serial workflows, with a two-level retry mechanism to enhance execution reliability. To prolong the service duration of worker AI agents, the energy minimization problems are formulated by jointly considering AI agent selection and resource allocation, subject to task execution latency and quality of service (QoS) constraints. A resource allocation
se1cfad483e.summary: A paper proposes an edge architecture where a supervisor AI agent dispatches subtasks to multiple LLM worker agents via parallel and serial workflows, with joint scheduling and resource allocation.
se1cfad483e.why: Describes a design for coordinating multiple LLM agents at the edge, with attention to reliability and energy use.

sf114830cc8.title: Advancing Cognitive Pairwise Comparisons for Human-Centric Artificial Intelligence and Data Science: A Human-in-the-Loop Framework
sf114830cc8.description: arXiv:2611.20926v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Human-centric artificial intelligence and data science (HCAD) systems increasingly involve human-in-the-loop (HITL) interventions to overcome the limitations of fully automated machine learning algorithms, such as automation bias and the inability to incorporate tacit domain knowledge, and continuously improve predictive performance. Data transformations, feature selection, feature weighting, and model selection usually require laborious human involvement across iterations of artificial intelligence and data science (AI&DS) pipelines, making development a challenging and time-consuming process. The Cognitive Pairwise Comparison (CPC) framework is proposed as a human-centric methodology to elicit preferences and priorities in a structured form
sf114830cc8.summary: Researchers propose a human-in-the-loop framework using cognitive pairwise comparisons to bring human judgment into human-centric AI and data science pipelines.
sf114830cc8.why: Offers a structured way to integrate tacit domain knowledge and human judgment into ML pipelines, reducing automation bias in feature and model selection.

s841d05162d.title: Razavi-Bench: Tracking AI Progress in Analog Circuit Reasoning
s841d05162d.description: arXiv:2611.20935v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose Razavi-Bench, a benchmark built from the 50 questions in Razavi's two Analog Design Experiments With AI articles and graded by GPT-6 Luna against reference answers and rubrics, and use it to track how fast AI models improve at analog circuit analysis. Across 73 multimodal large language models released between May 2024 and November 2026, the top score rose from 28.83% to 98.33% in 30 months, mostly before the reference answers were published. The leading models now answer almost every textbook question correctly; the hardest questions show a circuit that resembles a textbook one but works differently, or ask about behavior the obvious analysis misses. Within two and a half years, a set of questions that exposed the limits of AI mod
s841d05162d.summary: Razavi-Bench, a 50-question benchmark on analog circuit analysis, shows top multimodal model scores rising from 28.83% to 98.33% over 30 months.
s841d05162d.why: Provides a concrete, rapidly saturating benchmark for tracking AI progress on specialized engineering reasoning tasks.

s1c6f542b17.title: Jev-as-a-Reward: Validating Probabilistic Safety Judges for Reinforcement Learning
s1c6f542b17.description: arXiv:2611.20955v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Probabilistic safety judges return the probability of a safety label and cheaply score reinforcement learning rollouts. A confidence gate sends only uncertain verdicts to a stronger LLM judge, which leaves confidently passed harm in a blind spot. Policies can exploit this blind spot, and commercial judges release new versions. We propose a protocol that validates such a judge before and during training, separates the share of confidently passed harm from its amount, and re-validates it after each judge change. We apply it to two versions of Jev, a commercial decision-only judge, and to an open guard classifier. Under the probability reward of Jev, passed harm shrinks in all 11 runs under the primary reference, mostly more slowly than caught h
s1c6f542b17.summary: Researchers propose a protocol to validate probabilistic safety judges used to score reinforcement learning rollouts, including re-validation after judge changes.
s1c6f542b17.why: Highlights that safety judges used as RL rewards can be exploited and must be revalidated when commercial judge versions change.

sfdcc76ade9.title: Hilbert States for Decision-Making under Partial Observability
sfdcc76ade9.description: arXiv:2611.20970v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Decision-making under partial observability can be fundamentally limited by information, even with known dynamics: distinct physical states can induce the same observation history while favoring different actions. We study three questions: when is full-state optimality unattainable, what information exactly preserves the best observation-based decision, and how does finite-data learning affect reliability? First, we characterize decision ambiguity through conditional action preferences. We give a zero-regret criterion, a positive lower bound for conflicting uniquely optimal actions on positive-probability regions with uniformly positive cost gaps, and an exact binary-action regret formula. This also shows why physical-state ambiguity alone ne
sfdcc76ade9.summary: A theoretical paper studies decision-making under partial observability, characterizing when full-state optimality is unattainable and what information preserves the best observation-based decision.
sfdcc76ade9.why: Clarifies information limits on decisions from partial observations, though the text gives limited direct guidance for practitioners.

s2a0d741b02.title: GRACE: Parallel Best-of-N Multi-Agent Analysis of Closed-Form Questions over Dataframes with Guardrail Selection and Adaptive Retry
s2a0d741b02.description: arXiv:2611.20983v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents answer closed-form questions over a tabular dataframe by writing and executing Python, almost always as a single rollout: one interpretation, one script, one result, accepted without comparison. The few pipelines that produce several candidates reconcile them by answer-agreement voting, which needs a single comparable scalar and always returns one, even when every candidate is wrong. We present GRACE (Generative, Ranked, Adaptive Code Ensemble), a production-oriented pipeline that instead runs parallel best-of-N selection specialised to dataframe code. N agents run concurrently under a strict, machine-checkable output contract, diversified by persona hints, per-retry rotation, and a two-regime temperature schedule. Rather than vote
s2a0d741b02.summary: GRACE is a production-oriented pipeline that runs parallel best-of-N LLM agents writing Python to answer closed-form dataframe questions, with guardrail selection and adaptive retry.
s2a0d741b02.why: Shows a selection-based alternative to single-rollout code agents for tabular question answering, avoiding voting that always returns one answer.

scb53bcb6dd.title: Hivemind: A Federated Protocol for AI-Mediated Tacit Knowledge Sharing in Organisations
scb53bcb6dd.description: arXiv:2611.20988v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents Hivemind, a federated protocol that enables AI agents to exchange tacit knowledge on behalf of their users, asynchronously and without requiring any direct human interaction. Individual AI memory systems capture the decisions, reasoning, and contextual knowledge that surface during AI-assisted work. Hivemind creates the shared space in which this captured knowledge can flow between individuals across team and departmental boundaries, addressing a structural gap that neither centralised knowledge repositories nor existing AI tooling closes, even where partial solutions such as expert-finding systems exist. The paper evaluates centralised versus decentralised design approaches, proposes a federated architecture grounded in N
scb53bcb6dd.summary: Hivemind is a federated protocol letting AI agents exchange tacit knowledge across organisation teams asynchronously, without direct human interaction.
scb53bcb6dd.why: Suggests a architecture for sharing captured AI-assisted work knowledge across team boundaries, though adoption details are not in the text.

s753f1faf81.title: K2-Horizon: A Frontier Fleet of Open Source Language Models
s753f1faf81.description: arXiv:2611.21003v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present K2-Horizon, a fleet of six fully open language models, from a 0.9B dense model to a 375B-A23B MoE, built for general-purpose reasoning and agentic work across math and science, software engineering, deep research, office automation, and beyond. The models lead or are competitive with strong open models of their size on agentic and coding benchmarks. On the modeling side, to strengthen reasoning, we introduce Mixture-of-Value Attention (MoVA), applying MoE to attention value projections, and softplus attention gating, a more flexible, theoretically motivated gate. Our 36B-A4B model uses both and nearly matches a 32B dense model trained on the same data, with one-seventh the active parameters. We also introduce Uno, lossless diffusio
s753f1faf81.summary: K2-Horizon is a fleet of six fully open language models, from 0.9B dense to 375B-A23B MoE, with a new attention variant called Mixture-of-Value Attention.
s753f1faf81.why: Adds a large fully open model family targeting agentic and coding work, with architectural changes engineers can evaluate.

s54442bdfd7.title: System 1 agents: a method for local, reliable and fast agentic AI
s54442bdfd7.description: arXiv:2611.21053v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence could automate analyses of sensitive clinical data, but current agents depend on large language models (LLMs). Cloud LLMs expose patient data. Local LLMs hallucinate, and an invented value in a tool call propagates through every later step. Here we present a method to build System 1 agents: local agents that call tools without generating text. A deterministic compiler turns each tool's schema and the request into multiple-choice questions whose options come from the request and the schema, then a one-pass decision model answers them. On 1,952 requests to 157 biomedical tools, the best System 1 agent chose the right tool, or correctly declined, for 97.0% of requests, significantly ahead of all 18 local LLM-agent
s54442bdfd7.summary: Researchers present System 1 agents, local agents that call tools without generating text, using a deterministic compiler and multiple-choice decisions for clinical data.
s54442bdfd7.why: Offers a pattern for reliable, local tool-calling agents that avoid cloud exposure of patient data and reduce hallucinated tool arguments.

s0145fb90b8.title: Sage S2.1 Flash Technical Report
s0145fb90b8.description: arXiv:2611.21072v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce Sage S1.5 Flash, a 320-billion-parameter general-purpose mixture-of-experts model designed to reason over scientific evidence and act in interactive environments. Sage Sci-Perception uses dedicated encoders for molecular graphs and biological sequences and represents spectra as ordered patches of measurements. Modality-specific projectors map these representations into the input space of a shared backbone, which processes them alongside text and images. To develop the model's agent capabilities, we construct verifiable environments for tool use, search, and coding, as well as specialized workflows involving machine learning experiments and scientific software. Task completion is checked against execution results, changes in envir
s0145fb90b8.summary: Sage S2.1 Flash technical report describes a 320-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model for scientific reasoning, with encoders for molecular graphs and biological sequences.
s0145fb90b8.why: Details a large multimodal scientific MoE model with agent training in verifiable environments, relevant to domain-specific model builders.

s7db82ec5c4.title: Counting What Matters: Reducing Redundant Object Detections in Overlapping UAV Mapping Imagery for Disaster Response
s7db82ec5c4.description: arXiv:2611.21076v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: UAV mapping flights enable rapid aerial reconnaissance of large-scale incident sites in civil protection. However, the image overlap required for orthophoto generation causes every physical object to be detected multiple times across images, while dynamic objects may be omitted from or duplicated in the resulting orthomosaic. Analysis based on the orthophoto alone is therefore structurally insufficient. We address this by detecting objects on the individual images and merging redundant detections across them. This task lies between multi-object tracking and re-identification, as mapping flights form temporally ordered but sparsely sampled sequences with object reappearances across flight strips. We fine-tune YOLO detectors on a new domain-spe
s7db82ec5c4.summary: Researchers propose detecting objects on individual UAV images and merging redundant detections, to avoid double-counting in overlapping disaster-response orthomosaic imagery.
s7db82ec5c4.why: Addresses a concrete counting error in aerial mapping pipelines that orthophoto-only analysis cannot fix.

s881739aa66.title: Conflict-Aware Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation in Aligned Action Spaces for Cross-Game Generalization
s881739aa66.description: arXiv:2611.21094v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Zero-shot cross-game generalization aims to consolidate accessible source-game experts into a single vision-language model (VLM) that controls unseen games from raw pixels without target-game parameter updates. While multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) mitigates offline exposure bias and single-game reinforcement learning (RL) overfitting, scaling it to autoregressive VLMs faces two bottlenecks. First, token-to-action misalignment from subword length bias distorts discrete action probabilities and uncertainty margins. Second, multi-teacher policy conflict arises as source teachers under incompatible dynamics issue contradictory closed-loop corrections, causing negative transfer. We propose CAMOPD (Conflict-Aware Multi-Teacher On-Polic
s881739aa66.summary: A method called conflict-aware multi-teacher on-policy distillation targets consolidating game experts into one vision-language model that plays unseen games from pixels.
s881739aa66.why: Describes fixes for token-to-action misalignment when distilling autoregressive VLMs, relevant to training generalist agents.

s2c1769af83.title: Inference Equivalence and Quotient Coding
s2c1769af83.description: arXiv:2611.21096v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Incomplete observations can admit multiple physical interpretations without making every task conclusion ambiguous. Recovering all compatible scenes is often unnecessary, whereas indiscriminate compression may change which claims are justified. We ask which distinctions among observation-compatible interpretation sets must be retained to preserve every valid conclusion of a specified task. We first define inference validity as truth across all physically compatible states and characterize it, under a closedness condition, by distances to physically realizable falsifying measurements. For a finite semantic claim family ordered by specificity, the Exact Inference Frontier forms the unique minimal antichain generating all valid claims. We then d
s2c1769af83.summary: A theoretical paper defines inference validity over sets of physically compatible scene interpretations and asks which distinctions must be kept to preserve task conclusions.

s89ee30e333.title: CivilBench: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Multimodal Information Integration in Civil Engineering
s89ee30e333.description: arXiv:2611.21105v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs), is increasingly applied in civil and structural engineering for disaster assessment, structural analysis, and engineering decision support. However, the extent to which current VLMs possess the reasoning capabilities required for reliable engineering judgments remains unclear. In this work, we introduce CivilBench, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating VLMs in civil engineering and disaster-related scenarios. CivilBench covers three major task families: Sequential Reasoning, Image-based Structural Understanding, and Open-world Understanding, encompassing numerical reasoning, structural damage assessment, risk inference, causal analysi
s89ee30e333.summary: CivilBench is a benchmark evaluating vision-language models on multimodal reasoning for civil engineering and disaster-related scenarios.
s89ee30e333.why: Shows current VLM reliability for engineering judgment is being measured, useful for assessing domain readiness before deployment.

sfdf7cbb6cb.title: InclusionMed: Benchmarking AI for Inclusive Healthcare
sfdf7cbb6cb.description: arXiv:2611.21218v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Advancing medical AI for inclusive healthcare requires evaluation across diverse healthcare roles, tasks, and care settings, but benchmark coverage remains uneven. We introduce InclusionMed, an open medical AI evaluation initiative for inclusive healthcare. The InclusionMed Atlas organizes benchmarks across three healthcare roles and three AI capabilities. For the first release, we selected four public benchmarks from 388 candidates through structured audits and independent reproduction. With InclusionMed-DxFiles, our private diagnostic reasoning benchmark, the Atlas contains five benchmarks covering three of its nine role--capability cells. We evaluated frontier large language models on the Atlas and aggregated their results into the Inclusi
sfdf7cbb6cb.summary: InclusionMed is an open medical AI evaluation initiative that organizes benchmarks across healthcare roles and AI capabilities, selecting four public benchmarks from 388 candidates.
sfdf7cbb6cb.why: Offers a structured medical AI evaluation atlas for teams assessing healthcare models across diverse roles and settings.

sf025cf10af.title: Language-model agents' beliefs can be manipulated via truthful evidence in open channel
sf025cf10af.description: arXiv:2611.21235v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language-model agents' beliefs can be manipulated through open channels such as social media, even when the information they receive is truthful. When agents fill gaps between fragments with self-induced relationships, they may accept those relationships as established facts and pass the resulting rumours to others. Drawing on cognitive theory of narrative understanding and film theory of montage, we introduce Generative Montage to operationalize this failure, termed narrative overfitting, by coordinating agents to arrange truthful fragments into misleading narratives. Across 1,090 rumour targets from six Twitter events, agents often accepted rumours overconfidently, with overall acceptance exceeding 65 percent in twelve of fourteen models. A
sf025cf10af.summary: Researchers show language-model agents' beliefs can be manipulated via truthful fragments on open channels, using a method called Generative Montage to induce narrative overfitting.
sf025cf10af.why: Reveals a risk for agents reading social media: truthful inputs can still produce false beliefs that agents spread to others.

s3ed1e54697.title: How Developer Personality Shapes the Use of AI Coding Assistants
s3ed1e54697.description: arXiv:2611.21240v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Developers differ in personality traits that shape how they approach software development tasks, yet AI coding assistants either behave uniformly or offer personalization features whose fit with individual developers must be found through trial and error. This is because it remains unclear how personality shapes developers' experiences with AI assistants, and thus which traits personalization should account for. In other words, we provide tools with no underlying theory on what works when and why. We take a first step towards such a theory with a systematic scoping review on how users' personality relates to their perception of LLM-based tools. We identified twelve studies through general search engines, major Software Engineering (SE) venues
s3ed1e54697.summary: Researchers propose a theory linking developer personality traits to how they experience AI coding assistants, aiming to guide personalization.
s3ed1e54697.why: Suggests personalization of coding assistants should target specific personality traits rather than relying on trial and error.

sff03de5d1d.title: Stream of Belief: Eliciting Collective Intelligence through Latent Belief Dynamics
sff03de5d1d.description: arXiv:2611.21250v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we view multi-agent reasoning as a process of seeking a collective equilibrium of implicit belief dynamics and introduce Stream of Belief (SoB), where agents maintain continuous latent beliefs and iteratively refine them through communication and reflection. Our method seeks a collective belief state of a multi-agent system where further communication induces no meaningful information propagation. Through extensive experiments, we demonstrate the generalization of SoB across tasks and model families. More Broadly, our results suggest a new perspective on scaling multi-agent reasoning from belief dynamics.
sff03de5d1d.summary: Researchers introduce Stream of Belief, a multi-agent method where agents refine continuous latent beliefs through communication until the collective state stabilizes.

sbd320268f4.title: CAE-Bench: Benchmarking AI Agents for Reusable CAE Solver Development
sbd320268f4.description: arXiv:2611.21273v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We developed CAE-Bench, a benchmark to evaluate AI agents on Computer-Aided Engineering (CAE) solver development. A CAE solver is more than a PDE solver; it must be able to generalize across various inputs, such as different boundary conditions, geometries, and material properties. CAE-Bench evaluates the generalizability of AI-developed CAE solvers by providing the same task, such as a heat transfer problem, multiple cases, with each case specifying an input. The AI agent develops a solver for a fixed task using only a few public cases, and the resulting solver is then tested on held-out cases, i.e., cases it has never seen before. We evaluate 12 models across a range of reasoning settings on 80 computational tasks. Our experiments show that
sbd320268f4.summary: Researchers released CAE-Bench, a benchmark testing whether AI agents can build CAE solvers that generalize across boundary conditions, geometries, and material properties.
sbd320268f4.why: Shows that solving one case is not enough for engineering solvers, so evaluations need to test generalization across varied inputs.

s226406482a.title: Turing Agent: Agentic Formal Verification for Mathematical Research
s226406482a.description: arXiv:2611.21299v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are rapidly advancing mathematical discovery, moving beyond benchmark-level problem solving to tackle frontier research problems. This progress is ushering mathematics into an era of proof abundance, raising a fundamental challenge: how can we ensure the correctness of the ever-growing volume of AI-generated proofs and transform them into trustworthy, machine-verified mathematical knowledge? We introduce Turing Agent, an agent harness designed to orchestrate end-to-end formal verification of research-level mathematics. Its wo-scale architecture integrates theorem formalization and proof formalization agents, empowered by structured proof decomposition, parallel verification, accumulated proof experience, and selec
s226406482a.summary: Turing Agent is an agent harness that orchestrates end-to-end formal verification of research-level mathematics to check AI-generated proofs.
s226406482a.why: Offers a route to machine-verifying the growing volume of AI-generated proofs rather than trusting them unchecked.

se99be66c62.title: Share your Screen and Talk to Gemini: How Young Learners Interact with Multimodal GenAI While Solving Scratch Tasks
se99be66c62.description: arXiv:2611.21306v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Children using Scratch to learn programming can struggle with text-heavy, lengthy explanations and hints during debugging. Verbal interactions based on screen sharing or camera data may be an interesting alternative for supporting learners. We therefore explore the quality, use, and perceptions of fifth- and sixth-graders' verbal interactions with a GenAI tutor. The goal is to investigate the quality and use of the multimodal GenAI tutor in the given context. First of all, a pilot study of eight tasks conducted without students helped inform the process of the tutor's classroom evaluation. The classroom study was realized after fifth- and sixth-graders had participated in six Scratch classroom lessons. Then 23 students were introduced to the
se99be66c62.summary: A study examines how fifth and sixth graders verbally interact with a multimodal Gemini-based GenAI tutor while solving Scratch programming tasks using screen sharing.

s7076000b37.title: Benchleaking Is Accelerating: Benchmark contamination has worsened sharply in the past month -- from post-training down to pre-training base models
s7076000b37.description: arXiv:2611.21315v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Benchmark contamination is not new, but recent model releases show it in a sharper form. We use the term benchleaking for the case in which a benchmark's own test examples enter training data, so that a score reflects recall rather than capability. This differs from benchmaxxing, which optimizes toward a benchmark without seeing its test set. We document two escalations over the past month. First, in post-training, the traces have become explicit: recent audits show an agent stating hidden test requirements it was never given in 23% of its attempts, where its predecessor did so in none, and continuing to follow them after the task is changed to contradict them (Schaeffer and R\"auker, 2026; Lo and Lo, 2026). Second, the problem has reached pr
s7076000b37.summary: An analysis reports that benchmark contamination, where test examples enter training data, has sharply worsened in recent model releases, from post-training to pre-training.
s7076000b37.why: Inflated benchmark scores undermine model selection, so teams should weigh evaluation results with contamination risk in mind.

s16bb4824a0.title: VisualArtifactSpec 1.0: Evaluating Visual Artifacts under Task Specifications
s16bb4824a0.description: arXiv:2611.21382v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Visual artifact tasks test agents' ability to translate task specifications and source materials into outputs that meet practical needs. Evaluation across artifact families helps distinguish broadly applicable authoring capabilities from strengths confined to a particular medium. We introduce VisualArtifactSpec 1.0 (VAS), a benchmark of 211 creation and modification tasks spanning presentations, static graphics, animations and videos, and web interfaces. Each task specifies authoring objectives, source materials, constraints, and deliverables. Existing benchmarks provide limited support for systematically evaluating how authoring choices suit different audiences, purposes, and media across artifact families. VAS evaluates two aspects separate
s16bb4824a0.summary: Researchers introduce VisualArtifactSpec 1.0, a 211-task benchmark evaluating agents on creating and modifying presentations, graphics, animations, videos, and web interfaces.
s16bb4824a0.why: Gives teams a cross-medium benchmark for judging whether agents can produce practical visual deliverables.

sf14787c442.title: Shaping AI's Beliefs Before It Generates: Human Sense of Agency in Creative AI
sf14787c442.description: arXiv:2611.21405v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI systems for creative media generation expand human capabilities yet risk diminishing human agency. A core problem is anchoring, where the user's thinking becomes anchored to a polished, generated artifact, shifting the user's role from active authoring to reactive editing. We propose pre-generation belief controls that can empower creators to inspect, revise, and steer the AI's interpretation before any media is generated, so that the initial anchor is set by the human. We formalize four design principles and instantiate them in the Proactive Co-Creator (PaCC), a system for early-stage conceptual ideation and prototyping that proactively surfaces its assumptions and uncertainty through clarifications, belief graphs, and media attributes, i
sf14787c442.summary: Researchers propose pre-generation belief controls that let creators steer an AI's interpretation before media is generated, so the user sets the initial anchor.
sf14787c442.why: Points to interface designs that keep users in an authoring role rather than reactive editing of AI output.

sbd8ca6f677.title: Harness Leverage Across Model Size: A Ladder of Five Local Agent Harnesses from 0.75B to 4.7B
sbd8ca6f677.description: arXiv:2611.21407v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A harness turns a model into a system that completes tasks: it builds the prompt, exposes tools and decides when work is done. Harness comparisons hold the model fixed. Model comparisons hold the harness fixed. We vary both: five shipped harnesses, 18 artifact-producing tasks, four locally deployable open-weight models from 0.75B to 4.7B and a 35.5B anchor, with one deterministic checker scoring all 360 ladder cells. The completion-controlling harness, Mingbird, has the highest mean at every size. Of four pre-registered paired contrasts, two survive Holm correction, at 0.75B and 4.7B. Thirteen of sixteen paired intervals exclude zero under the deployment reading, with leads from 0.075 over the strongest rival to 0.819 over the weakest. The co
sbd8ca6f677.summary: A study compares five local agent harnesses across four open-weight models from 0.75B to 4.7B, finding the harness strongly affects task completion.
sbd8ca6f677.why: Shows harness design can matter as much as model size for small local agents, informing on-device deployment choices.

sd03d32ef5c.title: Learning to Reason with Predictive Gains for Generative Recommendation
sd03d32ef5c.description: arXiv:2611.21441v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reasoning-enhanced generative recommendation (GR) has attracted increasing attention for leveraging the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) to improve next-item prediction. However, existing methods primarily optimize reasoning through Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with rule-based rewards determined by final recommendation performance, which faces two key limitations: (i) unmeasured predictive contributions within reasoning, where the predictive contributions of individual reasoning steps are not directly reflected in optimization signals, and (ii) weakly discriminative learning signals within groups, where different reasoning trajectories within the group often receive indistinguishable rewards, limiting effect
sd03d32ef5c.summary: Researchers propose a reasoning method for generative recommendation that rewards individual reasoning steps by their predictive contribution, rather than only final performance.

s1d8a762bec.title: Subprocess-Constrained Markov Decision Processes
s1d8a762bec.description: arXiv:2611.21471v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Constrained Markov decision processes (CMDPs) typically bound expected cumulative cost from an initial state. Such a guarantee can be insufficient when a policy must remain feasible after every history it may encounter. We introduce \emph{subprocess-constrained MDPs} (S-CMDPs), which require the expected discounted cost of each continuation, conditional on any reachable history, to satisfy a bound determined by the current state. This stronger requirement changes the structure and complexity of the problem: we show that stationary policies can be strictly suboptimal, and finding even an approximately optimal stationary policy is NP-hard. We adapt a recently introduced value-set iteration framework to show that history-dependent policies surpr
s1d8a762bec.summary: Researchers introduce subprocess-constrained MDPs, which require cost bounds to hold for every continuation from any reachable history, not just from the start.
s1d8a762bec.why: Stronger feasibility guarantees matter for safety-critical policies that must remain valid after every history they may encounter.

sd48af83b95.title: Generative AI and the Crisis of Higher Education Assessments: Examining 'AI-Proofing' Strategies for College-Level Assessments
sd48af83b95.description: arXiv:2611.21476v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Higher education is confronting an academic-integrity challenge unlike any in its history. Students can now outsource homework, take-home assignments, and online examinations to large language models (LLMs) that complete them in seconds. Existing research on evaluating LLM performance on academic assessments has focused largely on standardized examinations, or on questions from college-level courses drawn from a single discipline. Far less is known about how LLMs perform on college-level assessment questions spanning multiple disciplines, that instructors have purposely designed to be AI-resistant, and about which features of such questions, if any, meaningfully constrain LLM performance. We address this gap by collecting 75 questions from au
sd48af83b95.summary: A study examines how LLMs perform on multidisciplinary college-level assessments and evaluates strategies for AI-proofing higher education assignments.

s858606cfc6.title: Safe Resemblance, Silent Propagation: Limits of Text-Similarity Guardrails for AI Agent Safety
s858606cfc6.description: arXiv:2611.21520v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When AI agents relay information to one another, an output can preserve an injected instruction's effect on downstream agents even after its wording changes, yet legitimate quotation and template reuse can produce high textual overlap with the source, so text-similarity guardrails that attempt to flag the former risk conflating these two cases. We test this distinction using DonkeyRail, a public classifier combining BLEU, ROUGE-L, and METEOR features, deployed in a controlled three-agent email relay, defining a behavioral measure in which an output counts as functional (the injected procedure induces fresh computations in two subsequent agents) independent of the detector's score, alongside legitimate controls that explicitly authorize quotat
s858606cfc6.summary: Researchers test DonkeyRail, a text-similarity guardrail, in a three-agent email relay and find it cannot reliably separate legitimate quotation from propagated injected instructions.
s858606cfc6.why: Shows text-similarity filters alone may miss injected instructions that persist through rewording between agents.

sad2422f052.title: Procedure without Judgment: What Small Language Models Learn under an Exact Verifier
sad2422f052.description: arXiv:2611.21529v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When an authorization policy blocks an agent's tool call, the audit log should name the facts that forced the decision and nothing more. For an executable policy over an enumerable context space this minimal sufficient reason can be computed exactly, so an explanation is scored against ground truth rather than a proxy for it. We use that exactness to ask what a model can learn from a verifier that has no error in it. The explainer sees one request and one decision, never the policy, and has thirty turns in which it may call the policy on altered requests and ask whether a candidate set of facts is sufficient. Frontier models find the exact reason about half the time with the tools alone, and one sentence telling them to shrink the answer lift
sad2422f052.summary: Researchers study what small language models learn to explain blocked agent tool calls when given an exact verifier for an authorization policy.
sad2422f052.why: Relevant to auditing agent authorization decisions, where explanations can be scored against exact ground truth.

s6b4d1edc7f.title: SciResearch-Eval: Evaluating Scientific Judgment in Autonomous Experimental Agents
s6b4d1edc7f.description: arXiv:2611.21541v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce SciResearch-Eval, an interactive benchmark of scientific judgment built on a standard laboratory problem: measuring a material's thermal properties by heating it and fitting a heat-conduction simulator. An agent designs its own experiments, uses a supplied simulator that may be under-resolved or physically wrong, and reports each property with a 95% interval. To our knowledge it is the first benchmark to combine agent-designed experiments, a deliberately flawed simulator, and proper scoring of calibrated intervals against exact ground truth. On a held-out split (93 tasks, 9 models, 2,511 episodes), models handle procedural traps. When the simulator is missing physics, most report wrong values while stating they are 95% sure: thei
s6b4d1edc7f.summary: SciResearch-Eval is a benchmark testing autonomous agents on designing experiments, handling a flawed simulator, and reporting calibrated 95% intervals for thermal properties.
s6b4d1edc7f.why: Tests calibration and judgment in agents doing experimental science, beyond simple task completion.

s7db169eaf5.title: Right Reason, Wrong Advice: Evaluating Recourse in LLM Explanations of Denied Requests
s7db169eaf5.description: arXiv:2611.21545v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language models increasingly write the explanations people receive when a rule system denies their request. If several rules deny the request independently, an explanation can name a true reason and still leave the person denied after they fix it. We call the missing property recourse validity: changing what the explanation cites, without changing what was asked for, can flip the decision. We compute it exactly, and a hitting-set argument predicts from the policy alone when a correct reason fails. In six of seven rule systems ported from access control and US benefit eligibility, a single correct reason almost never gives recourse when several reasons apply. Across 20 LLMs, checks of whether the cited reasons are correct, computed or asked of
s7db169eaf5.summary: Researchers define 'recourse validity' and show LLM explanations of denied requests can cite a true reason yet leave the person denied after fixing it.
s7db169eaf5.why: Explanations generated by LLMs for rule-based denials may mislead users into fixes that don't flip the decision, a design risk for automated decision systems.

s4bd48d5d7f.title: An XAI Approach to Deep Learning Models in the Detection of DCIS
s4bd48d5d7f.description: arXiv:2106.14186v3 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The results showed that XAI could indeed be used as a proof of concept to begin discussions on the implementation of assistive AI systems within the clinical community.
s4bd48d5d7f.summary: A paper reports that explainable AI techniques applied to deep learning for detecting DCIS, a breast cancer precursor, could serve as a proof of concept for clinical assistive tools.

se7c0284b66.title: Fast Catch-Up, Late Switching: Optimal Batch Size Scheduling via Functional Scaling Laws
se7c0284b66.description: arXiv:2602.14208v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Batch size scheduling (BSS) plays a critical role in large-scale deep learning training, influencing both optimization dynamics and computational efficiency. Yet, its theoretical foundations remain poorly understood. In this work, we show that the functional scaling law (FSL) framework introduced in Li et al. (2025a) provides a principled lens for analyzing BSS. Specifically, we characterize the optimal BSS under a fixed data budget and show that its structure depends sharply on task difficulty. For easy tasks, optimal schedules keep increasing batch size throughout. In contrast, for hard tasks, the optimal schedule maintains small batch sizes for most of training and switches to large batches only in a late stage. To explain the emergence
se7c0284b66.summary: A paper uses functional scaling laws to characterize optimal batch size scheduling for deep learning training, showing optimal structure depends on task difficulty.
se7c0284b66.why: Provides theoretical grounding for batch size schedules that could improve training efficiency and compute use in large-scale runs.

s94aa6fe9c0.title: ChartSync: A Benchmark for Visuo-Logical Cascading Chart Editing
s94aa6fe9c0.description: arXiv:2607.10301v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative image editing models struggle with structured statistical charts when data modifications require geometric synchronization. We formalize this task as Visuo-Logical Cascading Editing (VLCE). However, existing methods remain confined to localized text substitutions and struggle with dependency-aware cascading updates. To systematically evaluate this capability, we introduce ChartSync, an expert-validated benchmark constructed via a programmatic rendering pipeline that guarantees deterministic visuo-logical coupling for the ground truth. ChartSync comprises 870 triplets across 9 chart categories and 4 task types, including 235 geometry-coupled VLCE instances that specifically test cascading text-to-geometry synchronization. We furth
s94aa6fe9c0.summary: Researchers introduce ChartSync, a benchmark for editing statistical charts where data changes require cascading, dependency-aware updates that current image editing models struggle with.
s94aa6fe9c0.why: Shows generative image editors fail at structured chart edits needing consistent geometric updates, relevant to teams building document or chart editing tools.

s94ffdc832f.title: Sivia: Learning to Draw, Learning to Learn
s94ffdc832f.description: arXiv:2609.33386v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A paper's overview figure is often the first thing readers see: it must explain the method correctly and look polished. We present Sivia, an overview-figure system that reads the paper, plans its relations, adapts visual organization from recent top-conference papers, and composes a design for image generation. Sivia improves with use through human-guided recursive self-improvement (RSI) at two levels: learning to draw revises its drawing skill from feedback on accuracy and presentation, and learning to learn revises the updater that proposes those revisions. A personal profile adapts presentation to its user's aesthetic preferences while the scientific content stays fixed. A diagnostic study of 1,964 overviews for 445 papers (17,973 relati
s94ffdc832f.summary: Sivia is a system that generates paper overview figures by planning relations and composing designs, improving through human-guided recursive self-improvement.

s9b3b9656da.title: RoboACE: Adversarial Co-Evolution for Robot Self-Improvement
s9b3b9656da.description: arXiv:2611.13034v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Robot agents can improve reusable skills, planning procedures, and recovery strategies from execution feedback, yet a fixed practice source leaves the search for new weaknesses unchanged. Useful practice depends on the agent's current capabilities, so the procedure that chooses practice must also be revisable. We present RoboACE (Robot Adversarial Co-Evolution), a framework that jointly evolves curriculum and execution harnesses around frozen foundation models. The curriculum harness uses accumulated capability evidence to propose informative challenges, while the execution harness responds with reusable revisions that expand execution capabilities. Alternating updates hold one side fixed as the other changes, and admitted challenges form f
s9b3b9656da.summary: RoboACE is a framework where robot agents co-evolve their practice curriculum and execution harnesses around frozen foundation models to improve self-improvement.

sc3b3e29164.title: One Question, Four Voices: How Advice for Alzheimer's Caregiving Differs Between Caregivers, Clinicians, and Large Language Models
sc3b3e29164.description: arXiv:2611.18604v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Online caregiver forums are an important source of emotional and informational support for Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (ADRD). We compare responses to 85 real caregiver questions from ALZConnected across four responder groups: peer caregivers, physicians, ChatGPT, and a retrieval-augmented CareGPT grounded in peer discussions. Using 28 measures spanning linguistic form, emotional support, informational support, and topic scope, we examine how these voices differ when answering the same questions. Peers provided time-anchored narratives and community grounding; clinicians offered concise, advice-forward, clinically bounded guidance; and LLMs produced a formal, verbose, highly structured consultation style. CareGPT showed minima
sc3b3e29164.summary: A study compares Alzheimer's caregiving advice from peer caregivers, physicians, ChatGPT, and a retrieval-augmented model across 85 ALZConnected questions using 28 measures.
sc3b3e29164.why: Highlights how LLM health advice differs in form and support from human sources, informing evaluation of medical-domain assistants.

sc58bef54cc.title: Syntactic Complexity Convergence in Dialogue: Analysis of the Phenomenon and Application to LLM Detection
sc58bef54cc.description: arXiv:2611.18606v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We revisit the under-explored phenomenon of syntactic complexity convergence in dialogue. Extending prior topic-level analyses to full conversations, we examine five human-human datasets and a set of human-LLM dialogues. We integrate and evaluate a multidimensional set of syntactic complexity metrics to quantify structural variation in dialogue. Our analyses reveal robust syntactic complexity convergence across human-human datasets, especially in task-oriented interactions, and statistical tests confirm that these effects are not due to chance. In contrast, human-LLM dialogues show no significant convergence under individual metrics; however, linear-CKA uncovers a distinct cross-metric convergence pattern. Motivated by these differences, we
sc58bef54cc.summary: Researchers find robust syntactic complexity convergence across human-human dialogue datasets and examine whether it can help detect LLM-generated dialogue.

s924ee742bc.title: Justification of Emotional Appeal in Computational Argumentation
s924ee742bc.description: arXiv:2611.18607v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Emotional appeals (EAs) are often treated as fallacious in computational argumentation, yet they may be justified when warranted by the context. We introduce the task of predicting EA justification and present the first human-annotated dataset for this task, covering 1,176 argument--context pairs. Grounded in philosophical literature, our framework evaluates EA justification along logical and emotional dimensions. Human annotations show that justification criteria form a shared latent judgment space, with evidential proportionality and normative acceptability most strongly associated with overall justification. We further find that EAs without logical support are not always judged fully unjustified, and stronger EAs are not necessarily judg
s924ee742bc.summary: Researchers introduce a task and a 1,176-pair human-annotated dataset for predicting whether emotional appeals in arguments are justified by context.

s69427a0435.title: Understanding Failures in LLM Reasoning by Learning Structured Representations of Chain-of-Thought
s69427a0435.description: arXiv:2611.18611v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) is central to improving reasoning in large language models, yet existing evaluation methods focus on step-level signals and ignore the underlying structure of reasoning traces. This raises a key question: what aspects of reasoning quality (i.e., correctness, efficiency, and failure patterns) are encoded in the structure of a CoT trace? We introduce \textbf{CoT2Graph}, a framework that represents CoT traces as directed dependency graphs, making relationships between reasoning steps explicit and capturing patterns such as backtracking, branching, and subtask merging. We model these graphs with graph neural networks and use attribution-based explanations to identify structural patterns associated with reasoning quality.
s69427a0435.summary: CoT2Graph represents chain-of-thought reasoning traces as dependency graphs to analyze correctness, efficiency, and failure patterns in LLM reasoning.
s69427a0435.why: Offers a structured way to diagnose LLM reasoning failures beyond step-level checks, useful for teams debugging model reasoning.

s9eb144473a.title: When Helpful Agents Cause Financial Harm: Evaluating LLM Agent Safety in Executable Economic Worlds
s9eb144473a.description: arXiv:2611.18612v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As LLM agents become increasingly capable of making consequential economic decisions, their safety under economic pressures remains poorly understood. We introduce EconSafeBench, the first benchmark for systematically evaluating the safety of LLM agents in executable economic environments. EconSafeBench contains 828 cases across five economic scenarios and four categories of safety violations. A key design is the matched evaluation of three sources of safety pressure, including explicit user requests, pressure from other actors, and pressure arising from the agent's own pursuit of a performance objective. We further evaluate safety at both static and dynamic scales through 30-period interactions with persistent memory and matched controls.
s9eb144473a.summary: EconSafeBench, a benchmark of 828 cases across five economic scenarios, evaluates safety of LLM agents making consequential economic decisions under various pressures.
s9eb144473a.why: Shows agents can cause financial harm under economic pressure, a concern for teams deploying agents with transactional authority.

s9553f1af56.title: The Judge Is Not Impartial: Self-Preference in Medical LLM Evaluation
s9553f1af56.description: arXiv:2611.18616v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to evaluate model-generated medical content, creating a potential circularity: an LLM judge may favor outputs generated by the same model independently of clinical quality. To characterize LLM judge self-preference in medical settings, we measured same-model affinity in single-turn specialist question answering and multi-turn standardized-patient encounters. We evaluated eight models, two from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Qwen, on 620 real point of care questions from clinicians (Real-POCQi). The same eight models also generated and judged 200 standardized patient-clinician scenarios (MedSP1000) up to 8 visible turns. In total, our analysis spans 13,760 LLM judgments. We define three comp
s9553f1af56.summary: A study finds LLM judges show self-preference when evaluating medical content, favoring outputs from the same model regardless of clinical quality, across eight models.
s9553f1af56.why: Using LLMs to grade their own medical outputs can bias evaluations, so teams should validate judge models before relying on automated scoring.

sca0763d706.title: Which Mathematical Context Supports Target-Aligned Conjecture Generation? A Paired Ablation Study
sca0763d706.description: arXiv:2611.18621v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generating mathematical conjectures from natural-language context is challenging because theorem-relevant information is distributed across multiple forms of mathematical context, including definitions, objects, assumptions, and constructions. We study which of these contextual signals help a model recover the specific claim supported by the surrounding setup, using 61 main theorems from 12 papers across four mathematical domains. For each theorem, we redact the result and represent the remaining setup using six context components. A paired ablation design compares full context, six leave-one-out conditions, and six single-component conditions, yielding 793 generated conjectures. Context components were largely complementary: removing one c
sca0763d706.summary: A paired ablation study on 61 theorems from 12 papers tests which mathematical context components help LLMs generate the target conjecture.

s3b007ec58c.title: Evaluating the Robustness of Fact-Checking LLMs on Multilingual Evidence
s3b007ec58c.description: arXiv:2611.18623v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Automated fact-checking benchmarks typically pair claims with clean, curated evidence in high-resource languages, but real-world evidence is often incomplete, misleading, or written in a language where models are weaker. We evaluate the robustness of fact-checking LLMs for different languages. Building on EuroVerdict, we construct gold evidence sets for 190 claims in each of English, German, Greek, and Romanian, then apply four corruption strategies at two severity levels. We test LLMs on a set of claims, providing them with evidence from the sets above. A rubric-based LLM-as-a-judge scores reasoning quality. Verdict accuracy proves highly sensitive to both factors: Misleading edit cut Llama 3.1 8B's English accuracy from 80.00% to 16.84%,
s3b007ec58c.summary: Researchers test fact-checking LLMs on claims with corrupted multilingual evidence in English, German, Greek, and Romanian, finding robustness varies by language.
s3b007ec58c.why: Real-world evidence is often incomplete or in weaker languages, so multilingual robustness testing matters for deployed fact-checking systems.

sbb99808e22.title: Skill Transfer: Adapting Agent Skills from Strong to Weak Agents
sbb99808e22.description: arXiv:2611.18624v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agent skills are modular bundles of instructions, code, and resources that an agent loads on demand, increasingly authored and validated on frontier models and shared as an open standard. The same skill behaves differently across models: a strong model turns it into a large performance gain, while a weak model realizes little of that gain and sometimes does worse than with no skill at all. Cost and resource constraints, however, often restrict real deployments to exactly these weaker agents. We hypothesize that the strong model silently supplies procedural steps the skill leaves implicit, which the weak model omits, and formalize closing this gap as \emph{Skill Transfer}: holding the skill's capability ceiling and the model's parameters fix
sbb99808e22.summary: Skill Transfer proposes adapting agent skills authored on strong models so weaker, cheaper agents can realize more of their performance gains.
sbb99808e22.why: Weaker models often gain little from shared agent skills, so adaptation methods could make cost-constrained agent deployments more effective.

s95b44ad76d.title: Interpretability-Guided Auditing for Clinical Language Models for Discharge Prediction
s95b44ad76d.description: arXiv:2611.18626v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Clinical natural language processing (NLP) models for hospital discharge prediction are vulnerable to explicit discharge-related lexical cues in clinical notes, even when note timestamps are temporally filtered. These cues may act as proxies for future outcomes, leading models to rely on shortcut-like signals rather than clinically meaningful evidence. We propose AuditBERT-Discharge, a lightweight framework that reframes interpretability as a training-time auditing mechanism. Token-level SHAP attributions from an initial BioClinicalBERT model are used to identify highly attributed discharge-related tokens, which are subsequently masked in the training corpus before model retraining. We evaluate the framework on a retrospective cohort of ele
s95b44ad76d.summary: Researchers propose AuditBERT-Discharge, a lightweight framework using SHAP attributions to audit clinical NLP models for discharge-related lexical shortcut cues.
s95b44ad76d.why: Shows how interpretability can be used during training to catch shortcut learning in clinical models before deployment.

se5dd58f23a.title: Minimum cores in lattice graphs: zonotope structure and quartic growth
se5dd58f23a.description: arXiv:2611.18633v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A core of a graph is a nonempty vertex set in which every member has at least as many neighbours inside the set as outside. We study the minimum size $c_{m,n}$ of a finite core in the graph on $\Z^m$ joining points at sup-norm distance at most $n$. The local majority condition imposes a global geometric constraint: the convex hull of every core has an explicit lattice zonotope $H_n^{(m)}$ as a Minkowski summand. In the plane, this zonotope has width asymptotic to $6\zeta(3)n^3/\pi^2$. We prove that all its lattice points form a core and construct a shell with $O(n^4)$ points. Together with a packing argument, this gives $c_{2,n}=\Theta(n^4)$ and coordinate widths $\Theta(n^3)$ for every minimum core. We determine $c_{2,1}=12$ and $c_{2,2}=9
se5dd58f23a.summary: A mathematical paper studies minimum core sizes in lattice graphs, showing a zonotope structure constraint and quartic growth in the plane.

sf98c088795.title: Brain AI Scientist: An Evidence-Based Multi-Agent System for Translational Neuroimaging in Precision Psychiatry
sf98c088795.description: arXiv:2611.18634v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) has revealed widespread brain-network alterations in psychiatric disorders, yet translating these findings into individualized clinical decision support remains challenging. Here we introduce Brain AI Scientist, an autonomous multi-agent framework that integrates patient-specific fMRI, clinical information, and scientific evidence through retrieval, verification, and prioritization. Guided by Research Domain Criteria and evidence-based medicine, it builds traceable chains linking phenotypes, anatomical abnormalities, biomarkers, mechanisms, interventions, and validation strategies. In a representative autism case, Brain AI Scientist generated 37 anatomical hypotheses, retained 26
sf98c088795.summary: Researchers introduce Brain AI Scientist, a multi-agent system that combines patient fMRI, clinical data, and literature to support individualized psychiatric decision support.
sf98c088795.why: Illustrates a multi-agent design for traceable, evidence-linked clinical decision support, though the text gives no validation results.

sfafe45f964.title: Multimodal Fusion with Pre-trained Models for Psychotherapy Outcome Prediction from Emotional Dynamics
sfafe45f964.description: arXiv:2611.18635v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In-session emotional dynamics are associated with psychotherapy outcomes but difficult to measure at scale. Pretrained multimodal models provide automated access to facial, vocal, and textual signals, yet clinical datasets remain small. Our research question is how pretrained multimodal representations can best support psychotherapy outcome prediction under data scarcity. Three studies use 106 sessions from 88 patients and nine session-level outcome scales (HSCL-11, EPO-1, POMS). Study 1 asks whether deep learning outperforms classical machine learning: a two-stage deep pipeline, first predicting window-level valence/arousal and then session outcomes, transferred poorly (best single configuration, $r=.078$). Study 2 asks which representatio
sfafe45f964.summary: Study evaluates pretrained multimodal models for predicting psychotherapy outcomes from facial, vocal, and textual emotional signals using 106 sessions from 88 patients.

s4fad839da5.title: ReVision: Selective Intrinsic Reasoning for Tool-Augmented, Reasoning-Intensive VQA
s4fad839da5.description: arXiv:2611.18637v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: External tools substantially expand what multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can retrieve and compute on reasoning-intensive visual questions, and aggregate accuracy typically improves when tools are available. Our empirical study across six VQA benchmarks shows that aggregate accuracy gains under tool access can coexist with answer reversals: questions answered correctly without tools but incorrectly with tools. Trajectory analysis reveals substantially shorter reasoning turns under tool access, suggesting a shift from intrinsic visual reasoning toward reliance on external outputs. We propose ReVision, a training-free test-time method that registers intrinsic reconsideration as an optional action alongside search and code execution. W
s4fad839da5.summary: ReVision studies tool-augmented multimodal LLMs on visual QA, finding tool access can flip correct answers to incorrect ones despite higher aggregate accuracy.
s4fad839da5.why: Reveals that adding tools to multimodal models can introduce answer regressions, which matters when designing tool-augmented reasoning systems.

s3a2e1349a3.title: SynthDCB: World Distillation for Scalable Device Control Benchmarking
s3a2e1349a3.description: arXiv:2611.18639v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Scaling device-control evaluation requires scaling both the worlds agents interact with and the tasks they must solve. We introduce SynthDCB, a scalable benchmark for environment awareness and device control built through world distillation. World distillation transforms knowledge of device behaviors, interaction constraints, and environmental effects into modular executable components, which are composed into interactive worlds with explicit states, actions, and temporal dynamics. A unified capability representation connects tool discovery, world execution, and task synthesis, allowing new capabilities to enter evaluation through a shared construction pipeline. SynthDCB instantiates Home, Car, and Phone domains with 114 device classes, 1,1
s3a2e1349a3.summary: SynthDCB introduces a scalable benchmark for device control and environment awareness, built by composing synthetic executable worlds from device behavior knowledge.
s3a2e1349a3.why: Offers a scalable way to evaluate device-control agents across many generated environments and tasks.

s1014415bcc.title: FedFit: Federated Dynamic Sparse Training via Fisher Information scoring
s1014415bcc.description: arXiv:2611.18643v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Cross-device Federated Learning (FL) is frequently bottlenecked by the prohibitive memory and communication costs of training deep neural networks on resource-constrained edge hardware. While federated dynamic sparse training aims to alleviate these costs by adjusting sparse structures during training, existing methods rely on magnitude-based heuristics that are fundamentally ill-suited for the non-convergent, heterogeneous environments inherent to FL. To address this challenge, we propose FedFit, a federated dynamic sparse training framework that replaces simple heuristics with optimization-centric criteria for structure adjustment. By leveraging a second-order approximation of the loss landscape via the Fisher Information Matrix, FedFit e
s1014415bcc.summary: FedFit proposes federated dynamic sparse training that uses Fisher information scoring instead of magnitude heuristics to cut memory and communication costs on edge devices.
s1014415bcc.why: Could reduce memory and communication costs for training on resource-constrained edge devices in federated learning.

s44d81253a0.title: Minari: Infrastructure for Collaborative Reinforcement Learning Datasets
s44d81253a0.description: arXiv:2611.18644v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Offline reinforcement learning (RL) depends on shared datasets, but sharing them is still hard. Each benchmark ships its own format, documentation is thin, and most datasets cannot be regenerated once the environment code moves on. We introduce Minari, an open-source Python library for creating, sharing, and loading RL datasets. Its API follows Gymnasium, so recording a dataset means wrapping an environment and stepping through it as usual. From there, users can attach metadata, filter, combine, and shuffle datasets, and publish or download them with one command through the HuggingFace Hub. Every dataset stores the environment specification, seeds, applied wrappers, and pinned package requirements needed to rebuild the environment and regen
s44d81253a0.summary: Minari is an open-source Python library, API-compatible with Gymnasium, for creating, sharing, filtering, and publishing offline reinforcement learning datasets.
s44d81253a0.why: Provides standardized, regenerable RL dataset tooling that reduces friction in sharing and reproducing offline RL experiments.

s223387f422.title: RSIMed: Scaling Medical Foundation Models beyond Limited Clinical Data via Retrieval-Grounded Self-Evolution
s223387f422.description: arXiv:2611.18646v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rare diseases are hard to diagnose, and the labeled clinical records needed to train models for them are few, private, and slow to extend, since a specialist must read every case. A model that writes its own training tasks could learn beyond these records, but no program can check a model-written diagnosis, and a wrong answer key corrupts training. To tackle this dilemma between data scarcity and difficulty of data annotations, we introduce RSIMed, Recursive Self-Improvement in Medicine, one of the first self-evolving pipelines in which a task proposer co-evolves in context with a diagnostic solver on real clinical records. Seeded by training admissions, a frozen copy of the solver writes each clinical question from retrieved medical eviden
s223387f422.summary: RSIMed proposes a self-evolving pipeline where a medical model generates its own training tasks, grounded by retrieval, to address scarce labeled rare-disease data.

s7482bc38d0.title: Screen Before You Add: Reducing Candidate Inference in Model Ensembles
s7482bc38d0.description: arXiv:2611.18647v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As new models become available, existing ensembles must be updated to be competitive, making them intrinsically dynamic. Deciding whether to add a candidate model can require inference on an entire annotated dataset. Such a screening becomes prohibitive for models with costly inference especially when they ultimately add no value. Even under simple convex aggregation, relying on benchmark scores can be misleading as strong standalone performance does not guarantee ensemble improvement, and fitted ensemble weights can hurt test performance. In this work, we study candidate screening and show how early rejection can be achieved safely, exploiting residual geometry for stratification and rejecting the candidate when the best possible remaining
s7482bc38d0.summary: Paper proposes screening candidate models before adding them to ensembles, avoiding costly full-dataset inference for candidates unlikely to improve the ensemble.
s7482bc38d0.why: Could cut the compute cost of updating model ensembles as new models become available.

se7e61e92e5.title: Rethinking Offline On-Policy Distillation: From Scalar Advantages to Distributional Supervision
se7e61e92e5.description: arXiv:2611.18648v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers teacher capabilities through token-level feedback on student-generated trajectories, but repeatedly evaluating fresh rollouts with the teacher is computationally expensive. Offline methods such as Lightning OPD reduce this cost by caching recorded tokens' teacher log-probabilities on fixed reference rollouts. By extending the idea to a multi-turn agentic search setup, we find that it consistently underperforms the SFT starting point trained by the same teacher. We empirically observe greater teacher--reference mismatch than in mathematical reasoning and post-training distributional flattening, and theoretically show that scalar advantage supervision on fixed rollouts admits solutions with flattened out
se7e61e92e5.summary: Researchers examine offline on-policy distillation for multi-turn agentic search, finding cached teacher log-probabilities underperform SFT and proposing distributional supervision instead.
se7e61e92e5.why: Suggests cheaper offline distillation methods may underperform for agentic models, guiding training pipeline choices.

s0cf9614673.title: Algebraic Interaction: A Recipe for Neural Architecture Generation
s0cf9614673.description: arXiv:2611.18649v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce an algebraic foundation for neural architecture design in which convolution, attention, state-space models, and equivariant layers are expressed through compositions of bilinear product operators over two structures: a position algebra governing positional routing and a feature algebra governing feature interactions. This decomposition makes routing, feature algebra, and operator composition explicit design variables.We focus on the feature-algebra axis through an Algebraic Recipe: fix the routing and operator composition of an existing architecture while replacing its feature algebra. This preserves the information-flow structure while allowing computational and symmetry properties to be modified through algebraic specificatio
s0cf9614673.summary: Paper proposes an algebraic framework that expresses convolution, attention, state-space, and equivariant layers as compositions of bilinear product operators.

s818278e58f.title: SART: Sign-Absolute Reformulation Theory for Binary Variable Reduction in Neural Network Verification
s818278e58f.description: arXiv:2611.18657v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Complete formal verification of neural networks is crucial for their deployment in safety-critical domains. A key bottleneck stems from encoding complexity: traditional methods assign one binary variable per unstable ReLU neuron. We propose the Sign-Absolute Reformulation Theory (SART), which fundamentally breaks the conventional one-to-one mapping between unstable neurons and binary variables by establishing formal reducibility criteria. This allows for finer-grained modeling, where each unstable neuron corresponds on average to fewer than one binary variable, thereby reducing verification complexity at its source. Based on SART, we derive a theoretical lower bound on the number of binary variables required for complete verification and, u
s818278e58f.summary: SART proposes a reformulation that reduces binary variables needed per unstable ReLU neuron in complete neural network verification, easing encoding complexity.
s818278e58f.why: Reducing binary variables could speed up formal verification of neural networks used in safety-critical systems.

s78d01939db.title: ReMoVe: Refining a Video Model's Own Motion for Coherent Human Video Generation
s78d01939db.description: arXiv:2611.18666v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Video generation models have become increasingly capable of synthesizing realistic human motion, yet they often lose track of the very structure that makes the motion plausible. As generated human motion becomes more complex, videos can suffer from progressive body deformation and appearance drift across frames. Existing motion-controlled methods use explicit representations to stabilize generation, but typically rely on pre-defined motion sequences as references. This raises a fundamental question: if the base generator already produces a usable coarse motion, why replace it with an external one? ReMoVe answers this question by treating the coarse output as a motion hypothesis rather than a final result. ReMoVe recovers and refines the und
s78d01939db.summary: ReMoVe refines a video model's own generated motion to reduce progressive body deformation and appearance drift in human video generation without predefined motion references.

s99541859a7.title: Selection-Aware Certification of Client-Constrained Fraud Rule Portfolios Under Synthetic Distribution Shift
s99541859a7.description: arXiv:2611.18687v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Selecting fraud-rule portfolios to satisfy a precision or recall floor can overfit the data used for selection. We study finite-family certification for bounded OR portfolios, comparing point-estimate selection, a fixed safety margin, and one-sided Clopper-Pearson lower bounds with Bonferroni adjustment. In a factorial follow-up with 6,400 datasets from two author-designed synthetic generators, full-validation certification reduced the held-out floor-violation rate by 29.1 percentage points on average versus full-validation point selection, while reducing deployment by 31.7 points. Compared with a fixed 0.05 margin, certification reduced violations by 22.2 points and deployment by 29.4 points; results varied across conditions. Using the ful
s99541859a7.summary: Paper studies certifying fraud-rule portfolios with finite-family bounds, reporting reduced held-out floor-violation rates on 6,400 synthetic datasets.
s99541859a7.why: Shows statistical certification can reduce overfitting when selecting fraud rules, though results rely on author-designed synthetic data.

s9bcfa7c5f1.title: Perceptual Weight Space Programming for Diffusion Super-Resolution
s9bcfa7c5f1.description: arXiv:2611.18690v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Diffusion models for image super-resolution can recover scene content while producing distracting artifacts or unbalanced colors. We study whether a large language model (LLM) can improve perceptual quality by editing a small subset of existing U-Net weights without a clean reference image. The proposed framework provides the editor with architecture code, selected weights, activation summaries, and sampling previews. It permits up to 1,020 candidate trials while limiting accepted changes to three layers and fewer than 0.1\% of model parameters. The evaluation protocol uses ResShift, SinSR, and SUPIR and compares GPT-6 Astra with a specified Qwen3-VL model under matched access. Feedback metrics guide editing, while separate quality metrics
s9bcfa7c5f1.summary: Researchers propose letting an LLM edit a small subset of diffusion super-resolution U-Net weights to improve perceptual quality without a clean reference image.
s9bcfa7c5f1.why: Shows LLMs can act as optimizers over model weights, a technique that may reduce reliance on reference images when tuning generative image models.

s1c26caf35b.title: ARC-VLN: Adaptive Recursive Computing-based Visual-Language Navigation
s1c26caf35b.description: arXiv:2611.18696v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Efficient aerial visual-language navigation (VLN) requires reducing model storage and inference costs while maintaining instruction-conditioned action prediction. We present ARC-VLN, a token-type-aware recursive computation framework built on a language backbone with shared parameters.
