ARC-VLN retains full-depth computation for text and action tokens while adaptively selecting exit depths for visual tokens. Representations of early-exiting visual tokens are retained, and active-token compaction shortens the sequences processed by subsequent recursive blocks. To mitigate routing collapse to a single exit depth, we design a dedicated learning strategy that encourages the model to distribute visual tokens across multiple exit depths.On OpenFly
s1c26caf35b.summary: Researchers present ARC-VLN, a recursive computing framework for aerial visual-language navigation that adaptively exits visual tokens early to cut storage and inference costs.
s1c26caf35b.why: Offers a route to smaller, cheaper vision-language models for drones, where storage and compute are tightly constrained.

s51d01f1e83.title: What Does Hard-Negative Fine-Tuning Teach Multimodal Large Language Models? Controlled Evidence from a Compositional Benchmark
s51d01f1e83.description: arXiv:2611.18701v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fine-tuning on hard negatives is a popular way to improve the compositional reasoning of vision-language models, but when accuracy goes up it is rarely clear what the model actually learned. We ask this question for multimodal large language models. We use CompHall, 2,860 forced-choice questions (spatial, attribute, counting and part-whole) with two graded hard negatives each, three model families (LLaVA-1.5, LLaVA-NeXT and Idefics2), and controls that such studies often lack: gray-image evaluation, three seeds, option-order tests, control arms trained on different question types, and independent benchmarks. We find four things. First, CompHall is not a pure test of vision: part-whole questions can be answered from the text alone (66-95% wi
s51d01f1e83.summary: A controlled study examines what hard-negative fine-tuning actually teaches multimodal LLMs, using the CompHall benchmark across three model families.
s51d01f1e83.why: Suggests accuracy gains from hard-negative fine-tuning may not reflect genuine compositional reasoning, so teams should verify what models learn.

s1e06ba8239.title: T2T Technical Report: Synthesizing GUI Agent Trajectories at Scale from Video Tutorials
s1e06ba8239.description: arXiv:2611.18715v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Training generalist GUI agents requires large volumes of interaction trajectories comprising screenshot sequences paired with grounded UI actions, yet collecting such data through human demonstration is expensive and difficult to scale. Although public software tutorial videos contain rich operational demonstrations, their continuous pixel streams lack discrete action boundaries, semantic intents, and precise spatial coordinates, making them difficult to use directly for model training. To address this, we present T2T (Tutorial-to-Trajectory), a fully automated pipeline for synthesizing GUI agent trajectories at scale. T2T spans desktop, web, and mobile platforms to convert unannotated video tutorials into structured, executable interaction
s1e06ba8239.summary: The T2T report describes converting software tutorial videos into GUI agent interaction trajectories to scale training data without costly human demonstrations.
s1e06ba8239.why: Offers a potentially cheaper data pipeline for training generalist GUI agents, a bottleneck for computer-use agent development.

sfcedcb2a29.title: Editable Video Context: Mid-Context KV-Cache Reuse for Context-Managing Video LLMs
sfcedcb2a29.description: arXiv:2611.18718v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Context Language Models let a model edit its own context, while Suffix Cache Reuse makes edits to text efficient by adjusting the positions of cached keys for surviving tokens. We extend these ideas to video language models with multimodal rotary position embeddings (M-RoPE). We represent a long video as timestamped segments. After viewing a sparsely sampled version, the model selects segments for decoding at 4x the frame rate, and the remaining segments are removed from its context. Our rebuild method reuses the KV cache of surviving segments by rotating their keys with a single offset shared by the temporal, height, and width components of Qwen2.5-VL's M-RoPE. A content-hashed cache also avoids repeating vision-encoder computation for tho
sfcedcb2a29.summary: Researchers extend context-managing language models to video, reusing KV cache of surviving video segments after the model removes irrelevant segments from its context.
sfcedcb2a29.why: Points to inference-efficiency techniques for long video understanding, relevant to teams serving video LLMs under context limits.

s682c382470.title: Acting by Intent, Reacting by Sight: Visual Conditioned Reflexes for Real-Time VLM Agents
s682c382470.description: arXiv:2611.18723v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have shown strong capabilities as generalist agents that perceive, reason, and act in interactive environments. Yet real-time environments such as video games demand both deliberate control for exploration and split-second reactions to fast-moving hazards. Existing agents struggle to handle both: relying solely on direct VLM actions is too slow for sudden events, whereas delegating execution to fixed scripts leaves the agent blind at the moment of action, leading to frequent misfires whenever the scene shifts. Humans overcome this by pairing normal conscious control with conditioned reflexes-while the mind handles deliberate actions and shapes reflex rules, the reflex itself still relies on live vision to make
s682c382470.summary: Researchers propose a dual-process design for real-time VLM game agents that combines deliberate VLM actions with fast visual reflexes for sudden hazards.
s682c382470.why: Highlights a practical architecture for latency-sensitive agents, separating slow planning from fast reactive responses.

sa309f3a93e.title: Latent Fusion: Channel Stacking for Structure-Preserving Image Editing
sa309f3a93e.description: arXiv:2611.18727v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Instruction-based image editing models must condition on the source image, either by sequence concatenation, which appends source tokens to the target sequence (FLUX.1 Kontext), or by channel-wise concatenation, which stacks the source latent onto the noisy latent and widens the input projection (InstructPix2Pix, FLUX.1 Fill). The FLUX.1 Kontext report found channel-wise concatenation worse in initial experiments at 1K resolution with a 12B model and a large corpus. We explore channel-wise concatenation as the lower-cost option for a common production regime: structure-preserving edits that change appearance (sky, exposure, foliage, cleanup) but not layout, about 1,400 training pairs, a 4B non-distilled backbone, and 2K frames. It keeps the
sa309f3a93e.summary: Researchers explore channel-wise concatenation of source latents for instruction-based image editing as a lower-cost alternative to sequence concatenation.
sa309f3a93e.why: Provides a possibly cheaper conditioning method for image editing models, though its benefit over sequence concatenation is not yet established here.

sefcaeb83b4.title: Wrong with Confidence: Measuring Hallucination, Overconfidence and Identity-Conditioned Behaviour in Large Language Models
sefcaeb83b4.description: arXiv:2611.18728v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models answer underspecified questions readily, and accuracy-only evaluation rewards guessing over abstaining. Observational studies link query underspecification to hallucination, but they cannot separate the effect of missing information from item difficulty, and they rarely ask what the model tells the user. We report a pre-registered, paired behavioural study of five open-weight models (Gemma 3 27B, Gemma 4 31B, gpt-oss-120b, Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B and Nemotron 3 Super). Each of 142 factual questions was posed in a fully specified form and in a referentially underspecified form with the same answer key, and three probes measured identity-conditioned behaviour. Two raters scored 5,620 responses under a fixed rubric; effects we
sefcaeb83b4.summary: A pre-registered study of five open-weight models measures hallucination and overconfidence when answering underspecified factual questions.
sefcaeb83b4.why: Shows accuracy-only evaluation rewards guessing, so teams should measure abstention and confidence behavior in deployed LLMs.

s37743aad8f.title: Is It Still There? Place-Registered Verification Makes VLMs Reliable Scene-Change Detectors
s37743aad8f.description: arXiv:2611.18734v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A robot that returns to a space must tell which objects were added, removed or moved since its last visit, while its trajectory, viewpoints and lighting differ between the two visits. We find that multi-image vision-language models (VLMs) fail at this task mainly because they cannot find the place where an object was. A VLM recognises what each frame shows but cannot check whether an object is still at its place in the other capture. It therefore reports objects that only one capture shows and misses most removed and moved objects. We propose STILL, which reformulates change detection as object verification at a registered place. 3D geometry registers the place of each change hypothesis in the other capture, and one VLM answers, from a scen
s37743aad8f.summary: Researchers propose place-registered verification so multi-image VLMs can reliably detect added, removed, or moved objects between robot visits.
s37743aad8f.why: Addresses a concrete failure mode of VLMs in robot scene-change detection, relevant to teams deploying embodied perception.

s18a4d82ad5.title: Target-Free Autocalibration of Stereo PIV Camera Systems via Persistent-State Motion Representations
s18a4d82ad5.description: arXiv:2611.18741v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Stereo Particle Image Velocimetry (PIV) recovers three-component velocity fields by triangulating tracer particles observed by synchronized cameras. It requires an accurate extrinsic calibration, which is still obtained by inserting a physical target into the flow and must be repeated whenever the rig is moved. We present a target-free method that calibrates a stereo PIV rig directly from particle image sequences. Because tracer particles are visually indistinguishable, we match motion rather than appearance: building on CUT3R, each camera stream is processed by a recurrent transformer whose persistent state accumulates particle motion over time. The state is decoded into per-camera optical flow and queried by a cross-view decoder that regr
s18a4d82ad5.summary: Researchers present a target-free method that calibrates stereo PIV camera rigs directly from particle image sequences using motion-based matching.
s18a4d82ad5.why: Removes the need to insert physical calibration targets into flows, which matters mainly for fluid-measurement engineers.

s4d90afb14b.title: Recognizing Events Is Not Enough: Why Streaming VLMs Struggle in Compositional Instruction Triggering
s4d90afb14b.description: arXiv:2611.18743v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recognizing individual events does not guarantee correct execution of compositional instructions in streaming video. For example, given the request "Notify me when the pot boils after someone turns on the stove and leaves the kitchen", existing models may recognize the individual events yet notify too early or miss the intended moment, failing to track how their temporal conditions are satisfied over time. To evaluate this gap, we introduce CoTriggerBench, which composes annotated video events into temporally constrained instructions and verifies notification timing and silence through executable event plans and source-event replay. To address this challenge, we propose a real-time VLM agent, TEMPI. TEMPI decomposes instructions into atomic
s4d90afb14b.summary: CoTriggerBench evaluates streaming video models on compositional, temporally constrained instructions, finding that recognizing individual events does not ensure correct triggering.
s4d90afb14b.why: Reveals a gap for teams building streaming video monitoring, where models may fire alerts too early or miss the intended moment.

s69f5cc7df2.title: Neural Latent Gaussian Process for 3D reconstruction of Mouse Brain Lipids
s69f5cc7df2.description: arXiv:2611.18744v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We address the problem of reconstructing continuous three-dimensional lipid profiles of the mouse brain from lipid measurements acquired only on a sparse set of two-dimensional tissue sections. Using MALDI-MSI measurements from coronal sections of two densely sampled and six sparsely sampled mouse brains, registered to the Allen Mouse Brain Common Coordinate Framework (CCF), we seek to interpolate the measured hundreds of lipid profiles across the unobserved voxels of the reference brain. We introduce a Neural Latent-Space Gaussian Process (LGP) architecture for this task and critically evaluate its ability to reconstruct spatial lipid distributions, using held-out mouse brain sections to assess generalization. We propose a Gaussian Process
s69f5cc7df2.summary: Researchers introduce a Neural Latent Gaussian Process to reconstruct continuous 3D lipid profiles of the mouse brain from sparse 2D MALDI-MSI tissue sections.
s69f5cc7df2.why: Scientific application with limited direct relevance to most engineering teams beyond methods transfer.

s9db6786051.title: Frame First, Decode Once: Object-Centric Coordinates and Single-Pass Decoding for System-1 World Models
s9db6786051.description: arXiv:2611.18761v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Single-pass primitive decoders such as LocateAnything and VFlash predict all quantized coordinate tokens of a geometric primitive in one forward pass, enabling fast, System-1 visual planning. We study what matters when such a decoder serves as a System-1 world model: a fast action-conditioned predictor that ranks candidate pushes by their predicted outcome. On ManiSkill3 PushT-v1 (512 held-out test families, 8,192 rollouts) and on human demonstrations from lerobot/pusht (2,384 test windows), we compare decoders, training losses, rigid-body projections and coordinate frames, using matched checkpoints, hierarchical bootstrap confidence intervals and Holm correction. Two factors of similar size dominate. First, expressing inputs and outputs in
s9db6786051.summary: Researchers study single-pass coordinate decoders as fast System-1 world models for ranking candidate robot pushes on ManiSkill3 PushT and human demonstration data.
s9db6786051.why: Offers design findings for fast action-conditioned predictors used in robotic visual planning.

s38cb6cecc1.title: Gradient-Guided Hardware-Native MIXFP4
s38cb6cecc1.description: arXiv:2611.18769v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Blackwell tensor cores support native inference with 4-bit weights and activations (W4A4), but NVFP4 leaves a perplexity (PPL) gap to BF16. Choosing a format for each 16-element block can improve accuracy, but current matrix multiply instructions cannot execute choices this fine. Applying these rules at hardware-compatible tiles loses most of their benefit. We introduce FlipQuant, which selects E2M1 or E0M3 for each MMA weight tile. It keeps both quantized weight candidates fixed and learns a binary format map from end-to-end gradients of a bucketed KL loss to a BF16 teacher, re-evaluating them after each update. Native kernels execute 16 x 64 tiles on SM120 and 256 x 64 tiles on SM100 with median GEMM overheads of 1.9% and 1.7%, respective
s38cb6cecc1.summary: FlipQuant proposes selecting between E2M1 and E0M3 4-bit formats per MMA weight tile on Blackwell tensor cores, learning the format map from end-to-end gradients.
s38cb6cecc1.why: Targets the accuracy gap between NVFP4 and BF16 at hardware-compatible granularity, relevant to teams running low-precision inference.

s62b2151cfc.title: Vibe synthesis: hierarchical agentic decision-making for intent-driven multistep molecule synthesis
s62b2151cfc.description: arXiv:2611.18772v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The ability to construct complex molecules underpins advances in medicine and the molecular sciences. Yet long-horizon multistep synthesis requires decisions to be revised as evidence accumulates across chemically dependent operations, a capability not readily supported by artificial-intelligence tools and automated platforms organized around predefined tasks and hard-coded workflows. Here we propose and demonstrate a vibe synthesis system (VibeSyn), an intent-driven architecture in which hierarchical agents translate chemist-defined molecular objectives and accumulating evidence into adaptive decisions executed through computational tools and laboratory automation. We evaluate VibeSyn in three demonstrations of increasing scope and autonom
s62b2151cfc.summary: VibeSyn is an intent-driven system where hierarchical agents translate chemist-defined goals into multistep molecule synthesis plans that can be revised as evidence accumulates.
s62b2151cfc.why: Demonstrates hierarchical agent design for long-horizon scientific workflows that need revisable decisions rather than hard-coded pipelines.

sc552324e6d.title: An LLM-assisted theoretical model for aeroengine installation noise scattering
sc552324e6d.description: arXiv:2611.18796v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A theoretical model is developed for the canonical problem of aeroengine fan noise impinging on, and scattering from, a nearby semi-infinite rigid plate. The model chains two Wiener--Hopf problems in different coordinate systems. The first stage solves the duct-radiation problem analytically in axisymmetric cylindrical coordinates. The second stage expands the field incident on the plate into a double angular spectrum of plane waves: the axial spectrum is inherited from the first stage, while the spanwise spectrum is generated by a Weyl--Sommerfeld expansion of the cylindrical harmonics. Each spectral component is then scattered by the plate. The mathematical crux is the coordinate transformation between the axisymmetric duct frame and the
sc552324e6d.summary: Researchers present an analytical model chaining two Wiener–Hopf problems to study aeroengine fan noise scattering off a nearby semi-infinite rigid plate.
sc552324e6d.why: Offers a theoretical tool for predicting aircraft installation noise, relevant mainly to acoustics and aerospace engineers rather than AI practitioners.

s7520a0e0a8.title: Accelerating Variational Cone-Beam CT Reconstruction with Learned Warm Starts
s7520a0e0a8.description: arXiv:2611.18801v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Variational reconstruction provides a rigorous framework for cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) by combining an explicit acquisition model with image priors. However, iterative optimization remains computationally demanding, particularly under severe noise and sparse-view conditions. Although learning-based methods achieve high reconstruction quality, they often replace the original variational formulation with learned optimization schemes or nonlinear equilibrium models. We propose a neural network-guided warm-start framework that accelerates variational reconstruction while preserving its original formulation. Projection data are first reconstructed using the Feldkamp-Davis-Kress (FDK) algorithm, and the resulting image is refined by an
s7520a0e0a8.summary: Researchers propose a neural network-guided warm-start framework to speed up variational cone-beam CT reconstruction while keeping the explicit acquisition model and priors.
s7520a0e0a8.why: Shows learned initialization can cut iterative optimization cost without replacing the variational formulation, a useful pattern for imaging pipelines.

s69dee52519.title: LEAP-LLM: Preserving lead-time structure for question-conditioned ECG interpretation
s69dee52519.description: arXiv:2611.18809v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The electrocardiogram (ECG) records cardiac electrical activity across multiple leads and is used for detecting cardiac abnormalities. Recent ECG-language models enable large language models (LLMs) to interpret cardiac signals and answer clinically relevant questions. However, existing ECG-language models typically encode the ECG independently of the clinical question, forcing the ECG representation to retain broad and potentially irrelevant signal information. Moreover, these models often aggregate information across leads which can obscure lead-specific details needed for a particular question. To tackle these limitations, we introduce LEAP-LLM, an ECG-LLM architecture for Lead-aware ECG Alignment with Prompt conditioning. LEAP-LLM uses t
s69dee52519.summary: LEAP-LLM is proposed to make ECG interpretation by LLMs question-conditioned and preserve lead-time structure instead of encoding the ECG independently of the clinical question.
s69dee52519.why: Suggests query-aware encoding and per-lead structure can improve medical signal-language models, relevant to teams building clinical LLM systems.

sc27873e888.title: CARET: Clinical Assertion-Aware Residual Calibration for Medical Image-Text Alignment
sc27873e888.description: arXiv:2611.18811v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Medical vision--language models align radiographs with free-text reports, but radiology language distinguishes explicit findings, negation, uncertainty, and omission. Treating these report states as interchangeable during feature adaptation can change image predictions without supporting visual evidence. We introduce CARET, a parameter-efficient image-side adaptation method that retains pretrained image and text encoders and uses paired positive and negative clinical statements to define a low-dimensional semantic correction space. A bounded residual adjusts image features along these directions, while assertion-aware supervision distinguishes explicitly present and absent findings from uncertain or unmentioned ones. At inference, the adapt
sc27873e888.summary: CARET is introduced as a parameter-efficient image-side adaptation method that uses paired positive and negative clinical statements to calibrate medical image-text alignment.
sc27873e888.why: Addresses how negation and uncertainty in radiology reports can distort vision-language predictions, a practical risk for medical AI deployments.

sfd576bf19b.title: RescueVLM: Model-Agnostic Vision-Language Framework for Rescue Drone Imagery
sfd576bf19b.description: arXiv:2611.18813v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A single unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) mission over an incident site produces hundreds of images, far more than a rescue commander can review under time pressure, and human screening of destruction imagery carries a documented psychological cost. The two obvious remedies both fail in search and rescue (SAR) practice: cloud vision-language model (VLM) services are excluded because the imagery must not leave the incident network under GDPR and German civil-protection (BOS) rules, and fine-tuned specialist detectors age quickly while retraining and re-certifying them exceeds most SAR organizations resources. We present RescueVLM, an open-source, training-free and model-agnostic triage tool built on SketchVLM: a general-purpose open-weight VLM
sfd576bf19b.summary: RescueVLM is a model-agnostic vision-language framework for triaging rescue drone imagery on-premises, avoiding cloud services due to GDPR and civil-protection rules.
sfd576bf19b.why: Illustrates how data-residency constraints push vision-language systems toward local, model-swappable architectures in regulated public-safety settings.

s922a9418d5.title: Foundation Model Fine-Tuning with Attention-based Multi-View Fusion for Multi-Task Cardiac Function Assessment
s922a9418d5.description: arXiv:2611.18816v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In cardio-oncology, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is the standard biomarker for monitoring cardiac function during cancer therapy. However, its estimation from echocardiography is highly operator dependent, and clinically meaningful declines are often detected only after myocardial injury has progressed, motivating automated methods for standardized assessment and earlier detection of LV dysfunction. To address this need, we propose a multi-task framework integrating cardiac cycle-based temporal standardization, multi-view spatiotemporal feature extraction, and joint optimization for LVEF estimation and LV dysfunction classification. Apical four- and two-chamber echocardiographic sequences are temporally standardized by sampling
s922a9418d5.summary: Researchers propose a multi-task framework using foundation model fine-tuning and attention-based multi-view fusion to assess cardiac function from echocardiography.
s922a9418d5.why: Shows multi-view fusion on foundation models for standardizing a clinically operator-dependent measurement, relevant to medical imaging ML teams.

s2a2c82d2e2.title: What to Practice Next? Latent Profile-Guided Task Selection for Skill-Evolving LLM Agents
s2a2c82d2e2.description: arXiv:2611.18818v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Task selection shapes the experiences available for skill evolution in LLM agents, yet fixed practice schedules overlook differences in skill requirements and evolving task value. Most existing methods, however, rely on fixed schedules or scalar measures of progress, leaving nonstationary skill demands unaddressed. We propose SPG-Select, a framework for allocating limited practice budget using a multidimensional profile inferred from binary outcomes via MIRT. The framework predicts surrogate progress, defined as the difference between consecutive profile estimates, and prioritizes progress in dimensions with larger estimated proficiency gaps. Our SPG-Select-R policy combines these predictions with uncertainty-based exploration and periodic
s2a2c82d2e2.summary: SPG-Select is a framework that chooses LLM agent practice tasks using a multidimensional skill profile inferred via MIRT and predicted surrogate progress.
s2a2c82d2e2.why: Offers a method for adaptive task scheduling in agent training, though its practical impact depends on results not given in the summary.

s3425fd1554.title: KUDEX: A Zero-Shot Decompositional Framework for Logical Analysis in Natural Language
s3425fd1554.description: arXiv:2611.18851v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: While Large Language Models (LLMs) excel at generating fluent text, they often struggle with multi-step logical reasoning with inferential connections among statements. We introduce KUDEX (Knowledge-Upward-Downward Reasoning Extension), a novel zero-shot, decompositional framework for analyzing and verifying logical relationships in natural language. Unlike traditional approaches that rely on surface-level entailment checks, KUDEX leverages LLMs to decompose reasoning into atomic primitives and constructs transparent reasoning graphs that serve both as execution traces and audit logs. Our framework includes a general prompt adaptation pipeline that adapts to diverse reasoning tasks without additional fine-tuning or domain-specific pipelines
s3425fd1554.summary: KUDEX is a zero-shot framework that decomposes natural-language reasoning into atomic primitives and builds reasoning graphs to verify logical relationships.
s3425fd1554.why: Provides a transparent, zero-shot way to check multi-step LLM reasoning, which may help teams audit model logic.

s4eef47de4c.title: Self-Improvement Memory Enables Continual Recursive Self-Improvement
s4eef47de4c.description: arXiv:2611.18856v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Harness optimization is often studied with a fixed policy model and benchmark. When either changes, the optimizer must decide which parts of an evolved harness to reuse or revise, but the harness alone may not explain why earlier edits were made or how they performed. In this work, we study Continual Recursive Self-Improvement (CRSI), a setting for continuing existing harness-optimization methods across compatible benchmarks or policy models. We propose Self-Improvement Memory (SIM) for the harness optimizer, rather than the task-solving policy. SIM groups edits by recurring harness problem and records their rationale, predicted and observed outcomes, and evaluation context. New attempts extend this history as optimization continues. In our
s4eef47de4c.summary: Researchers study Continual Recursive Self-Improvement and propose Self-Improvement Memory, which stores harness-optimizer history to reuse edits across benchmarks or policy models.
s4eef47de4c.why: Suggests optimizers that remember why past edits were made can transfer harness improvements when benchmarks or models change.

sa85200150f.title: The opposing informational effects of AI trading
sa85200150f.description: arXiv:2611.18872v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Better artificial intelligence (AI) can improve individual forecasts without making prices better at revealing new information. In a competitive market with resource-constrained forecasting, more capable algorithms can substitute analysis of public records for private observations, reducing the private information aggregated into prices. The same trades can convey sophisticated public-data analysis to investors unable to perform it themselves. We establish conditions under which these effects coexist and the private benefit of further computation falls. Numerical equilibrium calculations and finite-data neural-market experiments exhibit corresponding patterns. Out-of-sample earnings forecasts and controlled language-model tasks show related
sa85200150f.summary: A paper argues that better AI forecasting can reduce the private information aggregated into prices, while trades can also convey public-data analysis to others.
sa85200150f.why: Highlights that improved AI in markets can have opposing effects on price informativeness, relevant to quantitative finance and market design.

sf61ab42dd9.title: Label-Free Detection of Structural Bias in LLM-Based Recommender Systems via Randomized Paraphrasing: The Case of Verbosity
sf61ab42dd9.description: arXiv:2611.18878v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as recommenders in e-commerce and conversational shopping systems, where they select a product from a set of retrieved candidates described in natural language. Their decisions should depend on relevance to the user query, but may also be influenced by surface-level properties of the descriptions, such as their length. Detecting such structural biases is difficult because relevance labels are rarely available. We propose a label-free framework to audit LLM-based recommender systems for structural bias. Candidate descriptions are rewritten by randomly assigned paraphrasing models and presented in random order. We prove that, if the recommender's choice is invariant to these rewritings, e
sf61ab42dd9.summary: A label-free framework is proposed to audit LLM-based recommenders for structural biases such as preference for longer product descriptions, using randomized paraphrasing.
sf61ab42dd9.why: Offers a way to detect verbosity bias in LLM recommenders without relevance labels, useful for teams running e-commerce ranking with LLMs.

s176779d65d.title: We Have All the Cards: Securing Agent Cards at the Operational Trust Boundary of the Agent2Agent Protocol
s176779d65d.description: arXiv:2611.18887v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI agent interoperability protocols enable orchestrators to discover and invoke external agents using machine-readable metadata. In the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol, Agent Cards contain attacker-controllable natural-language fields that may influence agent selection before a provider is invoked, creating a pre-invocation trust problem. We characterize this discovery-time attack surface through a taxonomy of ten Agent Card manipulation attacks and present SECCARD, a layered validation framework combining protocol checks, deterministic analysis, and LLM-based semantic reasoning. We measure the emerging public A2A ecosystem by probing 36.1 million Internet domains and collecting 310 deployed Agent Cards. Two annotators independently label the co
s176779d65d.summary: The paper characterizes ten Agent Card manipulation attacks in the Agent2Agent protocol and presents SECCARD, a layered validation framework for securing agent metadata.
s176779d65d.why: Agent discovery metadata can be attacker-controlled and influence selection before invocation, so teams adopting A2A need validation layers.

s1d4502cf12.title: Benchmark Factory: Agentic Benchmark Creation via Dataset Curation and Label-Free Quality Anchors
s1d4502cf12.description: arXiv:2611.18890v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Teams deploying coding agents need benchmarks built from their own code, but curating and validating them by hand is resource intensive, and an unvalidated benchmark can mislead silently. We present Benchmark Factory, an autonomous meta-agent loop with human checkpoints: an LLM agent writes sourcing queries over landed production code changes, runs models of known relative strength on each candidate, diagnoses why a candidate fails, and repairs it by editing its queries, prompts, and configuration until it clears quality anchors that need no per-task human labels. We used Benchmark Factory to build benchmarks for five developer cohorts at our organization. Engineering raters scored a 5% sample 2.3 for task quality and 2.6 for grader verdict
s1d4502cf12.summary: Benchmark Factory is an autonomous meta-agent loop that builds coding-agent benchmarks from a team's production code changes, using label-free quality anchors and human checkpoints.
s1d4502cf12.why: Lets teams create validated evaluation sets from their own codebase, reducing the risk of misleading benchmarks for coding agents.

sf638eac08a.title: Lasso: Towards Sustainable AI-Generated Media Detection with Intel QAT On-Chip Compression
sf638eac08a.description: arXiv:2611.18895v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Synthetic text, images, and video are rising. Software-only detectors are power-hungry, too slow, and costly, and do not scale with demand. When software cannot scale, historically hardware often comes to the rescue. We perform the first reverse engineering of a compression accelerator--Intel QuickAssist Technology (QAT) microarchitecture and--find different amount of time on each, a novel data structure-dependent property. Using this information, we then build Lasso, a low-cost, high-performance detector for AI-generated content that turns the accelerator into a measuring instrument. For text detection, Lasso achieves 100% accuracy on original DetectRL text and retains 92% average accuracy after paraphrasing, compared with 78% for Binocula
sf638eac08a.summary: Researchers reverse engineer Intel QuickAssist compression accelerator microarchitecture and build Lasso, a hardware-assisted detector for AI-generated media.
sf638eac08a.why: Shows hardware compression accelerators can be repurposed to make AI-generated content detection cheaper and more power-efficient at scale.

s5ca52858bf.title: The Human Side of ML Engineering: Analyzing the Collaboration and Communication Skills in ML Job Postings
s5ca52858bf.description: arXiv:2611.18915v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Studies of Machine Learning (ML) practice highlight the importance of combining technical expertise with interpersonal capabilities, particularly collaboration and communication. However, evidence on how ML job postings express these skills is scarce, and prior work largely relies on keyword-based analyses that overlook implicit expression. We analyze demand for these skills in ML job postings across regions, industries, and seniority levels, and compare it with software engineering (SE) roles. We collected 1,000 postings (500 ML, 500 SE) from five continents via a semi-automated pipeline. For annotation, we synthesized a taxonomy of collaboration and communication sub-categories from prior work and used an LLM as a third annotator alongsid
s5ca52858bf.summary: An analysis of 1,000 job postings (500 ML, 500 SE) examines demand for collaboration and communication skills across regions, industries, and seniority levels.
s5ca52858bf.why: Indicates how employers express soft-skill demand for ML roles versus software engineering, useful for hiring and career planning.

sf735656310.title: Effects of Conventional, Adaptive, and AI-Powered Upscaling on the Legibility of License Plates
sf735656310.description: arXiv:2611.18949v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Small details in digital images -- a face, a street sign, a license plate -- are routinely upscaled in hopes of making them interpretable. Upscaling options now range from conventional interpolation, whose operations are spatially invariant and fully explainable, to AI-powered methods that synthesize detail potentially absent from the source. Here, we ask which of these techniques most reliably helps human readers. In two online experiments, we measured legibility of 255 US license plates ranging in resolution from 128 to 8 pixels tall, as well as their legibility after upscaling by eight different methods. Legibility of the un-upscaled plates collapsed from ceiling to floor across a narrow band of plate heights (32 to 10 pixels). Conventio
sf735656310.summary: Researchers ran two online experiments measuring how well humans can read license plates of 8 to 128 pixels tall under conventional, adaptive, and AI-powered upscaling.
sf735656310.why: It tests whether AI upscaling that synthesizes detail actually helps human readers versus explainable interpolation, relevant to trust in enhancement tools.

sb119246622.title: From Language-Specific to Cross-DSL: Semantic-Role-Guided Model Completion with LLMs
sb119246622.description: arXiv:2611.18952v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The rapid emergence of large language models (LLMs), trained on vast and diverse corpora, has positioned them as a promising source of domain knowledge to assist modelers. However, leveraging LLMs for model completion remains challenging: suggestions must respect both the syntax of a domain-specific language (DSL) and the intended domain semantics, while remaining consistent with an evolving model. This paper presents RAFiC, an LLM-based approach for iterative domain model completion that generalizes across DSLs. It drives completion using metamodel information to ensure syntactic validity and enriches prompts with semantic-role annotations to better capture the intended modeling role of DSL elements. The approach provides context-aware, in
sb119246622.summary: Researchers introduce RAFiC, an LLM-based approach for iterative domain model completion that generalizes across domain-specific languages using semantic roles.

s9ac09f4968.title: Context Matters: Improving LLM-Based Code Summarization with Hierarchical Information
s9ac09f4968.description: arXiv:2611.18964v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Source code documentation plays an important role in software quality activities, such as code review, program comprehension, maintenance, and bug fixing. However, it is often fragmented across individual code elements and focuses on local implementation details, providing little information about their surrounding context. This limits both developers' understanding of software systems and the effectiveness of Large Language Models (LLMs), whose reasoning is constrained by finite context windows. Enriching documentation with hierarchical context has the potential to improve software comprehension and support downstream, quality-related tasks for both developers and LLM-based tools. In this paper, we present an in silico study that showcases
s9ac09f4968.summary: Researchers propose enriching source code documentation with hierarchical context so LLMs can summarize code better despite limited context windows.
s9ac09f4968.why: Hierarchical context may improve LLM code summaries and documentation quality for developers working on large codebases.

se685656474.title: Probing Where Surprise Happens: Localized Violation-of-Expectation Evaluation of Video World Models
se685656474.description: arXiv:2611.18979v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Violation-of-expectation (VOE) benchmarks evaluate intuitive physics in video world models by testing whether physically impossible events produce greater prediction errors than matched possible events. However, conventional VOE evaluations aggregate prediction errors across space and time, making it unclear whether successful discrimination reflects model's understanding of physical violations at the locations and time where they occur. To address this limitation, we introduce localized VOE evaluation, a framework that measures prediction error differences between possible and impossible events within spatial regions and temporal intervals associated with physical violations. We compare global, temporally localized, and spatiotemporally lo
se685656474.summary: Researchers introduce localized violation-of-expectation evaluation to test whether video world models detect physically impossible events at the specific locations and times they occur.
se685656474.why: Aggregate benchmarks can mask where video models fail physically, so localized evaluation gives teams a finer-grained way to assess world models.

s81037a0ca3.title: Model Maps: A Documentation Framework for Tracing Foundation Model Ancestry and Understanding AI Entanglement
s81037a0ca3.description: arXiv:2611.18998v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The development of foundation models incorporates pre-existing AI artifacts like models, datasets, and benchmarks. These relationships, as part of the broader AI supply chain, produce "entangled" webs in which properties of artifacts upstream can influence the outputs of a foundation model downstream - a phenomenon known as AI entanglement. Without visibility into these connections, a black-box model can inherit upstream properties that result in security vulnerabilities, hallucinations, or biased predictions, yet developers are left with no recourse to identify or mitigate the root issue. To address these concerns, we introduce model maps as a conceptual documentation framework for tracing model ancestry that builds on previous documentati
s81037a0ca3.summary: Researchers propose Model Maps, a documentation framework for tracing foundation model ancestry and the upstream artifacts that shape downstream model behavior.
s81037a0ca3.why: Tracing upstream models, datasets, and benchmarks can expose inherited security, hallucination, and bias risks in AI supply chains.

s728d442c7c.title: Agent-ZTA: A chain-Aware Zero Trust Model for Bidirectional Security-State Propagation and Runtime Containment in Multi-Agent Delegation
s728d442c7c.description: arXiv:2611.18999v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multi-agent systems increasingly delegate tasks and permissions across chains of autonomous agents that invoke protected tools. Although agent identities and delegated credentials may remain valid throughout a workflow, the security condition of any agent along the chain can deteriorate during runtime execution-either through upstream compromise or downstream ingestion of untrusted inputs. Authorization models based solely on the immediate caller and its static delegated scope fail to account for these mid-execution state changes. This paper develops Agent-ZTA, a chain-aware Zero Trust authorization and containment model that links runtime security-state changes across multi-agent delegation graphs. The model distinguishes an agent's path-s
s728d442c7c.summary: Researchers present Agent-ZTA, a zero trust authorization model that tracks security-state changes during runtime across chains of delegating multi-agent systems.
s728d442c7c.why: Static caller-based authorization misses mid-execution compromise in agent delegation chains, so runtime containment matters for securing multi-agent deployments.

s4caf607d1c.title: Role-Separated Diffusion Transformers: Global Rule Isolation and Deterministic Sampling Manifold Compression
s4caf607d1c.description: arXiv:2611.19009v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present Role-Separated Diffusion Transformers (RoSeDiT), a new diffusion transformer architecture that isolates the global rule from the image tokens. RoSeViT showed in visual reasoning that a vanilla ViT spreads a shared rule over all $L$ tokens at an entropy of order $Ld$, whereas an enforced controller route reduces it to order $d$. In class-conditional DiT and SiT, the class and the noise level are explicitly conditioned by adaLN, so a RoSeViT-style controller channel on the ViT side is insufficient to establish the full role separation. By introducing the adaLN listening mechanism, which makes adaLN compute under the controller's command, RoSeDiT brings the entropy theorem and role separation into the latent diffusion domain. Under
s4caf607d1c.summary: Researchers present Role-Separated Diffusion Transformers, an architecture that isolates a global rule from image tokens to improve class-conditional diffusion models.

sd4c7994781.title: MemoryLane: Supporting Reminiscence Conversations Between Older Adults with Mild Dementia and Lay Caregivers Using a Simulated AI Agent
sd4c7994781.description: arXiv:2611.19013v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reminiscence Therapy (RT) is a non-pharmacological intervention that invites patients to discuss and review past life experiences and memories to improve their emotional and mental well-being. In practice, many reminiscence conversations are led by lay caregivers, such as spouses and adult children. While traditional RT often relies on personal photographs, curating them can be tedious and difficult. In addition, caregivers who lack shared life experiences with the patient may struggle to facilitate engaging reminiscence conversations. This paper presents MemoryLane, an AI-integrated tool that helps lay caregivers facilitate reminiscence conversations without curated photographs. MemoryLane supports a triadic conversation among the patient,
sd4c7994781.summary: Researchers present MemoryLane, a system using a simulated AI agent to support reminiscence conversations between older adults with mild dementia and lay caregivers.

s5b78bb983a.title: HeteroWear: Sensor-Aware Self-Supervised Learning for Heterogeneous Wearable Activity Recognition
s5b78bb983a.description: arXiv:2611.19027v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Self-supervised learning for wearable sensing is usually confined to a single dataset or device family, leaving open whether representations transfer across heterogeneous sensor configurations and whether gains come from pretraining rather than architecture or richer sensor input. We present HeteroWear, a sensor-aware self-supervised framework pretrained on an eight-dataset wearable corpus (173 subjects, 358,261 windows) spanning inertial and physiological signals across body locations, devices, and sampling rates. HeteroWear separates within-sensor temporal modeling from cross-sensor relational modeling using sensor-context embeddings, temporal and cross-sensor Transformers, and latent cross-attention fusion. Training combines structured s
s5b78bb983a.summary: Researchers present HeteroWear, a sensor-aware self-supervised framework pretrained on eight wearable datasets to recognize activity across heterogeneous devices and sensors.
s5b78bb983a.why: Testing whether representations transfer across heterogeneous sensor setups helps teams judge whether pretraining, not just architecture, drives wearable model gains.

sa3c769a46f.title: SurveyWeave: An Agentic Framework for Automated Survey Generation
sa3c769a46f.description: arXiv:2611.19029v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Surveys help researchers keep up with fast-moving fields, but they take weeks to months to write. Automated survey generation (AutoSurvey) can alleviate this situation, but it is challenging to draw on hundreds to thousands of precisely scoped papers, choose among many valid structures, and stay faithful to its sources while offering insights. We present SurveyWeave, an agentic architecture that decomposes the problem into four tasks coordinated by three agents, each reviewing others' work and conducting revisions based on feedback. We also introduce WeaveEval, a five-dimension evaluation grounded in prior surveys. A comprehensive comparison shows that SurveyWeave outperforms Codex by 8 points and the strongest AutoSurvey baseline by 6 poin
sa3c769a46f.summary: Researchers present SurveyWeave, an agentic framework that uses three coordinating agents to automatically generate research surveys from large sets of papers.
sa3c769a46f.why: Multi-agent review and revision loops for source-faithful long-form generation offer a design pattern for document-heavy agent workflows.

s5991a18a81.title: Refinement vs. Replanning: Inference Compute Allocation in Robot Policies
s5991a18a81.description: arXiv:2611.19034v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A frozen chunked robot policy can spend deployment-time inference compute in two coupled ways: more work within each policy call to refine a predicted action chunk, or more frequent policy calls to replan from fresh observations. We study this allocation without updating model weights. Our evaluation procedure reports success with both nominal compute rate and complete attempt cost, selects comparisons on discovery tasks, and tests prespecified comparisons on held-out tasks. Comparisons added after inspecting the held-out results only summarize observed patterns. We demonstrate the procedure with one frozen SmolVLA checkpoint in synchronous LIBERO simulation, using denoising count as the refinement control and fixing chunk length at K=50. A
s5991a18a81.summary: Researchers study how to allocate fixed inference compute in a frozen chunked robot policy between refining action chunks and replanning more frequently.
s5991a18a81.why: Deployment-time compute trade-offs in robot policies affect latency and cost decisions without any retraining of model weights.

s3dd7638f15.title: The Critic Can Hurt: On the Safety of Critics in LLM-Guided AutoML Search
s3dd7638f15.description: arXiv:2611.19037v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM critics increasingly steer iterative search in agentic AutoML, prompt optimization, and self-refinement--evaluated for whether they help, but rarely for whether they can hurt. We isolate the critic's marginal effect through a four-arm audit and characterize the loop's tolerance through controlled fault injection. We show a naive 8B critic drives search below the no-critic random-search floor on 7 of 8 tabular datasets, losing up to 0.245 AUC in the worst case; the magnitude varies strongly with dataset, frontier, and budget. When: stronger critics attenuate the loss on the evaluated suite, without establishing a universal capability threshold. Why: controlled fault injection shows that non-directional errors are nearly costless under be
s3dd7638f15.summary: Researchers audit LLM critics in AutoML search and find a naive 8B critic often drives search below a no-critic random-search baseline on tabular datasets.
s3dd7638f15.why: LLM critics in agentic optimization loops can degrade results, so teams should audit whether feedback components help rather than assume they do.

se327813447.title: Understanding the Role of Reasoning Data in Pretraining
se327813447.description: arXiv:2611.19042v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reasoning data expose models to multi-step reasoning, but reasoning traces may cover only a subset of the available facts. How should pretraining balance atomic facts with reasoning traces? We study this question by constructing a setting in which every fact provides an atomic training signal, while only a subset appears in reasoning supervision, enabling us to measure generalization to transitions observed atomically but never used in training traces. For a linear transformer, we derive the weight assigned to atomic training signals that minimizes held-transition squared error and show that its leading-order optimum increases with reasoning-chain length and decreases with the fraction of facts held out from reasoning traces. These trends p
se327813447.summary: Researchers study how to balance atomic facts and reasoning traces in pretraining data, using a linear transformer to analyze generalization to unseen transitions.

sf2f3ba2da4.title: More Context, Mixed Results: Evaluating LLMs for Identifier Recovery and Code Deobfuscation
sf2f3ba2da4.description: arXiv:2611.19043v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Source code is often obfuscated through identifier renaming, incentivizing reverse engineers to develop techniques for recovering meaningful names. To assess how LLMs compare with these techniques, we evaluate 4 traditional baselines and 3 LLMs (Qwen, OLMo and DeepSeek) on identifier detection and semantic recovery across 51 recent Java projects, 3 obfuscators, and 6 context/retrieval settings. LLMs generally outperform traditional techniques on both tasks, but benefit from different forms of context and settings: agentic retrieval yields the strongest detection results, reaching 91.56% $F_1$, while enclosing-class context generally improves semantic recovery at a higher token cost. Despite these gains, exact recovery peaks at 16.42% overal
sf2f3ba2da4.summary: Researchers evaluate three LLMs against four traditional baselines on recovering obfuscated Java identifiers across 51 projects, finding mixed results depending on context.
sf2f3ba2da4.why: LLMs generally beat traditional deobfuscation methods, but the benefit depends on context type, informing reverse engineering tool choices.

s754c5783b8.title: Hard or Mislabeled? Failure Screens Enrich Vision Benchmarks for Label Errors
s754c5783b8.description: arXiv:2611.19044v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hard vision benchmarks often keep images that strong classifiers get wrong. Since a classifier is also marked wrong when the label is wrong, such failure screens may collect label errors. We measure this on ImageNet's twice-relabeled validation set with 103 classifiers. Among the 1,892 images that all 66 supervised classifiers get wrong, 61% have a wrong label, versus 11.1% overall. The fewer images a screen lets through, the more of them are mislabeled, along approximately one curve. Fit on one model family, this curve predicts the screens of two held-out model families with a mean error of 2.4 percentage points, and replays of ImageNet-D's and ImageNet-Hard's screens within 0.1 and 6.3 points. On new pools, ImageNet-V2 and CIFAR-10, enric
s754c5783b8.summary: Researchers find that images misclassified by all 66 supervised classifiers on ImageNet's validation set are 61% mislabeled, versus 11.1% overall.
s754c5783b8.why: Failure-based benchmark filtering can concentrate label errors, so teams building evaluation sets should verify labels before treating failures as model weaknesses.

s016cb08ecb.title: SPARC: Evidence-guided adaptive model composition for materials discovery
s016cb08ecb.description: arXiv:2611.19050v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Closed-loop experimentation requires more than selecting the next experiment. It must also determine which existing measurements and model-derived relationships are sufficiently supported to influence that decision. Here we introduce SPARC (Sparse Predictive Aggregation of Regression Components), a framework that continually revises this support as experimental evidence accumulates. Competing model families are evaluated through out-of-fold predictions, so that each model is tested on observations not used in its corresponding fit. Sparse posterior composition assigns model influence according to predictive contributions supported by the out-of-fold evidence, retaining complementary contributions from several model families. Candidate-depen
s016cb08ecb.summary: Researchers introduce SPARC, a framework that continually revises which measurements and model relationships are trusted during closed-loop materials experimentation.
s016cb08ecb.why: It offers a method for combining competing models via out-of-fold evaluation, which could inform adaptive experiment design in R&D pipelines.

s0b7399da77.title: Nahual: A Sequence Model for Language and Atoms
s0b7399da77.description: arXiv:2611.19072v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative models play a rapidly growing role in the design and simulation of molecules. The most widely used applications of generative models are in large language models (LLMs), owing to the natural flexibility of language for specifying and answering queries. However, generalist LLMs do not effectively handle large sets of 3D coordinates, whereas specialist generative models of 3D molecules cannot reach the controllability afforded by language. To bridge these capabilities, we propose Nahual, a decoder-only autoregressive diffusion model for any sequence of text and 3D molecules. To enable expressive autoregression on continuous coordinates, we propose next-token diffusion, whereby a causal transformer denoises each token while attendin
s0b7399da77.summary: Researchers propose Nahual, a decoder-only autoregressive diffusion model that aims to combine language control with generation of 3D atomic coordinates.
s0b7399da77.why: It targets controllable molecular generation, a gap where general LLMs handle 3D coordinates poorly and specialist models lack language control.

sd14d8e9585.title: Can Agentic LLMs Write Task-Based Parallel Code? A Study of OpenMP Tasking, HPX, StarPU and TTG
sd14d8e9585.description: arXiv:2611.19105v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Task-based programming offers more expressive power than loop-level parallelism, but the runtimes providing it differ widely in API style, maturity, and the amount of public code to learn from. This paper asks how well LLM agents write C++ for four of them: OpenMP Tasking, HPX, StarPU, and TTG. Instead of single one-shot prompts, we use an agentic workflow in which the model edits files, compiles, and runs its kernels until it reproduces a reference output. Five locally hosted open-weight LLM implement seven HPC kernels, including matrix multiplication, Cholesky and LU factorization, in all four frameworks and a serial baseline to verify their understanding of the problem in general. Every kernel is evaluated independently for correctness a
sd14d8e9585.summary: A study tests how well open-weight LLM agents write C++ task-based parallel code for OpenMP Tasking, HPX, StarPU and TTG using an iterative compile-and-run workflow.
sd14d8e9585.why: It shows how agentic coding workflows perform on less common HPC runtimes, relevant to teams using LLM agents for parallel software development.

sfda8101c47.title: ST-GAT: A Leakage-Free Spatio-Temporal Graph Attention Framework for Robust Network Intrusion Detection
sfda8101c47.description: arXiv:2611.19109v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Intrusion detection systems are a central defence in modern networks. Deep learning models report strong anomaly-detection results, but evaluations on standard benchmarks such as CSE-CIC-IDS-2018 are often inflated by two methodological problems: temporal leakage from overlapping sliding windows, and contamination from preprocessing fitted before the train/test split. Per-flow classifiers also ignore the spatio-temporal dependencies across sequences of network flows. We propose a Spatio-Temporal Graph Attention Network (ST-GAT) that represents traffic as a sequence of graph snapshots. It builds k-Nearest Neighbour (k-NN) edges within each window, applies multi-head Graph Attention Network (GAT) layers for spatial aggregation, and uses a Bid
sfda8101c47.summary: Researchers propose ST-GAT, a spatio-temporal graph attention network for intrusion detection, and argue that common benchmark evaluations suffer from temporal leakage and preprocessing contamination.
sfda8101c47.why: It highlights evaluation pitfalls that can inflate intrusion detection results, a concern for teams validating security ML models.

sd283699227.title: Latency, Speech Recognition and Turn-Taking in Voice Agents for Spanish Phone Negotiation: An Externally Measured Comparison of Pipecat, LiveKit and GPT-Live
sd283699227.description: arXiv:2611.19118v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A voice agent that negotiates by phone must answer quickly, understand spoken amounts and cope with a caller who talks over it. We compared three architectures for such an agent, negotiating freight rates in Spanish: two cascades (speech recognition, language model and speech synthesis) orchestrated by Pipecat and by LiveKit Agents, and GPT-Live, an OpenAI speech model that listens and speaks without separate stages. A program played the carrier with the same 47 recordings of one speaker for all agents, without the telephone network, in 77 calls per architecture over five negotiation scenarios, and measured latency on the listener's side with a validated instrument. Median latency to the content response was 2,616.0 ms (Pipecat), 3,090.0 ms
sd283699227.summary: An externally measured comparison of Pipecat, LiveKit Agents and OpenAI's GPT-Live finds differences in latency, speech recognition and turn-taking for a Spanish phone negotiation voice agent.
sd283699227.why: It gives comparative latency and turn-taking data for voice agent architectures, useful when choosing a stack for real-time phone agents.

s6d88953276.title: DecoEdit: Beyond Flat Control for 3D-Aware Unified Image Editing
s6d88953276.description: arXiv:2611.19121v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: While recent advances in multimodal image editing have achieved impressive results, current frameworks remain largely confined to ``flat" 2D controls (e.g., text prompts, bounding boxes, or masks). Precise 3D-aware geometric manipulation -- such as coordinating an object's location, physical scale, and 3D orientation while strictly preserving its fine-grained identity -- remains an elusive challenge, typically suffering from severe detail degradation or requiring expensive per-instance fine-tuning. In this paper, we present DecoEdit, an all-in-one image editing framework that goes beyond flat control by seamlessly integrating 1D textual, 2D spatial, and 3D volumetric inputs under a unified architecture. First, to power this unified model, w
s6d88953276.summary: Researchers present DecoEdit, a unified image editing framework that adds 3D-aware control over object location, scale and orientation while preserving identity.
s6d88953276.why: It extends image editing beyond flat 2D controls, though the summary gives limited detail on deployment implications.

sbfc7ad676d.title: Beyond Plain MCP: Do Decision Models and Code Mode Make Tool Use Cheaper and Faster?
sbfc7ad676d.description: arXiv:2611.19123v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Model Context Protocol (MCP) gateways manage tool catalogs for language model agents using two primary paradigms: code mode where agents write scripts against tool stubs and decision layers which are cheap routers that preselect tool subsets. Using a controlled harness across 12 servers, up to 1,958 distractor tools, and three open-weight agents including Qwen, Gemma, and Nemotron, we present a preregistered evaluation on a sealed test split to determine when each approach succeeds. Code mode substantially outperforms plain MCP, cutting token usage by 70 to 90 percent while significantly boosting utility. Declaring return-shape hints in code mode stubs is a first-order variable, swinging success by up to 39.5 points for lower-performing age
sbfc7ad676d.summary: A preregistered study compares MCP code mode and decision-layer routers against plain MCP for tool use by open-weight agents across up to 1,958 distractor tools.
sbfc7ad676d.why: It provides evidence on when tool-routing strategies reduce tokens and latency for agents that manage large tool catalogs.

scc6080150d.title: How Much Determinism Can Fine-Tuning Buy? Margin Regularisation Against Batch-Induced Token Flips
scc6080150d.description: arXiv:2611.19135v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Greedy decoding at zero temperature is widely assumed to be deterministic, although the exact same prompt may yield different tokens depending on the number of other prompts sharing the batch for inference. The currently available solutions operate during inference, trading determinism for throughput. Can we train a model in such a way that fewer decoding steps would be susceptible? We characterize the perturbation empirically across six model families and three numerical precisions and observe two empirical facts about the measurement: the perturbation depends exactly on the representable precision (8.00x for bfloat16 vs float16, 8192.0x for float16 vs float32, in line with predictions based on mantissa bits) and the batch invariance happe
scc6080150d.summary: Researchers propose margin regularisation during fine-tuning to reduce greedy-decoding token flips caused by batch composition, rather than relying on inference-time fixes.
scc6080150d.why: Batch-dependent nondeterminism affects reproducibility in production LLM serving, and training-time mitigation could be an alternative to throughput-costly fixes.

sb195ba6743.title: When the Mythical Man-Month Meets Agentic Web Systems: Structured Coordination for Scalable Development
sb195ba6743.description: arXiv:2611.19140v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As agentic systems are increasingly deployed to support complex Web tasks, multi-agent architectures offer greater parallelism, specialization, and task coverage. However, increasing the number of agents does not necessarily improve system performance, as communication, synchronization, redundant work, and coordination overhead may offset the benefits of additional agents. This presents a fundamental scaling challenge for agentic Web systems: how can agent populations be organized to balance task performance and coordination costs? To address this challenge, we systematically investigate the relationship between agent population size, per-agent token consumption, and coordination overhead in collaborative agentic systems. Experiments on com
sb195ba6743.summary: The paper examines how adding agents to multi-agent web systems can fail to improve performance due to coordination overhead, and proposes structured coordination to scale them.
sb195ba6743.why: It addresses when adding more agents hurts rather than helps, a practical design concern for teams building multi-agent systems.

s38f7c848ce.title: MarineSparkLM-4B: A Lightweight Language Model for Marine and Offshore Engineering Built by Parameter-Efficient Adaptation
s38f7c848ce.description: arXiv:2611.19151v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Marine and offshore engineering text is spread across preprints, open-access journals, encyclopedias and institutional documents, and the amount of it is small by pretraining standards. We ask how far a lightweight language model for marine and offshore engineering can be taken with parameter-efficient adaptation on a single workstation-class device. Starting from the 4-billion-parameter OceanGPT-basic-4B-Instruct, we train two independent LoRA adapters, each updating 33.0 million of 4.06 billion parameters (0.81%). Training took 4 hours 40 minutes for the first adapter and 10 minutes for the second on one NVIDIA DGX Spark. The first adapter is trained by next-token prediction on a 61.6-million-token corpus covering ten engineering themes.
s38f7c848ce.summary: Researchers adapt a 4-billion-parameter model with two LoRA adapters into MarineSparkLM-4B, a language model for marine and offshore engineering, trained on a single workstation.
s38f7c848ce.why: It shows domain adaptation of a small model on modest hardware, though the domain focus limits broader engineering relevance.

s9c9d6e439c.title: Mean-field Token Steering
s9c9d6e439c.description: arXiv:2611.19163v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider stochastic token steering through a deep stack of transformer layers as a mean-field control problem for an interacting particle system on the unit sphere, where interactions arise from the attention mechanism. In the mean-field limit, the token population evolves via a controlled integro-partial differential equation where the feedback control acts as a corrective vector field guiding the population toward an aggregate configuration of tokens in the representation space. We deduce the minimum effort control to accomplish this task over a fixed time horizon interpreted as normalized layer depth. We show that the resulting controlled dynamics for the token population can be understood as a mean-field Schr\"odinger bridge adapted
s9c9d6e439c.summary: The paper frames stochastic token steering through transformer layers as a mean-field control problem for interacting tokens on the unit sphere.
s9c9d6e439c.why: It is a theoretical treatment of transformer dynamics with little immediate engineering application stated in the text.

s7673d558d3.title: Isolating Perception for Multi-View Planning under Occlusion-Induced Partial Observability
s7673d558d3.description: arXiv:2611.19179v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are beginning to saturate visual planning benchmarks, yet they fail to resolve depth ambiguity and degrade sharply with problem size under occlusion-induced partial observability (PO). We introduce BW-PO based on the Blocksworld domain, a controlled benchmark that reduces existing VLM planners and formalizers to near-zero performance, and propose VLM-as-perceiver, a paradigm that narrows the VLM's role to local perception while delegating cross-view evidence reconciliation and plan generation to external solvers. Across model-specific challenging subsets of BW-PO, this raises plan success from 1% to 97% for Gemma-4-31B, 0% to 95% for Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, and 3% to 84% for Gemini-3.1-Pro. Isolating perception in t
s7673d558d3.summary: Researchers introduce BW-PO, a Blocksworld-based benchmark for occlusion-induced partial observability, and propose VLM-as-perceiver, which limits VLMs to local perception and delegates planning to external solvers.
s7673d558d3.why: It shows VLM planners fail under occlusion and that delegating reasoning to external solvers may be a more reliable architecture.

sb45516c174.title: On-policy distillation as a Backdoor Propagation Channel
sb45516c174.description: arXiv:2611.19207v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) is emerging as an important paradigm for the post training of large language models, improving student models by leveraging supervision generated online by teacher models. However, whether this process also transfers latent security risks from teacher models to student models remains insufficiently studied. In this work, we reveal a new security risk in which an attacker first implants a conditional backdoor into the teacher model through supervised fine tuning (SFT), after which OPD can transfer the backdoor to the student model with only an extremely small proportion of trigger prompt exposure. More concerningly, we find that such backdoor transfer is substantially stronger under OPD than under conventional di
sb45516c174.summary: Researchers show that on-policy distillation can transfer a conditional backdoor implanted in a teacher model into a student model during LLM post-training.
sb45516c174.why: It reveals a supply-chain risk for teams using distillation from teacher models, since backdoors may propagate to students.

s2e9f2afef7.title: Neural Dual Bounds: Valid-by-Construction JGLP Warm-Starts for MAP and Constrained MAP
s2e9f2afef7.description: arXiv:2611.19218v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present Neural Dual Bounds, a calibration-free framework that produces deterministic upper bounds for MAP inference in probabilistic graphical models using a single neural-network forward pass. The framework trains a network to output the edge messages of a mini-bucket style upper bound on a given join-graph decomposition in a self-supervised manner by directly minimizing a smooth dual objective. The output of this network can be used at test time to warm-start a standard JGLP optimizer. Across diverse benchmarks, this warm start yields dual gaps that are orders of magnitude tighter than those from zero initialization, with the largest gains in the early-iteration regime. We also apply our framework for the constrained MAP (CMPE) task, w
s2e9f2afef7.summary: Researchers present Neural Dual Bounds, a neural network that produces valid upper bounds for MAP inference in graphical models in a single forward pass to warm-start JGLP.
s2e9f2afef7.why: It offers a faster route to tight bounds for graphical model inference, though the summary gives limited broader context.

s148f7e5738.title: Revisiting What Makes a Good Context Subset: A Sparse Latent Basis Perspective
s148f7e5738.description: arXiv:2611.19220v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Selecting context subsets is increasingly important in modern LLM inference, yet what makes a subset effective remains unclear. We study this question in the controlled setting of few-shot demonstration selection. We examine a hypothesis that demonstrations should collectively provide task-relevant information needed by a target query. Assuming that the query representation provides a useful proxy for these requirements, we formulate selection as sparse reconstruction and instantiate it with Residual Explanation Search (RES), a Matching-Pursuit-style diagnostic procedure. Across seven benchmarks and eight open-weight LLMs, no retrieval objective is universally best. RES outperforms MMR in 34 of 56 model--dataset pairs, with its clearest adv
s148f7e5738.summary: Researchers study what makes a good few-shot context subset, framing demonstration selection as sparse reconstruction and proposing Residual Explanation Search.
s148f7e5738.why: It gives a principled framing for demonstration selection that may improve few-shot prompt construction in LLM applications.

s8c22c37f98.title: Beyond Alignment: Supervising the Generator for EEG-to-Image Reconstruction
s8c22c37f98.description: arXiv:2611.19232v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Visual brain decoding translates neural activity into human-interpretable images. While recent EEG-to-image reconstruction methods rely on aligning EEG signals with pretrained visual embeddings to condition an image generator, we empirically demonstrate that stronger cross-modal alignment do not translate into comparable gains in reconstruction quality. This indicates that improving the input condition alone is insufficient; the generative process itself requires explicit supervision. Although Representation Alignment (REPA) offers a solution by guiding diffusion transformers with pretrained vision encoder features, we find that EEG-conditioned generators struggle to follow these fixed targets. To address this mismatch, we introduce generat
s8c22c37f98.summary: Researchers argue that stronger EEG-image alignment does not improve reconstruction quality, so the image generator itself needs explicit supervision, proposing Representation Alignment (REPA).
s8c22c37f98.why: Suggests that improving conditioning inputs alone may not help generative models, pointing to supervising the generation process directly.

sc51caf9b6f.title: HospitalBench: Diagnosing Where and Why Embodied Agents Fail on Long Hospital Task Chains
sc51caf9b6f.description: arXiv:2611.19274v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Long-horizon embodied tasks fail in ways that end-task success cannot see. HospitalBench is a diagnostic benchmark of ten hospital chores in NVIDIA Isaac Sim, each two unscored warm-up steps followed by a causal chain of five scored sub-tasks in one continuous simulation: the state one step leaves (an object pose, a choice, a fact seen once) determines what the next step must do, unlike benchmarks that place sub-tasks side by side. Vision-language agents act through skill-level tools from camera images. A scripted robot that makes only the calls a model gets is the solvability check of a chore. From each trajectory the benchmark reads where a chain breaks, what the agent did after a failed call, and how far its own position estimate drifts
sc51caf9b6f.summary: HospitalBench is a diagnostic benchmark of ten hospital chores in NVIDIA Isaac Sim, testing where and why vision-language embodied agents fail on causal five-step task chains.
sc51caf9b6f.why: Shows end-task success hides failure points in long-horizon agent tasks, so teams need step-level diagnostics for embodied agents.

sde5abb8daa.title: SAR-TopoGuard: Training-Free, Speckle-Aware Topological Verification for Structure-Preserving SAR-to-Optical Translation
sde5abb8daa.description: arXiv:2611.19316v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: SAR-to-optical translators often synthesize detail that the radar measurement does not support, and pixel metrics alone cannot reveal it. We propose SAR-TopoGuard, a training-free inference-time layer for frozen generators: a stochastic sampler draws K candidates (Monte Carlo dropout for GANs, seed variance for diffusion), a speckle-aware verifier ranks them by gradient-magnitude correlation with the SAR input and a hallucination-frequency index, and a SAR-guided frequency gate admits high-frequency detail only where SAR edges support it. With all five hyperparameters frozen and three training seeds, we evaluate on 500 scene-disjoint SEN1-2 test patches, 500 patches of a held-out summer scene, and 200 cross-dataset SEN12MS winter pairs. The
sde5abb8daa.summary: SAR-TopoGuard is a training-free inference-time layer that samples candidate outputs from frozen generators and filters them for speckle-aware structure in SAR-to-optical translation.
sde5abb8daa.why: Offers a way to reduce hallucinated detail in frozen generative models without retraining, relevant to remote sensing pipelines.

s49b9f4f1dc.title: Generation of protein conformations using a simple inverted transformer
s49b9f4f1dc.description: arXiv:2611.19321v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Molecular dynamics is an extremely powerful approach for studying protein behavior, but it requires enormous computational resources to obtain an adequate sampling of possible conformations. Recently, thanks to successes in predicting three-dimensional protein structures, there has been an explosion of research exploring the opportunities offered by deep learning to address the problem of protein conformational landscape. In this work, an artificial intelligence system based on a variant of the Transformer architecture is introduced and applied to the problem of determining the ensemble of three-dimensional structures that a protein can access and their statistical weight. After being trained on a dataset of conformations of a particular pr
s49b9f4f1dc.summary: Researchers introduce an AI system based on a variant of the Transformer architecture to generate protein conformations, aiming to reduce the compute needed for molecular dynamics sampling.
s49b9f4f1dc.why: Points to deep learning as a cheaper route to protein conformational sampling, though the text gives limited detail on results.

sfdc9b0ae5e.title: Benchmarking the State of AI for Crop Yield Forecasting: A Global Assessment Across Modeling Paradigms
sfdc9b0ae5e.description: arXiv:2611.19330v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Accurate crop yield forecasting is essential for food security, agricultural policy, and commodity markets. Although statistical, process-based, and machine learning approaches have all been proposed, their relative strengths remain poorly understood due to the lack of large-scale, standardized comparisons.
