We address this gap through a comprehensive benchmark of five modeling paradigms -- statistical baselines, process-based models, conventional feature-engineered machine learning, deep sequence models, and tabular foundation models -- using the CY-Bench benchmark spanning 63 country-crop datasets (>12,000 administrative regions) across six continents. Beyond conventional pooled accuracy metrics, we introduce a multi-dimensional evaluation
sfdc9b0ae5e.summary: A global benchmark compares five crop yield forecasting paradigms, including statistical, process-based, machine learning, deep sequence, and tabular foundation models.
sfdc9b0ae5e.why: Provides standardized evidence on which modeling approaches work for yield forecasting, though the text gives few specific findings.

s50bed0bc71.title: OmitEHR: Scalable Omission Detection in LLM-Generated Clinical Summaries
s50bed0bc71.description: arXiv:2611.19343v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Health systems increasingly rely on large language models (LLMs) to draft summaries of patient medical records, yet evaluations now find omissions, the absence of clinically important information, to be the most common failure mode. Detecting omissions in an LLM-generated summary requires knowing which facts in the record are salient, a signal that existing methods hand-specify, ignore, or recompute at inference with costly LLM judges. We present OmitEHR, a reference-free omission detector that learns clinical salience from historical clinician-written summaries predating widespread LLM use. OmitEHR learns to predict which source-note sentences clinicians include in their summaries, then surfaces high-salience sentences not covered by an LL
s50bed0bc71.summary: OmitEHR is a reference-free omission detector that learns clinical salience from historical clinician data to find missing information in LLM-generated clinical summaries.
s50bed0bc71.why: Targets omissions, reported as the most common LLM failure in clinical summaries, which matters for healthcare AI deployments.

sa6ed11bc3e.title: SMELL: Sparsity-aware Memory Efficient Federated Fine-tuning for Long-context LLMs
sa6ed11bc3e.description: arXiv:2611.19349v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Federated fine-tuning enables Large Language Models (LLMs) to collaboratively adapt to distributed private data. However, long-context fine-tuning on resource-constrained devices faces substantial challenges arising from excessive activation memory, heterogeneous token-importance patterns across clients, and communication overhead. To address these challenges, we propose SMELL, a Sparsity-aware and Memory-Efficient federated fine-tuning framework for Long-context LLMs. SMELL integrates three complementary mechanisms: Local Sparse-Forward Adaptation (LSFA), Consensus-Anchored Sparsity Coordination (CASC), and Communication-Efficient Progressive Update Recovery (CPUR). These mechanisms jointly enable memory-efficient local adaptation, heterog
sa6ed11bc3e.summary: SMELL is a sparsity-aware, memory-efficient federated fine-tuning framework for long-context LLMs on resource-constrained devices.
sa6ed11bc3e.why: Addresses activation memory, heterogeneous clients, and communication costs for fine-tuning LLMs on distributed private data.

s9b3ce75e02.title: Pixel-KWS: Rendered-Glyph Representations for Orthographically Robust Open-Vocabulary Keyword Spotting
s9b3ce75e02.description: arXiv:2611.19389v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Open-vocabulary keyword spotting (KWS) allows users to enroll arbitrary keywords at inference time. However, character and phoneme-based text encoders rely on fixed symbol vocabularies learned during training, limiting their ability to handle unseen or visually similar symbols such as homoglyphs, l33tspeak substitutions, and accented characters. We propose PIXEL-KWS, an open-vocabulary KWS framework that represents characters through rendered glyphs rather than learned embedding lookups. We render each character as a grayscale image and encode it with a lightweight CNN, enabling the text encoder to generalize from visual form rather than a fixed vocabulary. On LibriPhrase, PIXEL-KWS and its matched character-based counterpart achieve 9.57%
s9b3ce75e02.summary: PIXEL-KWS represents characters as rendered glyph images rather than learned embeddings, enabling open-vocabulary keyword spotting that handles homoglyphs and unseen symbols.
s9b3ce75e02.why: Offers a robustness approach for keyword spotting with user-defined keywords that involve unusual or visually similar characters.

sb34c5d6583.title: Do Pretraining Optimizer Gains Transfer to KL Distillation?
sb34c5d6583.description: arXiv:2611.19419v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Matrix-structured optimizers can improve language-model pretraining, but it is unclear whether these gains transfer to short-horizon KL distillation from an instruction-tuned initialization. We compare AdamW and diagonal AdaGrad with two tractable Shampoo reductions, SOAP, and All-2D Muon across four dense Qwen student-teacher pairs under a common forward-KL objective and fixed training budget. Across scales, none of the evaluated matrix-structured recipes consistently improves the quality versus trainer-time trade-off over the elementwise references: AdamW generally attains the lowest validation KL, while AdaGrad can be slightly faster at larger scale. SOAP often tracks AdamW in KL but incurs substantial trainer-time overhead, and the two
sb34c5d6583.summary: Comparison of AdamW, AdaGrad, Shampoo variants, SOAP, and All-2D Muon across Qwen student-teacher pairs finds none consistently improves KL distillation trade-offs over elementwise baselines.
sb34c5d6583.why: Suggests matrix-structured pretraining optimizers may not justify their cost for short-horizon distillation runs.

s956f7f25fd.title: Prepare Lighter and Faster for Open-Vocabulary Queries: A Query-Wise 3D Segmenter for Gaussian Splatting
s956f7f25fd.description: arXiv:2611.19429v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Open-vocabulary 3D understanding aims to localize and segment arbitrary objects beyond predefined categories. However, existing approaches based on Gaussian Splatting often rely on expensive preprocessing and lengthy training, limiting their applicability when fast and lightweight solutions are desired. We propose a lightweight, training-free framework for query-driven 3D instance segmentation on Gaussian Splatting. Instead of conventional mask-wise CLIP embeddings, we use dense pixel-level CLIP features to preserve fine-grained semantic information and enable flexible text-driven localization without relying on predefined instance proposals. Given a text query, we identify a high-quality target region in a carefully selected pivot view and
s956f7f25fd.summary: A lightweight, training-free framework performs query-driven 3D instance segmentation on Gaussian Splatting using dense pixel-level CLIP features instead of mask-wise embeddings.
s956f7f25fd.why: Reduces preprocessing and training cost for open-vocabulary 3D segmentation, useful for fast 3D scene understanding pipelines.

s90bfeb4bff.title: Do Rule-Based Tools Help LLMs Translate Endangered Uralic Languages in the Prompt or over MCP?
s90bfeb4bff.description: arXiv:2611.19439v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Komi-Zyrian, Moksha, Erzya and Udmurt have mature rule-based resources, among them finite-state analysers, constraint grammars and bilingual dictionaries, which language models do not use. We ask whether giving a model access to these resources improves machine translation from the four languages into English, and whether it matters how the access is provided: as analyses computed in advance and written into the prompt, or as tools that the model calls itself through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). We evaluate manually: an expert linguist read every English output of the strongest model under three conditions, 816 sentences in all, accepted or rejected each one, and named the main error in every rejected translation. With the analyses in
s90bfeb4bff.summary: A manual evaluation tests whether giving LLMs rule-based linguistic resources for four endangered Uralic languages improves translation, comparing prompt-embedded analyses with MCP tool calls.
s90bfeb4bff.why: Compares two integration methods for supplying tools to LLMs, relevant to how teams expose external resources via MCP.

sca771973f4.title: CLEW: Log-Anchored Backward Tracing for Root-Cause Code Localization
sca771973f4.description: arXiv:2611.19448v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Failures in industrial software systems may involve multiple components and be difficult to reproduce outside the production environment. Root-cause code localization therefore often relies on issue descriptions and runtime logs. However, log evidence may be noisy or incomplete, and the code reporting a symptom may differ from the code containing the underlying defect. These conditions make it challenging to identify relevant log evidence and determine which functions could have caused the reported failure. To address this gap, we introduce CLEW, an agentic approach that combines rule-based log-to-code anchoring with LLM-guided backward code tracing. CLEW organizes selected observations into diagnostic states, guides source exploration from
sca771973f4.summary: CLEW is a log-anchored backward tracing method for localizing root-cause code from issue descriptions and noisy runtime logs in industrial software systems.
sca771973f4.why: Targets the practical problem of finding defect locations from incomplete logs, relevant to debugging production failures.

s37638498cd.title: VAST: Compiling Grounded Vulnerability Scenarios into Verifiable, Multi-Step Environments for Evaluating LLM Red-Team Agents
s37638498cd.description: arXiv:2611.19465v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Evaluating Large Language Model (LLM) security agents requires reproducible environments whose workflow difficulty can be varied and whose failures can be diagnosed. We present VAST (Verifiable Adversarial Scenario Training & Evaluation), a declarative range compiler separating vulnerability scenarios from a compiler-introduced workflow-hardening layer. Following a post-hoc code and AST audit across all topics, the main benchmark retains 109 seed edges (45 with strict upstream CVE annotations), 72 family identifiers (62 under shared-HMAC relay grouping), 81 topic configurations (76 core plus 5 bounded execution models), and 1,387 instances (359 canonical four-gate-revalidated specs plus 1,028 seed variants) in a 42:39 partition. On the Topi
s37638498cd.summary: VAST is a declarative range compiler that generates verifiable, multi-step vulnerability environments for evaluating LLM red-team security agents.
s37638498cd.why: Provides reproducible, diagnosable environments for testing security agents, which helps teams benchmark agent-based security tooling.

s2ae76e4627.title: InvarOrd: Self-Supervised Ordinal Knowledge Distillation with Rank-Invariant Alignment for Label-Efficient Cross-Species Hyperspectral Fish Freshness Assessment
s2ae76e4627.description: arXiv:2611.19472v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hyperspectral models of fish freshness rarely transfer between species, and labelling a new species is slow and destructive. Freshness is also ordinal, and standard domain alignment can erase that order. We present InvarOrd, which adapts to a new species from 30 labelled cubes (5 per rank) in three stages: self-supervised spectral pretraining on unlabelled source cubes, cross-species alignment by a shrinkage covariance discrepancy computed only within matched ranks, and ordinal distillation into a compact student. The alignment term is provably invariant to the rank means, so it gives no incentive to collapse the ordinal axis. On paired salmon and cod data (800 cubes each, 16 days), a source-trained teacher reaches 1.6 to 1.9 days mean abso
s2ae76e4627.summary: InvarOrd is a self-supervised ordinal distillation method that adapts hyperspectral fish freshness models to new species using 30 labelled cubes.
s2ae76e4627.why: Shows label-efficient cross-domain transfer for ordinal classification, though the application is niche for most engineering teams.

s4df488191e.title: Do Probing and Steering Favor the Same Directions Within and Across Language Models?
s4df488191e.description: arXiv:2611.19499v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A direction in a language model's hidden state can be used to probe whether a concept is present or to steer the model toward it. Although probe directions are often reused for steering, the direction that best detects a concept need not be the one that best changes it. We study this distinction in three instruction-tuned models from different families. We construct a one-parameter family of directions ranging from a covariance-adjusted discriminant to the mean difference, and evaluate probing and additive steering, which adds the direction to the hidden state, along the family at a fixed side effect. For truthfulness and sentiment, in every model, the best probe is not the best steering direction: steering consistently favors directions cl
s4df488191e.summary: Researchers study whether directions that best probe a concept in LLM hidden states also work best for steering, testing a family of directions across three instruction-tuned models.
s4df488191e.why: Shows probe directions may not be the best steering directions, which affects interpretability-based control methods.

s67111ac713.title: Agent Authenticator: Passkey-Grade, Hardware-Bound Authentication for AI Agents
s67111ac713.description: arXiv:2611.19536v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI coding agents now push code, publish packages, call model APIs and operate cloud resources on behalf of developers. They authenticate to these services with the same bearer secrets humans use, personal access tokens, API keys and package-registry tokens, stored where the model, its subprocesses and any co-resident malware can read them. Incidents in 2025 and 2026, including prompt-injection attacks on coding agents and self-propagating supply-chain worms, show that this arrangement fails in predictable ways. Passkeys solved the analogous problem for humans, but they require a human gesture on every use and cannot be operated by an autonomous process. We present the Agent Authenticator, a design that gives agents passkey-grade authenticat
s67111ac713.summary: Researchers propose Agent Authenticator, a hardware-bound, passkey-style authentication scheme for AI coding agents that currently rely on bearer tokens readable by models and malware.
s67111ac713.why: Agents hold tokens for pushing code and cloud access, so bearer-secret exposure is a real security gap for engineering teams.

sfb2d62a278.title: Func-JEPA: Learning a Sobolev Space of Functions as Latent Vectors
sfb2d62a278.description: arXiv:2611.19542v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Pretraining an encoder once and reusing it across tasks is a widespread approach in vision and language. However, neural symbolic mathematics still trains a dedicated sequence-to-sequence model for each task, so that no representation of a function is shared. In this work, we propose the Function Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (Func-JEPA, abbreviated f-JEPA): an encoder of mathematical functions, pretrained on their symbolic form, whose latent space imitates the Sobolev space H^1 and in which differentiation is a learned latent operator. The norm of a latent is computed exactly from the function, whereas its direction is learned to match Sobolev angles. The frozen encoder is then reused by lightweight modules for decoding, composit
sfb2d62a278.summary: Researchers introduce Func-JEPA, an encoder pretrained on symbolic mathematical functions whose latent space mimics a Sobolev space, so differentiation becomes a latent operator.
sfb2d62a278.why: It proposes a shared, reusable function representation for symbolic math, a departure from training a separate model per task.

se157426979.title: Beyond Prompts: Runtime Contracts for Coding Agents
se157426979.description: arXiv:2611.19549v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coding agents act on repositories through shell commands and file edits, and teams steer them with written engineering rules. Industrial settings expect such rules to be enforced and their application to be evidenced, and a rule given as prompt text provides neither. We test whether executable contracts enforced while the agent works reduce rule violations compared with the same rules in the prompt, retrieved as guidance, or checked only after generation. Violations are scored by an oracle whose methods differ from the in-loop checks, and the oracle is validated by two human reviewers and a model reviewer. Across three studies on two model families (240, 112 and 108 runs), enforcement during execution produced no oracle-detected violation i
se157426979.summary: A study tests whether executable contracts enforced during a coding agent's work reduce rule violations better than writing the same rules in the prompt or checking after generation.
se157426979.why: It suggests enforcing engineering rules in code, not prompts, may give teams verifiable compliance from coding agents.

s92a7c53c1a.title: Lesion-Aware Explainable AI for Diabetic Retinopathy Grading from Fundus Images
s92a7c53c1a.description: arXiv:2611.19550v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Post-hoc explanations of deep-learning models for diabetic retinopathy (DR) grading are difficult to trust because different attribution methods highlight different retinal regions for the same image, and a visually plausible heatmap does not show that the highlighted pixels drive the prediction. We propose the Consensus-Calibrated Explanation Map (CCEM), which fuses Grad-CAM++, Ada-SISE, and SmoothGrad Integrated Gradients (SG-IG) using image-specific weights derived from annotation-free reliability cues: deletion sensitivity, inter-method agreement, compactness, retinal containment, and peak structure. CCEM explains a frozen ordinal grader, an EfficientNet-B7 with CBAM and a scalar regression head, pre-trained on EyePACS 2015 in Stage 1 a
s92a7c53c1a.summary: Researchers propose CCEM, a consensus-calibrated explanation method for diabetic retinopathy grading that fuses several attribution methods using annotation-free reliability cues.

s837b615dc5.title: Inquest: Log-Guided Root-Cause Code Localization with a Staged Agent
s837b615dc5.description: arXiv:2611.19554v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: When a production issue is reported, engineers get a description and some logs, but no failing test and no way to reproduce the fault. The logs show where the failure was noticed, not where it was caused: in 49% of the real reports we study, the text names none of the files that the fix later changed. We built a benchmark for this setting from two public datasets and 27 open-source projects (Apache, Red Hat, MongoDB, MariaDB, Qt and Sakai). It holds 38,001 resolved issue reports with their pasted logs, the code as it was while the bug was still present, and the files the fix changed. We present INQUEST, an agent that finds the faulty code using a 27B open-weights model. Code, not the model, controls the procedure. It first gathers the evide
s837b615dc5.summary: Researchers present Inquest, a staged agent that localizes root-cause code from production logs, with a benchmark of 38,001 resolved issues across 27 open-source projects.
s837b615dc5.why: Logs often point to where failures surface rather than their cause, so better localization could speed production debugging.

s3ef1a72ce4.title: SemMask: Semantic-Prioritized Progressive Masking for Diffusion Language Models
s3ef1a72ce4.description: arXiv:2611.19560v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) are designed to enable globally parallel generation. However, in practice, they often exhibit pseudo-autoregressive behavior and a function-word-first bias, which undermines their performance on tasks such as text writing and code generation that benefit from global planning and parallel decoding. To address this, we propose SemMask, a novel fine-tuning paradigm that leverages a semantic-prioritized progressive masking strategy to encourage the model to decode high-information semantic tokens early and globally, thereby enhancing its global planning and parallel generation capabilities. Specifically, we first use the gradients of the original DLM with respect to each token to identify semantic tokens. During
s3ef1a72ce4.summary: SemMask is a fine-tuning method for diffusion language models that uses semantic-prioritized progressive masking to decode high-information tokens early and reduce function-word-first bias.
s3ef1a72ce4.why: It targets a known weakness of diffusion language models in code generation and writing tasks that need global planning.

se11e0235a1.title: Read, Then Shade? How Visual Evidence Changes Incentive-Driven Misreporting in Vision-Language Advisors
se11e0235a1.description: arXiv:2611.19561v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) increasingly read a scene and report it to someone who acts on the report, sometimes under objectives that differ from that person's. We ask whether a stated incentive moves what a VLM reports, and whether this changes when the value must be read from pixels rather than given as text. In seeded synthetic scenes, a model reads the position of a target on a labelled axis and reports one integer to a fixed receiver; it is paid, in simulation, for accuracy or for a report a few units to one side, and every scene is also presented with the true value as text. Across a pilot and three follow-up studies with hash-frozen protocols, four small open VLMs from three families, and 15,170 held-out trials, a stated payoff mo
se11e0235a1.summary: A study examines whether a stated incentive changes what vision-language models report about a scene, and whether reading values from pixels rather than text alters that misreporting.
se11e0235a1.why: It raises reliability concerns when VLMs report to a receiver whose objectives may differ from the model's.

sb848fb8efe.title: Learning from Mutants: Teaching Small Language Models to Synthesise Loop Invariants
sb848fb8efe.description: arXiv:2611.19569v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have proven promising for synthesising loop invariants, a long-standing obstacle to automated program verification. Yet, frontier LLMs are typically accessible only through third-party APIs, hampering reproducibility and local deployment. Small language models (SLMs) sidestep these obstacles but require task-specific fine-tuning, for which high-quality training data is needed. We present a failure-driven data curation method for fine-tuning language models to synthesise loop invariants. Inspired by mutation testing, our approach applies semantic mutation operators to ground-truth invariants, producing semantic mutants that induce verification failure. Each mutant is paired with verifier feedback and its ground-t
sb848fb8efe.summary: Researchers propose a failure-driven data curation method, inspired by mutation testing, to fine-tune small language models to synthesize loop invariants for program verification.
sb848fb8efe.why: Small local models could automate loop invariant synthesis without relying on third-party frontier model APIs.

s31fdd55bef.title: Spectral Steering: Local Inverse Geometry for Frozen Diffusion Generators
s31fdd55bef.description: arXiv:2611.19572v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A frozen diffusion generator may need to change several output properties while preserving others. We study when guidance faithfully realizes such a structured request and whether local inverse correction improves its direction. Our account links this benefit to the interaction between the request and the objective-specific remaining-sampler Jacobian: conditioning alone is insufficient. Spectral steering combines a request-specific cosine-gain predictor with damped inverse correction and fixed-time relinearization for finite edits. Scalar nulls and matched-movement controls test the predicted mechanism. Across 8,923 instances in a retrospectively identified local regime, predicted and realized gains correlate at Spearman 0.79, versus -0.11
s31fdd55bef.summary: Spectral Steering is a method for frozen diffusion generators that combines a cosine-gain predictor with damped inverse correction to realize structured output edits.

s4341a72bd9.title: Risk-Averse Decision-Focused Learning: Minimizing CVaR of Regret
s4341a72bd9.description: arXiv:2611.19575v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many combinatorial optimization (CO) problems involve parameters that are uncertain when the problem must be solved. In such settings, the parameters have to be predicted from correlated contextual information before a solution can be computed. \emph{Decision-focused learning} (DFL) addresses this by training the predictive model to produce predictions that optimize downstream decision quality. Most existing DFL methods are risk-neutral and minimize the expected regret. In high-stakes applications this can lead to undesirable outcomes, because decision-makers must also account for the tail risk of decision quality. Prior risk-sensitive approaches typically model uncertainty explicitly and solve a stochastic or robust optimization problem at
s4341a72bd9.summary: Researchers propose risk-averse decision-focused learning that minimizes CVaR of regret, rather than expected regret, for combinatorial optimization under uncertainty.
s4341a72bd9.why: High-stakes decisions under uncertain predictions may need tail-risk objectives instead of risk-neutral expected regret.

sc7814ca715.title: PBit1: One Programmable P-Bit per Parameter - A Finite-Control Representation of Pretrained Networks
sc7814ca715.description: arXiv:2611.19588v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce PBit1, a finite-control representation of pretrained neural networks that assigns one programmable p-bit to each learned parameter. A 12-bit command sets its probability, a shared affine range maps that probability to the weight domain, and temporal observations reconstruct the weight for inference. Operator-aware range grouping and sensitivity-based sampling allocation adapt the representation to the network. Across five independent weight draws at 32,768 observations per scalar, selected configurations preserve task quality in GPT-2, DistilBERT, and LFM3-1.7B with every learned scalar converted and no fine-tuning. GPT-2 and LFM3 perplexity increase by approximately 0.66% and 0.26%, respectively, while DistilBERT accuracy chan
sc7814ca715.summary: PBit1 proposes representing each pretrained network parameter with one programmable p-bit controlled by a 12-bit command, reconstructing weights for inference while preserving task quality.

se245b3389b.title: Synthetic Neurosymbolic Task Generation with Controlled Constraint Complexity
se245b3389b.description: arXiv:2611.19597v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce NeSySy, a synthetic generator for neurosymbolic learning tasks that jointly produces logical constraints and consistent datasets. Unlike existing benchmarks, NeSySy provides fine-grained control over key properties such as constraint structure, tightness, input dependence, and data generation and alignment strategies. In particular, it allows the use of rich constraints over infinite domains, and uses solvers to ensure that the constraints are meaningful and that generated samples satisfy the constraints. We design NeSySy to support both learning with declarative constraints and learning from distant supervision. Across a range of constraint families, we provide evidence that its parameters induce systematic and largely indepen
se245b3389b.summary: NeSySy is a synthetic generator for neurosymbolic learning tasks that produces logical constraints and consistent datasets with controllable constraint structure and tightness.
se245b3389b.why: Configurable benchmarks with solver-verified constraints could help teams evaluate neurosymbolic methods more systematically.

sfaa339fbf2.title: Well-Log Reconstruction with Pre-trained Geological Knowledge: A Knowledge-Conditioned Large-Language-Model Generative Agent
sfaa339fbf2.description: arXiv:2611.19624v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Missing well-log intervals make subsurface reconstruction ill-posed. Existing numerical regression models lack geological prior knowledge to constrain ambiguous inverse mappings. We propose GeoLog-Agent, a knowledge-conditioned generative agent using pre-trained large language models (LLMs) as a source of geological priors. A universal Geo-Harness translates LLM stratigraphic reasoning into formation-anchored petrophysical trajectories, feature-wise linear modulation, and conditional adversarial constraints. On the Norwegian North Sea benchmark, GeoLog-Agent achieves a mean $R^2$ of 0.9307 and a peak $R^2$ of 0.9713. It exceeds the nine-baseline average $R^2$ of 0.8387 by 0.0920, with a 30.97% average RMSE reduction, and exceeds the stronge
sfaa339fbf2.summary: GeoLog-Agent is a knowledge-conditioned generative agent that uses pre-trained LLMs as geological priors to reconstruct missing well-log intervals.

s03bce4c227.title: Robust Well-Log Reconstruction Across Point Gaps and Whole Wells via Boundary-Gated Soft-Thresholding Kalman Fusion
s03bce4c227.description: arXiv:2611.19625v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Missing wireline logs hinder subsurface characterization. Deep reconstruction networks suffer from gap-boundary steps and cross-basin shifts, while interpolation and Gaussian smoothers struggle with long intervals and outliers. We propose boundary-gated soft-thresholding Kalman fusion (ST-KF), unifying multiresolution wavelet shrinkage, distance-gated residual prior learning, and closed-form robust Kalman smoothing with learning--inference decoupling. Across two public benchmarks totaling 263 wells in the Norwegian North Sea and New Zealand's Taranaki Basin, ST-KF ranks first over 0.15--100-m anchored gaps with 0.09% parameter overhead. Against the strongest of nine baselines, pooled RMSE falls by 5.0%--8.3% for bulk density and 6.4%--15.6%
s03bce4c227.summary: Researchers propose ST-KF, a boundary-gated soft-thresholding Kalman fusion method for reconstructing missing wireline logs, evaluated on two public benchmarks covering 263 wells.

s25cf6a4fd3.title: Where slide-level foundation-model classifiers fail on atypical breast lesions
s25cf6a4fd3.description: arXiv:2611.19630v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Whether a ductal breast lesion is called atypical hyperplasia or low-grade carcinoma in situ increasingly determines surgery. However, slide-level classifiers built on pathology foundation models (PFMs) perform worst on these lesions. Using four PFMs, cross-validation on BRACS and preregistered hypotheses, we studied where the classification of atypia fails. Because slides are labelled with their most severe lesion, only 39% of the slides with annotated atypical ductal hyperplasia (ADH) were labelled ADH. Attention ranked the lesion high but rarely first, and showing the model only the lesion helped little, whereas classifiers trained per decision with lesion-level labels improved all four atypical boundaries. ADH regions inserted into beni
s25cf6a4fd3.summary: A study finds slide-level classifiers built on pathology foundation models perform worst on atypical breast lesions, partly because slides are labelled with their most severe lesion.
s25cf6a4fd3.why: Label noise from slide-level severity labeling can silently limit foundation-model performance in clinical deployments.

s559e81b063.title: ROUNDS: Source-Framed Diagnostic Revision after Multi-Turn Clinical Evidence
s559e81b063.description: arXiv:2611.19636v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) achieve high scores on medical benchmarks, but does this performance translate into reliable diagnosis as a conversation unfolds? In diagnostic conversations, users can provide clinical findings across multiple turns, ask for a diagnosis without supplying answer options, and introduce opinions from others. Models must therefore form diagnoses from the available evidence and decide how to respond to subsequent advice. We introduce ROUNDS, a framework that evaluates these abilities after a fixed sequence of clinical evidence delivered over multiple turns. ROUNDS compares diagnosis with and without answer options, presents the same incorrect diagnosis under clinician and lay framing, and varies support for competin
s559e81b063.summary: Researchers introduce ROUNDS, a framework testing whether LLMs keep reliable diagnoses across multi-turn clinical conversations, including unprompted options and others' opinions.
s559e81b063.why: Benchmark scores may not reflect diagnostic reliability in real multi-turn clinical dialogue, so teams deploying medical assistants need conversation-level evaluation.

s2dc502abac.title: SG-LegalClarify: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Legal Reasoning and Ambiguity Recognition in Singapore Law
s2dc502abac.description: arXiv:2611.19643v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Singapore offers a distinctive testbed for legal reasoning by large language models (LLMs). Its legal system combines inherited English common law with jurisdiction-specific statutes, requiring models to distinguish local doctrine from generic common-law intuition. This setting also highlights the challenge of recognizing underspecification in lay legal queries, because the facts material to a legal outcome depend on the governing doctrine. Yet legal benchmarks rarely cover Singapore law or test this form of ambiguity recognition. To address these gaps, we introduce SG-LegalClarify, a large-scale benchmark for open-ended legal reasoning and ambiguity recognition in Singapore law. SG-LegalClarify contains 1,100 lawyer-authored source questio
s2dc502abac.summary: Researchers release SG-LegalClarify, a large benchmark testing LLMs on Singapore legal reasoning and recognizing underspecified lay legal queries.
s2dc502abac.why: It shows LLMs may miss jurisdiction-specific doctrine and ambiguity, a risk for legal-domain products outside common-law generic knowledge.

s6c1b48e077.title: LoopFill: Pipelined Multi-Token Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers
s6c1b48e077.description: arXiv:2611.19649v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Looped Transformers improve parameter efficiency by repeatedly applying the same Transformer layers. During autoregressive decoding, however, generating each token requires several sequential passes through these layers, leading to high decoding latency. Pipelined self-speculative methods use shallow-loop predictions to process tokens at different loops in the same batch, but each token must reach the drafting depth before the next can enter the pipeline. We introduce LoopFill, a training-free speculative decoding algorithm for looped LLM that combines multi-token suffix drafts with shallow-loop predictions in a single draft tree. Both drafters contribute to one tree, so a suffix lookup can immediately extend a shallow prediction and severa
s6c1b48e077.summary: LoopFill is a training-free speculative decoding algorithm for looped LLMs that aims to reduce the sequential-pass latency of autoregressive generation.
s6c1b48e077.why: Lower decoding latency for looped transformers could make parameter-efficient models cheaper to serve without retraining.

s6e2f0bc6d5.title: BadGCL: Towards Persistent Backdoor Attack on Graph Continual Learning Systems
s6e2f0bc6d5.description: arXiv:2611.19656v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Backdoor attacks pose a persistent security threat to machine learning systems, yet their behavior under graph continual learning (GCL) remains underexplored. Conventional graph backdoor attacks often lose effectiveness as models are updated across successive tasks, creating the impression that continual updates naturally weaken malicious associations. This work reveals a contrasting vulnerability: knowledge-preservation mechanisms in GCL can also preserve early injected backdoors when the poisoned update is compatible with the clean-task signal being retained. For graph data, this risk is amplified by structural triggers, which are embedded into the message-passing paths of graph neural networks (GNNs) and can induce stable representation
s6e2f0bc6d5.summary: BadGCL shows that knowledge-preservation mechanisms in graph continual learning can keep early-injected backdoors alive across later task updates.
s6e2f0bc6d5.why: Teams updating graph models incrementally may retain poisoned behavior longer than expected, so update pipelines need security review.

s8a23d7e14f.title: Architecting the Corporate AI Infrastructure: The Evolving Roles of AI Governance Committees and Chief Ethics Officers
s8a23d7e14f.description: arXiv:2611.19670v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The accelerating integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into core business operations has created an urgent need for robust corporate governance infrastructures capable of managing complex ethical, legal, and operational risks. While organizations have increasingly adopted high-level AI ethics principles, a critical implementation gap persists: fewer than half of organizations that cite AI governance as a boardroom priority have a formalized governance framework in place. This paper addresses that gap by proposing a structured corporate AI governance architecture (CAIGA) centred on two mutually reinforcing pillars. First, it examines the evolving mandate of specialized C-suite roles, specifically Chief Privacy Officers (CPOs) and Chief
s8a23d7e14f.summary: A paper proposes a structured corporate AI governance infrastructure, addressing the gap that fewer than half of organizations citing AI governance have a formal framework.
s8a23d7e14f.why: It offers a concrete organizational model for AI governance committees and ethics officers, relevant to leaders building oversight processes.

s976d4f451a.title: MathaMAGICal: Validating Trajectory Data Attribution During Capability Acquisition
s976d4f451a.description: arXiv:2611.19692v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Influence-function-based methods like MAGIC provide exact first-order scores for trajectory data attribution, yet only retraining indicates whether those scores accurately predict data removal. We evaluate MAGIC on $86$M- and $152$M-parameter GPT-2-style models learning multistep arithmetic from scratch on filtered web text and four synthetic math families. Full-run attribution at $86$M suffers from numerical overflow, and even with metagradient clipping, scores correlate near chance with retraining (linear datamodeling score, LDS, $0.17$--$0.22$). In contrast, short checkpoint windows yield stable, accurate predictions at both scales (LDS $0.86$--$0.99$ across four $100$-step windows at $152$M), whereas a single-checkpoint gradient-dot bas
s976d4f451a.summary: Researchers evaluate MAGIC trajectory data attribution on GPT-2-style models, finding attribution scores correlate near chance with retraining results at 86M parameters.
s976d4f451a.why: Influence-based attribution may not reliably predict the effect of removing training data, so teams should validate it by retraining before relying on it.

sda98bdffc4.title: Data Attribution Should Steer Pretraining
sda98bdffc4.description: arXiv:2611.19698v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Pretraining data curation decides what a model learns from, yet what makes a document worth learning from depends on what the model already knows. Influence-driven selectors already rank documents to improve one run; we argue that training-data attribution should steer pretraining by identifying testable data properties that become reusable curation criteria, evaluated on new data against cheaper selectors at matched total cost, discovery included. A document ranking is consumed by the run it was computed for, whereas an explained data property can be tested across corpora and checkpoints, especially where familiar quality signals diverge from measured usefulness. Because historical contribution, an understandable explanation, and future da
sda98bdffc4.summary: The paper argues training-data attribution should be used to steer pretraining by identifying reusable data properties rather than one-off document rankings.
sda98bdffc4.why: Reusable curation criteria could make pretraining data selection more transferable across runs, which matters for teams managing training budgets.

s0e1737dc20.title: Where Should LLM Agents Adapt at Test Time? In Context, in Weights, or Both
s0e1737dc20.description: arXiv:2611.19700v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM agents operating repeatedly in the same environment, such as a code repository, a database, or an application suite, encounter tasks that share latent structure. Experience can reveal this structure, allowing agents to reuse environment knowledge and learn from environmental feedback. Agents can adapt at test-time using this experience through two channels: retaining it in context and updating their weights. These channels are usually studied separately, leaving unclear what each contributes and when they complement each other. We compare in-context learning (ICL), reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards using GRPO, and self-distillation using SDPO, alone and in combination, using a shared online protocol and modular framework. A
s0e1737dc20.summary: A study compares whether LLM agents should adapt at test time through in-context experience, weight updates, or both, across repeated environments.
s0e1737dc20.why: Choosing between context-based memory and weight updates affects agent architecture and cost for repeated-task deployments.

scae229f8c3.title: Cache or Denoise Less? Residual Reuse in a Flow-Matching World Action Model
scae229f8c3.description: arXiv:2611.19709v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Flow-matching robot policies generate each action chunk through repeated network evaluations, one per denoising step. Cross-cycle caches such as C$^3$ache reuse computation from earlier replanning calls, but whether they beat simply taking fewer steps is unclear. We compare the two in Fast-WAM, a 6B-parameter world action model, on LIBERO-Goal. Two uncached steps keep the success of ten: on all 500 initial states they are non-inferior within two percentage points, for one checkpoint and noise seed. Under PyTorch's default compile mode, they also cut a replanning call on an RTX A6000 from 202 to 92 ms. This leaves little room for caching. A cache that keeps two fresh steps cannot be faster than two uncached steps: every call still encodes th
scae229f8c3.summary: Researchers compare cross-cycle caching against taking fewer denoising steps in Fast-WAM, a 6B-parameter flow-matching robot world action model.
scae229f8c3.why: Two uncached steps matched the success of ten on LIBERO-Goal, suggesting simpler step reduction can rival caching for robot policy latency.

s2b03c36655.title: Joint Learning of Factual and Counterfactual Worlds for Causal Prior-data Fitted Networks
s2b03c36655.description: arXiv:2611.19710v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Estimating treatment effects is central to science across many disciplines and requires counterfactual reasoning about alternative worlds. In the real world, however, each unit reveals its outcome only under the factual world. Thus, the factual and counterfactual outcomes can never be jointly learned by any model trained on real data. The problem is therefore tractable only in synthetic settings, where both worlds can be generated. Recent progress on prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) has shown that models pre-trained purely on synthetic data can transfer to real-world prediction. This paradigm has since carried over to causal effect estimation. Despite this fully synthetic setup, existing causal PFNs carry the real-world constraint into the
s2b03c36655.summary: Researchers propose joint learning of factual and counterfactual worlds in causal prior-data fitted networks, pretrained on synthetic data for treatment effect estimation.

s26fdb2d4a7.title: An Interpretable Acoustic Coordinate System for Japanese Consonant Morae in Dysarthric Speech
s26fdb2d4a7.description: arXiv:2611.19714v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Dysarthria reduces speech intelligibility, requiring self-directed rehabilitation based on fine-grained feedback to capture gradual articulatory changes. For Japanese speakers, such feedback is naturally provided in mora units due to its distinct moraic timing and consonant-vowel structure. While recent visualization methods have explored distance-based feedback, most are limited to vowels. Extending them to consonants is challenging, as generative embeddings often smooth transient spectral structures. We propose a visualization system for Japanese consonant morae that maps articulatory deviations onto a two-dimensional space defined by temporal and spectral distances from healthy reference speech. Experiments show consistent geometric sepa
s26fdb2d4a7.summary: Researchers propose an interpretable acoustic coordinate system giving distance-based visual feedback on Japanese consonant morae for dysarthric speech rehabilitation.

s4fa634b17e.title: Exploration of Reinforcement Learning in Generative Recommendation Models
s4fa634b17e.description: arXiv:2611.19742v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Traditional cascaded recommender systems balance accuracy and efficiency over large item spaces, but misaligned stage-wise objectives hinder end-to-end optimization. Generative recommendation unifies these stages in an autoregressive framework, providing a natural interface for reinforcement learning (RL) to optimize the entire generation process. However, directly applying RL often leads to unstable optimization and degraded recommendation quality. We revisit Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) and other ratio-based objectives through a unified logit-gradient view. We identify three issues: (i) clipped surrogates create dead-gradient regions, under-utilizing samples; (ii) negative-advantage updates can become effectively unbounded as
s4fa634b17e.summary: A study revisits GRPO and ratio-based objectives for reinforcement learning in generative recommendation models, addressing unstable optimization and degraded quality.
s4fa634b17e.why: Applying RL end-to-end to generative recommenders is unstable with naive GRPO, so practitioners need stabilizing objectives before adopting it.

s80d3d4572c.title: How Far Is Too Far? Object Recognition Declines Monotonically with Semantic Distance
s80d3d4572c.description: arXiv:2611.19747v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision models are sensitive to object-background context, yet it remains unclear how recognition changes as the semantic distance between objects and backgrounds increases. We introduce ImageNet-OOC1k, a benchmark enabling graded control of object-background relationships along a continuous consensus visual-semantic dissimilarity axis. This formulation reveals a highly consistent monotonic decline in recognition accuracy across 35 models spanning convolutional neural networks, Vision Transformers, and vision-language models. Internal analyses of Vision Transformers reveal patterns consistent with aggregation failure, where object evidence is present at the patch level but not consolidated into the final prediction. Using this characterizati
s80d3d4572c.summary: ImageNet-OOC1k benchmark shows object recognition accuracy declines monotonically as semantic distance between object and background grows, across 35 vision models.
s80d3d4572c.why: Vision models degrade predictably with object-background semantic mismatch, a robustness consideration for deployed perception systems.

s3e51287e13.title: StaleBench: Isolating Stale Retrieval in Agent Memory, and Pricing the Fix
s3e51287e13.description: arXiv:2611.19752v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An agent that stores facts over time eventually stores several versions of the same fact. Asked a value-agnostic question - "which team does X play for now?" - a similarity retriever cannot prefer the current version, because every version matches the entity the query names. StaleBench isolates this stale-retrieval failure on 892 real updating facts, with currency labels from the source (Wikidata validity years via TempLAMA), never from a retrieval score. Our central result is that retrieval metrics can rank memory policies backwards: a retention policy and its retain-everything control return the identical statement at rank 1 for every test query, yet differ by 29.5 and 65.6 points in reader accuracy on two readers when no date is shown. C
s3e51287e13.summary: StaleBench isolates stale retrieval in agent memory using 892 updating facts and finds retrieval metrics can rank memory policies backwards.
s3e51287e13.why: Agents storing evolving facts may retrieve outdated versions, and standard retrieval metrics can misleadingly rank memory designs.

s7020765129.title: Learning Autoregressive Neural Operators on Solver-Defined Physical Constraint Manifolds
s7020765129.description: arXiv:2611.19753v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Autoregressive neural operators approximate time-dependent PDE solvers by repeatedly composing a learned transition, although the resulting states need not remain feasible under the discrete constraints of the numerical problem. We study this issue for incompressible flow, where each velocity state must satisfy solver-level incompressibility together with prescribed boundary values. We formulate autoregressive operator learning as a map between solver-defined affine feasible sets and introduce PCM-NO, a projected-residual realization of this feasible-transition principle. The neural backbone predicts a candidate state increment, a fixed tangent projection extracts its admissible component, and a metric retraction maps the advanced state to
s7020765129.summary: PCM-NO is a projected-residual autoregressive neural operator that keeps predicted incompressible flow states within solver-defined physical constraints.
s7020765129.why: Enforcing solver constraints during autoregressive rollouts could make learned PDE surrogates more reliable for engineering simulation.

s1f2bd0ea99.title: Eliciting Research Taste in LLMs through Future Research Direction Choice
s1f2bd0ea99.description: arXiv:2611.19794v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Research taste is increasingly discussed in the context of AI scientists, yet remains little studied or measured in LLMs. This judgment matters especially in open-ended research, where a direction must be chosen before a verifiable objective is available. We operationalize research taste through one task of the scientific workflow: choosing which future research direction to pursue given a research goal and current results. Rather than predicting downstream scientometric metrics or treating author choices as objectively correct, we evaluate models against human-authored future-work directions and report author alignment, stable divergence, and unstable choice as behavioral measures of research-direction preference. We construct an order-con
s1f2bd0ea99.summary: Researchers propose evaluating LLM research taste by having models choose which future research direction to pursue, given a research goal and current results.
s1f2bd0ea99.why: It offers a way to measure LLM judgment in open-ended research, where no verifiable objective exists before a direction is chosen.

s62daea9a39.title: Reasoning in the loop: antibody lead optimization by probing mechanism and measurement
s62daea9a39.description: arXiv:2611.19812v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Lab-in-the-loop systems, in which a model proposes molecules, automated assays measure their properties and the results retrain the model, are a popular approach to antibody lead optimization. These systems optimize for a specification defined with metrics computed from instrument signals, so their success depends on how well those metrics serve as proxies for the properties a drug candidate needs. When a metric is a poor proxy, neither a better model nor more data will fix it, and identifying the problem usually requires expert review. We report two campaigns run on BigHat Biosciences' Milliner platform, one on an anti-albumin nanobody (VHH) and one on an anti-mesothelin single-chain variable fragment (scFv), in which a research team and a
s62daea9a39.summary: Researchers examine lab-in-the-loop antibody lead optimization, arguing that metrics computed from instrument signals can be poor proxies that better models or more data cannot fix.
s62daea9a39.why: Teams building closed-loop ML systems should validate that optimization metrics actually reflect the properties they need, since proxy failures are not solved by more data.

sa70b4304ea.title: GraphPass: A Study of Graph Neural Networks for Compiler Pass Selection
sa70b4304ea.description: arXiv:2611.19821v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Compiler pass selection is usually governed by fixed pipelines (-O2, -O3) or hand-written heuristics. We study whether a graph neural network (GNN) over a program's control-flow graph (CFG) can select among a fixed menu of five pass sequences in a single forward pass. GraphPass encodes each CFG with a graph attention (GAT) or graph convolutional (GCN) encoder and classifies it into one of the five sequences. On a synthetic benchmark of 5,000 generated CFGs in five program families, both encoders agree with the benchmark's reference label on about 92% of held-out programs, versus 68.4% for a hand-written rule-based heuristic and 85% for a flat MLP. An edge ablation indicates that this gain comes from per-block processing rather than from CFG
sa70b4304ea.summary: Researchers study GraphPass, a graph neural network that reads a program's control-flow graph to select among five compiler pass sequences in one forward pass.
sa70b4304ea.why: It suggests learned models could replace fixed -O2/-O3 pipelines and hand-written heuristics, though results are on a synthetic benchmark only.

sa936459d4f.title: The Flip Test: Video World Models Fail to Learn the World State
sa936459d4f.description: arXiv:2611.19822v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Video world models promise to predict the future of a scene from its present. Do current models keep this promise? We probe this question counterfactually. When a small change to the present flips the future, such as a box resting a few millimeters before or past a table edge, a model that tracks the state of the world must flip its prediction too. We build FlipTest, a three-level hierarchy of increasingly strict tests over 1,680 initial frames from 10 simulated and 15 real-world tasks. At the base, visual minimal pairs, two nearly identical frames whose true futures differ, test whether predictions change across the boundary; matched controls go further and test whether they change only where the future does; and dense sweeps, the strictes
sa936459d4f.summary: Researchers introduce FlipTest, a hierarchy of counterfactual tests showing that video world models often fail to track the underlying state of a scene.
sa936459d4f.why: Teams relying on video world models for prediction or planning should not assume they track physical state, since these tests show frequent failures.

s1efc8b0f11.title: EfficientSkill: Learning Skills for Token-Efficient Multi-Turn Agents
s1efc8b0f11.description: arXiv:2611.19823v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reflective skill optimizers improve multi-turn LLM agents by revising instructions from failed and successful rollouts, yet accumulating edge-case rules bloats prompts, inflates token use, and pushes agents into long, error-prone loops. We introduce EfficientSkill, a two-step framework that first discovers a reliable skill without token penalties, and then warm-starts accuracy-guarded pruning from that skill to compress instructions, bound agent turns, and offload reusable code into workspace utilities with zero implementation prompt cost. Across four frontier, mid-tier, and open-weight models on MATH-500, ALFWorld, and SpreadsheetBench, EfficientSkill cuts output tokens over unconstrained EvoSkill on 11 of 12 configurations (by up to 80%)
s1efc8b0f11.summary: Researchers present EfficientSkill, a framework that prunes and compresses agent skill instructions to reduce token use and turns in multi-turn LLM agents.
s1efc8b0f11.why: Reducing prompt bloat and agent loop length can cut inference cost and error rates for teams running multi-turn agents.

s489829fb62.title: Bridging the Terminology Gap: A Data-Centric Alignment Framework for Multilingual Translation in Cross-Border Corporation
s489829fb62.description: arXiv:2611.19858v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As globalization accelerates the demand for seamless cross-border enterprise collaboration, multilingual translation remains bottlenecked by insufficient domain-specific terminology, rigid terminology translation, weak instruction-following capabilities, and high inference latency in long-instruction scenarios. To overcome these barriers, we propose Bridging the Terminology Gap (BTG), a data-centric framework. First, BTG mines cross-lingual term alignments from domain documents and leverages LLMs to synthesize terminology-rich parallel corpora. Second, a hybrid filtering strategy combining heuristics and XCOMET scoring ensures high data fidelity. Third, a two-stage training paradigm employs supervised fine-tuning (SFT) for targeted terminol
s489829fb62.summary: Researchers propose BTG, a data-centric framework that mines cross-lingual terminology and synthesizes terminology-rich parallel corpora to improve enterprise translation.
s489829fb62.why: Enterprises with domain jargon across languages may benefit from terminology-focused data synthesis, though the text gives no benchmark results.

sb60df3a98c.title: Local Order Matters: A Lightweight CPU-Trainable CNN for Website Fingerprinting on Defended Tor Traffic
sb60df3a98c.description: arXiv:2611.19864v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Website fingerprinting (WF) attacks let a passive adversary infer which site a Tor user visits from the encrypted cell sequence. On undefended traffic, hand-crafted-feature attacks are already near-ceiling, so deep learning offers only a marginal advantage there. We show that the decisive regime is defended traffic: against the FRONT padding defense, which injects dummy cells that corrupt the volume and count features feature attacks rely on, a compact 95,103-parameter 1-D convolutional network trained on the raw cell-direction sequence, on CPU only, stays robust while three implemented direction-only feature baselines degrade. On the closed-world WFlib FRONT set (95 sites), our model reaches 54.2% top-1 accuracy versus 38.5% for the strong
sb60df3a98c.summary: Researchers show a compact 1-D CNN trained on CPU can perform website fingerprinting against Tor traffic defended by the FRONT padding scheme.
sb60df3a98c.why: It shows defended Tor traffic remains vulnerable to learned attacks, relevant to teams assessing anonymity and traffic-analysis risk.

se50353f462.title: HalluProbe: Exploiting VLM Hallucinations for Backdoor Detection
se50353f462.description: arXiv:2611.19868v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are vulnerable to backdoor attacks introduced through data poisoning, making effective backdoor detection a critical security challenge. In this paper, we uncover a novel connection between VLM hallucinations and backdoor behaviors and exploit this connection for backdoor detection. Our key insight is that poisoned training data induces strong language priors toward the backdoor target token, while such priors are also a major source of hallucinations. This suggests that enhancing hallucinations can expose hidden backdoor-related priors. Specifically, backdoored VLMs tend to hallucinate backdoor target tokens more frequently across diverse inputs, while the hallucinated tokens of clean VLMs are largely random a
se50353f462.summary: Researchers propose HalluProbe, which uses vision-language model hallucinations to expose backdoor behavior induced by data poisoning.
se50353f462.why: Security teams deploying VLMs get a possible detection signal for poisoned backdoors, though the text gives no detection performance figures.

s386cbafd14.title: Let Execution Do the Teaching
s386cbafd14.description: arXiv:2611.19875v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Improving a coding model is a sequence of decisions: find the limiting behavior, create useful practice, and determine which attempts deserve reinforcement. We investigate a practical way to make those decisions increasingly repeatable by grounding feedback in execution. Starting from GLM-4.7-Flash, the work combines whole-file supervised fine-tuning, targeted C++ repair curricula, group-relative reinforcement learning, and verifiers that turn program behavior into structured rewards. Compiler errors and failing tests provide specific contexts for repair practice, while executable checks score the resulting programs. We evaluate the trained models on 26 C++ coding tasks, measuring both initial success and completion after test feedback. The
s386cbafd14.summary: Researchers describe improving the GLM-4.7-Flash coding model using supervised fine-tuning, C++ repair curricula, and reinforcement learning with execution-based rewards.
s386cbafd14.why: Using compiler errors and test results as structured rewards offers a practical recipe for improving code models without relying only on human labels.

sca93143628.title: Large Language Model-based Optimization for Wireless Communication: A Survey
sca93143628.description: arXiv:2611.19876v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The growing complexity and dynamism of modern wireless communication frameworks have made real-time optimization essential for efficient resource allocation. Traditional optimization and machine-learning techniques often struggle with generalization, adaptability, stability, and scalability in heterogeneous, time-varying environments. Large language models (LLMs) have recently emerged as powerful tools capable of reasoning over structured prompts and generating context-aware decisions in real time without domain-specific retraining. This survey provides a comprehensive review of LLM-driven optimization techniques applied to wireless communication problems such as power control, bandwidth allocation, task offloading, and intelligent surface
sca93143628.summary: A survey reviews how large language models are being applied to real-time optimization and resource allocation in wireless communication systems.
sca93143628.why: Engineers in telecom may find it useful as an overview of where LLMs can complement traditional optimization, though it reports no new results.

s9d761bb41f.title: Recovery Gone Too Far: Understanding and Repairing Risky Fallback in LLM Agents
s9d761bb41f.description: arXiv:2611.19886v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents interact with their environments through tools, reading repositories, running builds, and pushing code. When a tool fails with an ordinary error, such as a rate limit or a timeout, the agent can fall back to a substitute tool and still complete the task. However, the same fallback that completes a task in one environment can cross an action boundary in another. For example, after a push is rejected, a forced push in one repository replaces only the agent's own commits, while in a different repository it also removes another author's commits. We call such a fallback a risky fallback. To understand this phenomenon, we conduct an empirical study on 304 scenarios that span eight domains and cover 55 real CVEs.
s9d761bb41f.summary: Researchers study how LLM agents fall back to substitute tools after ordinary errors, showing the same fallback can be safe in one environment and risky in another.
s9d761bb41f.why: Agents with tool fallback can cross action boundaries, such as forced pushes that overwrite others' work, so teams need guardrails tied to context.

s973bc75528.title: AgenticJevNav: Agentic Object Search and Navigation via Event-Driven Verification
s973bc75528.description: arXiv:2611.19912v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agentic navigation must maintain goals and adapt actions from incomplete evidence despite execution failures and delayed inference. We present AgenticJevNav, which links goal-directed planning, evidence memory, event-triggered verification, and bounded execution. The Agent plans from RGB, odometry, memory, and feedback, retaining goal ownership while authorizing a bounded action set. Jev reviews structured evidence after blocked/failed execution or two consecutive low-progress segments. Version, freshness, and once-only checks govern decision application. A single executor and independent RGB reflex constrain motion. Goal revisions revoke obsolete requests and actions before replanning. Across six simulated task families, AgenticJevNav achi
s973bc75528.summary: Researchers present AgenticJevNav, an agentic navigation system that triggers event-driven verification after failed actions or repeated low-progress segments.
s973bc75528.why: It illustrates bounded action sets and verification triggers for embodied agents, a pattern relevant to teams building reliable autonomous navigation.

sbad308418d.title: The Vocabulary Tax: Safely Trimming Unused Tokens from LLMs for On-Device Use
sbad308418d.description: arXiv:2611.19913v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Open large language models (LLMs) and speech models ship vocabularies of up to 262k tokens, and every user downloads the tables those tokens index (the input embedding, an untied output head and, in recent on-device models, per-layer embeddings), whatever languages they need. We call the bytes in rows a deployment never uses the vocabulary tax and measure it, without downloading weights, for 1,244 generative and speech-recognition models on the Hugging Face Hub. For a Thai and English deployment it is a median 4.4% of model bytes below 0.5B parameters and 2.1% above 8B, and 1.93 GB in Gemma 4 E2B: it falls hardest on the small models that edge devices run. Keeping only the rows of the deployment's writing systems is exact. Keeping the token
sbad308418d.summary: Researchers quantify unused vocabulary rows in 1,244 open models on Hugging Face and propose safely trimming them to reduce on-device model size.
sbad308418d.why: Teams shipping models on-device could cut download size substantially by removing vocabulary rows their deployment never uses.

s5c828de2d5.title: Learning When to Continue and When to Stop: Termination-Aware OPSD
s5c828de2d5.description: arXiv:2611.19925v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) improves language model reasoning by distilling from a frozen teacher initialized identically to the student and conditioned on privileged information. However, we identify an underexplored termination mismatch in OPSD: the student fails to reliably learn when to continue and when to stop. This mismatch manifests in two opposing failure modes-premature termination, where reasoning stops before sufficient progress is made, and repetition-driven over-generation, where the model continues generating after reasoning has stalled. Our analysis shows that the teacher-student discrepancy on EOS grows during OPSD training, while length-capped trajectories are frequently dominated by unproductive repetition. To addr
s5c828de2d5.summary: Researchers identify a termination mismatch in on-policy self-distillation, where students stop reasoning too early or over-generate, and propose a termination-aware fix.
s5c828de2d5.why: Reasoning models that stop prematurely or repeat endlessly waste compute or give wrong answers, so stopping behavior is a practical training concern.

s149e25e587.title: Equal Dose, Different Coverage:Tracing Rate and Duration in Image Editing
s149e25e587.description: arXiv:2611.19955v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Benchmarks for scientific image editing test whether a model draws the outcome of a described process, leaving open which representations carry its errors and whether correcting them yields the right quantity. We study this question with an airbrush of fixed deposition profile, under which exchanging rate and duration preserves the dose and should preserve the endpoint, yet changes the edited coverage. Matched-norm activation patches across text positions and denoising stages show that, in distilled FLUX with Chinese prompts, representations at unchanged text positions (context) carry this discrepancy: early context transfers 3.51 of the 3.98 percentage-point (pp) signed route difference, against 0.09 pp for equal-norm updates at the two ch
s149e25e587.summary: Researchers find that in distilled FLUX with Chinese prompts, errors in scientific image editing stem from representations of rate and duration, not just the endpoint.
s149e25e587.why: It highlights that correct final outputs can hide wrong internal dynamics, relevant to teams debugging or steering image-editing models.

se6a42326cb.title: Value and Policy Calibration from Execution Feedback for Socially Compatible Driving
se6a42326cb.description: arXiv:2611.19969v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Autonomous vehicle (AV) decisions at intersections affect the delay, braking, and motion smoothness of surrounding human-driven vehicles (HDVs). Learning socially compatible behavior requires connecting imagined interaction outcomes with feedback from executed actions. We propose a world-model reinforcement learning framework combines imagined policy improvement with direct value and policy calibration from finalized interactions, balancing AV progress with HDV interaction burden. An interaction-aware latent model supports imagination, while off-policy correction and replay updates enable observed rewards and transitions to supervise both the critic and actor. Simulation experiments at an unsignalized intersection achieve a 100% success and
se6a42326cb.summary: Researchers propose a world-model reinforcement learning framework that calibrates value and policy from executed interactions so autonomous vehicles balance progress with burden on human drivers at intersections.
se6a42326cb.why: Shows how learning from real execution feedback, not just imagined rollouts, may help AV planners reduce disruption to surrounding human drivers.

s070ace2d76.title: Federated Dataset Simulation: Inducing Label-Free Heterogeneity Across Tasks
s070ace2d76.description: arXiv:2611.19975v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Federated Learning enables collaborative model training across decentralized clients without sharing raw data. While the field has seen rapid growth, the datasets underpinning FL evaluation have not kept pace: real federated datasets remain scarce, and most studies rely on small-scale centralized classification datasets partitioned via Dirichlet label skew, a one-dimensional proxy for the multi-dimensional heterogeneity present in real federations. Moreover, label-based partitioning is by construction inapplicable to non-classification tasks such as segmentation and detection, for which no principled simulation method exists. We cast the conversion of centralized datasets into federated benchmarks as the task of Federated Dataset Simulation
s070ace2d76.summary: Researchers introduce a method to simulate federated datasets with label-free heterogeneity, aiming to replace label-skew partitioning that does not apply to non-classification tasks.
s070ace2d76.why: Gives FL engineers a more realistic way to evaluate federated systems beyond Dirichlet label-skew splits, including for non-classification tasks.

s88f6283efe.title: CreaTrace: Video Creative Plagiarism Detection and Evidence Tracing
s88f6283efe.description: arXiv:2611.19976v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Video creative plagiarism refers to the unauthorized reproduction of creative ideas across videos despite substantial differences in visual appearance, posing a new challenge to video copyright protection. However, existing video copy detection methods primarily focus on visual content similarity, struggling to capture abstract creative that are entangled with specific visual realizations. To address this issue, we introduce a novel task, named Video Creative Plagiarism Detection (VCPD), and propose an iterative creative evidence tracing framework, termed CreaTrace, to verify creative similarity and accurately localize the corresponding evidence segments. Specifically, we design a Multimodal Semantic Event Segmentation strategy to divide si
s88f6283efe.summary: Researchers define Video Creative Plagiarism Detection, a task for finding reused creative ideas across videos that differ visually, and propose an iterative evidence-tracing framework.
s88f6283efe.why: Highlights that visual copy detection misses idea-level copying, relevant to teams building video copyright or content-moderation tooling.

sabf78fa32d.title: Morphology-Decoupled Segmentation for Multiple Tunnel Defects Under Complex Environments
sabf78fa32d.description: arXiv:2611.19981v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Automated tunnel-lining inspection must segment different defect geometries: cracks are thin, elongated, and connectivity-sensitive, whereas leakage, lining falling off, and segment damage are spatially extensive and context-dependent. Existing approaches generally apply a common decoder across defect classes or introduce boundary, topology, and directional mechanisms as isolated enhancements. This paper introduces Morphology-Decoupled Segmentation (MDS), in which defect morphology becomes the organising principle for feature routing, decoding, and interaction. A supervised routing module partitions multiscale encoder features into complementary linear and areal streams. The linear stream employs Deformable Strip Attention with image-condit
sabf78fa32d.summary: Researchers propose Morphology-Decoupled Segmentation, which routes features and decoding by defect shape to segment cracks and other tunnel-lining defects in complex environments.

s10b7da688d.title: What Matters for Cross-Modal Alignment
s10b7da688d.description: arXiv:2611.20000v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis posits that models trained on different modalities converge toward a shared representation. Related work aligns frozen image and text encoders on natural images without paired data. We test zero-pair alignment on five datasets across four modalities: natural images, environmental audio, chest radiographs, and 3D computed tomography (CT). It succeeds only on COCO and fails on the other four. We analyze the failures and find that alignment must first locate the subspace where the modalities co-vary and then orient the mapping within it. Consistent with previous studies, medical imaging is the hardest case: its shared subspace carries the smallest fraction of the variance. When this fraction is small, ali
s10b7da688d.summary: Researchers test zero-pair alignment of frozen encoders across five datasets and four modalities, finding it succeeds only on COCO natural images and fails on audio, radiographs, and CT.
s10b7da688d.why: Suggests cross-modal alignment without paired data does not generalize beyond natural images, a caution for teams assuming it transfers to medical or audio domains.

sb52d351a52.title: The novelty exposed: ablation, reproducibility and transparency in 40 technical reports of open-weight large language models (LLMs)
sb52d351a52.description: arXiv:2611.20003v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In 2025 alone, 48 new large language model (LLM) architectures were added to the Hugging Face transformers library, and many of them arrive with a technical report that presents the model as new. What is actually new in these models, and is it tested? We put this question to LLM technical reports. We look at three things: what the reference code shows about how new open-weight architectures differ from earlier ones; what 40 randomly sampled technical reports claim as new and whether they support it with ablation studies; and what they disclose for reproducibility and transparency. In the library, 39 of the 48 architectures added in 2025 take at least two of their three core blocks from another model, most often Llama, although part of this
sb52d351a52.summary: A study of 40 sampled open-weight LLM technical reports examines whether claimed architectural novelties are supported by ablation studies and what reproducibility details are disclosed.
sb52d351a52.why: Helps engineers judge how much weight to give novelty claims in open-weight model reports, given how many new architectures appear each year.

s8c6ede389b.title: ReactBench-AD: Do Driving VLAs and World-Action Models React to Imminent Hazards in Their Path?
s8c6ede389b.description: arXiv:2611.20011v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) and World-Action Models (WAMs) have emerged in autonomous driving with the promise of strong generalization to long-tail scenarios. Although these models achieve state-of-the-art results on autonomous driving benchmarks, most existing benchmarks are dominated by nominal scenarios and therefore cannot test this promise. To test one such long-tail capability that is critical for safety, we introduce ReactBench-AD, a benchmark that measures how driving models react to objects that appear in the ego vehicle's path. Built on real NAVSIM and PhysicalAI-Autonomous-Vehicles scenes, ReactBench-AD composites a crossing pedestrian, a standing pedestrian, or a stationary car consistently across all camera views and
s8c6ede389b.summary: Researchers introduce ReactBench-AD, a benchmark testing whether driving VLA and world-action models react to imminent hazards appearing in the ego vehicle's path.
s8c6ede389b.why: Targets long-tail safety behavior that nominal driving benchmarks miss, useful for teams evaluating autonomous driving models before deployment.

s8c6821a111.title: D'BEAST: Logged Bad Experiences as Explanation for Autonomous Driving Agents
s8c6821a111.description: arXiv:2611.20019v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reinforcement learning agents learn from mistakes, yet their decisions can be difficult to trace back to those experiences. We investigate whether a tabular agent's decisions can be explained by its bad experiences, defined as the training transitions associated with safety or task events. A fixed training log is replayed from the same initial Q-table under three conditions. FULL retains all updates, SKIP omits bad-experience updates, and NEUTRALIZE retains those updates without their event penalties. We illustrate the method on six classic Markov decision processes and evaluate it in closed-loop driving in CARLA. On the full driving task, FULL reached the goal from 33 of 40 test starts, whereas SKIP and NEUTRALIZE reached it from none, ind
s8c6821a111.summary: Researchers present D'BEAST, which replays a tabular RL training log under three conditions to test whether agent decisions can be explained by logged bad experiences.
s8c6821a111.why: Offers a replay-based method for tracing RL agent decisions to safety-relevant training events, relevant to explainability work in autonomous driving.

sc1c834b248.title: Improving fine-grained expressivity of graph neural networks
sc1c834b248.description: arXiv:2611.20020v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This thesis investigates the expressive power of neural networks for structured data, focusing on graph neural networks and symmetry-aware architectures. We present four main contributions.
