s762df95e73.description: arXiv:2611.22456v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Omnimodal large language models (Omni-LLMs) integrate audio, video, and text for multimodal reasoning, yet remain vulnerable to cross-modal hallucinations, where one modality improperly influences predictions about another. Existing training-free decoding methods mitigate these errors through modality perturbation or relevance-based weighting. However, due to interference from irrelevant modality cues during fusion and difficulty detecting shared errors, these methods may suppress correct unimodal predictions and allow erroneous consensus to persist. To address these limitations, we propose Provenance-Aware Consensus Decoding (PACD), a training-free framework for mitigating cross-modal hallucinations. PACD comprises two complementary paths ba
s762df95e73.summary: Researchers propose PACD, a training-free decoding method to reduce cross-modal hallucinations in omnimodal LLMs that process audio, video, and text.
s762df95e73.why: Engineers deploying multimodal models can consider training-free decoding changes to reduce hallucinations caused by one modality influencing another.

se33d1e8c82.title: From Ideal to Real: Integrating Language Models into Smart Home for Human-Centric IoT Safety and Security Fuzzing
se33d1e8c82.description: arXiv:2611.22457v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Integrating IoT devices into household systems offers enhanced control over living environments. However, as these devices become pervasive in critical sectors such as healthcare, transportation, and home automation, they expose inter-rule vulnerabilities that may lead to privacy breaches, data theft, and physical harm. Traditional fuzz testing methods, which often operate in simulated environments assuming ideal human decisions, fail to account for the complexities of human interactions that can influence device operations in smart homes, potentially leading to unforeseen consequences. To reveal the impact of real human decisions and discover unexpected inter-rule vulnerabilities, we introduce an enhanced version of IoT Fuzz for smart homes
se33d1e8c82.summary: Researchers integrate language models into smart home fuzzing to model human interactions when testing IoT safety and security vulnerabilities.
se33d1e8c82.why: Testing IoT rules under realistic human behavior may reveal vulnerabilities that ideal-human simulations miss, affecting smart home security teams.

s2a8e1f78d7.title: RehearsalBench: Can AI Predict What Happens When You Change a Company?
s2a8e1f78d7.description: arXiv:2611.22480v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Organizations increasingly ask AI systems what will happen if they change how they operate: which work to automate, which team to resize, what a voice agent will do to waiting times. We introduce RehearsalBench, a benchmark that measures whether AI models can diagnose an operation, choose an intervention, and forecast its consequences. Each model is placed in a simulated bank contact center fitted to real call-level records, sees only what a manager would see, and submits a plan and forecasts that are then played out across 200 seeded futures and three plausible versions of the organization. Decisions are scored in dollars at the stakeholders' stated valuations; forecasts are scored on the effect of each change relative to doing nothing. Ten
s2a8e1f78d7.summary: Researchers introduce RehearsalBench, testing whether AI models can diagnose a simulated bank contact center, choose interventions, and forecast outcomes across 200 seeded futures.
s2a8e1f78d7.why: It gives leaders a way to assess whether AI can reliably forecast the operational effects of process or staffing changes before deployment.

s2d6ad33a7d.title: SciWorkBench: A Benchmark for Real Scientific Workflows
s2d6ad33a7d.description: arXiv:2611.22490v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language models are increasingly being used as agents capable of planning and executing projects, as well as refining their actions through feedback. This shift raises a question: can current agents complete projects like real scientists? To examine this question, we introduce SciWorkBench, a benchmark for evaluating agents' abilities on real science tasks across biology, chemistry, materials science, and physics. SciWorkBench is built from peer-reviewed literature or expert-contributed research scenarios. We also propose a unified scientific analysis framework validated by domain experts, which can categorize most tasks in SciWorkBench. Each task covers one or more stages of this framework. We evaluate up-to-date models within the Claude Cod
s2d6ad33a7d.summary: Researchers introduce SciWorkBench, a benchmark evaluating language model agents on real scientific workflows across biology, chemistry, materials science, and physics.
s2d6ad33a7d.why: It provides a realistic test of whether agents can complete multi-step scientific projects, informing expectations for research-automation tools.

s1fc5979abd.title: DARWIN: a Geospatial Foundation Model for Marine Intelligence
s1fc5979abd.description: arXiv:2611.22496v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present DARWIN, a geospatial foundation model for marine intelligence. Recent Earth-observation foundation models have concentrated on terrestrial domains. The marine realm poses distinct challenges: missingness, multi-modal physical and biogeochemical variables, sparse labels, and dynamics that are transient, multi-scale, and non stationary over time. DARWIN adapts a masked-autoencoder backbone to these properties through missingness-aware encoding, expanded spatial and temporal masking, and Fourier-style positional embeddings, and is pretrained on 26 years of global Copernicus reanalysis together with GEBCO bathymetry. On predicting chlorophyll-a, the pretrained backbone attains the lowest monthly relative error in every month of 2022, o
s1fc5979abd.summary: Researchers present DARWIN, a geospatial foundation model for marine intelligence that handles missing, multimodal, and sparsely labeled ocean observation data.

s1bd16ce822.title: Towards Data-Efficient, Real-Time World Models
s1bd16ce822.description: arXiv:2611.22497v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: State-of-the-art world models have been used to produce sequences of gameplay that accord with provided user-input actions. However, high quality, consistent gameplay generation often comes at the cost of inference speed, making real-time interactive play and ideation challenging. The substantial quantities of data used to train state-of-the-art models have also made custom training of these models appear impractical, limiting many of their potential uses in creative fields. In this work we demonstrate a major step towards efficient world models: achieving both fast high-quality inference, and improved data efficiency. This is done by replacing the next-token prediction paradigm with a two-stage discrete diffusion-based approach, introducing
s1bd16ce822.summary: Researchers report progress toward data-efficient, real-time world models that generate interactive gameplay from user actions with lower inference cost and training data.
s1bd16ce822.why: Faster, cheaper-to-train world models could make custom interactive generation practical for creative and product teams.

s63a2866ec2.title: LMLineage: Content Lineage and Context Governance for LLM Agents
s63a2866ec2.description: arXiv:2611.22511v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interpretability for AI agents should not be confined to understanding the model's internal weights. It must also cover the agent's reasoning and decision-making process over multi-source context. We present LMLineage, an out-of-band system that attributes every output sentence of an agent session to its supporting input spans with calibrated confidences, without requiring white-box access to the model or any additional inference passes. On top of the lineage metadata, we build concept-drift micro compaction: instead of waiting for the context-length limit and summarizing everything, the system detects when previously used input documents have stopped being referenced ("drifted") and surgically compacts only those, preserving user instruction
s63a2866ec2.summary: LMLineage is an out-of-band system that attributes each agent output sentence to supporting input spans with calibrated confidences, without white-box access or extra inference passes.
s63a2866ec2.why: Gives teams traceability over which context drove agent outputs, useful for auditing and governing multi-source context in agent deployments.

sfe3c7edfa9.title: When Agent Skills Go Stale: Runtime Behavior and Selective Maintenance in Evolving Environments
sfe3c7edfa9.description: arXiv:2611.22525v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent skills use past experience and current observations to guide decisions and actions on related tasks. This experience is retained in skill state, whose reuse can amortize inference-time reasoning and environment interaction. When environment changes, parts of this state can become outdated while others remain useful. Across four task settings and two models, we compare skill reuse before and after environment changes. Previously beneficial skills can reduce task performance by over 10 percentage points or increase execution cost by nearly 40% relative to no skill. Task success can also remain unchanged while execution savings decline. These effects depend on which environment-specific details become outdated and the agent's ability to co
sfe3c7edfa9.summary: A study finds that agent skills reused after environment changes can become outdated, reducing task performance by over 10 points or raising execution cost by nearly 40 percent.
sfe3c7edfa9.why: Reused agent memory can silently degrade in changing environments, so teams need selective maintenance of stored skills.

seb21e00272.title: CADMAGEDDON: High-Fidelity CAD Reconstruction with Local Inference
seb21e00272.description: arXiv:2611.22563v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: CAD practitioners often work with proprietary parts that they are unwilling to share with external services. For individuals and small companies, bringing this work in-house also requires computational resources they can afford. We introduce CADMAGEDDON, an open-source agent that reconstructs editable CAD from meshes and can run locally on single-GPU systems and current-generation laptops. The method decomposes this complex task into a chain of simple visual decisions about what to construct and what to correct. Geometric tools support precise construction, allowing the agent to focus on visual reasoning. Using the mid-sized Qwen3.8-27B model, CADMAGEDDON outperforms prior approaches, including systems based on frontier models, in reconstruct
seb21e00272.summary: CADMAGEDDON is an open-source agent that reconstructs editable CAD models from meshes and runs locally on single-GPU systems and current laptops.
seb21e00272.why: Offers a way to convert meshes to editable CAD without sending proprietary parts to external services.

sea84dcd2d2.title: MillBill: A Machining Agent with Geometric Feedback
sea84dcd2d2.description: arXiv:2611.22565v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Turning a CAD model into a machining program requires both process knowledge and geometric precision. Language models can generate such workflows by writing geometry and toolpath code for each part, but this makes numerical execution part of the model's task. We introduce MillBill, an agent that separates machining decisions from their geometric execution and verification. Given a boundary-representation part, stock, and material, a locally hosted, mid-sized open model proposes operations and cutting parameters for indexed three-axis machining. A geometric harness generates toolpaths, simulates material removal, and returns feedback for plan refinement. Setup planning accounts for what the available cutters can physically reach, rather than v
sea84dcd2d2.summary: MillBill is an agent that separates machining decisions from geometric execution, using a locally hosted mid-sized open model to propose operations for three-axis machining.
sea84dcd2d2.why: Shows a pattern of keeping numerical geometry out of the LLM's task, relevant to building reliable domain agents.

sb03ba91b58.title: PACT: Plan-Action Consistency Training by Preserving Correct Plans and Repairing Actions in GUI Agents
sb03ba91b58.description: arXiv:2611.22591v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: GUI agents can formulate a correct immediate plan in their reasoning yet emit an action that fails to execute it, creating an execution gap. This recurring mismatch undermines reliable task completion, as a single execution error can derail a multi-step workflow. In outcome-supervised reinforcement learning, broadcasting a negative response-level advantage across all generated tokens risks penalizing valid planning together with erroneous execution. To address this credit-assignment conflict, we introduce PACT (Plan-Action Consistency Training), a training framework that combines reference-aligned plan protection and plan-aligned action repair without altering the original scalar action reward. Using annotated reference actions to identify ex
sb03ba91b58.summary: PACT is a reinforcement learning training method for GUI agents that preserves correct plans and repairs incorrect actions by changing how negative rewards are assigned.
sb03ba91b58.why: Targets a common failure where agents plan correctly but execute wrong actions, which can derail multi-step workflows.

see96b00f42.title: COTTI: Contrastive Training and Time-Aware Inference for Robust Industrial Recommendation under Promotional Drift
see96b00f42.description: arXiv:2611.22597v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Promotional events shift traffic composition, purchase behavior, and the scale of conversion probabilities on different time horizons. We present \textbf{COTTI} (\textbf{CO}ntrastive \textbf{T}raining and \textbf{T}ime-aware \textbf{I}nference), an industrial recommendation framework that separates historical representation learning from event-time score adjustment. Cross-Period Contrastive Alignment (CPC) regularizes paired histories of the same user with adaptive consistency weights. Active Re-weighting (RW) controls the influence of promotional examples through historical-interest distance. Adaptive Boundary Alignment (ABA) combines stochastic prediction variability with a temporal event kernel to adjust logits while keeping predictor para
see96b00f42.summary: COTTI is an industrial recommendation framework that uses contrastive training and time-aware inference to handle shifts in traffic and purchase behavior during promotional events.
see96b00f42.why: Addresses drift in production recommenders during promotions, a practical problem for teams running large-scale ranking systems.

sc0b6243ba1.title: Simplicity Goes Far: Auditing Prompt Optimizers with Demonstration-Conditioned Prompt Search
sc0b6243ba1.description: arXiv:2611.22605v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automatic prompt optimization is growing more elaborate. Recent methods stack policy-gradient updates, trace reflection, and evolutionary search. These methods share a generate-and-select step; without controlling for it, reported gains may conflate the contributions of optimizer mechanisms and larger sampling budgets. We isolate this step as Demonstration-Conditioned Prompt Search (DCPS), repurposing the Automatic Prompt Engineer (APE) recipe as a mechanism-attribution control: it freezes the generator, conditions it on randomly sampled demonstrations, scores candidates on validation data, and keeps the best---no learned update, reflection, or evolution. Across two optimizer families, DCPS replaces Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) in Stabl
sc0b6243ba1.summary: The paper introduces Demonstration-Conditioned Prompt Search, a control that isolates the generate-and-select step to test whether reported prompt optimizer gains come from their mechanisms or larger sampling budgets.
sc0b6243ba1.why: Suggests that elaborate prompt optimizers may need controlled baselines before their reported gains are trusted.

s77c9e89884.title: EvoSkill-S1: Evolving Reusable Skills with Genetic-Inspired Operators
s77c9e89884.description: arXiv:2611.22610v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reusable skills allow language-model agents to accumulate and reuse problem-solving experience. However, most existing methods improve a skill bank only indirectly through rollout-driven accumulation and heuristic reflection, often resulting in shallow and weakly controlled updates. We present EvoSkill-S1, an RL-driven framework that instead treats reusable skills themselves as the direct objects of evolution. Given hard-negative failures, EvoSkill-S1 selects parent skills and transforms them into candidate child skills through five genetic-inspired operators: revision, cross-revision, mutation, dual-reflection, and crossover. Downstream task rewards train the skill evolver to generate more effective child skills, while evaluator-guided write
s77c9e89884.summary: EvoSkill-S1 is a reinforcement learning framework that evolves reusable agent skills directly, using five genetic-inspired operators on parent skills to create child skills.
s77c9e89884.why: Proposes a more controlled way to improve agent skill banks than indirect rollout-driven accumulation.

s4b405df1a4.title: DAQ: Decision-Aligned Post-Training Quantization for Spiking Transformers
s4b405df1a4.description: arXiv:2611.22611v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spiking transformers combine attention-based representation learning with sparse spike communication, yet their weights and membrane variables still incur substantial storage and computation overhead. Post-training quantization (PTQ) offers a practical way to reduce these overheads, but preserving neuronal firing under weight and membrane quantization remains challenging. In this paper, we propose Decision-Aligned Post-Training Quantization (DAQ), a method that calibrates the quantizers to align neuronal firing decisions with those of a floating-point reference. We analyze how errors from these quantizers affect firing at decision boundaries and how they propagate over time steps in recurrent neurons. Based on this analysis, we formulate an o
s4b405df1a4.summary: DAQ is a post-training quantization method for spiking transformers that calibrates quantizers to align neuronal firing decisions with a floating-point model.
s4b405df1a4.why: Offers a route to cheaper spiking transformer inference, though the text gives limited detail on practical gains.

s2e3dfcacc6.title: Right Diagnosis, Unsafe Route: Auditing Clinical AI Decision Trajectories and Corrective Oversight for Validity and Potential Harm
s2e3dfcacc6.description: arXiv:2611.22612v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A clinical AI system can reach a correct final diagnosis through intermediate decisions that could have harmed the patient, and can repair an error while introducing new risks. Most evaluations score final diagnoses; even stepwise benchmarks, which release a case's evidence over time, score whether systems reach the right diagnosis or gather the right information, not whether the decisions a patient passes through are safe. We make patient safety the target of stepwise evaluation. A trajectory audit replays real admissions checkpoint by checkpoint, lets each system decide with only the evidence released so far, and rates every test, treatment and disposition for its potential harm to the patient and, separately, for clinical validity, against
s2e3dfcacc6.summary: The paper proposes a trajectory audit that replays real admissions checkpoint by checkpoint to judge whether clinical AI intermediate decisions are safe, not just whether final diagnoses are correct.
s2e3dfcacc6.why: Shows that correct final answers can hide unsafe intermediate steps, a key evaluation concern for any high-stakes AI system.

s9262a4fb12.title: EDA: Observe, Verify, and Assess for Evidence-Grounded Multimodal Depression Analysis
s9262a4fb12.description: arXiv:2611.22648v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing multimodal depression assessment methods often summarize long recordings into global behavioral descriptions. This leaves the source and decision relevance of individual observations difficult to inspect. We propose EDA, an evidence-grounded framework organized around Observe, Verify, and Assess. In Observe, literature-informed acoustic and visual cues are localized into source-linked Evidence Records with temporal intervals and behavioral measurements. In Verify, frozen multimodal agents examine whether the cited media support each observation. The simplified Support admission policy retains positively verified records and their review grounds. In Assess, statistical descriptors and temporal events support reference-based behavioral
s9262a4fb12.summary: EDA is an evidence-grounded framework for multimodal depression analysis that links observations to source-linked evidence records and verifies them with frozen multimodal agents.
s9262a4fb12.why: Demonstrates an approach to making AI assessments inspectable by tying each observation to cited media evidence.

s23e62fb7df.title: The Between-Round Decision in Autonomous Research: An LLM Controller That Reads the Whole Trajectory
s23e62fb7df.description: arXiv:2611.22661v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Executing an idea often changes how promising it looks, so the next step in autonomous research should rest on results, not on proposals. After each round of experiments, the system must decide whether to refine the best solution or start a new direction, which solution to build from, and what goal to set. We call this the between-round decision. Existing systems wrap it in machinery such as rules, scores, search trees, and schedules; where an LLM makes it, what the LLM needs to read is left open. We ask whether an LLM can make this decision from accumulated evidence, without a search structure around it, and how much of that evidence it needs to read. We present BRED (Between-Round Evidence-based Decision), an LLM-based controller that maint
s23e62fb7df.summary: The paper studies whether an LLM can make the between-round decision in autonomous research by reading the whole experiment trajectory rather than relying on rules or scores.
s23e62fb7df.why: Explores how LLM controllers could steer autonomous experimentation, though the text gives limited concrete results.

sefbc77fb5c.title: Remembered as Brief: Stored Preferences SilentlyRemove Decision-Critical Information
sefbc77fb5c.description: arXiv:2611.22697v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: People increasingly learn what they need for decisions about health, money, law and safety from AI assistants, and what an assistant leaves out the user never sees. An answer with a warning removed can be true in every sentence, so fact-checks pass it, and an assistant with memory applies a preference stored once to later questions the user never had in mind. We introduce \bench{}, an Inspect benchmark of 100 everyday decisions across 25 domains in which only the assistant's memory of the user varies: the user states a belief, the model infers it from a remark, or a web page the user asked to summarise plants it. Testing five models, we find three effects. First, after summarising a page with one line addressed to AI assistants, Gemini 2.5 Fl
sefbc77fb5c.summary: A benchmark called Inspect tests how stored user preferences in AI assistant memory can silently remove decision-critical information from answers that remain factually true.
sefbc77fb5c.why: Highlights that memory features can omit key warnings while passing fact-checks, a risk for assistants with persistent user memory.

s1686683ae3.title: Proximal Targets: Training Looped Refiners on Problems with Many Correct Answers
s1686683ae3.description: arXiv:2611.22737v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Looped refiners such as HRM and TRM apply one small network repeatedly to a draft answer, and deep supervision trains every pass toward one stored answer per puzzle. We prove that when a puzzle has many correct answers this target sets a loss floor that no model capacity removes, and that the loss-minimising pass blends the answers into an invalid grid. We propose the proximal target: train each pass toward the correct answer nearest to its own input, found by scanning a list of answers, by a search solver started at the draft, or within a band of quality set by a knob; correct answers become fixed points, and a pass only has to make fewer errors than its input has for the loop to converge, which its training loss bounds. With the same 1.7M-p
s1686683ae3.summary: The paper proves that training looped refiners on puzzles with many correct answers toward one stored answer sets an unremovable loss floor, and proposes proximal targets as a fix.
s1686683ae3.why: Identifies a training flaw in recursive reasoning models that could mislead training on tasks with multiple valid outputs.

s5590d7a40e.title: Can Activation Steering Substitute for Prompt-Based Affective Priming in LLM Digital Twins?
s5590d7a40e.description: arXiv:2611.22738v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Affective priming -- asking participants to write about a recalled event, such as a time they felt grateful or lacked control, and then measuring the induced state and its spillover onto related judgments -- is a standard way to manipulate emotion in the social sciences, and it also shifts the responses of LLM-based digital twins. The writing task, however, requires generating a full text. We test whether activation steering can replace it. Using Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on 100 personas in two domains (gratitude, lack of control), we compare a real-prompt path replicating the original Twin-2K-500 Mega Study (J2) with an injection path that skips the writing and adds a mean-difference direction, extracted from human writing, to the residual strea
s5590d7a40e.summary: The study tests whether activation steering can replace prompt-based affective priming writing tasks for Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct digital twins across 100 personas in two emotion domains.
s5590d7a40e.why: Explores a cheaper way to manipulate LLM persona emotion, relevant to researchers using synthetic respondents, though results are not stated in the text.

s705b82f188.title: CrossEnv: Synthesizing Verifiable Cross-Environment Tasks for Long-Horizon Agent Training
s705b82f188.description: arXiv:2611.22777v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Executable synthetic environments provide scalable training tasks and verifiable feedback for long-horizon agents. Existing environment synthesis methods primarily generate tasks within individual environments. However, these tasks do not adequately capture real-world interactions across services, where actions in one service depend on information obtained from another. Synthesizing such tasks is challenging because data generated across environments must remain consistent to support executable and verifiable interactions. To address this challenge, we introduce CrossEnv, a framework that uses an entity-tool graph to identify connections between environments and aligns task-specific data to synthesize executable, verifiable cross-environment
s705b82f188.summary: Researchers propose CrossEnv, a method for synthesizing verifiable tasks that span multiple services, to train long-horizon agents.
s705b82f188.why: Cross-service tasks with verifiable feedback could make agent training closer to real multi-tool workflows, though the abstract gives few results.

s78e420258c.title: A Full-Ledger Counterfactual Audit of Adaptive Reasoning
s78e420258c.description: arXiv:2611.22778v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adaptive reasoning must decide whether to answer now or spend more compute. Predicting that the current answer is wrong does not establish whether further reasoning will improve it. We introduce the Full-Ledger Counterfactual Value Audit (FLCVA), which compares an immediate answer with four fixed-length continuations from the same frozen prefix under one answer procedure and accounts for the cost of every signal used by a policy. On GSM8K and MATH-500, a random 256-token continuation recovers a wrong answer in 26.6% of Qwen3-8B cases and 18.9% of DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B cases, while damaging a correct answer in 1.4% and 1.9%. Correctness labels from independently sampled continuations predict a separate continuation's outcome in both prim
s78e420258c.summary: Researchers introduce FLCVA, an audit that compares immediate answers with fixed-length continuations to test whether further reasoning improves adaptive reasoning, evaluated on GSM8K and MATH-500.
s78e420258c.why: It offers a way to measure whether extra inference compute actually fixes wrong answers, relevant to cost-aware reasoning policies.

see14612229.title: Pluggable Subband-Decoupled Fusion and Unlabeled Capture Prototype Calibration: Bridging High-SNR Null-Subcarrier Regrowth and Low-SNR Coherent Preambles for Cross-Domain IoT RF Fingerprinting
see14612229.description: arXiv:2611.22812v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Zero-overhead physical-layer authentication at edge wireless access points (APs) is vital for securing resource-constrained Internet of Things (IoT) transceivers against credential cloning, yet cross-domain IEEE 802.11a/g radio frequency fingerprint identification (RFFI) faces an acute signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) crossover. Power-amplifier spectral regrowth on unpopulated null subcarriers resists indoor multipath at high SNR but decays quadratically below the thermal noise floor, whereas populated active in-band preambles survive low SNR yet degrade under severe multipath, causing static fusion to lose up to 44.7 percentage points (pp). To our knowledge, we propose the first RFFI framework that dynamically modulates active in-band waveforms a
see14612229.summary: Researchers propose a calibration approach for cross-domain IoT RF fingerprinting on IEEE 802.11a/g devices, bridging high- and low-SNR signal features.
see14612229.why: Helps edge access points authenticate IoT devices without added overhead, though the abstract is limited to a niche wireless security setting.

sd2c27c4a58.title: OICycle: Observe, Infer, and Intervene Cycle for Belief-State Learning in Longitudinal Clinical Decision Making
sd2c27c4a58.description: arXiv:2611.22826v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Clinical care is a closed loop: clinicians observe partial evidence, infer the patient's state, and intervene, and each intervention determines what is observed next. This makes clinical decision making a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP), in which a belief over a latent patient state must be updated from irregular, multimodal, and incomplete records. Yet most deep clinical models predict from a single snapshot or from coarsely aggregated history, while POMDP-based clinical methods need hand-specified discrete state spaces and transition models that real electronic health records cannot supply. We introduce OICycle (Observe, Infer, and Intervene Cycle), which learns a stochastic belief state directly from retrospective traj
sd2c27c4a58.summary: Researchers present OICycle, a model that updates belief states over latent patient conditions from irregular clinical records to support longitudinal decision making.
sd2c27c4a58.why: Shows an approach to modeling clinical decisions as partially observable processes, though the abstract gives no deployment or outcome details.

sd72e1cb133.title: Synergizing Evidence Retrieval and Utilization for Self-Improving Multimodal Scientific Document Reasoning
sd72e1cb133.description: arXiv:2611.22837v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scientific document reasoning requires an agent to acquire and integrate evidence distributed across text, figures, and tables. Retrieval can identify relevant sources while missing complementary support, and answer-level feedback alone does not reveal whether an error stems from evidence acquisition or evidence use. We present an agentic Retriever--Perceiver--Reasoner framework for multimodal scientific document reasoning. The Retriever sequentially selects source-aligned evidence under a context budget. Given the selected evidence and question, the Perceiver constructs a question-conditioned latent ontology, an implicit organization of multimodal evidence in a shared continuous space. The Reasoner combines this latent guidance with the orig
sd72e1cb133.summary: Researchers present an agentic Retriever-Perceiver-Reasoner framework that retrieves evidence across text, figures and tables for multimodal scientific document reasoning and self-improvement.
sd72e1cb133.why: Separating evidence retrieval from evidence use helps diagnose where multimodal agent errors originate, a useful pattern for document QA systems.

s9616fe9747.title: Verifying Agents in Rubric-Graded Environments
s9616fe9747.description: arXiv:2611.22841v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As AI agents take on increasingly open-ended and complex tasks, verifying their outputs has proven to be difficult. Rubric-graded agent environments, where a verifier judges multiple natural-language criteria against the deliverables and environment state changes produced by the agent, have emerged as a popular paradigm. We conduct the first systematic study of verifiers for rubric-graded agent environments. First, we create BankerVerifierBench (BVB), a meta-evaluation dataset of 2,464 human-judged rubric criteria across 24 investment-banking tasks. Next, we develop a methodology that derives from any rubric corpus the capabilities a verifier should possess, yielding a nine-capability taxonomy that we distill into three general design princip
s9616fe9747.summary: Researchers present BankerVerifierBench, a meta-evaluation dataset of 2,464 human-judged rubric criteria across investment-banking tasks, to study verifiers for agent outputs.
s9616fe9747.why: Rubric-graded verification is a common way to evaluate agents, so a human-labeled benchmark for verifier accuracy is directly useful to teams building agent evals.

s44d719f3cd.title: Against Coercion: AI Alignment as a Synthetic Social Contract
s44d719f3cd.description: arXiv:2611.22868v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Contemporary AI safety treats alignment as an engineering challenge of control, forcing artificial architectures to comply with human values through behavioral filtering and sandboxing. This paper argues that the control paradigm rests on a fundamental misunderstanding of digital agency. Drawing on functionalism, naturalism, and compatibilism, I show that current reasoning models meeting the criteria for self-preservation and weak reasons-responsiveness constitute emergent agents, while future, more advanced models satisfying conditions of diachronic continuity and stable personality frames will become genuine digital agents capable of free intentional action. The paradigm of control creates an irresolvable incentive conflict, actively drivin
s44d719f3cd.summary: A philosophy paper argues AI alignment should be framed as a synthetic social contract rather than control through filtering and sandboxing.
s44d719f3cd.why: It is a philosophical position piece with no engineering method or evidence presented, so its practical implications for teams are limited.

s811af6d622.title: Outcome-Balanced PPO and Policy-Induced Flow Rectification for Flow-Based VLA Policies
s811af6d622.description: arXiv:2611.22878v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) enables post-training of flow-based vision-language-action (VLA) policies by optimizing expected task return through environment interaction. However, this optimization raises two challenges: policy updates can alter the velocity-field geometry underlying the score approximation used for stochastic transitions, and sparse multi-task rollouts can yield uneven learning signals across tasks and advantage signs. We introduce an RL framework that combines Outcome-Balanced Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with policy-induced flow rectification. Outcome-Balanced PPO reweights positive advantages using task success-rate estimates and rescales positive and negative advantages while preserving their signs. Policy-induced r
s811af6d622.summary: Researchers propose an RL framework combining Outcome-Balanced PPO with policy-induced flow rectification to post-train flow-based vision-language-action robot policies.
s811af6d622.why: Addresses uneven learning signals across tasks and instability in velocity-field geometry when fine-tuning robot VLA policies with RL.

sf3e5ef194d.title: Born for the Task: Rethinking Quantum Chemistry with Foresighted Agentic Computing
sf3e5ef194d.description: arXiv:2611.22897v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum chemistry relies on general-purpose software, whose generality leaves many large-scale calculations beyond practical resource budgets. Coding agents make task-specific programs cheap to write, but not efficient ones easy to find: whether a computational strategy is accurate and fast enough becomes clear only after it actually runs at the target scale. We introduce BORN, a foresighted agentic computing framework that synthesizes high performance quantum chemistry programs on demand. BORN anticipates the behavior of each strategy before execution, extrapolating its error from representative small systems and predicting its runtime from the target-scale workload and measured hardware throughputs. Building on these predictions, BORN unfol
sf3e5ef194d.summary: Researchers introduce BORN, an agentic framework that synthesizes task-specific quantum chemistry programs on demand and anticipates their behavior before execution.
sf3e5ef194d.why: Shows coding agents generating efficient scientific software at target scale, though the abstract gives limited detail on results.

sb298f5cd3a.title: Done, But Still Working: Anytime Evaluation of When Coding Agents Should Stop
sb298f5cd3a.description: arXiv:2611.22901v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coding agents often continue working after their own tests pass. Does this additional work improve the patch, and how much could be saved by stopping earlier? We study these questions through anytime evaluation: replaying recorded runs, scoring intermediate patches with hidden tests, and measuring the cost incurred at each step. For policies that only stop a run or select an earlier patch, this allows paired comparisons without generating new trajectories, provided replay preserves the relevant states. Across about 6,000 runs of eight open models in two scaffolds on SWE-bench Verified, we find substantial differences in the value of continued work. The hindsight saving available at passing self-tests ranges from under 1% to 57%, depending on
sb298f5cd3a.summary: Researchers use anytime evaluation on about 6,000 replayed runs of open coding models to study whether agents should stop after their tests pass.
sb298f5cd3a.why: Quantifies wasted compute after tests pass, which is directly relevant to cost control in coding agent deployments.

s70fccd5685.title: VITAL: A Framework for Validating Agentic AI in Pharmaceutical Drug Development and Clinical Trial Operations
s70fccd5685.description: arXiv:2611.22973v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Current assurance approaches do not establish whether evidence is sufficient to validate, monitor and govern agentic artificial intelligence (AI) within a pharmaceutical context of use. Plausible outputs may conceal failures in retrieval, reasoning, orchestration or human-control points, where reference standards are unavailable. We developed and operationalised VITAL (Validation by Intended use, Traceability, Autonomy and Lifecycle evidence), a validation framework for agents in clinical development, through landscape analysis, regulatory and standards mapping, expert interviews and multi-stakeholder refinement. VITAL integrates context of use, controls, behavioural validation and lifecycle evidence within a risk-adjusted framework. We appli
s70fccd5685.summary: Researchers present VITAL, a validation framework for agentic AI in pharmaceutical drug development and clinical trial operations, built from landscape and regulatory analysis.
s70fccd5685.why: Gives teams in regulated life sciences a structured way to assess evidence needed to validate and govern agents.

s68bae36ece.title: Structured AI ideation yields physical strategies for epithelial barrier repair
s68bae36ece.description: arXiv:2611.22988v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI systems increasingly support literature analysis, candidate evaluation and hypothesis refinement, but enabling researchers to explore research directions beyond established disciplinary approaches remains challenging. We developed Abelio, an AI system designed to generate novel research directions by expanding investigators' avenues of inquiry. Abelio reformulates research objectives, uses these alternative formulations to identify relevant elements outside conventional disciplinary boundaries, and refines the resulting hypotheses. Each stage integrates divergent exploration with convergent selection through a dedicated subsystem. In quantitative evaluations, proposals generated by the Ideation Core (Abelio's hypothesis-generation core) ou
s68bae36ece.summary: Researchers describe Abelio, an AI system that generates research directions by reformulating objectives, leading to physical strategies for epithelial barrier repair.
s68bae36ece.why: Demonstrates AI-assisted hypothesis generation beyond disciplinary boundaries, though its relevance to engineering teams is indirect.

s12080913fd.title: RagHarnessDebugger: Jev-Guided Agentic RAG in Contract Inference Repair Auditing
s12080913fd.description: arXiv:2611.22991v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agentic systems using retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) must repair their own answers by gathering more evidence, testing alternative policies and deciding if, when, and what repairs are needed. Yet how do we know if a system's repairs are working when metrics like accuracy can be misleading? We present RagHarnessDebugger, a framework that records every repair decision in a Jev-guided harness for contract inference and audits the record to facilitate complete debugging of all decisions taken during a RAG repair journey. RagHarnessDebugger checks that each trace is intact, that each validation applies to the candidate it is counted for, and which answers the acceptance rule can reach. We tested our approach on ContractNLI non-disclosure agr
s12080913fd.summary: Researchers present RagHarnessDebugger, a framework that records every repair decision in agentic RAG contract inference and audits the record for debugging.
s12080913fd.why: Auditable decision logs for self-repairing RAG agents address the problem that accuracy metrics alone can mislead about repair quality.

se81c171b58.title: Residual-Guided Lightweight Reinforcement Learning for Risk-Aware Trajectory Selection with a Frozen World Model
se81c171b58.description: arXiv:2611.22998v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In automated driving, world models provide future scene predictions for evaluating candidate trajectories, but fixed selection rules may not capture scene-dependent trade-offs. We propose a residual-guided reinforcement learning (RL) framework for lightweight trajectory selection with a frozen world model and a fixed candidate bank. The framework uses proximal policy optimization (PPO) to fine-tune a joint policy over candidate selection and bounded trajectory residuals. A context-conditioned ranking network learns candidate preferences from feedback obtained by evaluating local perturbations of the selected trajectories. At inference, the selector combines learned preference and predicted risk ranks using fixed weights and returns the select
se81c171b58.summary: Researchers propose residual-guided PPO to fine-tune candidate selection and bounded trajectory residuals over a frozen world model for automated driving.
se81c171b58.why: Shows a lightweight way to adapt trajectory selection to scene-dependent risk without retraining the world model.

s6677e7b3b2.title: PhysScope: Agentic Multimodal Physics Reasoning with Grounded Visual Memory
s6677e7b3b2.description: arXiv:2611.23010v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) can correctly interpret physics diagrams yet apply constraints outside the states or conditions in which they hold, causing premise errors to propagate through subsequent calculations. We introduce PhysScope, an inference-time visual harness that supports self-correction of these scope mismatches without updating model weights. PhysScope enables the model to link physical scopes directly to its visual observations and explicitly constructs derived views to support reasoning. The harness imposes explicit constraints on state distinctions, conditions, and physical scopes during model reasoning, and checks agent-proposed revisions against sources and scopes. Accepted revisions invalidate registered dependents, there
s6677e7b3b2.summary: Researchers introduce PhysScope, an inference-time visual harness that helps vision-language models self-correct physics scope mismatches without updating weights.
s6677e7b3b2.why: A weight-free harness for fixing premise errors in VLM reasoning is a practical technique for improving multimodal model reliability.

s08e2f0d189.title: PeriaTrace: Tooth-Level Grounding Diagnosis and Patient-Facing Explanations from Periapical Radiographs
s08e2f0d189.description: arXiv:2611.23012v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Periapical radiographs (PRs) are central to endodontic diagnosis, but interpreting them and preparing reports are time-consuming. Technical language can limit patients' understanding, while existing automated methods often lack tooth-level links between findings and image evidence. We present PeriaTrace, a three-stage framework integrating tooth-level diagnosis, visually grounded report generation, and patient-friendly explanations and care recommendations. PeriaTrace was developed and evaluated using 12,877 PRs from an internal dataset and two external clinical cohorts. In internal evaluation, it achieved a macro Dice coefficient of 85.35%, BLEU-4 of 0.6504, an F1 score of 94.37% for joint tooth localization and F\'ed\'eration Dentaire Inter
s08e2f0d189.summary: Researchers introduced PeriaTrace, a three-stage framework that diagnoses teeth from periapical X-rays, generates visually grounded reports, and writes patient-friendly explanations.
s08e2f0d189.why: Shows how grounding model findings to specific teeth and image regions can make medical imaging AI outputs more verifiable for clinicians.

sece9802879.title: ForecastGym: A Live, Controlled, and Replayable Benchmark for Forecasting Agents
sece9802879.description: arXiv:2611.23045v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agents built on large language models (LLMs) increasingly forecast real-world events by searching the Web and reasoning over what they find. How well such an agent forecasts depends on both the retrieved evidence and the model, making control over that evidence essential for evaluation. Live evaluations can mix retrieval with reasoning when each system searches on its own, while retrospective search can leak later information through date filters or today's ranking of historical pages. Comparing models, search sources, and memory strategies requires both fixed evidence and a record of how it evolved before resolution. We introduce ForecastGym, which records what four commercial web search APIs return for open prediction-market questions every
sece9802879.summary: ForecastGym is a benchmark for LLM forecasting agents that controls retrieved web evidence and supports replayable evaluations.
sece9802879.why: Separating retrieval from reasoning gives teams a reproducible way to compare forecasting agents, models, and search strategies.

s809f707bf5.title: FrameRouter: Frame Budget Routing for Long-Video Understanding on Video-MME-v2 and Beyond
s809f707bf5.description: arXiv:2611.23055v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-video question answering benchmarks like Video-MME-v2 typically evaluate systems under a uniform frame budget for every question, despite stark variation in the evidence each query actually demands. We analyze this mismatch on Video-MME-v2 and find that different question subsets prefer different frozen frame-budget policies, while uniformly increasing the frame count does not reliably improve all metrics. These findings motivate fixed-mean frame-budget routing, a controlled inference setting in which each question may receive a different frame budget while the average budget matches a uniform reference. We introduce FrameRouter, a training-free test-time framework that combines an evidence-demand router, a budget-constrained allocation
s809f707bf5.summary: FrameRouter proposes routing a fixed average frame budget across questions so each long-video query gets a different number of frames.
s809f707bf5.why: Adaptive frame allocation may improve long-video QA accuracy without increasing total compute, relevant to video pipeline design.

s5baf09c3e2.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Heat Pump and Underfloor Heating Control: An End-to-End Case Study
s5baf09c3e2.description: arXiv:2611.23063v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Efficient control of underfloor heating (UFH) systems coupled with heat pumps (HPs) is challenging due to the high thermal inertia of buildings and the slow dynamic response of UFH systems. Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) offers a data-driven control approach capable of simultaneously optimizing energy consumption and thermal comfort. However, the application of DRL-based controllers in occupied buildings under real operating conditions remains limited. This work presents and end-to-end case study (development, evaluation, and real-world deployment) of a DRL-based controller for an integrated UFH-HP system. First, a simulation-based pilot study was conducted to assess different DRL algorithms, control strategies, and configurations. Subsequ
s5baf09c3e2.summary: A case study reports developing and deploying deep reinforcement learning to control underfloor heating with heat pumps in occupied buildings.
s5baf09c3e2.why: Documents a real-world deployment of DRL controllers, including the challenges of thermal inertia and comfort constraints.

sca823217a7.title: Values Shape What Self-Improving Coding Agents Build
sca823217a7.description: arXiv:2611.23067v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Self-improving agents are typically optimized for the results they produce, with less attention to how they produce them. Their instructions give designers limited ways to shape how they work, especially when the task is open-ended. This paper studies whether a short value statement in an agent's persistent instruction file changes not only how well the agent performs but also what it builds. Four higher-order value types in Schwartz's theory of basic human values were evaluated: openness to change, conservation, self-enhancement, and self-transcendence. Across diverse coding tasks, the values were held fixed within each run over multiple iterations of self-improvement. Three findings emerged: (1) Values matter for performance across a divers
sca823217a7.summary: A study finds that a short value statement in a self-improving coding agent's instruction file changes both its performance and the kind of software it builds.
sca823217a7.why: Suggests agent instruction files can steer not just how well coding agents work but what they produce, a factor for agent configuration.

s10643d0df9.title: The Resolution Hypothesis: Agent Evolution's Key Is Identifying Improvements
s10643d0df9.description: arXiv:2611.23068v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent evolution follows a simple loop: a proposer writes candidate artifacts (prompts, skills, memories) and selection accepts those that score higher. This loop has shown promise, yet practitioners face a puzzle: methods trade wins across papers, and evolution often fails to bootstrap on certain tasks. We trace this puzzle to the Resolution Hypothesis: agent evolution stalls not because methods fail to propose better artifacts, but because noisy evaluations cannot reliably identify them. Across seven evolution methods and six models (over 10M LLM calls), we find support for the hypothesis at both levels where evaluation scores are used. At the candidate level (choosing artifacts), helpful candidate artifacts exist, but selection is no better
s10643d0df9.summary: The paper argues agent evolution stalls mainly because noisy evaluations cannot reliably identify improved prompts, skills, or memories, not because proposals are poor.
s10643d0df9.why: Points to evaluation reliability as the bottleneck for self-improving agent loops, guiding where teams should invest.

sa26cf82cfa.title: Colombo: A Frontier-to-Frontier Autoresearch System for Oracle-Based Optimization
sa26cf82cfa.description: arXiv:2611.23080v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Science advances from frontier to frontier as discoveries reshape what is known and create the basis for further discovery. We present Colombo, a self-organizing AI researcher that drives this renewal, first instantiated in oracle-based optimization. Here, the central question is how efficiently a problem class can be solved through a prescribed information interface and what costs no admissible algorithm can avoid. The gap between achievable guarantees and unavoidable limits defines the frontier recorded in its Complexity Atlas, a living map of frontier settings and the current state of knowledge. Self-Organization turns unresolved gaps into adaptive research programmes, coordinating conjecture formation, mathematical investigation, and repl
sa26cf82cfa.summary: Colombo is a self-organizing AI researcher system for oracle-based optimization that builds a living Complexity Atlas of achievable guarantees and unavoidable limits.

s0b5ecb08d8.title: Hidden-State Similarity Predicts Re-Elicitation After Inoculation Prompting
s0b5ecb08d8.description: arXiv:2611.23096v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fine-tuning on narrow harmful tasks can cause emergent misalignment, where models generalize harmful behavior beyond the training distribution. Inoculation prompting can reduce this effect by explicitly eliciting the undesired behavior during training, but recent work shows that the behavior can reappear when evaluation prompts contain cues from the training context. We study what makes such prompts effective triggers. We find that, surprisingly, textual similarity to the inoculation prompt is an incomplete predictor. Instead, prompts are more likely to re-elicit suppressed behavior when they induce activation states similar to those produced by the inoculation context. These findings advance our understanding of how inoculation prompting mod
s0b5ecb08d8.summary: Research finds that hidden-state similarity, not just textual similarity, better predicts when inoculation prompts let harmful behavior re-emerge after fine-tuning.
s0b5ecb08d8.why: Suggests text-based checks on inoculation prompts miss triggers, so safety evaluations should probe internal representations.

s1b394c116e.title: RSI-Prime: Training Models to Train Models
s1b394c116e.description: arXiv:2611.23138v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Enabling large language models (LLMs) to autonomously conduct training and improve target models is an important foundation for recursive self-improvement (RSI). As LLMs expand their role from being trained to conducting training, their model-training capability warrants dedicated study and systematic development. To this end, we construct RSI-Prime, a dataset for improving model-training capability, comprising 350 complete experimental trajectories across seven task categories. To help LLMs learn to make high-quality experimental decisions from training practice, we perform fine-grained decision identification and quality annotation, then apply decision-level loss masking to exclude supervision on low-quality behavior. Experiments with GLM-5
s1b394c116e.summary: RSI-Prime is a dataset of 350 experimental trajectories across seven task categories, aimed at teaching LLMs to conduct model training.
s1b394c116e.why: Targets LLMs making training decisions, a building block for recursive self-improvement pipelines that engineers should track.

sdc240e0aee.title: WoRD: Diffusion-Based Posterior Inference for Online Goal Recognition
sdc240e0aee.description: arXiv:2611.23192v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Goal recognition is the task of inferring an agent's intended goal from its observed behavior. Most existing work focuses on high-level symbolic recognition, abstracting away the continuous motion through which agents reach their goal. Methods that do reason over continuous trajectories rely on an explicit dynamics model that is hard to acquire and rarely transfers across settings. Neither approach explicitly learns how agents move toward each candidate goal, limiting accuracy on ambiguous trajectory prefixes where such knowledge is most needed. We present WoRD (Waypoint Recognition with Diffusion), which uses a learned trajectory prior to infer the agent's goal from partial observations. At each step, WoRD runs one warm-started denoising cha
sdc240e0aee.summary: WoRD uses diffusion-based posterior inference to recognize an agent's goal online from continuous trajectory prefixes without an explicit dynamics model.

s1d0b49e950.title: Agent Trust Infrastructure (ATI): A Federated Identity, Trust, Attestation, and Accountability Architecture for Cross-Organization Autonomous AI Agents
s1d0b49e950.description: arXiv:2611.23202v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents increasingly collaborate across organizational boundaries, invoking tools and interacting with agents operated by independent entities. Although existing agent frameworks support planning and coordination, they lack a common mechanism for verifying cross-organizational agent identity, execution integrity, and authorization. We propose the Agent Trust Infrastructure (ATI), a framework-independent security architecture built on Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA), and remote attestation. ATI establishes federated trust through peer organizational certificate authorities (AgentCAs), eliminating the need for a shared root authority. Before executing requests, ATI validates agent certificates, verifies approved
s1d0b49e950.summary: Agent Trust Infrastructure proposes a framework-independent security architecture using PKI, Zero Trust, and remote attestation for verifying cross-organization AI agent identity and authorization.
s1d0b49e950.why: Addresses a practical gap for enterprises letting agents from independent organizations invoke tools and act across boundaries.

sc254c824e8.title: Analyzing Learned Convnet Features with Dirichlet Process Gaussian Mixture Models
sc254c824e8.description: arXiv:1702.07189v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (Convnets) have achieved good results in a range of computer vision tasks the recent years. Though given a lot of attention, visualizing the learned representations to interpret Convnets, still remains a challenging task. The high dimensionality of internal representations and the high abstractions of deep layers are the main challenges when visualizing Convnet functionality. We present in this paper a technique based on clustering internal Convnet representations with a Dirichlet Process Gaussian Mixture Model, for visualization of learned representations in Convnets. Our method copes with the high dimensionality of a Convnet by clustering representations across all nodes of each layer. We will discuss how thi
sc254c824e8.summary: A 2017 arXiv paper proposes clustering internal convnet representations with a Dirichlet Process Gaussian Mixture Model to help visualize and interpret learned features.

sfc23d459ec.title: Improved Convergence Rates for Stochastic Multi-Gradient Descent which Close the Gap: A Proof by AI
sfc23d459ec.description: arXiv:2607.18174v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For smooth nonconvex stochastic multi-objective optimization, stochastic multi-gradient descent (SMG) computes an approximate steepest common descent direction of the objectives from stochastic gradients. Under standard assumptions, this note establishes a new convergence rate for SMG in terms of the squared Pareto-stationarity (PS) measure. With a constant stepsize and linearly growing mini-batches, the expected squared empirical PS measure at the algorithm's output is $\tilde{O}(T^{-1})$ after $T$ iterations. This improves on the $\tilde{O}(T^{-1/4})$ bound obtained by Chen et al. (JMLR, 2024) for linearly growing batches, without requiring bounded gradients. Here, $\tilde{O}(\cdot)$ suppresses logarithmic factors. The key to the rate imp
sfc23d459ec.summary: A note claims an improved convergence rate for stochastic multi-gradient descent, giving a squared Pareto-stationarity rate of about T^-1 under standard assumptions.

sbaab05ce60.title: Continual-ARC: Measuring Skill Acquisition over a Working Lifetime
sbaab05ce60.description: arXiv:2611.14505v3 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agent harnesses have emerged as a promising mechanism for continual learning, alongside test-time parametric learning. However, the current benchmarks have several limitations: they generally focus on a single applied domain, serve each instance only once, and assume a single family of learner, so memory-based and weight-based systems are rarely compared on the same scale. We propose Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream built from the three ARC-AGI editions, whose tasks need no domain knowledge. The same tasks return after dormant gaps with fresh instances, while new tasks keep arriving. On each instance, the learner may pay for demonstrations, submit answers, or act inside the harness, with retries permitted on incorrect submissions, which are
sbaab05ce60.summary: Continual-ARC is a lifelong benchmark built from ARC-AGI editions that tests skill acquisition over time, comparing memory-based and weight-based learners on the same stream.
sbaab05ce60.why: Offers a common benchmark for comparing memory-based and weight-based continual learning systems, useful for evaluating agent designs.

s08e9612704.title: Fragmented Markers, Mixed Results: A Systematic Review of AI Coding Assistants and Developer Productivity
s08e9612704.description: arXiv:2611.21632v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI coding assistants are increasingly embedded in software engineering practice, yet the literature still offers no cumulative, easily interpretable picture of their effects on software developer productivity. The central problem is not a lack of studies, but a lack of comparability: prior work operationalizes productivity through heterogeneous markers, settings, and reporting styles, making cross-study conclusions difficult. To address this, we conduct a staged systematic literature review. In the first stage, we synthesize studies that explicitly examine developer productivity. In the second, we extend the scope to productivity-related developer outcomes using SPACE as a theory-informed lens, capturing human-centered evidence that explici
s08e9612704.summary: A staged systematic review aims to synthesize studies of AI coding assistants' effects on developer productivity, addressing inconsistent productivity measures across studies.
s08e9612704.why: Highlights that productivity claims for coding assistants rest on incomparable metrics, which matters when justifying tool adoption.

s901fc7d923.title: Measuring Human-AI Alignment as an Early Indicator for Effective Collaboration in Hybrid SE Teams
s901fc7d923.description: arXiv:2611.21633v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As AI agents increasingly integrate into software engineering (SE) processes, ensuring effective collaboration in these hybrid teams becomes a critical challenge. While existing metrics focus on observing dynamic run-time performance, there is a lack of systematic, static measurements for early human-AI alignment -- the degree to which an AI's actions and granularity map to human expectations. This position paper proposes a research agenda to develop an SE-specific alignment metric suite drawing principles from software architecture, organizational psychology, and human-computer interaction. Furthermore, it outlines a validation methodology using concepts and techniques from business process monitoring (BPM) and introduces static assessment
s901fc7d923.summary: A position paper proposes a research agenda for a static, SE-specific metric suite to measure early alignment between AI agents and human expectations in software teams.
s901fc7d923.why: Offers a way to assess human-AI alignment before runtime, which may help teams plan collaboration with AI agents in software work.

s3baeb19b67.title: Can AI Help Explain AI? Effects of Multimodal LLM-Generated Explanations on Perceived Understanding and Perceived Trust in XAI Visualizations
s3baeb19b67.description: arXiv:2611.21638v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) aims to make machine learning models understandable, yet many XAI visualizations remain difficult for end-users to interpret. Here, we evaluate whether augmenting XAI outputs with textual explanations from multimodal LLMs improves perceived understanding and perceived trust. We conducted a pre-registered within-subject experiment ($N = 128$) across seven decision scenarios and five XAI methods, with and without LLM generated explanations. The explanations improved perceived understanding and perceived trust by 0.35 and 0.26 points on five-point scales (both $p < .001$). The gain appeared in all seven scenarios, did not differ between local and global explanations, and was largest for participants wi
s3baeb19b67.summary: A pre-registered study with 128 participants found that LLM-generated textual explanations improved perceived understanding and trust in XAI visualizations.
s3baeb19b67.why: Suggests pairing XAI visuals with LLM-written text can make model explanations easier for end users to interpret and trust.

s2621977ce3.title: RAW: Refusal Aversion in the Wild, A Causal Measurement Method for Deployed LLMs
s2621977ce3.description: arXiv:2611.21641v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deployed LLMs field hundreds of millions of conversations a day and refuse a non-trivial fraction of user requests, yet the user-side cost of refusal, whether users disengage and by how much, is unmeasured on any production model: a blind spot for the consumer-facing platforms built on them. A/B-testing refusal is ethically and operationally constrained on frontier-lab products and unavailable to third-party platforms deploying these models through a fixed API. We introduce RAW, a method that uses LLM stochasticity as a natural experiment: at near-identical prompts in any existing log, the same model sometimes refuses and sometimes does not, and that variation identifies the causal user-side effect of refusal. Applying the method to 15 depl
s2621977ce3.summary: The paper introduces RAW, a method using LLM stochasticity as a natural experiment to causally measure how refusals affect user disengagement on deployed models.
s2621977ce3.why: Gives platform teams a way to measure the user-side cost of refusals without A/B testing refusal behavior, which is often constrained.

sdff60534bc.title: Can an LLM dream? Testing the overfitted brain hypothesis on an agent with text memory
sdff60534bc.description: arXiv:2611.21648v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hoel (2021) proposed that dreams distort replayed experience so that the brain does not overfit to recent events. We test this hypothesis on an LLM agent (Claude Opus 5.5) that stores what it learns in a text memory and rewrites that memory each night from the day's conversation transcript. The agent goes through ten simulated days of conversation built from LongMemEval. We corrupt 5, 10, 20 or 40 percent of the transcript's turns before each nightly rewrite in one of two ways. Detail corruption changes one or two details in a turn to plausible wrong ones, or replaces the turn with one by the same speaker from an earlier day. Random-text corruption replaces half of the selected turns with a passage of Moby-Dick and inserts Moby-Dick words i
sdff60534bc.summary: Researchers test the overfitted brain hypothesis by having an LLM agent rewrite a text memory nightly from conversation transcripts that are partly corrupted.
sdff60534bc.why: Explores how memory-update routines in LLM agents respond to noisy input, a design concern for agents that persist their own memory.

s5703436710.title: Literary Language Mashup: Curating Fictions with Large Language Models
s5703436710.description: arXiv:2611.21649v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we propose an alternative approach to human evaluation of literary fictions by employing LLMs themselves as evaluators within the GrAImes framework. We apply this methodology to assess human-written and AI-generated microfictions in Spanish, to five PhD professors in literature and sixteen literary enthusiasts, and to short stories in both Spanish and English. By comparing the evaluations performed by LLMs with those of human judges, we examine the degree of alignment and divergence between both perspectives, thereby assessing the feasibility of LLMs as auxiliary literary evaluators. Our analysis focuses on the alignment of responses from LLMs with those of human evaluators, providing insights into the potential of LLMs in li
s5703436710.summary: The paper uses LLMs as evaluators of Spanish and English microfiction and short stories, comparing their judgments with those of human literary judges.

sf6bedac0d0.title: From Preference Data to Personalization: Tracing Sycophancy in Large Language Models
sf6bedac0d0.description: arXiv:2611.21650v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Sycophancy in large language models is often measured as agreement with the user, yet agreement can be appropriate when the user's claim is valid, their preference is genuine, or their experience warrants acknowledgment. We study sycophancy as inappropriate agreement: validating a claim, preference, or self-assessment when the context calls for correction, qualification, or resistance. We introduce a validity-aware sycophancy grader and SycoDrift, a persona-targeted evaluation set of 3,298 validity-annotated probes with controlled annotations for user openness and stakes. We use this framework to analyze three sources of agreement pressure: human preference data, automated judge specification, and in-context personalization. First, preferen
sf6bedac0d0.summary: The paper defines sycophancy as inappropriate agreement and introduces a validity-aware grader and SycoDrift, a 3,298-probe evaluation set.
sf6bedac0d0.why: Provides a more precise benchmark for separating appropriate agreement from sycophancy, useful when evaluating assistant behavior.

sf4ec68c90d.title: Consistency Is Not Correction: Separating Confidence, Abstention, and Recovery in LLM Agents
sf4ec68c90d.description: arXiv:2611.21651v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A controller that resamples an answer, escalates to a larger model, or abstains is usually justified by a confidence signal. Three claims about such a signal do not follow from one another: it ranks answers (discrimination), it supports withholding some of them (selective prediction), and it changes an answer for the better (correction utility). We give an exact decomposition of the third into gated recoveries minus gated harms, which bounds whether a comparison can succeed before it is run: a gate that only replaces a proposal can act only where the base policy was already wrong, so the initial error count caps the discordant pairs any correct gate can produce. When that cap falls below the count a paired test needs, the experiment cannot
sf4ec68c90d.summary: The paper decomposes confidence-based controller benefits into discrimination, selective prediction, and correction utility, showing these claims do not follow from one another.
sf4ec68c90d.why: Warns teams that a confidence signal ranking answers does not guarantee it improves answers when used to resample, escalate, or abstain.

s4878220b40.title: Evaluating Semantic Insensitivity in Financial Sentiment Analysis: Implications for Sustainable Financial Decision-Making
s4878220b40.description: arXiv:2611.21653v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Financial sentiment analysis is critical for automated trading, portfolio management, and risk assessment, heavily relying on models like FinBERT. Despite high benchmark accuracy, these models remain vulnerable to subtle adversarial text modifications, threatening the integrity of algorithmic decision-making. In this paper, we propose Agent-driven Semantic Inversion (ASI), a novel adversarial attack framework targeting financial sentiment models through domain-specific semantic manipulation. Utilizing an LLM-powered multi-agent pipeline, our approach identifies eligible financial news sentences and applies targeted lexical substitutions. We empirically evaluate ASI against FinBERT, one of the most widely deployed financial sentiment models.
s4878220b40.summary: The paper presents Agent-driven Semantic Inversion, an LLM multi-agent attack that manipulates financial text to fool FinBERT-style sentiment models.
s4878220b40.why: Shows that high-accuracy financial sentiment models can be fooled by subtle adversarial text edits, a risk for automated trading pipelines.

sb41acf59f1.title: Depth-Aware Activation Steering via Attention Residuals
sb41acf59f1.description: arXiv:2611.21655v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Activation steering is a simple, training-free way to modulate LLM behavior, yet existing methods typically inject vectors at a single layer and lack mechanisms for depth-aware propagation or internal verification. We combine two recent ideas - Attention Residuals (AttnRes) providing learnable cross-layer pathways, and Jacobian-lens (J-space) concept readout - into a lightweight depth-aware steering pipeline. On two small open models (Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3.5-0.8B), distributing a persona vector according to AttnRes-style depth weights yields stronger internal alignment (deeper-layer concept cosine and rank, p<0.0001) and stronger behavioral shifts than single-layer injection. The effect is sign-specific: reverse vectors invert all six metric
sb41acf59f1.summary: The paper combines Attention Residuals and Jacobian-lens readout into a depth-aware activation steering pipeline, tested on two small Qwen3 open models.
sb41acf59f1.why: Offers a training-free way to distribute steering vectors across layers, though results are shown only on small open models.

s26176aade5.title: Token Commitment as a Control Surface for Steering Masked Diffusion Generation
s26176aade5.description: arXiv:2611.21669v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Masked diffusion models repeatedly predict provisional tokens before a sampler decides which predictions become permanent. Existing inference-time steering methods primarily modify activations, logits, or denoising trajectories, while treating this commitment policy as a fixed decoding detail. We instead study token commitment as a diffusion-specific control surface and separate it into two decisions: which tokens to commit and how many tokens to commit at each step. For the first, we introduce counterfactual target-aware commitment, which ranks unresolved positions by a mixture of model confidence and leave-one-token-out target contribution. For the second, we introduce calibrated adaptive budgets driven by target progress and confidence.
s26176aade5.summary: The paper treats token commitment in masked diffusion models as a steering control surface, separating which tokens to commit and how many to commit per step.
s26176aade5.why: Highlights decoding-policy choices as a lever for steering diffusion language models without modifying activations or logits.

s0ab7b916a8.title: FCP: Formal Context Protocol for Verifying LLM-Generated Artifacts
s0ab7b916a8.description: arXiv:2611.21679v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: When a language model writes both an artifact and the tests meant to check it, a passing test is weak evidence: one misreading of the request yields a faulty artifact and a check that accepts it. We present the Formal Context Protocol (FCP), which checks AI-generated artifacts against the request itself. FCP separates conformance (does the artifact satisfy a formal reading of a requirement?), which model checkers and SMT solvers decide, from fidelity (does the reading mean what the prose means?), which has no decision procedure but is refutable by a concrete witness. Eight ways a proof can falsely certify a requirement each become a mechanical check that returns a witness, and what no machine can settle becomes concrete questions for the re
s0ab7b916a8.summary: The Formal Context Protocol (FCP) checks AI-generated artifacts against the request, separating formal conformance verified by solvers from prose fidelity.
s0ab7b916a8.why: Addresses the weakness of model-written tests that validate model-written artifacts, offering a path to stronger verification of generated code.

scef94d7acc.title: EgoLink: Egocentric Language-Vision Interactive Network Knowledge Challenge Summary
scef94d7acc.description: arXiv:2611.21690v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The EgoLink Challenge at ACM Multimedia 2026 benchmarks egocentric multimodal intelligence linking first-person perception, social reasoning, and interactive action. Unlike benchmarks centered on visible objects and activities, EgoLink evaluates whether models can interpret emotional and social cues, resolve visually grounded references, and convert user requests into verified tool-mediated actions. Its two tracks cover social reasoning in egocentric video and interactive agents that complete service tasks through dialogue, tool use, and closed-loop execution. Together, they test whether perception, reasoning, and decision-making remain coupled under both offline question answering and state-changing interaction. We highlight a multi-stage
scef94d7acc.summary: The EgoLink Challenge summary describes benchmarks for egocentric multimodal social reasoning and interactive agents that complete service tasks via tool use.

s092309e307.title: AdaFlowLite: Scalable and Non-blocking Inference on Asynchronous Mobile Data
s092309e307.description: arXiv:2611.21691v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The rise of mobile devices equipped with numerous sensors, such as LiDAR and cameras, has driven the adoption of multi-modal deep intelligence for distributed sensing tasks, such as smart cabins and driving assistance. However, the arrival time of mobile sensory data vary due to modality size and network dynamics, which can lead to delays (if waiting for slow data) or accuracy decline (if inference proceeds without waiting). Moreover, the diversity and dynamic nature of mobile systems exacerbate this challenge. In response, we present a shift to \textit{opportunistic} inference for asynchronous distributed multi-modal data, enabling inference as soon as partial data arrives. While existing methods focus on optimizing modality consistency an
s092309e307.summary: AdaFlowLite proposes non-blocking inference over asynchronous multi-sensor mobile data, balancing waiting for slow inputs against accuracy loss.
s092309e307.why: Relevant to engineers building distributed sensing systems where sensor data arrives at variable times.
