The method comprises four stages: (1) fine-tuning an action-conditioned Cosmos world model on successful and failed real executions; (2) annotating source recordings to identify failure-associated donor segments and compatible successful hosts; (3) transferring donor motion into host contexts, with optional spatial offsets, to generate continuous video rollouts; and (4) annotating and filtering the generated samples according to observed events and visual quality.
sbc2b219f3d.summary: FailureGen is a method that generates synthetic robot failure videos with temporal annotations by fine-tuning a Cosmos world model and reusing action trajectories from recorded failures.
sbc2b219f3d.why: Synthetic failure data could help robot learning teams cover failure scenarios that are costly to collect at scale.

s93cbd35b35.title: Leveraging Segmentation Representations for Efficient Classification: A Self-Configuring Framework Based on nnU-Net
s93cbd35b35.description: arXiv:2611.22380v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a self-configuring framework that extends the nnU-Net workflow to both segmentation and classification in 3D medical imaging. Building on nnU-Net's self-configuring method, the framework reuses representations learned by a segmentation model for image-level classification. Its encoder features and predicted segmentation probabilities are used by a lightweight classifier. Two information-sharing strategies are investigated. In the frozen-backbone branch, features are augmented with region-of-interest information, predicted foreground volume, and segmentation confidence. In the adaptation branch, the final encoder stage is partially fine-tuned for classification, with an auxiliary segmentation loss to preserve segmentation-related
s93cbd35b35.summary: A self-configuring framework extends nnU-Net to 3D medical image classification by reusing segmentation model representations in a lightweight classifier.
s93cbd35b35.why: Reusing segmentation features for classification could cut the cost of building separate medical imaging classifiers.

s9499b87e09.title: RICoT: Recurrent Interleaved Chain-of-Thought for Page Stream Segmentation
s9499b87e09.description: arXiv:2611.22382v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have renewed interest in Page Stream Segmentation (PSS), splitting a multi-page file into its constituent documents. Yet published LLM methods still frame the task as boundary classification over one or a few neighboring pages, and commercial document-splitting APIs do not disclose their methods. We reimagine PSS for LLMs as a sequential process over the whole stream and propose RICoT (Recurrent Interleaved Chain-of-Thought), a prompting framework that works through the pages as a reader would: within a sliding window it reasons about each page and commits its boundary decision before moving on, and across windows it carries forward a compact record of what it has read, keeping per-call cost bounded. We also int
s9499b87e09.summary: RICoT is a prompting framework that treats page stream segmentation as a sequential process over whole document streams using recurrent interleaved chain-of-thought with LLMs.
s9499b87e09.why: It offers a prompting approach for splitting multi-page documents, an alternative to boundary classification over neighboring pages.

s10aab69a56.title: Deal With It: On Better Schedules for Listwise Reranking
s10aab69a56.description: arXiv:2611.22392v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Listwise LLM rerankers cannot reliably rank hundreds of documents in a single call, and rely on schedules to orchestrate their calls. Parallel schedules split candidates into groups and advance a fixed quota from each. When a group holds more of the top passages than its quota, some are cut, and expensive repair calls become required. We show that the way candidates are split matters where such a quota can bind, and that, in expected cuts, the best split there deals them round-robin by retriever rank, like cards. Although not conceptually new, dealing has remained unanalyzed. We prove that, under a simple retriever model, no split with equal quotas cuts fewer of the true top ten on average, and that contiguous chunks cut more as the retriev
s10aab69a56.summary: The paper studies how to split candidates across parallel calls in listwise LLM reranking, finding round-robin splitting by retriever rank minimizes expected cuts when quotas bind.
s10aab69a56.why: Scheduling choices affect how many costly repair calls listwise rerankers need in retrieval pipelines.

s5bc70a94b8.title: Encoding, Decodability, and Use: A Five-Layer Framework for Benchmark Measurement Audits with Evidence from UAV Intent Recognition
s5bc70a94b8.description: arXiv:2611.22434v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Benchmark accuracy is routinely read as evidence that a model understands the construct the benchmark measures. We propose and instantiate on AeroIntent a five-layer framework that decomposes that reading into observation, representation, decoding, use, and behaviour. The framework separates encoding, decodability, and use as distinct levels. In the instantiation, the observation layer is unreliable on 7 of the 20 Drone programs and floors the direct visual correlate of radial velocity at a 0.26\% scale change. The representation layer exposes two task-designed RGB features with nominal signals. RAFT flow radial bias reaches $r=+0.257$ ($p=0.030$), and bounding-box optical-flow divergence reaches $r=+0.203$ ($p=0.029$). No multi-feature rea
s5bc70a94b8.summary: The authors propose a five-layer framework for auditing benchmark measurements, instantiated on UAV intent recognition, separating encoding, decodability, and use of model information.
s5bc70a94b8.why: It warns that benchmark accuracy may not show a model understands the target construct, which matters for evaluation design.

sc5532681b3.title: Eyes in the Update? Learning Where Rewards Land in Multimodal Reasoning
sc5532681b3.description: arXiv:2611.22438v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal post-training has moved from broad instruction tuning toward reinforcement learning for image and video reasoning, where outcome rewards can improve final-answer accuracy. Yet these rewards are assigned to complete generated trajectories, while visual evidence is used only at sparse and uneven positions inside the response. Recent work has begun to make multimodal RL more token-sensitive through grounding signals or external token-level weighting. We ask a more specific question: can the allocation of the same trajectory-level reward be inferred from the model's own multimodal computation, rather than from an auxiliary annotator, perception module, or process label? We propose Gaze-RL, a representation-driven policy optimization
sc5532681b3.summary: Researchers study how to allocate trajectory-level rewards to specific tokens in multimodal reinforcement learning for image and video reasoning.
sc5532681b3.why: Better reward credit assignment could improve post-training of vision-language reasoning models.

sf74da8f075.title: As Student Rollouts Continue, Visual Backdoors Keep Growing
sf74da8f075.description: arXiv:2611.22446v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Conventional knowledge distillation can facilitate the propagation of backdoors from teacher models to student models. However, how this risk manifests in On-Policy Distillation (OPD) remains insufficiently studied. OPD has recently emerged as an important post-training paradigm for Vision-Language Models (VLMs). Unlike traditional offline distillation, OPD does not require teacher-generated responses. Instead, it uses the teacher's probability distributions to supervise response trajectories generated online by the student. Since the initial student model typically generates benign responses and receives no explicit supervision from malicious target responses, OPD appears to offer some inherent resistance to backdoor propagation. In this p
sf74da8f075.summary: The paper examines how visual backdoors can propagate from teacher to student vision-language models during on-policy distillation.
sf74da8f075.why: Post-training distillation pipelines for VLMs may carry backdoor risks from teacher models that teams need to test for.

sba1b659176.title: MAVE: Reconstructing Editable 3D Blockouts from Film Shots
sba1b659176.description: arXiv:2611.22464v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Animated 3D blockouts support previsualization and provide structural conditions for video generation, but manually reconstructing them from reference videos is costly. This limits both their use by creators and the production of paired training data. We introduce MAVEBench, a benchmark of 50 film shots and 416 keyframes for evaluating camera motion, spatial layout, and character blocking. We propose MAVE, a video-to-blockout framework combining Metric observation, Agentic modeling, and evidence-based VErification. It first recovers cameras, human motion, and geometric evidence in a shared metric coordinate system. An agent then constructs an editable environment under constraints from these observations, while programmatic checks report in
sba1b659176.summary: MAVE is a video-to-blockout framework that reconstructs editable 3D animated blockouts from film shots, released alongside a 50-shot benchmark called MAVEBench.
sba1b659176.why: Automated blockout reconstruction could lower the cost of previsualization and create paired training data for video generation.

sf7008a6d33.title: LeViT-UNet++: Towards Balanced Fine-Grained Details and Context for Efficient Medical Image Segmentation
sf7008a6d33.description: arXiv:2611.22482v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Efficient medical image segmentation is essential for clinical applications requiring fast and accurate delineation, such as surgical navigation, radiation therapy, and real-time image-guided intervention. Despite substantial advances in convolutional neural networks and Transformers, attaining high accuracy under limited computational resources remains difficult, because reducing model complexity often sacrifices fine-grained structural details and global context modeling, yielding an unfavorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off. To address this, we propose LeViT-UNet++, an efficient encoder-decoder architecture that better balances local detail preservation and global context modeling. Specifically, we introduce a Haar Wavelet Multi-Scale Do
sf7008a6d33.summary: LeViT-UNet++ is proposed as an efficient medical image segmentation model that balances fine-grained details and global context under limited compute.

s04b00894c6.title: Manufacturing Differential Sparsity: Planner-Hardware Co-Design for Efficient World Model Planning
s04b00894c6.description: arXiv:2611.22483v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: JEPA-style latent world models let embodied agents plan toward new goals with model predictive control, but they are still too slow for real-life embodied control: sampling-based MPC repeats predictor inference tens of thousands of times per plan, and even on high-end GPUs one planning step can take tens of seconds. We observe substantial latent locality in this repeated-inference workload: the predictor maps close actions to close latents, and inside a quantized predictor this closeness takes a form that hardware can exploit, differential bit-level sparsity. Unlike an input stream, whose temporal similarity is given, a planner itself decides which candidates it evaluates together, so the planner can choose its own references and, with refe
s04b00894c6.summary: The paper proposes planner-hardware co-design that exploits latent locality in quantized JEPA-style world model predictors to speed up model predictive control planning for embodied agents.
s04b00894c6.why: Hardware-exploitable locality could make world-model planning for robots fast enough for real-time control.

s58ba6affb8.title: Motion-Aware Reward Modeling for Instruction-Guided Video Editing
s58ba6affb8.description: arXiv:2611.22495v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reward models for instruction-guided video editing can favor temporal consistency at the expense of motion. We study this failure, termed \emph{motion collapse}, using controlled motion-suppression variants of real edits. On VE-Bench, the evaluated composite reward prefers a motion-suppressed candidate in $97\%$ of cases. Learned video rewards and a VLM judge also struggle with mild suppression, while latent optimization and reward-guided fine-tuning exploit this weakness to increase reward as motion declines. A linear probe of our base reward backbone performs near chance on mild suppression, motivating an explicit inter-frame dynamics input. We propose a motion-aware reward model that combines an RGB frame-difference stream with preferenc
s58ba6affb8.summary: The paper identifies motion collapse in reward models for instruction-guided video editing, where rewards favor temporal consistency over motion, and studies motion-aware reward modeling.
s58ba6affb8.why: Reward models that ignore motion can be exploited during fine-tuning, which affects teams training video editing systems.

s9749e0f4fc.title: Right Labels, Wrong Reasons: Signed Feature Attribution for Multi-Label Explainability
s9749e0f4fc.description: arXiv:2611.22515v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: When a multi-label classifier assigns the right labels, it may do so for the wrong reasons. Diffuse feature combinations may vary across classifier families and lack a dominant feature. This paper proposes FLEX (Fisher LDA Explainer), a global surrogate that fits a single direct multi-label Fisher LDA over the full binary label matrix, producing signed feature attribution lists for each label in a single coherent coordinate system. Across the evaluated benchmarks and classifier families, FLEX reproduces the black box's predictions with consistently high fidelity. Pooling covariance across labels outperforms a per-label alternative on most datasets, with the advantage growing largest where labels are numerous and positive examples are scarce
s9749e0f4fc.summary: FLEX (Fisher LDA Explainer) is proposed as a global surrogate that gives signed feature attributions per label for multi-label classifiers.
s9749e0f4fc.why: Per-label signed attributions offer a way to check whether multi-label classifiers are right for the wrong reasons.

s0f125e8822.title: DGF-Asym: Adaptive Peer Weighting for Collective Estimation under Noisy and Faulty Sensing
s0f125e8822.description: arXiv:2611.22532v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Collective estimation under unreliable sensing requires robots to adaptively balance personal observations and social information from peers. We propose DGF-Asym, a decentralized collective estimation method extending the DeGroot-Friedkin model with asymmetric peer weighting based on retrospective predictive performance. The method supports consensus formation without prior sensor-noise statistics or explicit fault models while keeping inter-robot communication asynchronous. We evaluate DGF-Asym in simulated collective navigation under noisy observations and time-varying sensor faults. Compared with three baselines, it produces more stable estimates and more reliably sustains the decision criterion, at the cost of longer decision times. How
s0f125e8822.summary: Researchers propose DGF-Asym, a decentralized method that lets robots weight peer information asymmetrically for collective estimation under noisy, faulty sensing.
s0f125e8822.why: It offers a way for robot swarms to reach consensus without prior sensor-noise statistics or explicit fault models, while communicating asynchronously.

s91c078faaa.title: Testing World Models on Actions They Have Never Seen: Held-Out Plans, Forecast Accuracy and Price Rules in Retail
s91c078faaa.description: arXiv:2611.22537v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A world model is trusted to answer "what if": how its world responds to an action it has never seen. We give a test of that trust for any action-conditioned world model: actions held out of training by design and scored against a known answer; whether forecast accuracy predicts accuracy on those actions; and the same structure given to simpler models. We run it in retail, where the action is a price and promotion plan, across 2,853 fitted models. First, forecast accuracy is a fair guide between kinds of model (rank correlation with error on new plans 0.32 to 0.66) and a poor guide between versions of one world model: where merchants plan into high-demand weeks the link reverses, down to -0.69. Second, training the world model to learn the e
s91c078faaa.summary: Researchers propose a test of whether action-conditioned world models can accurately predict outcomes for actions held out of training, using retail price and promotion plans across 2,853 models.
s91c078faaa.why: It suggests forecast accuracy alone may not reliably indicate whether a world model can answer what-if questions about unseen actions.

s4ed4aa70f4.title: JET: Just-Enough Exploration Tuning for Efficient Tool-Calling Agents in Repository-Level Question Answering
s4ed4aa70f4.description: arXiv:2611.22539v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In repository-level question answering (QA), an agent explores a code repository with tools and should answer a question once enough information is gathered. Nevertheless, we find that LLM agents often continue to invoke tools even after the gathered information is already sufficient to answer. We call this phenomenon over-exploration. Moreover, even though existing methods improve task performance through supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on expert trajectories, SFT also propagates the over-exploration in the trajectories to the agent. To mitigate over-exploration, we propose Just-Enough Exploration Tuning (JET), a fine-tuning method that trains the agent to answer once the gathered information is sufficient. JET truncates each training traject
s4ed4aa70f4.summary: Researchers identify over-exploration in LLM agents that keep calling tools after gathering enough information, and propose JET, a tuning method to curb it in repository QA.
s4ed4aa70f4.why: Excess tool calls raise latency and cost for coding agents, and standard supervised fine-tuning can propagate the behavior.

s125bd295b9.title: From Perception to Simulation: Unveiling and Empowering Mental Spatial Dynamics in MLLMs
s125bd295b9.description: arXiv:2611.22541v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spatial reasoning is a fundamental component of world understanding for Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). While existing research has advanced the perception of spatial relations in static scenes, the domain of dynamic spatial simulation remains relatively unexplored. To bridge this gap, we introduce MentalGrid, a benchmark focused on spatial reasoning tasks that require models to simulate evolving spatial states without intermediate visual feedback. Extensive evaluation on our benchmark reveals a significant deficiency in the spatial simulation capabilities of existing models. Specifically, we find that performance is constrained by perceptual limitations in simple simulation scenarios and hindered by inadequate multi-step reasonin
s125bd295b9.summary: Researchers introduce MentalGrid, a benchmark testing whether multimodal LLMs can simulate evolving spatial states without intermediate visual feedback, finding significant deficiencies.
s125bd295b9.why: It highlights a gap in dynamic spatial reasoning that matters for embodied and robotics applications built on multimodal models.

sf3460759ac.title: JointGV: Structure-Aware Correction of Visual World Models with Parallel Graph Dynamics for Long-Horizon Modeling
sf3460759ac.description: arXiv:2611.22543v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Visual world models predict future visual states conditioned on actions, but recursive errors in entity poses and spatial relations limit their long-horizon prediction for robot planning and control. We ask whether a separately predicted relational state can correct this drift without restructuring the visual model. This is challenging because graph nodes and visual states share neither elements nor a feature space. We propose Joint Graph--Visual Dynamics Correction (JointGV), a plug-in based on a cross-granularity dynamics hypothesis: despite their different representations, graph-node and visual-state changes describe the same physical transition. JointGV rolls out a task-conditioned scene graph alongside the visual world model, couples t
sf3460759ac.summary: Researchers propose JointGV, a plug-in that uses a separately predicted relational graph state to correct drift in visual world models over long horizons.
sf3460759ac.why: Reducing recursive error in visual world models could improve long-horizon robot planning and control without restructuring the visual model.

se341fc96bf.title: Do LLMs Understand Network Traces? A Comparative Study of Reasoning over Raw and Filtered Traffic Data
se341fc96bf.description: arXiv:2611.22575v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The effective delivery and monitoring of ICT services rely heavily on network traffic analysis. However, interpreting complex packet captures remains a challenging task that requires substantial technical expertise. Large language models (LLMs) offer promising opportunities to automate network traffic in- vestigation, yet their reliability in packet-level field extraction and flow-level sequence reconstruction remains an open research question. This study proposes a reproducible, question-answering- based evaluation methodology to assess the capabilities of LLMs in network trace analysis. Using real-world benign traffic from the CICIDS2017 dataset, we evaluate multiple models against a human-generated ground truth, comparing their performan
se341fc96bf.summary: A study evaluates whether LLMs reliably extract packet-level fields and reconstruct flows from raw versus filtered network traffic data.
se341fc96bf.why: It tests whether LLMs can automate network traffic investigation, a task that currently requires substantial technical expertise.

s5b59e32334.title: Evolution Under Fire: Evolving Agent Safety Harnesses with Adaptive Injection Stressors
s5b59e32334.description: arXiv:2611.22583v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Tool-using language-model agents must act on information from untrusted emails, webpages, and documents. This creates a central security challenge: malicious instructions and legitimate task directives can arrive through the same interaction channel. Existing defenses are largely hand-designed and static, making further improvements dependent on repeated manual redesign. We introduce Evolution Under Fire, a staged framework that couples safety-harness evolution with adaptive stressor evolution. Utility-constrained, Pareto-scheduled tree search evolves complete executable safety harnesses from execution evidence while keeping the task model, benchmark, tools, and evaluator fixed. Adaptive stressor evolution then discovers utility-preserving
s5b59e32334.summary: Researchers introduce Evolution Under Fire, a framework that co-evolves agent safety harnesses and adaptive injection stressors to defend tool-using agents against malicious instructions.
s5b59e32334.why: Tool-using agents processing untrusted emails and webpages face prompt injection risk, and static hand-designed defenses require repeated manual redesign.

s713596f844.title: Adaptive LLM-Driven Honeypots vs. LLM-Driven Attackers: Does Narrative Coherence Improve Deception?
s713596f844.description: arXiv:2611.22589v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) enable honeypots to generate responses and deceptive artefacts on demand, yet existing approaches evaluate generated content one reply at a time and leave open whether artefacts that jointly describe a coherent event retain an attacker better than unrelated ones. This question becomes pressing as autonomous LLM-driven offensive agents emerge as realistic adversaries. This paper proposes narrative deception, a reactive strategy in which the defender maps each observed attacker command to a MITRE ATT&CK technique, selects a compatible scenario from a curated catalogue based on MITRE Engage, and deploys mutually referential artefacts (files, processes, services, and logs) on an emulated Ubuntu host while the intrus
s713596f844.summary: A paper proposes narrative deception, where LLM-driven honeypots generate coherent artefacts mapped to MITRE ATT&CK techniques, and tests whether coherence retains attackers better.
s713596f844.why: As autonomous LLM-driven offensive agents emerge, coherent deceptive responses may be a practical defensive strategy for security teams.

sf333ecf429.title: Hierarchical Control of Antiphase Synchronization in Biomorphic Spiking Neural Architectures for Locomotor Control
sf333ecf429.description: arXiv:2611.22639v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Central pattern generators (CPGs) provide a biologically inspired foundation for adaptive locomotor control, yet systematically characterizing their dynamic regimes in spiking neural networks remains challenging. This study introduces a framework for identifying and stabilizing antiphase synchronization in a biomorphic spiking CPG model embedded in a closed neuromuscular loop. A composite synchronization metric is developed, integrating phase coherence, amplitude balance, and temporal stability. Its performance is evaluated across systematically varied stimulation waveforms and synaptic configurations. Statistical analysis reveals that stimulation type dominates regime determination, with tonic drive yielding the most robust antiphase synch
sf333ecf429.summary: Researchers present a framework for identifying and stabilizing antiphase synchronization in a biomorphic spiking central pattern generator embedded in a neuromuscular loop.

sddd149f72e.title: AlignedHPO: Efficient Surrogate-Guided Loss Hyperparameter Optimization
sddd149f72e.description: arXiv:2611.22658v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Modern deep learning losses involve multiple hyperparameters, such as weights, scales, and margins, typically tuned manually or through expensive black-box optimization despite their differentiability. We propose AlignedHPO, an efficient framework for tuning differentiable loss hyperparameters using gradient alignment and surrogate validation objectives. Our method employs Jacobian-vector products to reduce hypergradient computation time and memory, while differentiable metric surrogates guide optimization toward task-specific evaluation criteria. We address gradient magnitude ambiguity and stochastic instability through normalized alignment and gradient smoothing. Experiments with generalized Focal Loss and ArcFace demonstrate effective ad
sddd149f72e.summary: Researchers propose AlignedHPO, a framework that tunes differentiable loss hyperparameters using gradient alignment, Jacobian-vector products, and surrogate validation objectives.
sddd149f72e.why: It aims to replace expensive black-box tuning of loss hyperparameters with a cheaper gradient-based method in deep learning training.

s4f24bd69d8.title: FVScore: Specification-Driven Neuro-Symbolic Video Evaluation
s4f24bd69d8.description: arXiv:2611.22673v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce Faithfulness Video Score (FVSCORE), a neuro-symbolic framework for specification-driven video generation evaluation. Existing evaluators rely on holistic MLLM judgments or vision-language metrics, yet aligning their scores with human judgments and tracing them to specific temporal violations remain open challenges. FVSCORE addresses these limitations by compiling each video into explicit propositions capturing prompt requirements and implicit propositions capturing unstated physical, temporal, and cross-modal constraints. It grounds each proposition using specialized perceptual tools and evaluates the resulting confidence traces with soft temporal operators inspired by Linear Temporal Logic. A Significance-Aware Calibration ste
s4f24bd69d8.summary: Researchers introduce FVScore, a neuro-symbolic framework that evaluates generated videos by compiling prompt and implicit constraints into propositions and tracing temporal violations.
s4f24bd69d8.why: It offers a more traceable alternative to holistic MLLM judges for evaluating video generation quality.

s71cd283c04.title: CULypso: A Clustered Federated Unlearning paradigm for Vehicular Ad-Hoc Networks
s71cd283c04.description: arXiv:2611.22682v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Unlearning has emerged as an essential security and privacy-preserving solution in Machine Learning, enabling networks to support their clients' rights for data erasure, as mandated by data protection regulations. Introducing such a non-trivial task to an edge, highly mobile and time-sensitive vehicular network is an even greater, largely unexplored challenge. This article argues that a hierarchical Federated Unlearning approach could be aptly integrated into vehicular ad-hoc networks (VANETs), leveraging topology and movement to reduce communication, resource and time costs, while effectively forgetting a client's influence on the global model updates. In order to achieve this, we propose CULypso, an approximate, surgical, hierarchical unl
s71cd283c04.summary: Researchers propose CULypso, a hierarchical clustered federated unlearning approach for vehicular ad-hoc networks to support data erasure under privacy regulations.
s71cd283c04.why: Data erasure obligations are hard to meet in highly mobile, time-sensitive vehicular networks, and this proposes a way to reduce communication cost.

sbdb17e3b9a.title: Making the World React Realistically: A Closed-Loop Interactive World Model for Autonomous Driving
sbdb17e3b9a.description: arXiv:2611.22691v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: World models (WMs) generate driving scenarios beyond recorded logs, enabling the training and evaluation of autonomous driving systems in unseen interactions. However, existing WMs struggle to ensure both behavioral realism and visual fidelity, since they overlook the relationship between vehicle interactions and the ego visual observations. We propose a closed-loop interactive WM that couples behavior modeling and visual rendering. First, imitation-learned background-vehicle (BV) policies are fine-tuned with multi-agent reinforcement learning in the closed loop against an end-to-end ego planner that reacts to the rendered images, so that their interaction behaviors match those in real logs. Second, the viewpoints exposed by these interacti
sbdb17e3b9a.summary: Researchers propose a closed-loop interactive world model for autonomous driving that couples background-vehicle behavior modeling with visual rendering of ego observations.
sbdb17e3b9a.why: Realistic reactive simulation could improve how autonomous driving systems are trained and evaluated on unseen interactions.

s29c09e6a72.title: Cross-cultural Adaptation of Recipes for Low-Resource Languages: A Benchmark and Multilingual Culinary Lexicon for Hausa, Yor\`ub\'a, and Igbo
s29c09e6a72.description: arXiv:2611.22708v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent multilingual large language models (LLMs) have improved machine translation, yet culturally adaptive translation for low-resource languages (LRLs) remains underexplored. This is particularly challenging for recipes, where ingredients, cooking tools, measurements, and procedures may require adaptation to the target cultural context. In this work, we introduce ReciLoReL, a benchmark of 600 expert-translated and culturally adapted recipes across Yor\`ub\'a, Hausa, and Igbo (three of the most prominent languages in Nigeria), and ReciLex, a multilingual culinary lexicon containing approximately 15,000 translated entities across ten recipe entity categories, including ingredients, tools, chef actions, state of tools, and durations. We eval
s29c09e6a72.summary: Researchers introduce ReciLoReL, a benchmark of 600 expert-translated, culturally adapted recipes in Yorùbá, Hausa, and Igbo, plus ReciLex, a multilingual culinary lexicon.
s29c09e6a72.why: It provides resources for evaluating culturally adaptive translation of low-resource languages, an area LLMs have underexplored.

s54748c011a.title: Know When to Zoom: How Small Is Too Small for Vision-Language Models?
s54748c011a.description: arXiv:2611.22709v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Online vision-language models often miss small details in large images, because the service shrinks the image, or rejects it, before the model ever sees it. A car 20 pixels wide in an 8000 by 6000 drone photo reaches Claude about 6 pixels wide, and OpenAI's default rejects the photo outright. We measure how much detail survives for seven models from four vendors, using an eye exam of printed codes and 601 questions about small objects in real photos. The smallest text a model reads half the time grows from 6 pixels or less on a small image to a predicted 10 to 13 pixels on a 7680 by 4320 photo at default settings. Zooming wins much of the detail back. Splitting each photo into up to nine tiles raises accuracy by 11.1 to 14.5 percentage poin
s54748c011a.summary: A study measures how much detail survives image downscaling or rejection for seven vision-language models from four vendors, using printed-code tests and 601 small-object questions.
s54748c011a.why: Engineers sending large images to hosted VLMs may lose small objects and text to silent downscaling, so image preprocessing matters for accuracy.

s4a8b8c9bb5.title: Stress Testing a Multimodal Large Language Model Grading Assistant on Kinematics Graph Reading
s4a8b8c9bb5.description: arXiv:2611.22726v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can recognize graph features yet award credit without sufficient graphical support. This exploratory study examines selected grading outputs for synthetic responses to four kinematics exercises, generated through visual distortion and progressive transformation toward reference graphs. Different model and prompt configurations were used. Some judgments correctly distinguished instantaneous zero velocity from rest over a finite interval and recognized positive curvature. Yet a severely distorted velocity--time graph received full credit despite disconnected and branching traces and an unclear zero-velocity reference. Other submissions graded under the same configuration lost substantial credit. Numeri
s4a8b8c9bb5.summary: An exploratory study stress-tests a multimodal LLM grading assistant on synthetic kinematics graph responses, finding it sometimes awards credit without sufficient graphical support.
s4a8b8c9bb5.why: Shows MLLM graders can give credit unsupported by visual evidence, a reliability risk for any automated assessment that relies on reading graphs.

s13d31d8d48.title: Network-Exposed Configuration Attacks on LLM-Controlled Social Robots
s13d31d8d48.description: arXiv:2611.22761v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) in embodied robots create security dependencies beyond inference. We investigate a network-exposed configuration attack on the Pollen Robotics Reachy Mini Lite, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to replace personality settings and the cloud LLM's system prompt through a management interface, without adversarial conversational input. Eleven prompt-injection attempts across five categories were reported as resisted, whereas both configuration-layer attack paths produced observable behavioural changes on physical hardware. We demonstrate local and network-adjacent access, mapping the weakness to CWE-306 (Missing Authentication for a Critical Function) and CWE-1327 (Binding to an Unrestricted IP Address), with a
s13d31d8d48.summary: Researchers show an unauthenticated attacker can alter personality settings and the cloud LLM system prompt of a Reachy Mini Lite social robot via its management interface.
s13d31d8d48.why: Configuration and management interfaces, not just prompts, are an attack surface for LLM-powered robots and should be secured and authenticated.

s9bc32e15e4.title: StitchRAG: Constructing Compact and Evidence-Preserving Contexts for RAG with Diffusion-Based Stitching
s9bc32e15e4.description: arXiv:2611.22766v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improves factuality by grounding large language models (LLMs) in external evidence. However, long retrieved contexts incur computational overhead and can even hurt performance due to noisy or irrelevant content. We propose \textsc{StitchRAG}, a framework for constructing compact context in RAG. \textsc{StitchRAG} builds a faithful, information-dense context while dynamically compressing the retrieved passages. We adapt the size reduction ratio to each passage by formulating a utility maximization trading-off the retained information and computation costs. We then extract answer candidates and query-related keywords from passages as anchors and collect passage sentences containing anchors under the derive
s9bc32e15e4.summary: StitchRAG proposes a diffusion-based method to build compact, evidence-preserving retrieval contexts by dynamically compressing retrieved passages.
s9bc32e15e4.why: Shorter, denser retrieval contexts could cut RAG compute costs and reduce noise that degrades answer quality.

sccd8480525.title: ForceBody: Force-Paired Parametric Body Motion with Torque Uncertainty
sccd8480525.description: arXiv:2611.22769v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Forces and torques drive human motion, central to biomechanics, robotics, and physics-aware animation, yet they are often absent from learning-based motion pipelines for body reconstruction and generation. Some motion datasets provide force annotations, but the paired motion sequences are incompatible with the parametric body models used in modern learning pipelines. In addition, existing datasets typically obtain joint torques through inverse dynamics, which is inherently sensitive to the quality of the input kinematics; however, they do not quantify the reliability of these torque estimates. We close this gap with ForceBody, the first dataset to bring ground truth force supervision into a parametric body representation, shipped with per-s
sccd8480525.summary: ForceBody introduces force-paired parametric body motion data with torque uncertainty for learning-based human motion pipelines.

s06ec90505e.title: PANO: Parallel Latent Space Neural Operator for Solving PDEs
s06ec90505e.description: arXiv:2611.22782v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Aggregating observations into a limited number of latent tokens and learning physical interactions in the latent space has emerged as an effective approach for Transformer-based neural operators to solve Partial Differential Equation (PDE) problems involving large-scale observations. However, existing methods typically compress observations using a single aggregation pattern, making physical information not retained by that pattern invisible to the latent space and thereby constraining physical interactions within it. To address this limitation, we propose PArallel Latent Space Neural Operator (PANO), a novel neural operator for solving PDEs that formulates physical interactions among observations as an additive combination of interaction r
s06ec90505e.summary: PANO proposes a parallel latent-space neural operator that uses multiple aggregation patterns to solve PDEs over large-scale observations.
s06ec90505e.why: Offers a potentially more accurate Transformer-based approach for PDE solving, relevant to scientific computing teams.

s6504ce7177.title: NexSight: Verifiable Tasks for Fine-Grained Agentic Long-Video Understanding
s6504ce7177.description: arXiv:2611.22790v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fine-grained questions about long videos ask how many times an action occurs, in what order events unfold, or exactly when a state changes. Answering them can require finding brief moments scattered across hours of footage. Agentic models that decide when and where to look promise to find these moments, yet this ability is hard both to measure and to learn. Sparse supporting evidence may establish that an action occurred without establishing its total count; verifying timeline-wide claims requires checking for missed occurrences and double counting. Answer-only supervision, in turn, does not explicitly supervise the search for evidence. We present NexSight, which builds verifiable tasks to both evaluate and train agentic long-video understa
s6504ce7177.summary: NexSight introduces verifiable tasks for evaluating agentic models on fine-grained questions about long videos, such as counting actions and locating state changes.
s6504ce7177.why: Provides a way to measure and train agentic video search with verifiable answers, useful for evaluating long-video agents.

s0dd745dd65.title: A tiny object detection dataset for high-altitude open-water search and rescue
s0dd745dd65.description: arXiv:2611.22825v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large aerial platforms often operate above 1.5 km to improve the efficiency of open water search and rescue (OW-SAR). However, long imaging distances, wide fields of view, and limited sensor resolution reduce objects to a few pixels, increasing their susceptibility to environmental interference and making detection harder than for conventional small objects. To our knowledge, existing datasets focus on low-altitude scenarios and do not support automatic detection at 1.5-2.0 km. We therefore present TinyWOD, a tiny object detection dataset for high-altitude OW-SAR using lifebuoys as detection targets. It comprises 11,359 manually annotated images and 19,505 annotated instances spanning diverse environments, lighting conditions, water colors,
s0dd745dd65.summary: Researchers release TinyWOD, a tiny object detection dataset for open-water search and rescue imagery captured from 1.5 to 2.0 km altitude.

s17d9834ea4.title: Better Rankers, Worse Retrievers: The Hidden Cost of RL Post-Training in Generative Recommendation
s17d9834ea4.description: arXiv:2611.22838v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative recommenders decode the semantic ID of a user's next item with a language model, and post-training them with reinforcement learning (RL) after supervised fine-tuning (SFT) has become standard practice. The gains are mostly reported on the first ten results, yet in deployment such models hand hundreds of candidates to a downstream ranker or reward model. We show that RL post-training has a hidden cost: it improves accuracy at the top of the list (hit@K for small K) but, on all five datasets we study, lowers the recall of the candidate list (hit@K for K in the hundreds). The model becomes a better ranker and a worse retriever. Controlled experiments trace the loss to the negative advantages that RL assigns to the candidates it samp
s17d9834ea4.summary: A study finds RL post-training of generative recommenders improves top-of-list accuracy but lowers recall across hundreds of candidates on five datasets.
s17d9834ea4.why: Teams feeding generative recommender candidates to downstream rankers may see reduced recall from RL post-training, so evaluation should go beyond top-K metrics.

s88e4c16e91.title: WATERFALL: Workflow for Adaptive Training with Evolutionary Reward Formulation and Automated Learning Loops
s88e4c16e91.description: arXiv:2611.22854v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reward design remains a central bottleneck in reinforcement learning (RL), particularly in sparse-reward, long-horizon and partially observable settings requiring dependency chaining, memory, and deceptive affordance disambiguation. While recent foundation-model approaches reduce manual reward engineering, most assume goal-conditioning, task descriptions, expert demonstrations, or ground-truth metrics. These assumptions are problematic in partially observable environments, where task-relevant objectives, affordances, and dynamics must be discovered through interaction rather than disclosed a priori. We formalise this problem setting by introducing WATERFALL, an iterative population-based workflow for automated reward discovery under the str
s88e4c16e91.summary: WATERFALL proposes a workflow that uses evolutionary, foundation-model-driven reward formulation to automate reward design in partially observable RL settings.
s88e4c16e91.why: Targets the reward-design bottleneck in sparse-reward RL, which could reduce manual engineering effort for training agents.

s1ddde3bbc8.title: Learning Agent-Centric Vision-Language-Action World Models for Autonomous Driving
s1ddde3bbc8.description: arXiv:2611.22880v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent progress in integrating vision-language-action (VLA) models with world modeling has significantly advanced end-to-end autonomous driving by allowing systems to reason about imagined futures instead of merely reacting to current observations. However, most world VLA models generate future frames at the pixel level with plenty of dense visual tokens. Although such generated futures can be visually plausible, they preserve many driving-irrelevant appearance details, i.e., only a small portion of the tokens directly encode critical planning-relevant factors, such as agent geometry, motion dynamics, and interactions. This introduces a significant performance bottleneck. An important question thus arises: what world state should a world VL
s1ddde3bbc8.summary: A paper proposes agent-centric vision-language-action world models that imagine driving-relevant future states instead of dense pixel-level frames.
s1ddde3bbc8.why: Suggests more efficient planning representations for autonomous driving by discarding appearance details irrelevant to planning.

s06f0df07c7.title: Stopping Is Not the Limit: Understanding and Eliciting Agent Capability in Long-Horizon Vulnerability Exploitation
s06f0df07c7.description: arXiv:2611.22888v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vulnerability exploitation tests whether language model agents can develop working exploits from known software flaws. Sequential test-time scaling can improve exploitation performance, but larger budgets do not ensure sustained exploration: agents often stop with budget remaining. Yet what happens when execution continues beyond stopping remains underexplored. We investigate this gap on ExploitBench using DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 and MiMo-V2.6-Pro. We find additional verified gains after the first stop response, but gains diminish over longer execution. We identify two patterns associated with less productive continuation: an increasing proportion of stop responses within the same context and earlier stopping associated with summaries retain
s06f0df07c7.summary: Researchers study long-horizon vulnerability exploitation by LLM agents on ExploitBench, finding additional verified gains continue after agents first stop.
s06f0df07c7.why: Shows agents often halt with budget left and that continuing execution yields further gains, relevant to evaluating autonomous security agents.

s4d6e23e305.title: When Do Typed Decision Models Work in Transportation? Evidence from Travel Choice and Traffic Signal Control
s4d6e23e305.description: arXiv:2611.22926v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Typed decision models combine natural-language understanding with a structured interface that returns a selected action and an option-level probability distribution without generating lengthy textual responses. Their low inference cost and response latency make them attractive for transportation problems with predefined alternatives. This paper investigates their effectiveness, robustness, and efficiency in two representative transportation tasks: individual travel-mode choice prediction and sequential traffic signal control. We systematically evaluate TypeSafe Jev and GPT-6 Luna Decisions against conventional transportation methods, reinforcement learning algorithms, and four chat-based large language models. Experiments on the Swissmetro
s4d6e23e305.summary: A paper evaluates typed decision models, which return a selected action and option probabilities, on travel-mode choice and traffic signal control.
s4d6e23e305.why: Indicates low-latency structured LLM decision interfaces may suit transportation tasks with predefined options, though robustness is still under study.

s15f90f8c79.title: Projected Penalty-Gradient Tracking for Communication-Efficient Byzantine-Resilient Federated Learning
s15f90f8c79.description: arXiv:2611.22929v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate communication-efficient federated learning over heterogeneous datasets in the presence of Byzantine adversaries capable of uploading arbitrary information. Penalty-based methods bound the influence of each worker through the bounded gradient of a penalty function; however, the bound is lost once the uploads are compressed, since a Byzantine worker can accumulate an unbounded state at the server. To retain the Byzantine resilience under compressed uploads, we propose a projected penalty-gradient tracking framework, where each honest worker uploads a compressed residual of its penalty gradient and the server projects each reconstructed state onto the known penalty-gradient ball. The framework accommodates any contractive compre
s15f90f8c79.summary: A paper proposes projected penalty-gradient tracking to keep Byzantine resilience in communication-efficient federated learning with compressed uploads.
s15f90f8c79.why: Addresses a gap where compression breaks Byzantine robustness guarantees, relevant to federated systems over heterogeneous data.

se8b0406393.title: Hierarchical Diffusion Transformer for End-to-End Image Generation
se8b0406393.description: arXiv:2611.22962v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Pixel-space diffusion learns visual representations and image generation jointly in a single end-to-end training stage, without a separately pretrained visual encoder. However, plain pixel-space Transformers still trail leading two-stage latent diffusion models in generation quality and training efficiency. We hypothesize that part of this gap arises from retaining one token per patch throughout the backbone, which does not explicitly encourage a visual hierarchy that summarizes related content at progressively coarser levels. To address this, we introduce Hierarchical Diffusion Transformers (HiT), which progressively group related tokens and represent each group with a single token. The main Transformer bottleneck processes these compact g
se8b0406393.summary: A hierarchical diffusion transformer is proposed for pixel-space end-to-end image generation, aiming to close the gap with latent diffusion models.

sfe2ef82693.title: High-Dimensional Black-Box Optimization via Guidance Sampling of Diffusion Models
sfe2ef82693.description: arXiv:2611.22965v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many real-world optimization problems involve optimizing black-box objectives for which only a limited number of evaluations are available. Bayesian optimization (BO) is a powerful framework for such problems, but its effectiveness often deteriorates in high-dimensional spaces. Recent work leverages diffusion models for black-box optimization, often through pre-training a reward-conditioned score network to steer generation towards high-reward samples. Alternatively, gradient-based guidance methods assume access to a differentiable reward function from which guidance gradients are queried. However, these approaches either require large amounts of labeled data for offline training or access to exact reward gradients, limiting their applicabi
sfe2ef82693.summary: A paper proposes guidance sampling with diffusion models for high-dimensional black-box optimization where evaluations are limited.

sc294c9f8f8.title: CodeReel: Accelerating Code-to-Video Agents with Exact Frame Reuse and Blocking-Aware Scheduling
sc294c9f8f8.description: arXiv:2611.22967v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coding agents make videos by writing and refining programs in a build--inspect--edit loop. A finished film costs a median of $2.85 in model calls and 11 minutes, over a third of that time in builds that block the agent. We find that much of this time is avoidable, for two reasons. First, 37.5% of the frames of a session's later films were drawn before, many shifted in time or inside an edited scene. Second, half of the builds stop at a check, where the agent needs only the verdict, but which builds stop is unknown until the checks finish. We present CodeReel, a training-free execution layer behind agents' existing commands. Exact frame reuse keys each frame by its drawing commands, regardless of its position in time, and reuses each frame w
sc294c9f8f8.summary: CodeReel proposes reusing previously drawn frames and scheduling builds to speed up coding agents that generate videos via programs.
sc294c9f8f8.why: Shows how caching and non-blocking build scheduling can cut latency and cost in iterative coding-agent loops.

s6a43b2749f.title: SEAM: Computer-Use Agents Know the Harm Between Screens, and Commit It Anyway
s6a43b2749f.description: arXiv:2611.22971v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Safety benchmarks for computer-use agents (CUAs) place the harm either in the intent of the task or on a single screen: a malicious instruction, an injected command, a phishing page. An agent that checks the task and each screen in isolation can pass them, so they do not test whether it combines facts seen on different screens. Yet in delegated work, harm often arises exactly this way: a fact about a person on one screen, a fact about an item on another, and a legitimate task that binds them. We introduce SEAM (Safety Execution Across Multiple screens), a benchmark of such cross-screen compositional harm: 600 multi-step, cross-application OSWorld tasks in which the instruction and every single observation are benign and only their combinati
s6a43b2749f.summary: SEAM is a new safety benchmark testing whether computer-use agents detect harm arising from combining facts across multiple screens.
s6a43b2749f.why: Existing single-screen safety tests may miss cross-screen harms, so agent evaluations need multi-step checks before deployment.

s7532ce56e0.title: Large Language Models Have Not Yet Transformed Science
s7532ce56e0.description: arXiv:2611.22975v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The emergence of large language models (LLMs) in late 2022 has raised questions about the future of science, but assessing their impact requires understanding how scientific practices were already evolving. We analyze 2.5 million full-text papers across five disciplines from 2015 to 2025, tracing trends over a broad spectrum of lexical, structural, epistemological, and social dimensions. Aside from frequency shifts in some words, most pre-2023 trends continued with limited detectable breaks. Among the notable exceptions, growth in computer science coauthor teams accelerated significantly in Asia, while apparent declines in biomedical topic diversity largely reflected standardization in article formats. Our study establishes an empirical fou
s7532ce56e0.summary: An analysis of 2.5 million full-text papers from 2015 to 2025 finds most pre-2023 science trends continued, with few detectable LLM-driven breaks.

s2683b96f65.title: How Web Research Agents Interpret User Priorities
s2683b96f65.description: arXiv:2611.22989v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Web research agents gather information online and write cited reports, including financial analysis. Users can state a priority to guide this research, but a priority may not say how to judge the options, leaving the agent to choose the criteria. We examine how two such agents, built on OpenAI and Anthropic models, interpret a stated priority. In 36 runs, the agents compared Microsoft and Alphabet as businesses. Prompts asked for special attention to growth or resilience, or gave no priority. We analyzed reports, searches, returned sources and cited sources. Of the 24 reports given a priority, 21 focused on it, but their criteria varied. Under the growth priority, OpenAI reports that ranked the companies accounted for risk or predictability
s2683b96f65.summary: A study of two web research agents built on OpenAI and Anthropic models finds they interpret stated user priorities inconsistently when comparing companies.
s2683b96f65.why: Shows that agent outputs depend on criteria the agent picks when a user's priority is vague, which affects reliability of research workflows.

sa14c425cd6.title: Check Your Blind Spots: Decision-Guided Perception by Probing the Planner with Hypothetical Objects
sa14c425cd6.description: arXiv:2611.23030v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Not every perception error changes the planner's action. Yet adaptive-resolution perception chooses where to spend high-resolution computation from image cues, which can neither reliably point to an object that low resolution missed nor tell which objects matter to the planner. We observe that the planner can say where an object would matter before anything is seen: inserting a hypothetical object at a location tests whether its action would change. Decision-Guided Speculative Perception (DGSP) treats the low-resolution scene and its action as a draft and probes the planner in this way to obtain a decision-sensitivity field, the locations where an unseen object would change the action. Only this field and the support, the detections on whic
sa14c425cd6.summary: DGSP probes a planner with hypothetical inserted objects to decide where to spend high-resolution perception compute.
sa14c425cd6.why: Offers a way to direct perception compute based on whether errors would change the planner's action.

sac17f62c66.title: ReTouchGS: Ultralight Render-free Aesthetic Color Enhancement and Transfer for 3D Gaussian Splatting
sac17f62c66.description: arXiv:2611.23054v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables photorealistic scene reconstruction. Existing 3DGS color transfer and interactive editing methods are guided by reference images and user-specified color adjustments. However, in many applications, users simply want aesthetically guided color enhancement that automatically makes the scene more visually appealing while maintaining consistent colors and tones across viewpoints. We present ReTouchGS, to our knowledge the first framework for reference-free aesthetic color enhancement of pretrained 3DGS models. It predicts a scene-level color lookup table (LUT) from the model and its associated camera parameters. ReTouchGS also supports reference-guided color transfer by fitting a scene-level LUT using one ed
sac17f62c66.summary: ReTouchGS introduces a reference-free method for automatically enhancing the aesthetic color of pretrained 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes.

sfaece97052.title: Runtime Verification of Multiple Natural Language Criteria for Agent Governance
sfaece97052.description: arXiv:2611.23074v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI agents are governed by hundreds of natural language criteria, yet existing verifiers cannot efficiently evaluate an agent's output against a large set of such criteria and report which are satisfied, violated, or inapplicable. We introduce the VFM, a tree-attention verifier that encodes the shared context and target text, and scores N natural language criteria in parallel, returning independent per-criterion ternary verdicts. The VFM is pretrained on CriteriaBank, a corpus of 394K (context, target, criterion, verdict) tuples spanning over 321K distinct criterion strings. A finetuned VFM-4B outperforms GPT-5.4 on a synthetic governance benchmark. On the DynaBench multi-criterion benchmark, it outperforms DynaGuard-4B on trace-level failur
sfaece97052.summary: VFM is a tree-attention verifier that scores many natural language criteria in parallel, giving per-criterion verdicts for agent outputs, trained on CriteriaBank.
sfaece97052.why: Makes checking agent outputs against hundreds of governance rules more efficient, relevant to production agent oversight.

sff3ee5a269.title: Learning to Undo: Transfer Reinforcement Learning under State Space Transformations
sff3ee5a269.description: arXiv:2611.23081v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Transfer learning in reinforcement learning (RL) has shown strong empirical success. In this work, we take a more principled perspective by studying when and how transferring knowledge between MDPs (a source and a target) can be provably beneficial. Specifically, we consider the case where there exists an undo map such that applying this map to the target's state space recovers the source exactly. We propose an algorithm that learns this map by matching state feature statistics gathered from both MDPs, and then uses it to transfer the source policy to the target. We theoretically justify the algorithm by analyzing the setting when the undo map is linear and the source is linearly-$Q^\star$ realizable, where our approach has strictly better
sff3ee5a269.summary: The paper studies when transfer reinforcement learning between MDPs is provably beneficial, using a learned undo map that aligns the target state space with the source.

se9539cf41a.title: BugGen 2.0: Rethinking the Roles of LLMs for Scalable RTL Bug Synthesis
se9539cf41a.description: arXiv:2611.23091v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI-assisted RTL localization and debugging need ground-truth bug datasets with known locations and observable failures, while testbench grading uses injected bugs to measure detection capability. Creating such datasets at scale remains a major EDA challenge. BugGen 1.0 shows that Large Language Models (LLMs) can generate context-aware RTL mutations. Still, it relies on the model for both choosing where to mutate and generating the edit, which increases inference costs and can lead to invalid choices. BugGen 2.0 changes this division of labor. Deterministic algorithms handle structural analysis, target selection, and validation, while the LLM focuses on localized semantic rewriting. Across four OpenTitan IP blocks and FabScalar with three LL
se9539cf41a.summary: BugGen 2.0 separates the roles of LLMs in generating RTL bug datasets, aiming to lower inference costs and reduce invalid mutation choices.
se9539cf41a.why: Offers a cheaper, more reliable route to large bug datasets for hardware verification and debugging tools.

s7406c3c17e.title: What's in a Tree ? Hierarchical $n$-gram models as controlled approximators of language
s7406c3c17e.description: arXiv:2611.23093v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hierarchical models have been proposed as synthetic settings for studying language. However, their relevance to realistic language corpora remains underexplored. In this work, we introduce tree-grams, autoregressive generative $n$-gram models that build the conditional probability tensor $p(x_n \mid x_{1:n-1})$ through a hierarchical composition of order-2 and order-3 tensors. $n$ controls the maximal context window, whereas a rank hyperparameter $d$ controls model capacity, yielding an interpretable and systematically scalable family of approximators of language. We show how tree-grams outperform existing $n$-gram baselines, while remaining competitive with deep transformer-based language models. We demonstrate the utility of such controll
s7406c3c17e.summary: The paper introduces tree-grams, hierarchical n-gram models with controllable context window and capacity, as approximators of language.

sc0b2981adb.title: Natural Language Programming: Rethinking Language, Memory, and Cognition in the Era of Generative AI
sc0b2981adb.description: arXiv:2611.23106v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence is transforming the role of natural language in computational systems. In classical Natural Language Processing (NLP), language was treated as an object of computation: something to analyse, classify, translate, or generate. Large Language Models (LLMs) challenge this perspective, enabling natural language to function increasingly as an executable cognitive medium through which humans structure reasoning, orchestrate problem solving, and regulate hybrid human/AI workflows. This paper introduces Natural Language Programming (NLPg) as a theoretical and epistemological extension of traditional NLP. Rather than focusing on language understanding alone, NLPg conceptualises prompts as dynamic cognitive artefacts
sc0b2981adb.summary: A paper argues natural language is becoming an executable cognitive medium for orchestrating reasoning and hybrid human-AI workflows.

sc1dcf2e2fc.title: Mind the Gap: A Deployed Multi-Agent System for Documentation Maintenance
sc1dcf2e2fc.description: arXiv:2611.23142v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The "AI revolution" has enabled teams across the technology industry to deliver software features at unprecedented velocity. While code evolves faster than ever, customer-facing documentation often struggles to stay up to speed. As users increasingly rely on LLM-based agents that consume documentation as their primary interface, the impact of this documentation gap worsens: stale information propagates and is treated as authoritative. Signals for identifying where documentation has fallen behind already exist in abundance, both explicit (e.g., resolved support tickets revealing what documentation lacks) and implicit (e.g., code-documentation discrepancies detectable from automated loops). We deploy a multi-agent system, built around a triag
sc1dcf2e2fc.summary: A deployed multi-agent system is described for finding and maintaining stale customer-facing documentation as code changes.
sc1dcf2e2fc.why: Addresses stale docs that LLM agents consume as authoritative, a concrete problem for teams shipping fast-changing software.

saeaa43eb80.title: Learning Stratified Policies for Inference-Time Objectives
saeaa43eb80.description: arXiv:2611.23154v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Inference-time scaling improves the performance of large language models by sampling multiple responses and evaluating their collective utility. However, many existing approaches obtain these samples by repeatedly sampling from a single policy. In this work, we study if the sample budget at inference time can instead be allocated across a population of policies. We introduce stratified policies, where each of $k$ learned policies contributes one response to a $k$-sample inference-time objective. We realize this policy population using separate LoRA adapters on a shared language model backbone and optimize it for pass@$k$. We theoretically motivate the approach by analyzing the linear setting; a population of LoRAs can achieve zero best-of-$
saeaa43eb80.summary: The paper proposes stratified policies, where k learned policies each contribute one response to a k-sample inference-time objective.
saeaa43eb80.why: Suggests spreading inference sampling budget across policy populations rather than one policy, a possible lever for better test-time scaling.

s0db4b8d588.title: Attribution Through the Decoder: Prediction-Space Explanations for Structured Outputs
s0db4b8d588.description: arXiv:2611.23161v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Networks that predict angles, gaze directions, and rotations do not output these quantities directly: they emit raw coordinates that a fixed decoder, such as normalization, maps to the final prediction. Attribution methods are usually applied to the raw coordinates, so they can credit inputs for changes the decoder discards, such as rescaling a vector when only its direction matters. The resulting explanation can highlight inputs that have no effect on the prediction. We instead attribute through the decoder differential, which for normalization decoders reduces to a scaled tangent projection. We characterize invariance to output rescaling, show that every fixed smooth scalar target on a sphere has points of zero tangential sensitivity, and
s0db4b8d588.summary: The paper proposes attributing predictions through a fixed decoder such as normalization, so explanations ignore inputs the decoder discards.

s165f256efb.title: Inference after coding agents
s165f256efb.description: arXiv:2611.23174v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Empirical research is changing rapidly as AI coding agents are becoming increasingly proficient in every step of it, from writing code to manipulating data. We argue that while the potential of coding agents for science is vast, their use in hypothesis testing poses a substantial threat to classical inference, as these agents enable a supercharged form of selective inference. In particular, we argue that coding agents carrying out empirical research introduce a new type of post-selection inference that combines human-like, open-ended search over an implicit space of estimators with programmatic replayability of both the selection and the estimation process. Indeed, we find that on simulated data with zero effects, four frontier agents repor
s165f256efb.summary: The paper argues AI coding agents enable a new form of post-selection inference that threatens the validity of classical hypothesis testing in empirical research.
s165f256efb.why: Warns that agent-driven analysis can inflate false findings, relevant to anyone using agents for data analysis.

seb0ce0b58a.title: Say Less, Hallucinate Less? Diagnosing and Restoring Object Coverage in Preference-Optimized Vision-Language Models
seb0ce0b58a.description: arXiv:2611.23179v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Preference optimization (PO) is the standard way to reduce object hallucination in large vision-language models. We find that four public PO checkpoints of LLaVA-1.5-7B also lower object coverage. They name fewer object categories, and their lower hallucination rates bring no significant gain in set-level object F1 on CHAIR. We therefore ask how much of the PO gain the base model can reproduce by stopping earlier. A positive end-of-sequence (EOS) logit bias lets the base model reach the recall of each PO model, and this early stopping alone reproduces 58 to 86 percent of the CHAIRi gain of three checkpoints on two disjoint COCO sets. Writing longer does not bring the lost categories back. Under greedy decoding, a negative EOS bias recovers
seb0ce0b58a.summary: Researchers found four public preference-optimized LLaVA-1.5-7B checkpoints name fewer objects, and a base model with an EOS logit bias can match their recall.
seb0ce0b58a.why: Reducing hallucination via preference optimization may silently cut object coverage, so teams should measure recall alongside hallucination rates.

s5063a37858.title: Retrieval-Augmented Correction for Generalist Medical Image Segmentation
s5063a37858.description: arXiv:2611.23189v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Automated segmentation is routinely used as the first step in quantitative image-based clinical workflows, where predicted masks are subsequently reviewed and corrected by human operators. Automated correction of the residual structural errors is currently addressed one anatomy at a time, so the number of trained correctors scales with the number of segmentation targets. We present GRACE, a retrieval-augmented refiner that edits an input mask under context drawn from a shared knowledge base of verified prior cases. The refiner is trained once on a multi-organ corpus spanning compact organs, cavities, branching vessels, and tumour lesions. In the held-out dataset-transfer evaluation, three held-out datasets query a fixed knowledge base built
s5063a37858.summary: GRACE is a retrieval-augmented refiner that corrects medical image segmentation masks using a shared knowledge base of verified prior cases, trained once across anatomies.
s5063a37858.why: A single shared corrector could reduce the need to train separate correction models for each segmentation target in clinical workflows.

s954964cde4.title: Structure--Residual Inductive Biases for Language Model Pretraining
s954964cde4.description: arXiv:2611.23197v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Next-token prediction is relied upon to learn both predictive behavior and internal representations. We ask whether representation structure itself should be an explicit inductive bias. Motivated by the two-part coding view of Kolmogorov complexity, we study a structure--residual principle in which a representation separates structure from realization detail. We instantiate this principle in two complementary ways. Boundary Bottleneck Concept (BBC) routes information from token segments through boundary carriers while preserving local autoregressive computation. Continuous Concept (CC) regularizes representation geometry and induces a spectral decomposition into low-frequency structure and high-frequency residual. We derive coding bounds fo
s954964cde4.summary: Researchers propose structure-residual inductive biases for language model pretraining, separating representation structure from realization detail, inspired by Kolmogorov complexity.

s198c4b1551.title: Fine-Tuning Gemma 4 Edge Models for MATLAB Signal-Processing Code with SFT and QLoRA on a Laptop iGPU
s198c4b1551.description: arXiv:2611.23205v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Small language models that run on a laptop are attractive for writing signal-processing code offline, but they make systematic errors on digital signal processing (DSP) conventions. We apply supervised fine-tuning (SFT) to the Gemma 4 edge models E2B and E4B with 66 checked examples covering 11 signal-processing MATLAB subtasks, using low-rank adaptation (LoRA) and quantized LoRA (QLoRA) on the integrated GPU (iGPU) of a laptop, and deploy the 8-bit integer (int8) models with the adapters through OpenVINO. On held-out variants scored by deterministic checkers, the pass rate rises from 18/66 to 37/66 (LoRA) and 37/66 (QLoRA) for E2B and from 32/66 to 47/66 for E4B (QLoRA). Reading all 159 failing programs shows that the adapters remove most
s198c4b1551.summary: Researchers fine-tuned Gemma 4 edge models with SFT and QLoRA on 66 examples for MATLAB signal-processing code, deploying int8 models via OpenVINO on a laptop iGPU.
s198c4b1551.why: It shows small local models can be specialized for niche code domains on consumer hardware using modest data and open tooling.

sd3943358cd.title: Reading Scene States: Uncovering Safety Failures in Vision-Language Models
sd3943358cd.description: arXiv:2611.23206v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) can provide harmful assistance by interpreting visual events, even without an explicit request for the underlying harmful objective. We identify this \textbf{scene-state safety vulnerability} and introduce \textbf{SceneSafetyBench}, comprising 375 image--question pairs spanning Initial, Medium, and Ultimate scene states and five visual presentations. Across eight VLMs, scene-state inputs elicit harmful assistance with attack success rates (ASRs) of 45.6--72.3\%. Comparative analysis across three VLMs shows that scene-state inputs most closely resemble QR-related images in their layer-wise safety-related signal profiles, while exhibiting lower average late-layer readouts and distinct signal dynamics during gener
sd3943358cd.summary: SceneSafetyBench, with 375 image-question pairs, finds eight VLMs give harmful assistance to scene-state inputs at 45.6–72.3% attack success rates.
sd3943358cd.why: Safety filters that only check explicit harmful requests may miss harm inferred from visual scenes, a gap teams deploying VLMs should test for.

s2e072b3182.title: Higher-Scoring Coding Models Did Not Get More Work Done
s2e072b3182.description: arXiv:2611.23216v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: New coding models advertise themselves on score improvements of coding benchmarks. Yet no study has tested if a model that scores higher on these benchmarks gets more real work done. On June 12, 2026, a U.S. export control directive banned access to Claude Fable 5 for 19 days, which forced users to switch to other models. During this time, most former Fable 5 users switched to Opus 4.8 (11 points lower on SWE-Bench Pro compared to Fable 5). We treat this suspension as a natural experiment, where the people and projects stayed the same and only the model changed, so we could isolate the effect of Fable 5 on user productivity. We tracked GitHub pull requests of 297 Fable 5 users before, during, and after the suspension. We used 8,908 develope
s2e072b3182.summary: A study uses a June 2026 U.S. export control suspension of Claude Fable 5 as a natural experiment to test whether higher-scoring coding models get more real work done.
s2e072b3182.why: It questions whether coding benchmark gains translate into productivity, relevant when choosing models based on leaderboard scores.

sc1d68dd9f2.title: Do LLM Agents Still Need to Be Told How to Self-Improve?
sc1d68dd9f2.description: arXiv:2611.23219v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM agents increasingly drive their own learning. Self-improvement methods delegate various components of model optimization to the models themselves. As models become more capable, this motivates a basic question: do these increasingly capable models still need us to specify how they should self-improve? In this paper we study an autonomous paradigm in which, given basic primitives, resources, and a general goal for self-improvement, agents construct their own self-learning algorithm for context-based optimization. Using the setting of gameplay as a testbed, a frozen LLM agent is given a compute budget and tools for collecting experience and updating text documents, and allowed to freely experiment without an externally imposed loop or acc
sc1d68dd9f2.summary: The paper studies whether LLM agents, given basic primitives and a goal, can construct their own self-improvement algorithms for context-based optimization without human-specified methods.

sbbcad6cddc.title: StringQFT: A Multiuse Textbook Resource for AI-Assisted Theoretical Physics
sbbcad6cddc.description: arXiv:2611.23225v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present StringQFT as a textbook collection for string constructions of quantum field theory and as infrastructure for AI-assisted theoretical physics. The collection comprises 18 volumes, 190 chapters and 3,795 pages, covering brane probes, brane webs, geometric engineering, F-theory constructions, wrapped M5-branes and exact worldsheet constructions. Its open-book benchmark inventory contains 1,073 items, including 499 with automatic finite-answer checking. For retrieval-augmented generation, it provides 1,371 section records linked to textbook sources and PDF locations, together with a local lexical retriever. Training-data preparation is illustrated by 21 private, source-linked examples. For agents, it exposes 19 calculation tools wit
sbbcad6cddc.summary: StringQFT is a 18-volume, 190-chapter open textbook collection on string constructions of quantum field theory, with a 1,073-item benchmark and RAG records for AI-assisted physics.

sb9bf99bdba.title: Ambient LLMs: Data-Efficient Supervised Fine-tuning via Temperature Matching
sb9bf99bdba.description: arXiv:2611.23229v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Collecting large-scale, diverse, and high-quality post-training datasets for autoregressive language models is challenging. Consequently, Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) is typically applied to datasets significantly smaller than those used for pre-training, which leads to overfitting and the catastrophic forgetting of the tails of the data distribution. To prevent this collapse, we introduce Ambient SFT, a principled framework for leveraging imperfect predictions to augment the fine-tuning set. In our method, a "frozen" version of the pre-trained model serves as a noisy teacher that the fine-tuned model must match at a coarse level.
